source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: De quibusdam præambulis in expositione duodecim Prophetarum
1.title_en: On certain preliminaries to the exposition of the twelve Prophets

paras.t: SICUT in novo Testamento evangelicis […] documentis adjuncta est apostolica doctrina, in Epistolis Pauli aliisque septem Canonicis, in Apocalypsi quoque et Actibus Apostolorum contenta, ita in veteri Testamento legi Mosaicæ prophetica dicta ac scripta succedunt : non tamen consimili modo parique causa per omnia. Evangelicæ nempe Christi doctrinæ superadditum est apostolicum dogma : non propter insufficientiam vel imperfectionem evangelicæ disciplinæ ; imo evangelica doctrina prorsus perfecta est, tum quantum ad omnis culpæ exclusionem, tum quantum ad præceptorum et consiliorum evidentissimam traditionem, tum etiam quantum ad exemplaris vitæ exhibitionem, fidei corroborationem, cœlestisque præmii pollicitationem : sed propter particulariorem ac diffusiorem admonitionem ac prosecutionem eorum quæ in Evangelio continentur, et ad præcavendos futuros errores, itemque ad solvendum quæstiones incidentes. Legi vero Moysis prophetia succedit, ut minus dicta suppleat, obscura elucidet, et de Christi mysteriis plenius tractet. Quum enim finis legis sit Christus, secundum Apostolum, in hoc patet imperfectio legis, quod de Christo ejusque mysteriis tam modice tamque obscure profatur.
paras.en: As in the New Testament the apostolic teaching, contained in the Epistles of Paul and the seven other Canonical Epistles, in the Apocalypse also and the Acts of the Apostles, has been joined to the gospel […] documents, so in the Old Testament the prophetic sayings and writings follow upon the law of Moses: not, however, in a like manner and for the same reason in every respect. For the apostolic teaching was added to the gospel doctrine of Christ not because of any insufficiency or imperfection in the gospel discipline; on the contrary, the gospel doctrine is altogether perfect, as regards the exclusion of all fault, as regards the most evident handing down of precepts and counsels, and as regards the showing forth of an exemplary life, the strengthening of faith, and the promise of the heavenly reward: but it was added for a more particular and more extended admonition and pursuit of the things contained in the Gospel, to guard against errors to come, and to resolve questions as they arise. But prophecy follows upon the law of Moses in order to supply what was said too little there, to make plain what is obscure, and to treat more fully of the mysteries of Christ. For since, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 10:4|the end of the law is Christ|finis legis sit Christus]], the imperfection of the law appears in this, that it speaks of Christ and his mysteries so scantily and so obscurely.

paras.t: Denique, secundum Glossam, quemadmodum in corporalis fabricæ constructione tria sunt, quibus ad majora consurgitur, scilicet fundamentum, paries, tectum ; ita et spiritualis structura Ecclesiæ tribus quasi munimentis continetur ac consummatur, videlicet lege, prophetia, Evangelio. Lex ergo quasi lapidem ponit in fundamento, prophetia parietes constituit, Evangelium tectum consummat. In lege enim dicitur : Gentibus multis fœnerabis, fratri autem tuo non fœnerabis. Ecce quasi inchoatio, dum in parte prohibetur usura. In prophetia vero ille fertur in tabernaculo Domini quieturus, qui pecuniam suam non dederit ad usuram; et Ezechiel, Usuram, inquit, et superabundantiam non accipies. Ecce profectus. In Evangelio autem dives ille splendide epulans condemnatur, non quia aliena rapuerit, sed quoniam sua non erogavit. Ecce consummatio. Lex itaque elementum est incipientium, prophetia eruditio proficientium, Evangelium consummatio pervenientium : quatenus a fundamento inchoantium, per parietem proficientium, ascendamus ad tectum pervenientium, tanquam cum Apostolo rapti usque ad tertium cœlum, ubi audiamus arcana verba, quæ carnalis homo non percipit. Primum cœlum in lege, secundum in prophetia, tertium in Evangelio. Hi sunt tres panes Eliæ appositi, quos et in Evangelio amicus commodat postulanti. Primus panis est purgatorius, quoniam lex saltem timore pœnæ retrahit a peccatis. Secundus, consolatorius, quoniam prophetia claris de Christo promissionibus consolatur præstolantes. Tertius, consummatorius, quia legis et Prophetarum eloquia Evangelium Christi consummat. Hæc insuper tria, videlicet legalis profunditas, prophetalis subtilitas, evangelica veritas, sunt quasi tria candelabra Ecclesiam illustrantia.
paras.en: Further, according to the Gloss, as in the building of a material house there are three things by which it rises to greater height, namely the foundation, the wall and the roof, so too the spiritual structure of the Church is held together and completed by three bulwarks, as it were: the law, prophecy and the Gospel. The law, then, lays the stone in the foundation, as it were; prophecy builds the walls; the Gospel completes the roof. For in the law it is said: [[Deut 15:6|Thou shalt lend to many nations|Gentibus multis fœnerabis]], [[Deut 23:19|Thou shalt not lend to thy brother|fratri autem tuo non fœnerabis]] [Denis joins Deut 15:6 and 23:19, as the margin shows]. See the beginning, as it were, when usury is forbidden in part. But in prophecy the one who shall rest in the tabernacle of the Lord is said to be he that [[Ps 14:5|hath not put out his money to usury|pecuniam suam non dederit ad usuram]]; and Ezechiel: [[Ezech 18:17|usury|Usuram]], he says, [[Ezech 18:17|and increase|et superabundantiam]] thou shalt not take[[Ezech 22:12||]] [Denis gives the prophet's words as a command; in Ezechiel they describe the just man, and at 22:12 the sinful city]. See the progress. But in the Gospel that rich man who feasted sumptuously is condemned[[Luke 16:19||]], not because he had seized what belonged to others, but because he did not give away what was his own. See the completion. The law, therefore, is the first lesson of beginners, prophecy the instruction of those who are making progress, the Gospel the completion of those who arrive: so that from the foundation of beginners, through the wall of those making progress, we may ascend to the roof of those who arrive, as it were [[2 Cor 12:2|caught up to the third heaven|rapti usque ad tertium cœlum]] with the Apostle, where we may hear [[2 Cor 12:4|secret words|arcana verba]] which the carnal man does not perceive[[1 Cor 2:14||]]. The first heaven is in the law, the second in prophecy, the third in the Gospel. These are the three loaves set before Elias[[3 Kings 17:6||]][[3 Kings 17:11||]][[3 Kings 17:15||]][[3 Kings 19:6||]], which in the Gospel too the friend lends to him who asks[[Luke 11:5||]]. The first loaf is purgative, since the law at least by fear of punishment draws men back from sins. The second is consoling, since prophecy consoles those who wait with clear promises of Christ. The third is perfecting, because the Gospel of Christ completes the sayings of the law and the Prophets. These three, moreover, namely the depth of the law, the subtlety of prophecy and the truth of the Gospel, are as it were three candlesticks giving light to the Church.

paras.t: Quemadmodum autem ad materialis domus perfectionem atque ornatum alia multa concurrunt, præter tria præfata, videlicet fenestræ, ostia atque solaria, sic ad spiritualis ædificii matris Ecclesiæ perfectionem ac decorem concurrunt præter prædicta, alia multa, videlicet apostolica documenta, de quibus jam tactum est.
paras.en: And as, besides the three things aforesaid, many others go to make up the perfection and adornment of a material house, namely windows, doors and upper rooms, so besides those already named many other things go to make up the perfection and beauty of the spiritual building of Mother Church, namely the apostolic documents, which have already been touched upon.

paras.t: Præterea S. Hieronymus in exordio explanationis duodecim Prophetarum testatur, paucos ante se exstitisse horum Prophetarum expositores. Affirmat tamen se vidisse ac perlegisse commentarios Apollinaris Laodicensis, qui propter nimiam suam brevitatem ad perfectam intelligentiam non perduxit. Origenes quoque, secundum quod refert Hieronymus, parvum super Osee scripsit libellum, in quo omnia quæ contra Ephraim dicit Osee, ad hæreticos refert. Pierius etiam et Eusebius Cæsariensis aliqua super Osee scripserunt. Insuper dicit Hieronymus, quod dum rogatu S. Paulæ esset Alexandriæ, vidit Didymum virum sui temporis eruditissimum, eumque frequenter audivit, atque rogavit ut in Osee scriberet commentarios. Precibus ergo Hieronymi acquiescens Didymus, tres libros super hunc dictavit Prophetam, quos Hieronymus lætabundus recepit.
paras.en: Moreover, St Jerome testifies at the beginning of his explanation of the twelve Prophets that there were few expositors of these Prophets before him. He affirms, however, that he had seen and read through the commentaries of Apollinaris of Laodicea, who because of his excessive brevity did not lead to a perfect understanding. Origen also, as Jerome reports, wrote a little book on Osee, in which he refers to heretics all that Osee says against Ephraim. Pierius too and Eusebius of Caesarea wrote something on Osee. Jerome says besides that when, at the request of St Paula, he was at Alexandria, he saw Didymus, the most learned man of his time, heard him often, and asked him to write commentaries on Osee. Didymus, then, yielding to Jerome's prayers, dictated three books on this Prophet, which Jerome received with joy.

paras.t: Ego quoque nunc opus istud aggrediens, habeo expositionem Hieronymi, Bedæ quoque, qui pauca ponit, nisi quæ sumpsit ex commentariis Hieronymi. Habeo et Glossam ordinariam cum expositione brevissima Nicolai de Lyra. Glossa vero quæ communiter allegatur, intelligenda est Glossa ordinaria: quæ ordinaria dicitur, tanquam regularis et satis authentica, utpote ex sanctorum ac catholicorum patrum sive doctorum dictis collecta.
paras.en: I too, now setting about this work, have the exposition of Jerome, and also of Bede, who sets down little except what he took from the commentaries of Jerome. I have also the Ordinary Gloss with the very brief exposition of Nicholas of Lyra. The Gloss that is commonly cited is to be understood as the Ordinary Gloss, which is called ordinary as being regular [that is, the standard gloss, in common use] and of good authority, since it is gathered from the sayings of the holy and catholic fathers or doctors.

paras.t: Advertendum postremo, quia ut recitat Glossa, S. Hieronymus præsenti libro prologos duos præmittit, quorum primus, qui incipit, Non idem est ordo duodecim Prophetarum, ad totum pertinet librum; secundus specialiter ad Osee : qui prologus incipit, Temporibus Oziæ, habeturque in Bibliis. In primi initio prologi dicit Hieronymus : Non idem est ordo Prophetarum apud Hebræos, qui et apud nos. Unde secundum quod ibi leguntur, hic quoque dispositi sunt. Pro cujus intellectu sciendum, quod Ecclesia usque ad translationem Hieronymi utebatur translatione Septuaginta interpretum. Secundum quos iste est ordo Prophetarum duodecim, Osee, Amos, Michæas, Joel, Abdias, Jonas, Nahum, Habacuc, Sophonias, Aggæus, Zacharias, et Malachias. Ideo dicit Hieronymus, non eumdem esse ordinem Prophetarum istorum apud Hebræos et nos, id est apud Ecclesiam pro tempore illo quo utebatur translatione Septuaginta interpretum. Hieronymus vero ordinando Prophetas, secutus est Hebræos, apud quos ordinantur Prophetæ secundum ordinem quem habent in translatione Hieronymi, qua utimur modo. Propterea modo idem est ordo duodecim Prophetarum apud Hebræos, qui et apud nos, qui translatione Hieronymi utimur.
paras.en: Lastly it must be noted that, as the Gloss records, St Jerome sets two prologues before the present book, of which the first, which begins, The order of the twelve Prophets is not the same, belongs to the whole book; the second specially to Osee: this prologue begins, In the times of Ozias, and is found in the Bibles. At the beginning of the first prologue Jerome says: The order of the Prophets is not the same among the Hebrews as among us. Hence they are arranged here too according to the order in which they are read there. To understand this it must be known that until Jerome's translation the Church used the translation of the Seventy interpreters, according to whom the order of the twelve Prophets is this: Osee, Amos, Micheas, Joel, Abdias, Jonas, Nahum, Habacuc, Sophonias, Aggeus, Zacharias and Malachias. Therefore Jerome says that the order of these Prophets is not the same among the Hebrews and us, that is, in the Church, for the time when it used the translation of the Seventy. But Jerome in ordering the Prophets followed the Hebrews, among whom the Prophets are arranged in the order they have in Jerome's translation, which we now use. Hence now the order of the twelve Prophets is the same among the Hebrews as among us who use Jerome's translation.

paras.t: Osee commaticus est, id est divisus, quia in singulis clausulis diversas vel plenas promit sententias. Idcirco in Prologo scribitur : Et quasi per sententias loquens. Dicitur quoque in Prologo, Osee fuisse synchronon (id est contemporaneum) Isaiæ.
paras.en: Osee is commatic, that is, divided [*commaticus*, from the Greek *komma*, a short clause], because in each clause he brings out different or complete sentences. Therefore it is written in the Prologue: And speaking as it were in sentences. It is also said in the Prologue that Osee was *synchronon* (that is, contemporary) with Isaias.

1.title: Expositio primi capituli Osee prophetæ
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter of the prophet Osee

paras.t: VERBUM Domini quod factum est ad Osee filium Beeri, in diebus Oziæ, Joathan, Achaz, Ezechiæ, regum Juda, et in diebus Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel. Hucusque proœmium, prologus, ac titulus libri sequentis. In quo prologo declaratur nomen Prophetæ auctoris libri præsentis, nomen quoque patris ejus, et tempus prophetalium revelationum huic vati factarum : ut sit sensus : Verbum Domini quod factum est, id est sermo propheticus divinitus factus, seu revelatus ministerio angeli, quia ut Dionysius adstruit, propheticæ revelationes factæ sunt ministerio angelorum. Hic itaque sermo factus ad Osee filium Beeri (qui sermo in processu libri hujus describitur) est materia hujus voluminis, vel liber præsens, seu contentus libro præsenti. Estque sermo (id est sermones libro isto descripti, multi enim fuerunt atque diversis temporibus revelati) factus ad Osee in diebus Oziæ regis Juda, qui alio nomine dictus est Azarias, regnavitque in Jerusalem quinquaginta duobus annis. Quumque officium sacerdotale sibi temerarie usurpasset, thurificando in templo contra prohibitionem legis atque pontificis, mox percussus est lepra, et habitavit seorsum. Joathan vero filius ejus gubernavit palatium, et populum judicavit. Quæ omnia plenius scripta sunt secundo Paralipomenon et quarto Regum.
paras.en: [[1:1|The word of the Lord, that came to Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Ozias, Joathan, Achaz, and Ezechias, kings of Juda|VERBUM Domini quod factum est ad Osee filium Beeri, in diebus Oziæ, Joathan, Achaz, Ezechiæ, regum Juda]], [[1:1|and in the days of Jeroboam, the son of Joas, king of Israel|et in diebus Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel]]. Thus far the proem, prologue and title of the book that follows. In this prologue are declared the name of the Prophet who is the author of the present book, the name also of his father, and the time of the prophetic revelations made to this seer; so that the sense is: [[1:1|The word of the Lord, that came|Verbum Domini quod factum est]], that is, the prophetic discourse made by God, or revealed by the ministry of an angel; for, as Dionysius maintains, prophetic revelations were made by the ministry of angels. This discourse, then, which came [[1:1|to Hosea, the son of Beeri|ad Osee filium Beeri]] (the discourse which is set down in the course of this book), is the matter of this volume, or the present book, or what is contained in the present book. And this discourse (that is, the discourses set down in this book, for they were many, and revealed at different times) came to Osee [[1:1|in the days of Ozias|in diebus Oziæ]], king of Juda, who by another name was called Azarias[[4 Kings 15:1||]], and reigned in Jerusalem two and fifty years[[4 Kings 15:2||]][[2 Par 26:1||]][[2 Par 26:3||]]. And when he had rashly usurped the priestly office for himself, burning incense in the temple against the prohibition of the law and of the high priest, he was forthwith struck with leprosy, and dwelt apart[[4 Kings 15:5||]][[2 Par 26:16||]][[2 Par 26:21||]]. But Joathan his son governed the palace and judged the people[[4 Kings 15:5||]]. All of which is written more fully in the second book of Paralipomenon and in the fourth of Kings.

paras.t: Cœpit itaque Osee vaticinari regnante Ozia, et exinde prophetavit sub tribus regibus sequentibus, scilicet Joathan, qui secundum Hieronymum super Isaiam, justissimus fuit, et sedecim annis regnavit; et Achaz filio Joathan, qui Achaz etiam sedecim annis regnavit, cujus iniquitates quarto Regum descriptæ sunt; et Ezechia, de quo quarto Regum habetur, quod ante eum non fuit similis ei, nec postea, quem constat viginti octo annis regnasse. Et in diebus Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel. Quemadmodum scriptum est quarto Regum, anno quintodecimo Amasiæ regis Juda patris prædicti Oziæ, regnavit Jeroboam filius Joas regis Israel in Samaria quadraginta et uno annis. Fecitque malum coram Domino, incedens in peccatis Jeroboam filii Nabat Ephratæi primi regis Israel, seu decem tribuum : quarum regnum a præfato Jeroboam Ephratæo usque ad ultimum regem earum, dictum Osee, duravit annis ducentis et quinquaginta, secundum Hieronymum. Denique, anno vicesimo septimo Jeroboam filii Joas, de quo jam sermo, cœpit regnare Ozias : ex quo elucescit, quod iste Jeroboam et Ozias simul regnabant quatuordecim annis.
paras.en: Osee therefore began to prophesy in the reign of Ozias, and thereafter prophesied under the three kings who followed: namely Joathan, who according to Jerome on Isaias[[Is 7:1||]] [the margin points to Jerome's comment on Isaias 7:1] was most just, and reigned sixteen years[[4 Kings 15:33||]]; and Achaz the son of Joathan, who also reigned sixteen years, and whose iniquities are described in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 16:2||]]; and Ezechias, of whom we have it in the fourth of Kings that there was none like him before him, nor after[[4 Kings 18:5||]], and who is known to have reigned twenty-eight years[[4 Kings 18:2||]] [a printed marginal note corrects this to twenty-nine, as 4 Kings 18:2 has it]. [[1:1|and in the days of Jeroboam, the son of Joas, king of Israel|Et in diebus Jeroboam filii Joas regis Israel]]. As is written in the fourth of Kings, [[4 Kings 14:23|In the fifteenth year of Amasias|anno quintodecimo Amasiæ]], king of Juda, the father of the aforesaid Ozias, [[4 Kings 14:23|reigned Jeroboam, the son of Joas, king of Israel, in Samaria, one and forty years|regnavit Jeroboam filius Joas regis Israel in Samaria quadraginta et uno annis]]. And he did evil before the Lord, walking in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nabat the Ephrathite[[4 Kings 14:24||]], the first king of Israel, or of the ten tribes; whose kingdom, from the aforesaid Jeroboam the Ephrathite to their last king, named Osee, lasted two hundred and fifty years, according to Jerome. Lastly, in the seven and twentieth year of Jeroboam the son of Joas, of whom we are now speaking, Ozias began to reign[[4 Kings 15:1||]]: from which it is clear that this Jeroboam and Ozias reigned together for fourteen years.

paras.t: Ponit autem Osee propheta in titulo libri sui non solum reges Juda, sed etiam regem decem tribuum, quoniam utriusque regni populo prophetavit. Pauca tamen, secundum Glossam, loquitur duabus tribubus, scilicet populo Juda ac Benjamin. Sed quia Osee prophetavit non solum sub uno regum Israel, puta Jeroboam jam prædicto, verum et sub filio ejus, imo sub omnibus regibus Israel posterioribus, multis quoque annis post eos, cur non ponit in titulo nomina plurium regum Israel sub quibus prophetavit, sicut commemorat quatuor reges Juda ? Dici potest, quod propter peccata et idololatriam eorum ipsos non exprimit. Sed huic responsioni objicitur, quod etiam Achaz atque Jeroboam idololatræ erant. Ideo dici potest, quod reges Israel non explicantur, quia expressis regibus Juda, dantur intelligi, tanquam contemporanei eis. Porro nono anno Osee regis Israel, scilicet undecimo anno Achaz regis Juda, captæ atque in Medos translatæ sunt decem tribus a Salmanasar rege Assyriorum. Quoniam ergo Osee propheta, prophetare exorsus est tempore Jeroboam et Oziæ, qui multis annis præcesserunt prædictum regem Osee filium Ela, prophetavitque usque ad tempora Ezechiæ, qui cœpit regnare sexto anno post decem tribuum captivitatem : constat Osee vaticinatum ante captivitatem præfatam, et post eam. Propter quod ait Hieronymus, quod futuram captivitatem Israel prænuntiavit, præsentem deplanxit, præteritam vero pro correctione duarum tribuum cum fletu retexuit.
paras.en: Now Osee the prophet sets down in the title of his book not only the kings of Juda but also the king of the ten tribes, since he prophesied to the people of both kingdoms. Yet, according to the Gloss, he says little to the two tribes, that is, to the people of Juda and Benjamin. But since Osee prophesied not only under one of the kings of Israel, namely the Jeroboam already mentioned, but also under his son, indeed under all the later kings of Israel, and for many years after them as well, why does he not put in the title the names of more of the kings of Israel under whom he prophesied, as he records four kings of Juda? It can be said that he does not name them because of their sins and idolatry. But against this answer it is objected that Achaz and Jeroboam too were idolaters. So it can be said that the kings of Israel are not set out because, the kings of Juda being named, they are given to be understood as their contemporaries. Further, in the ninth year of Osee king of Israel, that is, in the eleventh year of Achaz king of Juda, the ten tribes were taken and carried away into Media by Salmanasar king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. Since, then, Osee the prophet began to prophesy in the time of Jeroboam and Ozias, who preceded by many years the aforesaid king Osee the son of Ela, and prophesied until the times of Ezechias, who began to reign in the sixth year after the captivity of the ten tribes, it is plain that Osee prophesied both before that captivity and after it. Wherefore Jerome says that he foretold the captivity of Israel to come, bewailed it when it was present, and when it was past recounted it with weeping for the correction of the two tribes.

paras.t: Præterea, secundum Glossam modus tractandi in Osee, est talis : Primo ponit prœmium, sicut nunc patuit. Secundo dicit Dominum in ipso præcipue esse locutum. Postea sub metaphora meretricis atque adulteræ ait de decem tribubus ac duabus, nunc conjunctim, nunc separatim. Deinceps ait de Christi passione et surrectione, dicendo : Vivificabit nos post duos dies, in die tertia suscitabit nos. In fine autem ostendit voluminis difficultatem, quum ait : Quis sapiens, et intelliget ista?
paras.en: Moreover, according to the Gloss, the manner of treatment in Osee is this. First he sets down the proem, as has now appeared. Secondly he says that the Lord spoke chiefly in him. Then, under the metaphor of a harlot and an adulteress, he speaks of the ten tribes and of the two, now together, now separately. After that he speaks of the passion and resurrection of Christ, saying: [[Osee 6:3|He will revive us after two days: on the third day he will raise us up|Vivificabit nos post duos dies, in die tertia suscitabit nos]]. And at the end he shows the difficulty of the volume, when he says: [[Osee 14:10|Who is wise, and he shall understand these things?|Quis sapiens, et intelliget ista]]

paras.t: Advertendum quoque, quia ut Beda testatur, sive dicatur regnum Juda, sive regnum duarum tribuum, scilicet Juda et Benjamin, semper subintelligenda est tertia tribus, videlicet sacerdotalis sive Levitica, quæ a tempore separationis decem tribuum a domo David, adhæsit regibus Juda, quia in eis permansit cultus divinus, eratque templum Dei in sorte eorum.
paras.en: It is to be noted also that, as Bede testifies, whether one says the kingdom of Juda or the kingdom of the two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin, a third tribe is always to be understood with them, namely the priestly or Levitical tribe, which, from the time when the ten tribes were separated from the house of David, adhered to the kings of Juda[[2 Par 11:13||]][[2 Par 11:14||]], because the worship of God remained among them, and the temple of God was in their lot.

paras.t: Adhuc autem quod dictum est, Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Osee, Hieronymus et Beda exponunt de increato æternoque Verbo Dei Patris, de quo legitur : In principio erat Verbum. Quod licet factum non sit, tamen factum est ut hoc Verbum fieret, id est, loqueretur ad Osee : ac per hoc ipse Osee per inspirationem et gratiam hujus Verbi quodammodo factus est deus, populique salvator, quoniam doctrina et vita cooperabatur eorum saluti, quemadmodum ait Apostolus : Quatenus salvos faciam quosdam ex eis. Hinc Christus dixit Judæis : Si illos dixit deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est, etc. Ex quo clarum est, quod per divinas revelationes fiant homines dii. Quæ gratia consonat nomini hujus Prophetæ, quia Osee interpretatur salvator. Beeri vero, cujus Osee est filius, interpretatur, putei mei. Idcirco Osee significat Christum Salvatorem Filium Patris æterni, qui dicitur puteus, fons, atque abyssus, prout per Jeremiam testatur : Me dereliquerunt fontem aquæ vivæ. Beeri autem pater Osee creditur fuisse propheta, quoniam teste Hieronymo, Hebræi affirmant omnes patres seu avos qui in principiis Prophetarum ponuntur, fuisse prophetas, quamvis eorum vaticinia non sint descripta, quia nec omnes Prophetæ libros ediderunt, vel revelationes sibi desuper factas scripserunt.
paras.en: Furthermore, what is said, [[1:1|The word of the Lord, that came to Hosea|Verbum Domini quod factum est ad Osee]], Jerome and Bede expound of the uncreated and eternal Word of God the Father, of whom we read: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. And though this Word was not made, yet it was brought about that this Word should come, that is, should speak to Osee [Latin *factum est*, "it was made", the same words that the Douay-Rheims renders "that came": the Word is not made, yet it "was made" to come to the Prophet]; and through this, Osee himself, by the inspiration and grace of this Word, was in a certain manner made a god, and a saviour of the people, since by his teaching and his life he worked together for their salvation; as the Apostle says, so that he [[Rom 11:14|may save some of them|salvos faciam quosdam ex eis]]. Hence Christ said to the Jews: [[John 10:35|If he called them gods to whom the word of God was spoken|Si illos dixit deos, ad quos sermo Dei factus est]], etc. From which it is clear that men become gods through divine revelations. And this grace agrees with the name of this Prophet, for Osee is interpreted *saviour*. And Beeri, whose son Osee is, is interpreted *of my well*. Therefore Osee signifies Christ the Saviour, the Son of the eternal Father, who is called a well, a fountain and an abyss, as he testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 2:13|They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water|Me dereliquerunt fontem aquæ vivæ]]. Beeri, the father of Osee, is believed to have been a prophet, since, as Jerome testifies, the Hebrews affirm that all the fathers or grandfathers who are set down at the beginnings of the Prophets were prophets, though their prophecies are not written down; for not all the Prophets put forth books, or wrote down the revelations made to them from above.

paras.t: Finito prologo inchoatur tractatus, quum dicitur : Principium loquendi Domino in Osee. Quod dupliciter intelligi potest, secundum Hieronymum : Primo, quod Dominus locutus sit huic Prophetæ antequam aliis, qui sequuntur in hoc libro duodecim Prophetarum. Ut sit sensus : Principium loquendi fuit Domino in Osee, ita quod ab ipso sumpsit loquendi exordium, quantum ad Prophetas sequentes. Huic autem expositioni alii satis apparenter objiciunt, quod Abdias est unus duodecim Prophetarum, et quartus in ordine. Hic vero Abdias, secundum doctores Hebraicos ac Latinos, fuit dispensator Achab regis Israel. A fine autem vitæ Achab usque ad principium regni Oziæ, sub quo Osee orsus est prophetare, fluxerunt centum circiter anni, ut patet numeranti tempora regum intermediorum. Unde apparet, quod Dominus primo locutus sit Abdiæ, quam Osee. Verumtamen objectio ista nil certum concludit : Primo, quoniam teste Hieronymo, et communiter sic tenetur, illi Prophetæ in quibus tempus non præfertur in titulo, sub illis regibus prophetaverunt, sub quibus et illi qui ante eos habent titulos certum tempus continentes. Abdias autem non habet tempus in titulo; sed Amos, qui ponitur ante eum, habet in titulo tempus et nomen Oziæ regis : ergo Abdias sub Ozia prophetavit sicut Osee. Propterea non est certum quod Abdiæ locutus sit Dominus prius quam Osee, quamvis certum sit, secundum Glossam, quod Osee, Isaias, Joel, Amos, Abdias, Jonas et Michæas eisdem temporibus prophetarunt. Rursus, visio seu prophetia Abdiæ est brevissima, propter quod æstimari potest quod Dominus non sit ei locutus tam diu ac sæpe sicut Osee. — Nihilo minus secunda expositio certior est, scilicet ista : Principium loquendi Domino in Osee est id quod immediate subjungitur de acceptione fornicariæ, ita quod Dominus prius locutus est hoc, quam reliqua quæ sequuntur.
paras.en: The prologue finished, the treatise begins, where it is said: [[1:2|The beginning of the Lord's speaking by Hosea|Principium loquendi Domino in Osee]]. This can be understood in two ways, according to Jerome. First, that the Lord spoke to this Prophet before the others who follow in this book of the twelve Prophets; so that the sense is: The beginning of speaking was the Lord's in Osee, so that he made the opening of his speaking with him, as regards the Prophets who follow. Against this exposition others object, plausibly enough, that Abdias is one of the twelve Prophets, and fourth in order; and this Abdias, according to the Hebrew and Latin doctors, was the steward of Achab king of Israel. Now from the end of Achab's life to the beginning of the reign of Ozias, under whom Osee began to prophesy, about a hundred years passed, as is plain to anyone who counts the times of the kings in between. Whence it appears that the Lord spoke to Abdias before Osee. Yet this objection concludes nothing certain. First, because, as Jerome testifies and as is commonly held, those Prophets in whose title no time is set down prophesied under the same kings as those before them whose titles contain a definite time. Now Abdias has no time in his title; but Amos, who is placed before him, has in his title the time and the name of king Ozias[[Amos 1:1||]]: therefore Abdias prophesied under Ozias, as Osee did. Hence it is not certain that the Lord spoke to Abdias before Osee; though it is certain, according to the Gloss, that Osee, Isaias, Joel, Amos, Abdias, Jonas and Micheas prophesied in the same times. Again, the vision or prophecy of Abdias is very short, so that it may be thought that the Lord did not speak to him so long or so often as to Osee. — Nevertheless the second exposition is the more certain, namely this: [[1:2|The beginning of the Lord's speaking by Hosea|Principium loquendi Domino in Osee]] is what is added immediately after, about the taking of the harlot; so that the Lord spoke this first, before the rest that follows.

paras.t: Porro quod ait, In Osee, quidam exponunt sic : id est ad Osee. Hieronymus tamen et Glossa distinguunt inter hæc duo : ut Dominus dicatur locutus in Osee, in quantum per ipsum proposuit aliis verbum Dei; ad Osee vero, revelando ei verba prophetica. Vel ideo dictum est, In Osee, ut insinuetur quod ista locutio fuit interna per imaginariam repræsentationem, quemadmodum Zacharias disseruit : Angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur.
paras.en: As for his saying *In Osee* [the Douay-Rheims has "by Hosea"], some expound it thus: that is, *to* Osee. But Jerome and the Gloss distinguish between these two: so that the Lord is said to have spoken *in* Osee inasmuch as through him he set the word of God before others; but *to* Osee, by revealing prophetic words to him. Or else it is said *In Osee* to suggest that this speaking was inward, by an imaginary representation [that is, through images formed in the Prophet's imagination], as Zacharias related: [[Zach 2:3|the angel that spoke in me went forth|Angelus qui loquebatur in me, egrediebatur]].

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad Osee : Vade, sume tibi uxorem fornicationum, et fac filios fornicationum. Prophetæ interdum rebus seu factis, interdum verbis prophetaverunt. Unde Dominus jubet sancto Osee, ut fornicariam ducat, ad designandum prophetice quod populus Israel et etiam regnum Juda spiritualiter fornicaretur, recedendo a Deo per idololatriam, vel potius per idololatriæ multiplicationem, quemadmodum in regno Juda patet impletum tempore Achaz. Ideo subditur, quia fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino.
paras.en: [[1:2|and the Lord said to Hosea: Go, take thee a wife of fornications, and have of her children of fornications|Et dixit Dominus ad Osee : Vade, sume tibi uxorem fornicationum, et fac filios fornicationum]]. The Prophets prophesied sometimes by things or deeds, sometimes by words. Hence the Lord commands holy Osee to take a harlot to wife, to signify prophetically that the people of Israel, and the kingdom of Juda also, would commit spiritual fornication, departing from God by idolatry, or rather by the multiplying of idolatry, as was plainly fulfilled in the kingdom of Juda in the time of Achaz[[4 Kings 16:1||]][[2 Par 28:1||]]. Therefore it is added: [[1:2|for the land by fornication shall depart from the Lord|quia fornicans fornicabitur terra a Domino]].

paras.t: De hac muliere fornicationum Hieronymus diversimode loquitur. In Prologo enim affirmat, eam sic dici propter fornicationem spiritualem seu idololatriam. Unde sic ait : Fornicariam non elocati corporis meretricem, sed gentilem, Deum ignorantem, debemus accipere, quæ Creatoris sui amore contempto, simulacrorum desideriis se subjecit. In commentario autem multa ponit Hieronymus, ex quibus sentire videtur, quod fuerit meretrix. Ait namque : Mulier ista, quam Propheta sumit in conjugem, non semel, sed frequentius fornicata est, ut quanto illa sordidior, tanto sit Propheta patientior, qui talem accepit. Nec culpandus Propheta, si meretricem converterit ad pudicitiam, sed potius laudandus, quod ex mala fecerit bonam. Ex quo intelligimus, non Prophetam perdidisse pudicitiam, fornicariæ copulatum, sed illam assumpsisse pudicitiam, quam antea non habebat. Hinc alii dicunt, quod erat publica meretrix. Propheta tamen obedivit in hoc Deo, quamvis secundum communem legem turpe esset ac vile, quemadmodum Isaias de regio semine natus, Deo jubente, incessit nudus ac discalceatus, et Ezechiel polluto vescitur pane.
paras.en: Of this woman of fornications Jerome speaks in different ways. For in the Prologue he affirms that she is so called on account of spiritual fornication, that is, idolatry. Thus he says: By the harlot we must understand not a prostitute who has hired out her body, but a Gentile woman, ignorant of God, who, despising the love of her Creator, has given herself up to the desire of idols. But in the commentary Jerome sets down much from which he seems to hold that she was a harlot. For he says: This woman whom the Prophet takes to wife committed fornication not once but often, so that the fouler she was, the more patient might the Prophet be who took such a one. Nor is the Prophet to be blamed if he turned a harlot to chastity; rather he is to be praised for making a good woman of a bad one. From this we understand, not that the Prophet lost his chastity by being joined to a harlot, but that she took on the chastity she had not had before. Hence others say that she was a public harlot. Yet the Prophet obeyed God in this, though by the common law it was shameful and base; as Isaias, born of royal stock, at God's bidding [[Is 20:2|went naked, and barefoot|incessit nudus ac discalceatus]], and Ezechiel eats defiled bread[[Ezech 4:12||]][[Ezech 4:15||]].

paras.t: Est igitur sensus : Sume tibi uxorem fornicationum, id est feminam spiritualibus fornicationibus seu idololatriæ vitiis deditam, secundum primam opinionem ; aut certe corporaliter fornicari assuetam, secundum aliam opinionem, accipe in legitimam conjugem. Et fac filios fornicationum. Hoc dupliciter explanatur. Primo sic : Fac filios fornicationum, id est, ex femina ista genera pueros : qui dicuntur filii fornicationum, non quia illegitime, sed quia ex ea nati, quæ fornicaria fuit et meretrix : sicut nunc aliquis dicitur filius sacerdotis, non quia pater ejus sacerdos fuit, quum genuit eum, sed postea. Sic isti dicuntur filii meretricis, quia mater eorum talis aliquando exstitit. Ideo ratio Lyræ improbantis hanc expositionem non cogit. Secundo exponitur sic : Fac filios fornicationum, id est, feminam istam sume cum filiis suis in fornicatione natis, sicque filios fornicationum fac tuos per adoptionem. Huic expositioni consonat translatio Septuaginta interpretum, quæ continet : Vade, tolle tibi uxorem fornicationis et filios fornicationis. Unde secundum Lyram, in Hebræo habetur : Accipe uxorem fornicationum, et fac filios fornicationum.
paras.en: The sense, then, is: [[1:2|take thee a wife of fornications|Sume tibi uxorem fornicationum]], that is, take as thy lawful wife a woman given to spiritual fornications, or the vices of idolatry, according to the first opinion; or else one accustomed to fornicate in the body, according to the other opinion. [[1:2|and have of her children of fornications|Et fac filios fornicationum]] [Latin *fac filios*, literally "make children": on the first reading "beget them", on the second "make them thine"]. This is explained in two ways. First thus: [[1:2|have of her children of fornications|fac filios fornicationum]], that is, beget children of this woman; who are called children of fornications, not because they were born unlawfully, but because they were born of her who had been a fornicator and a harlot; as a man is now called the son of a priest, not because his father was a priest when he begot him, but afterwards. So these are called children of a harlot because their mother had once been such. Hence the argument of Lyra, who rejects this exposition, is not compelling. Secondly it is expounded thus: [[1:2|have of her children of fornications|fac filios fornicationum]], that is, take this woman with her children born in fornication, and so make the children of fornications thine by adoption. With this exposition agrees the translation of the Seventy interpreters, which has: Go, take to thee a wife of fornication and children of fornication. Whence, according to Lyra, the Hebrew reads: Take a wife of fornications, and make children of fornications.

paras.t: Hujus matrimonii mystica ratio subinfertur : Quia fornicans fornicabitur terra, id est populus decem tribuum, et etiam regnum Juda, a Domino. Per hanc reduplicationem seu ingeminationem, qua ait, Fornicans fornicabitur, denotatur vehementia seu multiplicatio idololatriæ utriusque regni. Itaque desponsatio fornicariæ fuit propheticum signum, quod populus Israel idololatriæ adhæreret. Quod autem Propheta fecit sibi filios fornicationum, significat quod Synagoga filios genuit recedentes ac fornicantes a Deo.
paras.en: The mystical reason for this marriage is added: [[1:2|for the land by fornication shall depart|Quia fornicans fornicabitur terra]], that is, the people of the ten tribes, and the kingdom of Juda also, [[1:2|from the Lord|a Domino]]. By this redoubling or repetition, in saying *Fornicans fornicabitur* [literally "fornicating it shall fornicate"], is denoted the vehemence or multiplication of the idolatry of both kingdoms. So the espousal of a harlot was a prophetic sign that the people of Israel would cleave to idolatry. And that the Prophet made himself children of fornications signifies that the Synagogue bore children who departed from God and went fornicating away from him.

paras.t: Præterea alia ratio, quod Osee fornicariam duxit, est, quatenus quod ipse fecit corporaliter, figuraretur Deus facere spiritualiter. Deus enim Synagogam spiritualiter ac corporali fornicatione contaminatam (cui per Ezechielem locutus est, Et tu, meretrix, audi verbum Domini) suscepit clementer et sibi spiritualiter copulavit, quandocumque ad Deum converti curavit.
paras.en: Another reason, moreover, why Osee took a harlot to wife is that what he did in the body might figure what God does spiritually. For God mercifully received the Synagogue, defiled by spiritual and bodily fornication (to whom he spoke through Ezechiel: And thou, [[Ezech 16:35|O harlot, hear the word of the Lord|meretrix, audi verbum Domini]]), and joined her spiritually to himself, whenever she took care to be turned to God.

paras.t: Propter quod per Jeremiam etiam loquitur : Tu fornicata es cum amatoribus multis ; tamen revertere ad me, dicit Dominus. Rursus dictum est, quod Osee tenet figuram Christi. Per hoc ergo quod Osee duxit gentilem seu meretricem, figurabatur quod Christus Ecclesiam ex gentilitate assumptam, collectam, electam, in sponsam assumeret et uxorem. Cujus uxor est Æthiopissa, quæ confitetur in Canticis : Nigra sum, sed formosa, filiæ Jerusalem. Unde in Apocalypsi legitur : Venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se : quam, juxta Apostolum, Christus dilexit, et tradidit semetipsum pro ea, ut illam sanctificaret, mundans eam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ. Quemadmodum autem Osee fecit sibi filios fornicationum ex conjuge sua, illos adoptando vel legitimos procreando, ut dictum est : sic Deus in veteri Testamento filios Synagogæ idololatras et perversos misericorditer convertit, et in filios adoptivos mutavit. Fideles quoque ex ea filios genuit, quos præservavit ab idololatria, prout loquitur ad Eliam : Reliqui mihi septem millia virorum, quorum genua non sunt curvata ante Baal. Similiter tempore evangelicæ legis fecit Christus in Ecclesia ex gentibus congregata.
paras.en: For this reason he says also through Jeremias: [[Jer 3:1|thou hast prostituted thyself to many lovers: nevertheless return to me, saith the Lord|Tu fornicata es cum amatoribus multis ; tamen revertere ad me, dicit Dominus]]. Again, it has been said that Osee bears the figure of Christ. So by Osee's taking a Gentile woman or harlot it was figured that Christ would take as his bride and wife the Church, taken up, gathered and chosen out of the Gentiles. His wife is the Ethiopian woman who confesses in the Canticle: [[Cant 1:4|I am black but beautiful, O ye daughters of Jerusalem|Nigra sum, sed formosa, filiæ Jerusalem]]. Whence we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:7|the marriage of the Lamb is come: and his wife hath prepared herself|Venerunt nuptiæ Agni, et uxor ejus præparavit se]]; whom, as the Apostle says, [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved|Christus dilexit]], and [[Eph 5:25|delivered himself up for it|tradidit semetipsum pro ea]], [[Eph 5:26|That he might sanctify it, cleansing it by the laver of water in the word of life|ut illam sanctificaret, mundans eam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ]]. And as Osee made himself children of fornications from his wife, by adopting them or by begetting them lawfully, as has been said, so God in the Old Testament mercifully converted the idolatrous and perverse children of the Synagogue, and changed them into adopted children. He also begot faithful children of her, whom he preserved from idolatry, as he says to Elias: [[Rom 11:4|I have left me seven thousand men|Reliqui mihi septem millia virorum]], [[3 Kings 19:18|whose knees have not been bowed before Baal|quorum genua non sunt curvata ante Baal]] [the margin gives 3 Kings 19:18 and Rom 11:4; Denis's wording joins the two]. Christ did likewise in the time of the law of the Gospel, in the Church gathered from the Gentiles.

paras.t: Denique habet locum hic quæstio illa, quam movet Thomas in secunda secundæ, videlicet an Deo in omnibus sit obediendum. Et arguit Thomas quod non, quoniam Deus jussit Abrahæ innocentem filium occidere, et filiis Israel Ægyptios spoliare, item Osee fornicariam ducere, quæ omnia videntur contrariari justitiæ. Et respondendum, quod Deus sublimis et benedictus, est omnium rerum primus motor, atque totius justitiæ regula ac mensura. Unde eo ipso est aliquid justum, quo a Deo præcipitur, quum a Deo dependeat omnis virtus et rectitudo voluntatis creatæ. Quemadmodum ergo divinæ motioni ac voluntati cuncta naturalia naturali necessitate subduntur, sic divinæ jussioni omnes voluntates creatæ, naturali necessitate justitiæ obedire tenentur. Sed sicut in naturalibus aliqua agit Deus supra naturam, non tamen contra eam, quum hoc sit unicuique naturale quodammodo, quod Deus operatur in eo ; sic Deus nil præcipit contra justitiam vel virtutem, quamvis aliquando quædam præcipiat supra solitum modum virtutis. Unde prædicta de Abraham et spoliatione Ægypti, et facto Osee, non erant contra virtutem, quoniam Deus habet imperium vitæ et mortis. Ideo potest, cui vult, vitam auferre ac dare. Ejus quoque sunt omnia ; et cui vult, tribuit ea. Item quum ipse sit ordinator generationis humanæ, ille est debitus modus utendi mulieribus, quem ipse præfigit.
paras.en: Lastly, here is the place for that question which Thomas raises in the Secunda Secundæ [Summa theologiae II-II, q. 104, a. 4], namely whether God is to be obeyed in all things. And Thomas argues that he is not, since God commanded Abraham to kill his innocent son[[Gen 22:2||]], and the children of Israel to despoil the Egyptians[[Ex 3:22||]], and also Osee to take a harlot to wife; all of which seem contrary to justice. And the answer is that God, most high and blessed, is the first mover of all things, and the rule and measure of all justice. Hence a thing is just by the very fact that it is commanded by God, since all the virtue and rectitude of the created will depends on God. As therefore all natural things are subject by natural necessity to the divine motion and will, so all created wills are bound by a natural necessity of justice to obey the divine command. But as in natural things God does some things above nature, yet not against it, since it is in a manner natural to each thing that God should work in it; so God commands nothing against justice or virtue, though he sometimes commands some things above the ordinary mode of virtue. Hence the things mentioned, about Abraham, the despoiling of Egypt and the deed of Osee, were not against virtue, since God has dominion over life and death. So he can take away life and give it to whom he will[[Acts 17:25||]]. All things too are his, and he gives them to whom he will. Likewise, since he is the ordainer of human generation, that is the due manner of using women which he himself appoints.

paras.t: Et abiit Osee, Deo prompte obediens, non carnali concupiscentia provocatus, et accepit Gomer filiam Debelaim, id est viri sic appellati, vel de loco sic dicto natam; et concepit, et peperit ei filium. Quamvis autem Propheta dicat sibi divinitus imperatum, accipere uxorem fornicationum, non tamen evidenter exprimit, an Dominus determinaverit ei, quam sumeret. Unde non videtur certum, an Osee acceperit Gomer propria electione, an divina præfixione. Quidquid tamen dicatur de hoc, probabile reor quod aliquid occultæ virtutis aut probitatis erat in femina ista, propter quod electa est jungi viro tam sancto, sicut et Rahab meretrix præ ceteris suis concivibus est salvata, et filio principis tribus Juda conjuncta, propter fidelitatem suam.
paras.en: [[1:3|So he went|Et abiit]] (Osee, readily obeying God, not moved by carnal desire), [[1:3|and took Gomer, the daughter of Debelaim|et accepit Gomer filiam Debelaim]], that is, of a man so called, or born of a place so named; [[1:3|and she conceived, and bore him a son|et concepit, et peperit ei filium]]. Now although the Prophet says he was commanded by God to take a wife of fornications, he does not clearly say whether the Lord fixed for him which woman he should take. Hence it does not seem certain whether Osee took Gomer by his own choice or by God's appointment. But whatever be said of this, I think it probable that there was some hidden virtue or goodness in this woman, for which she was chosen to be joined to so holy a man; as Rahab the harlot too was saved before the rest of her fellow citizens[[Jos 6:25||]], and joined to the son of the prince of the tribe of Juda[[Matt 1:5||]], because of her fidelity.

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad eum, videlicet ad Osee : Voca nomen ejus Jezrael, id est, infantulo tibi nato impone nomen hoc, Jezrael. Consuetudo est Hebræis, nomen imponere rebus ab aliqua proprietate, vel ad aliquid designandum, quemadmodum in Isaia, Christus qui spoliavit infernum, jubetur vocari, Velociter spolia detrahe. Jezrael autem est nomen regiæ civitatis, atque unius metropolis in regno decem tribuum. Jubetur itaque puer iste Jezrael nuncupari, quia per eum Dominus significavit punitionem et captivationem decem tribuum, vel ultionem sanguinis injuste effusi in Jezrael, ut alii dicunt. Ideo subditur ratio appellationis pueri, quoniam adhuc modicum, id est intra breve tempus, et visitabo, id est ulciscar, sanguinem Jezrael, id est sanguinem innoxium in hac urbe effusum, super domum Jehu, id est in posteritate ipsius Jehu regis Israel : quæ posteritas regnando super decem tribus, dicitur aliquos bonos occidisse in Jezrael, idcirco visitatur sanguis illorum in eis. Haymo per sanguinem Jezrael, intelligit sanguinem Naboth, quem fecit Jezabel occidi in Jezrael. Cui concordat quod in Prologo dicit Hieronymus : Sanguis (inquit) Naboth in Jezrael fusus, in domo Jehu propter peccata redundaturus significatur.
paras.en: [[1:4|And the Lord said to him|Et dixit Dominus ad eum]], that is, to Osee: [[1:4|Call his name Jezrahel|Voca nomen ejus Jezrael]], that is, give this name, Jezrael, to the little child born to thee. It is the custom of the Hebrews to give names to things from some property, or to signify something; as in Isaias Christ, who despoiled hell, is ordered to be called [[Is 8:1|Take away the spoils with speed|Velociter spolia detrahe]] [the margin gives Is. viii, 1; the child is named in Is 8:3, where the Douay-Rheims has "Hasten to take away the spoils"]. Now Jezrael is the name of a royal city, one of the chief cities of the kingdom of the ten tribes. This child, then, is ordered to be called Jezrael because by him the Lord signified the punishment and captivity of the ten tribes, or, as others say, the avenging of the blood unjustly shed in Jezrael. Therefore the reason for the child's name is added: [[1:4|for yet a little while|quoniam adhuc modicum]], that is, within a short time, [[1:4|and I will visit|et visitabo]], that is, I will avenge, [[1:4|the blood of Jezrahel|sanguinem Jezrael]], that is, the innocent blood shed in this city, [[1:4|upon the house of Jehu|super domum Jehu]], that is, on the posterity of this Jehu king of Israel: which posterity, reigning over the ten tribes, is said to have slain some good men in Jezrael, and therefore their blood is visited upon them. Haymo understands by the blood of Jezrael the blood of Naboth, whom Jezabel had put to death in Jezrael[[3 Kings 21:1||]][[3 Kings 21:13||]]. With this agrees what Jerome says in the Prologue: The blood of Naboth (he says) shed in Jezrael is signified as about to overflow upon the house of Jehu for its sins.

paras.t: Sed contra hoc alii arguunt, quia nec Jehu, nec posteri ejus occiderunt Naboth; secundo, quoniam quarto Regum legitur Jehu Domino placuisse, eo quod vindicasset sanguinem Naboth, delendo domum Achab, et Jezabel occidendo. Sicque domus Jehu non fuit propter sanguinem Naboth punita, sed potius sublimata, Domino pollicente ipsi Jehu quod filii ejus usque ad quartam generationem sederent super thronum Israel. Ad quod dici potest, quod sicut Christus in Evangelio dicit, omnem sanguinem justum effusum ab Abel usque ad Zachariam, venturum super Judæos incredulos, quoniam imitabantur peccata eorum qui justum Abel et Zachariam interemerunt, sic sanguis Naboth dicitur visitari super domum Jehu, quia et ipse Jehu et filii ejus ad idololatriam sunt conversi, atque ad multa crimina populum Israel induxerunt.
paras.en: But against this others argue, first, that neither Jehu nor his descendants killed Naboth; secondly, that we read in the fourth book of Kings that Jehu pleased the Lord because he avenged the blood of Naboth[[4 Kings 10:30||]], destroying the house of Achab and killing Jezabel. And so the house of Jehu was not punished for the blood of Naboth, but rather exalted[[4 Kings 9:1||]][[4 Kings 10:1||]], the Lord promising Jehu himself that his sons should sit upon the throne of Israel to the fourth generation[[4 Kings 10:30||]]. To this it can be said that, as Christ says in the Gospel that all the just blood shed from Abel to Zacharias would come upon the unbelieving Jews[[Matt 23:35||]], because they imitated the sins of those who slew the just Abel[[Gen 4:8||]] and Zacharias[[2 Par 24:20||]][[2 Par 24:21||]], so the blood of Naboth is said to be visited upon the house of Jehu, because both Jehu himself and his sons turned to idolatry, and led the people of Israel into many crimes.

paras.t: Porro visitatio ista sanguinis Jezrael super domum Jehu, facta est in Zacharia filio prædicti Jeroboam regis Israel, sub quo cœpit Osee prophetare : quem Zachariam sexto mense imperii sui occidit Sellum de alia tribu, et regnavit pro eo. De isto Jehu legitur quarto Regum, quod Elisæus misit ad eum unum adolescentem de filiis Prophetarum, qui unxit eum in regem. Quumque Jehu occidisset omnem domum Achab et sacerdotes Baal, propter quod agendum assumptus fuit in regem, locutus est ei Dominus : Quia studiose egisti quod rectum et placitum erat in oculis meis, et omnia quæ erant in corde meo fecisti contra domum Achab, filii tui usque ad quartam generationem sedebunt super thronum Israel. Jehu autem genuit Joachaz, de quo natus est Joas, qui generavit Jeroboam patrem præfati Zachariæ, in quo Dominus ultus est sanguinem Jezrael. Eratque Zacharias ultimus rex de semine Jehu.
paras.en: Further, this visiting of the blood of Jezrael upon the house of Jehu was done in Zacharias, the son of the aforesaid Jeroboam king of Israel, under whom Osee began to prophesy: Sellum, of another tribe, slew this Zacharias in the sixth month of his reign[[4 Kings 15:8||]], and reigned in his stead[[4 Kings 15:10||]]. Of this Jehu we read in the fourth of Kings that Eliseus sent to him one of the young men of the sons of the prophets, who anointed him king[[4 Kings 9:1||]]. And when Jehu had slain all the house of Achab and the priests of Baal, for the doing of which he had been raised to be king, the Lord said to him: [[4 Kings 10:30|because thou hast diligently executed that which was right and pleasing in my eyes, and hast done to the house of Achab according to all that was in my heart: thy children shall sit upon the throne of Israel to the fourth generation|Quia studiose egisti quod rectum et placitum erat in oculis meis, et omnia quæ erant in corde meo fecisti contra domum Achab, filii tui usque ad quartam generationem sedebunt super thronum Israel]]. Now Jehu begot Joachaz[[4 Kings 13:1||]], of whom was born Joas[[4 Kings 13:9||]], who begot Jeroboam[[4 Kings 13:13||]], the father of the aforesaid Zacharias, in whom the Lord avenged the blood of Jezrael. And Zacharias was the last king of the seed of Jehu[[4 Kings 15:8||]][[4 Kings 15:10||]][[4 Kings 15:12||]].

paras.t: Et quiescere faciam regnum domus Israel, id est, totum regnum decem tribuum permittam a rege Assyriorum destrui et auferri : quod impletum est nono anno Osee regis. Statim vero occiso Zacharia, cœpit regnum decem tribuum a regibus Assyriorum vehementer affligi, primo a Phul, deinde a Theglathphalasar, postremo a Salmanasar, qui transtulit populum Israel in terram suam. A prædicto autem Zacharia usque ad nonum annum Osee regis, sub quo captæ sunt decem tribus, fluxerunt anni quadraginta novem.
paras.en: [[1:4|and I will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel|Et quiescere faciam regnum domus Israel]], that is, I will allow the whole kingdom of the ten tribes to be destroyed and taken away by the king of the Assyrians: which was fulfilled in the ninth year of king Osee[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. But straightway, once Zacharias was slain, the kingdom of the ten tribes began to be grievously afflicted by the kings of the Assyrians: first by Phul[[4 Kings 15:19||]], then by Theglathphalasar[[4 Kings 15:29||]], lastly by Salmanasar, who carried the people of Israel away into his own land[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. And from the aforesaid Zacharias to the ninth year of king Osee, under whom the ten tribes were taken, forty-nine years passed.

paras.t: Et in illa die, id est eo tempore, quum visitavero sanguinem Jezrael super domum Jehu (sicut expositum est), conteram arcum Israel, id est, omne robur et arma decem tribuum superari atque corrumpi permittam, in valle Jezrael, id est in valle latissima sita juxta Jezrael : in qua valle præliantibus decem tribubus contra Assyrios, victæ et cæsæ sunt tribus Israel.
paras.en: [[1:5|And in that day|Et in illa die]], that is, at that time when I shall visit the blood of Jezrael upon the house of Jehu (as has been explained), [[1:5|I will break in pieces the bow of Israel|conteram arcum Israel]], that is, I will allow all the strength and arms of the ten tribes to be overcome and broken, [[1:5|in the valley of Jezrahel|in valle Jezrael]], that is, in the very broad valley lying near Jezrael: in which valley, when the ten tribes fought against the Assyrians, the tribes of Israel were conquered and slain.

1.title: Prosecutio expositionis hujus primi capituli: Et concepit adhuc et peperit filiam
1.title_en: Continuation of the exposition of this first chapter: And she conceived again, and bore a daughter

paras.t: Postquam Deus prænuntiavit cessationem regni decem tribuum, jam per verba et facta denuntiat captivitatis diuturnitatem atque finalem derelictionem earum. Et concepit Gomer adhuc ab Osee, et peperit filiam. Postquam cæsus est Israel, et regnum ejus dejectum, non jam masculus, sed femina nascitur, quatenus per sexus imbecillitatem atque femineum animum, infirmitas populi Israelis, et puerile cor ejus idola colens, declaratur. Et dixit Dominus ei, puta Osee: Voca nomen ejus, id est filiæ tuæ, Absque misericordia, id est, tale nomen ei impone, quod significet misericordiæ abstractionem. Sic nempe vocata est filia ista, non quod ipsa fuerit expers divinæ clementiæ, sed quia per ejus appellationem præfigurabatur durissima atque longissima captivitas decem tribuum: sicut opposito modo Salomon dictus est Amabilis Domino, quoniam Dominus dilexit eum. Ideo subditur ratio impositionis hujus nominis:
paras.en: After God foretold the ending of the kingdom of the ten tribes, He now proclaims by words and deeds the long duration of their captivity and their final abandonment. [[1:6|And she conceived again|Et concepit]], that is, Gomer, by Osee, [[1:6|and bore a daughter|et peperit filiam]]. After Israel had been struck down and its kingdom overthrown, no longer a male but a female is born, so that by the weakness of the sex and a womanish spirit the infirmity of the people of Israel, and its childish heart that worshipped idols, might be declared. [[1:6|And he said to him|Et dixit Dominus ei]], namely to Osee: [[1:6|Call her name|Voca nomen ejus]], that is, the name of thy daughter, [[1:6|Without mercy|Absque misericordia]]: that is, give her a name that signifies the withdrawal of mercy. For this daughter was so called, not because she herself was without the divine clemency, but because by her name was prefigured the most harsh and most long captivity of the ten tribes; just as, in the opposite way, Solomon was called [[2 Kings 12:25|Amiable to the Lord|Amabilis Domino]], because the Lord loved him. Therefore the reason for giving this name is added:

paras.t: Quia non addam ultra misereri domui Israel, id est, populo decem tribuum non parcam de cetero, sicut peperci hucusque. Hoc ideo dicitur, non quod Deus misericordiam suam prorsus populo huic subtraxit (quum in omni opere Dei misericordia et justitia commisceantur, puniatque etiam in inferno citra condignum: propter quod ait Psalmista, Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas), sed ideo hoc dictum est, quoniam Deus ultra non distulit captivitatem Israel, nec a regibus vastantibus eos eripuit, sed durissime permisit eos opprimi, occidi, captivari, transferri. Sicque in hac ultione divina justitia clarius resplenduit, quam misericordia. Sed oblivione oblivisci eorum. Per hanc ingeminationem insinuatur, quod populus iste vehementer relinquendus esset a Deo. Quamvis autem in incommutabili Deo non cadat oblivio, nec aliquid ei ignotum sit, dicitur tamen hominum oblivisci, dum misericordiam suam eis non exhibet, nec solitam gratiam beneficiaque impendit; sed ita se habet ad eos, quasi nequaquam cognosceret ipsos, vel sicut se habet homo ad eum quem penitus non agnoscit. Econtrario dicitur hominum recordari, quando misericorditer auxiliatur gratioseque adest. Hinc ait Psalmista, In memoria æterna erit justus; et Salomon in Proverbiis, Nomen impiorum putrescet.
paras.en: [[1:6|for I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel|Quia non addam ultra misereri domui Israel]]: that is, I will not spare the people of the ten tribes henceforth, as I have spared them until now. This is said, not because God withdrew His mercy altogether from this people (since in every work of God mercy and justice are mingled, and He punishes even in hell less than is deserved [that is, short of what the sin strictly merits]; wherefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]]), but it is said because God no longer put off the captivity of Israel, nor rescued them from the kings who laid them waste, but permitted them most harshly to be oppressed, slain, taken captive and carried away. And so in this vengeance the divine justice shone forth more clearly than mercy. [[1:6|but I will utterly forget them|Sed oblivione oblivisci eorum]] [literally "I will forget them with forgetting"; the printed text has *oblivisci*, "to forget", for the Vulgate's *obliviscar*]. By this doubling it is suggested that this people was to be utterly forsaken by God. Now although forgetfulness has no place in the unchangeable God, and nothing is unknown to Him, yet He is said to forget men when He does not show them His mercy, nor bestow His wonted grace and benefits, but behaves towards them as though He did not know them at all, or as a man behaves towards one whom he does not know at all. On the contrary, He is said to remember men when He helps them mercifully and is graciously present. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 111:7|The just shall be in everlasting remembrance|In memoria æterna erit justus]]; and Solomon in the Proverbs: [[Prov 10:7|the name of the wicked shall rot|Nomen impiorum putrescet]].

paras.t: Quæritur, quomodo verum est quod Dominus ait nunc, Non addam ultra misereri domui Israel, quum infra dicatur, Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum. Dicendum, quod verbis prædictis non denegatur conversio populi hujus circa finem mundi, quando juxta Apostolum, plenitudine gentium ingressa, omnis Israel salvus erit, detecta per Eliam Antichristi perfidia. Unde per verba inducta designatur diuturnitas, non omnimoda perpetuitas abjectionis populi Israel.
paras.en: It is asked how what the Lord now says is true, [[1:6|I will not add any more to have mercy on the house of Israel|Non addam ultra misereri domui Israel]], since below it is said: [[Osee 3:5|after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God|Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum]]. The answer is that the words above do not deny the conversion of this people about the end of the world, when, according to the Apostle, [[Rom 11:25|the fulness of the Gentiles should come in|plenitudine gentium ingressa]], and [[Rom 11:26|all Israel should be saved|omnis Israel salvus erit]], once the treachery of Antichrist has been laid bare by Elias[[Matt 17:11||]]. Hence the words quoted signify the long duration, not the utter perpetuity, of the casting off of the people of Israel.

paras.t: Et domui, id est regno et populo, Juda, id est tribus Juda: per quam denotantur et aliæ duæ tribus, videlicet Levi et Benjamin, sicut jam patuit; miserebor, liberando eos tempore Ezechiæ a Sennacherib rege Assyriorum. Alia quoque diversa bona spiritualia ac temporalia præstitit Deus regibus, sacerdotibus, ac populo huic tempore Osee prophetæ, regnantibus Ozia, Joathan et Ezechia, quamvis tempore Achaz maximas miserias passi sint. Quamvis autem in Scripturis [designetur] frequenter nomine Israel, totus populus de Jacob, qui dictus est Israel, generatus; tamen ab eo tempore, quo sub filio Salomonis decem tribus recesserunt a domo David, per Israel designatæ sunt communiter decem tribus propter earum multitudinem.
paras.en: [[1:7|And|Et]] [[1:7|on the house|domui]], that is, on the kingdom and people, [[1:7|of Juda|Juda]], that is, of the tribe of Juda (by which the other two tribes also are meant, namely Levi and Benjamin, as has already appeared), [[1:7|I will have mercy|miserebor]], by delivering them in the time of Ezechias from Sennacherib king of the Assyrians[[4 Kings 19:35||]]. God also bestowed various other goods, spiritual and temporal, on the kings, priests and people of this nation in the time of the prophet Osee, under the reigns of Ozias, Joathan and Ezechias, although in the time of Achaz they suffered very great miseries. Now although in the Scriptures the name Israel often signifies the whole people begotten of Jacob, who was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]][[Gen 35:10||]], yet from the time when, under the son of Solomon, the ten tribes withdrew from the house of David[[3 Kings 12:19||]], the ten tribes have commonly been signified by Israel, because of their great number.

paras.t: Et salvabo eos in Domino Deo suo, id est, in me ipso, seu Filio meo unigenito, vel propria vel divina virtute liberabo regnum Juda ab impugnatione Sennacherib. His verbis innuitur pluralitas Personarum in Deo, quum Dominus ait de Domino: Salvabo eos in Domino Deo suo. Juxta quem modum loquendi scriptum est in Genesi: Dominus pluit super Sodomam et Gomorrham ignem et sulfur a Domino. Estque iste modus loquendi frequens in veteri Testamento, rarus autem in novo, quamvis quandoque inveniatur in eo, ut quum dicit Apostolus: Det illi Dominus misericordiam invenire a Domino in die illa.
paras.en: [[1:7|and I will save them by the Lord, their God|Et salvabo eos in Domino Deo suo]]: that is, in Myself, or in My only-begotten Son; by My own, that is, by divine power I will deliver the kingdom of Juda from the assault of Sennacherib. In these words the plurality of Persons in God is hinted at, since the Lord says of the Lord: [[1:7|I will save them by the Lord, their God|salvabo eos in Domino Deo suo]]. In the same manner of speaking it is written in Genesis: [[Gen 19:24|the Lord rained upon Sodom and Gomorrha brimstone and fire from the Lord|Dominus pluit super Sodomam et Gomorrham ignem et sulfur a Domino]]. And this manner of speaking is frequent in the Old Testament, but rare in the New, though it is found there sometimes, as when the Apostle says: [[2 Tim 1:18|The Lord grant unto him to find mercy of the Lord in that day|Det illi Dominus misericordiam invenire a Domino in die illa]].

paras.t: Et non salvabo eos in arcu et gladio et in bello, id est virtute armorum et prælii. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Non enim in arcu meo sperabo, et gladius meus non salvabit me. Et in equis et in equitibus, id est, non in robore aut multitudine equorum atque equestrium eos salvabo: quia, ut legitur quarto Regum, angelus Domini percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia virorum. Sicque per manum angeli Judæi salvati sunt a rege Assyriorum: quam salvationem fecit angelus divino nutu atque imperio, ideo principaliter Deo adscribitur. Hinc Salomon loquitur: Equus paratur ad diem belli, Dominus autem salutem tribuet. Et alibi legitur: Non in multitudine exercitus, sed de cælo victoria est.
paras.en: [[1:7|and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle|Et non salvabo eos in arcu et gladio et in bello]]: that is, by the strength of arms and of fighting. Wherefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 43:7|For I will not trust in my bow: neither shall my sword save me|Non enim in arcu meo sperabo, et gladius meus non salvabit me]]. [[1:7|nor by horses, nor by horsemen|Et in equis et in equitibus]]: that is, I will not save them by the strength or number of horses and horsemen; for, as we read in the fourth book of Kings, [[4 Kings 19:35|an angel of the Lord came, and slew in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand|angelus Domini percussit in castris Assyriorum centum octoginta quinque millia]] men. And so by the hand of an angel the Jews were saved from the king of the Assyrians; and because the angel wrought this deliverance at the divine bidding and command, it is ascribed chiefly to God. Hence Solomon says: [[Prov 21:31|The horse is prepared for the day of battle: but the Lord giveth safety|Equus paratur ad diem belli, Dominus autem salutem tribuet]]. And elsewhere we read: [[1 Mach 3:19|not in the multitude of the army, but strength cometh from heaven|Non in multitudine exercitus, sed de cælo victoria est]] [Denis's wording: "not in the multitude of the army, but from heaven is the victory"].

paras.t: Denique Deus spiritualiter salvavit multos de regno Juda in se ipso tanquam in fonte et fine beatitudinis universæ, quia in regno Juda tempore præfatorum regum, multi justi fuerunt. De qua salute Isaias professus est: Israel salvatus est in Domino salute æterna. Salvavit quoque Dominus domum Juda, quoniam licet permisit eos tempore Sedeciæ capi, et in Babylonem perduci, tamen post septuaginta annos de licentia Cyri regis Persarum, in Judæam reversi sunt.
paras.en: Lastly, God saved many of the kingdom of Juda spiritually in Himself, as in the source and end of all beatitude, for in the kingdom of Juda in the time of the aforesaid kings there were many just men. Of this salvation Isaias declared: [[Is 45:17|Israel is saved in the Lord with an eternal salvation|Israel salvatus est in Domino salute æterna]]. The Lord also saved the house of Juda in that, though He permitted them in the time of Sedecias to be taken and led away to Babylon[[4 Kings 25:7||]] [the margin gives IV Reg. xxv, 24; the carrying away of Sedecias to Babylon is told at 4 Kings 25:7, 11], yet after seventy years, by leave of Cyrus king of the Persians, they returned into Judæa[[1 Esd 1:2||]][[1 Esd 1:3||]] [the margin gives I Esdr. i, 2–5].

paras.t: Et ablactavit Gomer eam quæ erat Absque misericordia, id est filiam suam vocatam Absque misericordia, amovit a lacte. Per quod prophetice notabatur, quod populus decem tribuum divina consolatione privaretur, nec proprio cibo in terra paterna aleretur, sed cibis externis, videlicet idololatriis, in terra captivitatis vesceretur.
paras.en: [[1:8|And she weaned her that was called Without mercy|Et ablactavit Gomer eam quæ erat Absque misericordia]]: that is, Gomer took from the milk her daughter called Without mercy. By this it was prophetically signified that the people of the ten tribes would be deprived of the divine consolation, and would not be nourished with their own food in their fathers' land, but would feed on foreign foods, namely idolatries, in the land of their captivity.

paras.t: Et concepit Gomer tertium fetum, et peperit ei, puta Osee marito suo, filium. Et dixit Deus ad Osee: Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus, id est, hunc filium tuum nomina tali vocabulo quod designet, Non populus meus. Quamvis autem nomina ista, in Latino complexa sunt, in Hebræo tamen incomplexa fuisse reputantur. Causa demum hujus appellationis subjungitur, quum Dominus ait: quia vos, o Judæi, estis non populus meus per prædestinationem et gratiam, quamvis sitis populus meus per creationem et providentiam generalem; et ego non ero vester Deus per cultum devotum seu gratiosam ac piam inhabitationem, ita quod non colatis me reverenter et caritative, sed in infidelitate et perversitate vestra manebitis. Deus quippe universorum, proprie fertur Deus eorum qui eum super omnia amant, et colunt ut Deum. Istud, ut Haymo dicit, referri potest ad Judæos tempore Osee captos, vel ad eos qui erant in primo Salvatoris adventu, et Christum negantes, coram præside conclamabant: Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum; et item, Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem. De quibus in Daniele erat prædictum: Non erit ejus populus, qui eum negaturus est. Unde et super eos pervenit ira Dei usque in finem, secundum Apostolum; perdideruntque locum et gentem, et dicuntur filii, non Dei, sed dæmonis. Qui enim non credit in Filium, nec Patrem habet. Propter quod audiunt a Salvatore: Vos ex patre diabolo estis.
paras.en: [[1:8|And she conceived|Et concepit]], that is, Gomer, a third offspring, [[1:8|and bore|et peperit]] him, namely Osee her husband, [[1:8|a son|filium]]. [[1:9|And he said|Et dixit]], that is, God, to Osee: [[1:9|Call his name, Not my people|Voca nomen ejus, Non populus meus]]: that is, name this son of thine with a word that signifies "Not my people". Now although in Latin these names are compound [that is, phrases of several words], in Hebrew they are thought to have been simple. Lastly the reason for this name is added, when the Lord says: [[1:9|for you are not my people|quia vos non populus meus]], O Jews, by predestination and grace, although you are My people by creation and general providence; [[1:9|and I will not be yours|et ego non ero vester]] (your God, Denis adds) by devout worship or by a gracious and loving indwelling, so that you will not worship Me with reverence and charity, but will remain in your unbelief and perversity. For the God of all things is properly called the God of those who love Him above all things and worship Him as God. This, as Haymo says, can be referred to the Jews taken captive in the time of Osee, or to those who were there at the Saviour's first coming and, denying Christ, cried out before the governor: [[John 19:15|Away with him: Away with him: Crucify him|Tolle, tolle, crucifige eum]]; and again: [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]]. Of these it had been foretold in Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Non erit ejus populus, qui eum negaturus est]]. Hence also, according to the Apostle, [[1 Thess 2:16|the wrath of God is come upon them to the end|pervenit ira Dei usque in finem]]; and they lost both place and nation, and are called sons not of God but of the devil. For he who believes not in the Son, [[1 John 2:23|the same hath not the Father|nec Patrem habet]] [Denis's wording; the Vulgate has "Whosoever denieth the Son"]. Wherefore they hear from the Saviour: [[John 8:44|You are of your father the devil|Vos ex patre diabolo estis]].

paras.t: Et erit numerus filiorum Israel quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est, et non numerabitur. Et erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis. Quidam hoc loco incipiunt secundum capitulum, quidam vero loco sequenti, quo dicitur: Dicite fratribus vestris. Porro litteram istam diversi variis modis exponunt, quemadmodum breviter tangam.
paras.en: [[1:10|And the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, that is without measure, and shall not be numbered. And it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God|Et erit numerus filiorum Israel quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est, et non numerabitur. Et erit in loco ubi dicetur eis, Non populus meus vos; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis]]. Some begin the second chapter at this place, others at the following place, where it is said: [[Osee 2:1|Say ye to your brethren|Dicite fratribus vestris]]. Now different writers expound this text in various ways, as I shall briefly touch on.

paras.t: Et erit numerus filiorum Israel, id est, populus Judæorum multus erit, quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est quantitatis discretæ, id est sine numero hominibus cognito. Ideo sequitur: et non numerabitur præ multitudine. Absolute tamen loquendo, non est in creaturis aliquid actualiter infinitum, nec in magnitudine, nec in multitudine, nec in perfectione. Deus namque gloriosus et sapiens, in numero, pondere et mensura universa constituit. Sic filii Israel præ multitudine nequeunt numerari: quod aliqui dicunt impletum in Judæis ab Assyriis captivatis; aliqui vero, in Judæis qui usque in præsens sub Romano imperio capti tenentur. Quidam autem referunt ad Judæos a Babylone reversos in propriam terram, qui per successum temporis multiplicati sunt vehementer. Nonnulli referunt ad eos qui circa finem sæculi erunt, veniente Elia.
paras.en: [[1:10|And the number of the children of Israel|Et erit numerus filiorum Israel]]: that is, the people of the Jews shall be many, [[1:10|as the sand of the sea, that is without measure|quasi arena maris, quæ sine mensura est]] of discrete quantity [that is, of number, as opposed to continuous magnitude], that is, without a number known to men. Therefore there follows: [[1:10|and shall not be numbered|et non numerabitur]], for their multitude. Yet, speaking absolutely, there is nothing actually infinite among creatures, either in size, or in number, or in perfection; for the glorious and wise God has established all things in number, weight and measure[[Wis 11:21||]]. Thus the children of Israel cannot be numbered for their multitude; which some say was fulfilled in the Jews taken captive by the Assyrians; others, in the Jews who to this day are held captive under the Roman empire. Some, again, refer it to the Jews who returned from Babylon to their own land, who in the course of time multiplied exceedingly. Some refer it to those who will be about the end of the world, when Elias comes.

paras.t: Secundum hanc diversitatem, etiam quæ sequuntur, diversimode explanantur. Subditur enim: Et erit, id est, continget quod sequitur: in loco, id est in Jerusalem et locis vicinis, ubi dicetur eis, id est ubi Deus per Prophetas dixit Judæis, Non populus meus estis vos, quando coluistis idola: hoc enim per Jeremiam sæpe dixit Dominus populo huic; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis estis: id est, ibi post conversionem suam vocabuntur filii adoptivi Dei vivi ac veri, a quo fontaliter profluit omnis vita naturæ, vita gratiæ, vitaque gloriæ. Christo enim incarnato, et inter Judæos conversante ac prædicante, multi crediderunt in eum, multoque plures post Paracleti missionem a Christi Apostolis sunt conversi. Alii per locum istum intelligunt totum orbem, in quo Judæi dispersi sunt, et jam multi eorum ad Christum conversi sunt.
