paras.en: Since a man is punished by the same things by which he sins[[Wis 11:17||]], the Lord therefore adds: [[2:10|And now|Et nunc]], that is, in the time of the Babylonian captivity, [[2:10|I will lay open her folly|revelabo stultitiam ejus]], that is, I will make manifest the error, or idolatry, or idol of the Synagogue, [[2:10|in the eyes of her lovers|in oculis amatorum ejus]], that is, to the Chaldeans or the Egyptians, with whom the Jews at one time had friendship. For when the Chaldeans, having overcome Jerusalem, entered the temple, they saw how the Jews had worshipped idols in the temple, and how foolishly they had been deceived in trusting in the Egyptians. The Egyptians too perceived these things, and so they were made manifest in their mind's eyes. [[2:10|and no man shall deliver her out of my hand|Et vir non eruet eam de manu mea]], that is, no one will be able to free the Jews from the vengeance or power which I shall exercise upon them by the hands of the Chaldeans. For no one can resist God[[Esth 13:9||]], as it is written in Job: [[Job 23:13|he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought|Deus solus est, et cogitationem ejus nemo avertere potest]]; [[Job 23:13|and whatsoever his soul hath desired, that hath he done|et anima ejus quodcumque voluit, fecit]].

paras.t: Et cessare faciam omne gaudium ejus, id est, destruendo templum atque Jerusalem, populum quoque fame, peste et gladio occidendo, imponam finem lætitiæ Judæorum ad tempus. In maxima enim tribulatione fuerunt Judæi, quum a Chaldæis obsiderentur, ita quod nec in spiritualibus, nec in carnalibus delectabantur. Unde ab Isaia dictum est : Erit pro suavi odore fœtor, et pro crispante crine calvitium. Et Threnorum ultimo : Defecit gaudium cordis nostri, versus est in luctum chorus noster. Faciam quoque cessare solennitatem ejus, id est festa Judæorum, ut ponatur singulare pro plurali. Vel per solennitatem, secundum Bedam, intelligitur paschalis festivitas, tanquam solennior, quæ fiebat in commemorationem liberationis eorum de terra Ægypti. Frequenter autem Scriptura utitur singulari pro plurali, et econtra, quemadmodum in Exodo Dominus ait Pharaoni : Dimitte filium meum, ut sacrificet mihi in deserto. Per filium namque intelligit universos filios Israel.
paras.en: [[2:11|And I will cause all her mirth to cease|Et cessare faciam omne gaudium ejus]], that is, by destroying the temple and Jerusalem, and by slaying the people with famine, pestilence and the sword, I will put an end to the gladness of the Jews for a time. For the Jews were in the greatest tribulation when they were besieged by the Chaldeans, so that they took delight neither in spiritual things nor in carnal. Hence it was said by Isaias: [[Is 3:24|instead of a sweet smell there shall be stench|Erit pro suavi odore fœtor]], [[Is 3:24|and instead of curled hair, baldness|et pro crispante crine calvitium]]. And in the last chapter of Lamentations: [[Lam 5:15|The joy of our heart is ceased, our dancing is turned into mourning.|Defecit gaudium cordis nostri, versus est in luctum chorus noster]] I will also cause to cease [[2:11|her solemnities|solennitatem ejus]], that is, the feasts of the Jews, the singular being put for the plural [the Latin has *solennitatem*, “solemnity”, in the singular]. Or by the solemnity, according to Bede, is understood the paschal festival, as being the more solemn, which was kept in commemoration of their deliverance from the land of Egypt. Now Scripture often uses the singular for the plural, and the reverse, as in Exodus the Lord says to Pharao: [[Ex 4:23|Let my son go|Dimitte filium meum]], [[Ex 5:1|that they may sacrifice to me in the desert|ut sacrificet mihi in deserto]] [the margin gives Exod. iv, 23; v, 1, etc.: Denis joins the two verses, and has “that he may sacrifice”]. For by the son he means all the children of Israel.

paras.t: Deinde ponuntur festa Judæorum in speciali : Neomeniam ejus, id est festivitatem Calendarum, quæ fiebant tempore innovationis lunæ, seu in principio mensium. Sabbatum ejus, id est festivitatem septimæ diei, in qua Judæi epulis otiisque vacabant, secundum Glossam. Fiebatque ista solennitas in memoriam creationis mundi, quoniam septimo die requievit Deus ab omni opere quod patrarat. Et omnia festa temporum ejus, id est solennitates quæ fiebant semel in anno, videlicet Paschæ, Pentecostes, et Tabernaculorum, ac Dedicationis. Eamdem enim Dedicationem non celebrabant nisi semel in anno, quamvis quolibet anno plures celebraverunt Dedicationes.
paras.en: Then the feasts of the Jews are set down in particular: [[2:11|her new moons|Neomeniam ejus]], that is, the festival of the Calends, which were kept at the time of the renewal of the moon, or at the beginning of the months. [[2:11|her sabbaths|Sabbatum ejus]], that is, the festival of the seventh day, on which the Jews gave themselves to feasting and rest, according to the Gloss. And this solemnity was kept in memory of the creation of the world, since [[Gen 2:2|he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done|septimo die requievit Deus ab omni opere quod patrarat]]. [[2:11|and all her festival times|Et omnia festa temporum ejus]], that is, the solemnities that were kept once a year, namely those of the Pasch, of Pentecost, of Tabernacles and of the Dedication. For they kept the same Dedication only once a year, though in any year they celebrated several Dedications.

paras.t: Hæc omnia fecit Deus cessare in populo Judæorum, quando a Chaldæis capti, occisi, vel translati fuerunt. Propter quod scriptum est : Viæ Sion lugent, eo quod non sint qui veniant ad solennitatem. Hinc in Isaia loquitur Dominus : Solennitates vestras odivit anima mea.
paras.en: All these things God caused to cease among the Jewish people when they were taken, slain or carried away by the Chaldeans. Wherefore it is written: [[Lam 1:4|The ways of Sion mourn, because there are none that come to the solemn feast|Viæ Sion lugent, eo quod non sint qui veniant ad solennitatem]]. Hence the Lord speaks in Isaias: [[Is 1:14|your solemnities|Solennitates vestras]] [[Is 1:14|My soul hateth|odivit anima mea]].

paras.t: Denique, secundum Thomam in prima secundæ, in veteri Testamento erant septem festivitates temporales, id est, quæ certis diebus anni celebrabantur. Prima erat Sabbati, in memoriam beneficii creationis mundi, ut dictum est. Secunda fuit Neomeniæ, in primo cujuslibet mensis, in memoriam gubernationis rerum a Deo, et quoniam inferiora secundum cursum lunæ mutantur, a qua mensis nomen accepit, juxta illud Ecclesiastici : Luna ostensio temporis, et signum ævi ; mensis secundum nomen ejus. Idcirco fiebat ista solennitas in principio cujuslibet lunationis seu lunæ, non in plenitudine ejus. Quod item fiebat propter idololatriæ exclusionem, quia gentiles in plenilunio sacrificabant. Et quoniam hæc duo beneficia Dei, scilicet creationis et gubernationis, communia sunt cunctis hominibus, festa hæc frequenter in anno iterabantur. Alia quinque festa celebrabantur semel in anno, in memoriam beneficiorum specialiter collatorum populo Israel. Quorum primum fuit solennitas Paschæ, de qua prætactum est. Et post quinquaginta dies sequebatur solennitas Pentecostes, in memoriam beneficii legis datæ. Alia vero tria festa servabantur septimo mense, qui apud Judæos quasi totus celebris fuit. Nam primo die hujus mensis erat festum Tubarum, in memoriam liberationis Isaac. Unde tunc cornibus buccinabant, quoniam Abraham vidit arietem cornibus hærentem vepribus, quem immolavit pro Isaac. Erat quoque festum Tubarum, in quo invitabantur Judæi ad solennitatem Expiationis, quæ decima die septimi mensis fiebat in memoriam beneficii quo Deus ad preces Moysis propitiabatur eis de adoratione vituli aurei atque conflatilis. Post hæc celebrabatur solennitas Scenopegiæ seu Tabernaculorum, septem diebus, in memoriam protectionis ac deductionis eorum in deserto. Unde tunc afferebant fructus arboris pulcherrimæ. Porro in die octava fuit festum Cœtus atque collectæ, quando colligebantur a populo necessaria ad divini cultus expensas. — Denique, per sabbatum, figurabatur spiritualis requies nobis collata per Christum ; per Neomeniam, quæ est novæ lunæ incensio, figurabatur primitivæ Ecclesiæ illuminatio ; per festum Tubarum, prædicatio Apostolorum ; per festum Expiationis, emundatio Christianorum a vitiis ; per festum Tabernaculorum, peregrinatio Christianorum in hoc mundo exsulantium : per festum autem Cœtus atque collectæ, congregatio electorum in regno cœlesti : unde hoc festum dicebatur sanctissimum. De his festis loquitur Moyses in Numeris. — Erat præterea in veteri Testamento una festivitas velut continua, qua immolabatur quotidie agnus mane et vespere. Per quam repræsentabatur perpetuitas felicitatis futuræ. Hinc secundum Glossam, prædicta festa Judæis ablata, a fidelibus spiritualiter celebrantur.
paras.en: Further, according to Thomas in the *Prima Secundæ* [the first part of the second part of the *Summa Theologiæ*; see I-II, q. 102, a. 4, ad 10], in the Old Testament there were seven temporal festivals, that is, festivals kept on fixed days of the year. The first was the Sabbath, in memory of the benefit of the creation of the world, as has been said. The second was the New Moon, on the first day of each month, in memory of God's government of things, and because things here below change according to the course of the moon, from which the month took its name, according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 43:6|the moon|Luna]] [[Ecclus 43:6|is for a declaration of times and a sign of the world|ostensio temporis, et signum ævi]]; [[Ecclus 43:8|The month is called after her name|mensis secundum nomen ejus]]. Therefore this solemnity was kept at the beginning of each lunation or moon, not at its full. This was done also to shut out idolatry, because the gentiles sacrificed at the full moon. And since these two benefits of God, namely creation and government, are common to all men, these feasts were repeated often in the year. The other five feasts were kept once a year, in memory of benefits bestowed in particular on the people of Israel. The first of these was the solemnity of the Pasch, which has been touched on above. And fifty days after followed the solemnity of Pentecost, in memory of the benefit of the giving of the law. The other three feasts were kept in the seventh month, which among the Jews was almost wholly festal. For on the first day of this month was the feast of Trumpets, in memory of the deliverance of Isaac. Hence they then blew on horns, because Abraham saw a ram caught by its horns in the briers, which he offered up in place of Isaac[[Gen 22:13||]]. The feast of Trumpets was also that in which the Jews were summoned to the solemnity of the Expiation, which was kept on the tenth day of the seventh month in memory of the benefit by which God, at the prayers of Moses, was propitiated towards them for their adoration of the golden and molten calf[[Ex 32:14||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxxii, 7-14]. After these the solemnity of the Scenopegia or Tabernacles was kept for seven days, in memory of God's protecting them and leading them in the desert. Hence they then brought [[Lev 23:40|the fruits of the fairest tree|fructus arboris pulcherrimæ]]. And on the eighth day was the feast of Assembly and Congregation[[Lev 23:36||]], when the things needed for the expenses of divine worship were collected from the people. Lastly, by the Sabbath was figured the spiritual rest bestowed on us through Christ; by the New Moon, which is the kindling of the new moon, the enlightening of the primitive Church; by the feast of Trumpets, the preaching of the Apostles; by the feast of the Expiation, the cleansing of Christians from vices; by the feast of Tabernacles, the pilgrimage of Christians living in exile in this world; and by the feast of Assembly and Congregation, the gathering of the elect in the heavenly kingdom: hence this feast was called most holy. Moses speaks of these feasts in Numbers[[Num 28:1||]][[Num 29:1||]]. There was moreover in the Old Testament one festival that was as it were continual, in which a lamb was offered every day, morning and evening[[Ex 29:38||]][[Ex 29:39||]][[Num 28:3||]][[Num 28:4||]]. By it was represented the perpetuity of the happiness to come. Hence, according to the Gloss, the aforesaid feasts, taken away from the Jews, are celebrated spiritually by the faithful.

paras.t: Et corrumpam vineam ejus et ficum ejus, id est, vites et ficus ceterasque fructiferas Judæorum arbores destruam grandine, ariditate et gelu, vel per manus Chaldæorum, qui talia destruxerunt, vastando Judæam ; de quibus vineis et ficu, dixit : Mercedes hæ, meæ sunt, id est, bona ista sunt mihi pro præmio data, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei, id est dii gentium quos colui. Omnia enim mobilia atque immobilia bona sua, putabant Judæi idololatræ sibi ab idolis condonari, sicque beneficia Dei idolis adscripserunt.
paras.en: [[2:12|And I will destroy her vines, and her fig trees|Et corrumpam vineam ejus et ficum ejus]], that is, I will destroy the vines and fig trees and the other fruit-bearing trees of the Jews by hail, drought and frost, or by the hands of the Chaldeans, who destroyed such things in laying waste Judea; [[2:12|of which she said|dixit]] of these vines and fig tree: [[2:12|These are my rewards|Mercedes hæ, meæ sunt]], that is, these good things are given me as a reward, [[2:12|which my lovers have given me|quas dederunt mihi amatores mei]], that is, the gods of the gentiles whom I have worshipped. For the idolatrous Jews thought that all their goods, movable and immovable, were bestowed on them by the idols, and so they ascribed God's benefits to idols.

paras.t: Et ponam eam in saltum. Saltus vocatur multitudo arborum infructuosarum. Est itaque sensus, quod Synagoga comparabitur saltui seu infructuosis arboribus, amittendo fructus Spiritus Sancti, imo omnibus bonis spoliata, sterilis facta, in solitudinemque redacta. Hoc fuit impletum, dum a Chaldæis vehementissime opprimebantur Judæi, ita quod Jeremias prædixit : Terra sabbatizavit sabbata sua.
paras.en: [[2:12|and I will make her as a forest|Et ponam eam in saltum]]. A multitude of unfruitful trees is called a forest. So the sense is that the Synagogue will be likened to a forest or to unfruitful trees, losing the fruits of the Holy Ghost, nay, stripped of all good things, made barren and reduced to a wilderness. This was fulfilled when the Jews were most grievously oppressed by the Chaldeans, so that, as Jeremias foretold, [[2 Par 36:21|the land might keep her sabbaths|Terra sabbatizavit sabbata sua]] [Denis has “the land hath kept its sabbaths”].

paras.t: Et comedet eam bestia agri. Per bestiam istam, intelligi potest incultus atque crudelis exercitus Chaldæorum, vel Nabuchodonosor rex eorum, qui (ut Daniel recolit) versus in amentiam, fœnum ut bos comedit, eratque cum bestiis habitatio ejus. Unde Jeremias ait : Primus Assur comedit eum ; iste novissimus Nabuchodonosor exossavit eum, scilicet populum Judæorum. Hæc igitur bestia comedit, id est, occidit ac minuit Synagogam. Quidam per bestiam agri, intelligunt principem vel exercitum Romanorum, qui finaliter dejecit Judæos : de quo exponunt Judæi illud in Psalmo, Exterminavit eam aper de silva. Potest quoque nomine bestiæ dæmon intelligi, qui spiritualiter devoravit Judæos, inducendo eos ad vitia idololatriæ ceteraque peccata. De quo in Apocalypsi legitur : Projectus est draco ille magnus. Unde et alibi scriptum est : Ne tradas bestiis animam confitentem tibi.
paras.en: [[2:12|and the beasts of the field shall devour her|Et comedet eam bestia agri]]. By this beast may be understood the rude and cruel army of the Chaldeans, or Nabuchodonosor their king, who (as Daniel relates) was turned to madness, [[Dan 4:30|did eat grass, like an ox|fœnum ut bos comedit]], and his dwelling was with the beasts. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 50:17|first the king of Assyria devoured him|Primus Assur comedit eum]]; [[Jer 50:17|and last this Nabuchodonosor|iste novissimus Nabuchodonosor]] [[Jer 50:17|hath broken his bones|exossavit eum]], namely the Jewish people. This beast, then, devoured, that is, slew and diminished, the Synagogue. Some understand by the beast of the field the prince or the army of the Romans, who in the end cast down the Jews; of whom the Jews expound that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 79:14|The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste|Exterminavit eam aper de silva]]. By the name of beast the devil may also be understood, who devoured the Jews spiritually, leading them into the vices of idolatry and other sins. Of whom we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 12:9|that great dragon was cast out|Projectus est draco ille magnus]]. Hence it is also written elsewhere: [[Ps 73:19|Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee|Ne tradas bestiis animam confitentem tibi]] [Denis has the singular, “the soul that confesseth to thee”].

paras.t: Et visitabo super eam dies Baalim, id est, peccata et idololatriam, quæ commisit Synagoga tempore quo idolis Baal servivit, ulciscar per exercitum Chaldæorum. Baalim est pluralis numeri, significatque pluraliter, quod Baal singulariter. Solet autem diei seu temporis attribui, id quod attribuitur his quæ sunt vel fiunt in tempore. Unde Salvator, Sufficit (inquit) diei malitia sua ; et ibidem, Crastinus dies sollicitus erit sibi ; Apostolus quoque, Redimentes tempus, quoniam dies mali sunt. Sic modo dies visitari dicuntur, id est peccata dierum puniri. Porro visitatio quandoque in bono accipitur, scilicet pro gratioso vel pio affectu Dei, ut quum ait Psalmista, Respice de cœlo, et vide, et visita vineam istam ; quandoque in malo, videlicet pro justa punitione, quemadmodum Jeremiæ Dominus loquitur : Numquid super his non visitabo, et in gente tali non ulciscetur anima mea? Sic quoque accipitur nunc.
paras.en: [[2:13|And I will visit upon her the days of Baalim|Et visitabo super eam dies Baalim]], that is, the sins and idolatry which the Synagogue committed in the time when it served the idols of Baal I will avenge by the army of the Chaldeans. *Baalim* is of the plural number, and signifies in the plural what *Baal* signifies in the singular. Now what is attributed to the things that are or are done in time is commonly attributed to the day or the time. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:34|Sufficient for the day|Sufficit]] [[Matt 6:34|is the evil thereof|diei malitia sua]]; and in the same place: [[Matt 6:34|the morrow will be solicitous for itself|Crastinus dies sollicitus erit sibi]]; and the Apostle also: [[Eph 5:16|redeeming the time, because the days are evil|Redimentes tempus, quoniam dies mali sunt]]. So here the days are said to be visited, that is, the sins of the days to be punished. Further, visitation is sometimes taken in a good sense, namely for the gracious or loving affection of God, as when the Psalmist says: [[Ps 79:15|look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard|Respice de cœlo, et vide, et visita vineam istam]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxix, 15; the verse is Ps 79:15]; and sometimes in a bad sense, namely for just punishment, as the Lord speaks to Jeremias: [[Jer 5:9|Shall I not visit for these things|Numquid super his non visitabo]], [[Jer 5:9|and shall not my soul take revenge on such a nation?|et in gente tali non ulciscetur anima mea?]] And so it is taken here.

paras.t: Quibus diebus seu idolis accendebat incensum, id est thymiama, tanquam aliquid divinitatis haberent, et honorem Deo debitum ad falsos transtulit deos, et ornabatur inaure sua et monili suo, id est inauribus seu ornamentis ad aures pendentibus, ac ceteris decoramentis, ad honorem deorum suorum : sicut fideles in festis ornant se ad honorem Dei atque Sanctorum ; et ibat post amatores suos, id est, idolis suis, a quibus se putavit ditari, amari et gubernari, adhæsit corporaliter, quia ad loca certa idololatriæ deputata processit. Propter quod Dominus ait per Ezechielem Judæis idololatris : Quid est excelsum istud, ad quod vos ingredimini? In locis enim sublimibus idolis sacrificabant frequenter. Et mei obliviscebatur, dicit Dominus. Nam vero Deo relicto, deos gentium coluerunt.
paras.en: [[2:13|to whom|Quibus]] days or idols [[2:13|she burnt incense|accendebat incensum]], that is, thymiama [that is, sweet-smelling incense], as though they had something of divinity, and she transferred the honour due to God to false gods, [[2:13|and decked herself out with her earrings, and with her jewels|et ornabatur inaure sua et monili suo]], that is, with earrings or ornaments hanging from the ears, and with other adornments, in honour of her gods, as the faithful adorn themselves on feast days in honour of God and of the Saints; [[2:13|and went after her lovers|et ibat post amatores suos]], that is, she cleaved bodily to her idols, by which she thought herself enriched, loved and governed, because she went to fixed places set apart for idolatry. Wherefore the Lord says by Ezechiel to the idolatrous Jews: [[Ezech 20:29|What meaneth the high place to which you go?|Quid est excelsum istud, ad quod vos ingredimini?]] For they often sacrificed to idols in high places. [[2:13|and forgot me, saith the Lord|Et mei obliviscebatur, dicit Dominus]]. For having forsaken the true God, they worshipped the gods of the gentiles.

paras.t: Sed quoniam Dominus non solum vulnerat, sed et medetur, et quum iratus fuerit, misericordiæ recordatur, juxta illud Tobiæ, Post tempestatem tranquillum facis, et post fletum exsultationem infundis; idcirco post verba comminationis, inducit Dominus verbum consolationis. Propter hoc, id est, quoniam tot mala pœnalia Synagogæ induxi, ecce ego lactabo eam, id est, blandiar ei, et consolationibus Spiritus Sancti eam implebo ; et ducam eam in solitudinem, id est, ab inquietudine et tumultu eam eripiam, atque ad loca contemplationi orationique apta, ipsam deducam; et loquar ad cor ejus, id est, verbis dulcibus, consolatoriis et amorosis alloquar eam. Per locutionem namque ad cor, designatur allocutio talis quemadmodum Booz loquebatur ad cor Ruth, et Sichem ad cor Dinæ. Vel, Loquar ad cor ejus, per revelationem secretorum cœlestium.
paras.en: But since the Lord not only [[Job 5:18|woundeth|vulnerat]] but also [[Job 5:18|cureth|medetur]], and when he is angry remembers mercy[[Hab 3:2||]], according to that saying of Tobias: [[Tob 3:22|after a storm thou makest a calm|Post tempestatem tranquillum facis]], [[Tob 3:22|and after tears and weeping thou pourest in joyfulness|et post fletum exsultationem infundis]]; therefore after the words of threatening the Lord brings in a word of consolation. [[2:14|Therefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because I have brought so many penal evils upon the Synagogue, [[2:14|behold I will allure her|ecce ego lactabo eam]], that is, I will speak tenderly to her and fill her with the consolations of the Holy Ghost [*lactabo* can also be heard as “I will give her milk”]; [[2:14|and will lead her into the wilderness|et ducam eam in solitudinem]], that is, I will snatch her from disquiet and tumult, and lead her to places fit for contemplation and prayer; [[2:14|and I will speak to her heart|et loquar ad cor ejus]], that is, I will address her with sweet, consoling and loving words. For by speaking to the heart is meant such an address as when Booz spoke to the heart of Ruth[[Ruth 2:13||]], and Sichem to the heart of Dina[[Gen 34:3||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxxiv, 2, 3]. Or, [[2:14|I will speak to her heart|Loquar ad cor ejus]] by the revelation of heavenly secrets.

paras.t: Istud secundum Hieronymum impletum est post Christi adventum, quando (ut Lucas narrat in Actibus) Ecclesia per totam Judæam et Galilæam habebat pacem, discipuli quoque replebantur gaudio et Spiritu Sancto. Hinc apud Isaiam Dominus dixit : Sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta. Quidam autem exponunt hæc de Judæis a captivitate Babylonica redeuntibus per desertum, alii vero de gentilitate per prædicationem Apostolorum conversa.
paras.en: This, according to Jerome, was fulfilled after the coming of Christ, when (as Luke relates in the Acts) [[Acts 9:31|the church had peace throughout all Judea and Galilee|Ecclesia per totam Judæam et Galilæam habebat pacem]], [[Acts 13:52|and the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Ghost|discipuli quoque replebantur gaudio et Spiritu Sancto]]. Hence the Lord said in Isaias: [[Is 32:18|my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest|Sedebit populus meus in pulchritudine pacis et in tabernaculis fiduciæ, et in requie opulenta]]. Some, however, expound these words of the Jews returning through the desert from the Babylonian captivity, and others of the gentiles converted by the preaching of the Apostles.

paras.t: Et dabo ei, id est Synagogæ in Christum credenti, vinitores ejus, id est spiritualis vineæ spirituales cultores. Synagoga quippe dicitur vinea, juxta illud Isaiæ : Vinea Domini exercituum, domus Israel est. Hujus vineæ vinitores post Christi adventum et passionem fuerunt sancti Apostoli, quibus dixit Salvator : Ite ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel. Nam verbo, prece et exemplo eam coluerunt, superflua seu peccata amputando, semine verbi cœlestis irrigando, atque per pastoralem præsidentiam ad spiritualium maturitatem fructuum perducendo. Fueruntque vinitores hi ex eodem loco nativitatis, id est nati ex Judæa et Isra[…]
paras.en: [[2:15|And I will give her|Et dabo ei]], that is, to the Synagogue believing in Christ, [[2:15|vinedressers|vinitores ejus]] [Latin “her vinedressers”], that is, spiritual tillers of the spiritual vineyard. For the Synagogue is called a vineyard, according to that saying of Isaias: [[Is 5:7|the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel|Vinea Domini exercituum, domus Israel est]]. The vinedressers of this vineyard after the coming and passion of Christ were the holy Apostles, to whom the Saviour said: [[Matt 10:6|go ye rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel|Ite ad oves quæ perierunt domus Israel]]. For they tilled it by word, prayer and example, cutting off what was superfluous, that is, sins, watering it with the seed of the heavenly word, and bringing it by their pastoral oversight to the ripeness of spiritual fruits. And these vinedressers were [[2:15|out of the same place|ex eodem loco]] of birth, that is, born of Judea and Isra[…]

paras.t: Ægyptum. Submersis quippe in mari Rubro Ægyptiis, Israelitæ laudabant Deum, dicentes, Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est : ut patet in Exodo. Sic primitiva Ecclesia ex Judaismo conversa, et de spirituali Ægypto, id est caligine vitiorum, educta, et ducta per mare Rubrum, id est Baptismum Christi sanguine consecratum, in quo peccata ac dæmones submerguntur, Deum devotissime jugiterque laudavit, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum copiose describitur. Unde apud Isaiam dicitur : Simul laudabunt, quia oculo ad oculum videbunt quum converterit Dominus Sion. Judæa autem in altiori situ est, quam Ægyptus. Propterea filii Israel dicuntur ascendisse de Ægypto, pergentes ad sanctam terram : multo amplius, qui de spirituali Ægypto ad terram promissionis, id est de tenebris et peccatis hujus mundi ad patriam, ascendit : quia de terrenis ad cœlestia, de carnalibus ad spiritualia, de conversatione vilissima ad vitam tendit puram atque angelicam.
paras.en: […] Egypt. For when the Egyptians had been drowned in the Red Sea, the Israelites praised God, saying: [[Ex 15:1|Let us sing to the Lord: for he is gloriously magnified|Cantemus Domino, gloriose enim magnificatus est]], as is plain in Exodus. So the primitive Church, converted from Judaism and brought out of the spiritual Egypt, that is, the darkness of vices, and led through the Red Sea, that is, Baptism consecrated by the blood of Christ, in which sins and demons are drowned, praised God most devoutly and without ceasing, as is described at length in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 2:47||]] [the margin gives Act. ii–iv]. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 52:8|they shall praise together: for they shall see eye to eye when the Lord shall convert Sion|Simul laudabunt, quia oculo ad oculum videbunt quum converterit Dominus Sion]]. Now Judea lies higher than Egypt. Therefore the children of Israel are said to have gone up out of Egypt when they went to the holy land; much more does he go up who goes from the spiritual Egypt to the land of promise, that is, from the darkness and sins of this world to the heavenly country: for he is tending from earthly things to heavenly, from carnal to spiritual, from a most base manner of life to a life pure and angelic.

paras.t: Et erit in die illa, ait Dominus, id est tempore evangelicæ legis et primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quando electi Judæi in Christum crediderint, vocabit me Synagoga conversa, Vir meus, id est, dicet quod ego Dominus sum vir ejus: secundum sensum sæpe prætactum; et non vocabit me ultra, Baali: id est, quamvis posset me ita vocare, quantum ad rem significatam (nam Baal interpretatur, habens; Baali autem, habens me: sicque sponsa vel conjux posset maritum seu virum suum vocare Baali, id est habens me in conjugium), non tamen vocabit me ita, propter magnam convenientiam hujus nominis, Baali, cum hoc nomine, Baalim, quod est nomen idoli. Tanquam dicat: Ego Dominus in tantum idola detestor et odio, fideles quoque perfecti in hoc mihi conformantur, quod propter convenientiam vocum, nolo a fidelibus, quorum congregatio est uxor et sponsa mea, dici Baali, sed vir vel sponsus, ne dicendo Baali, recordentur idoli nomine Baalim. Denique Ninus ædificator Ninive, fecit idolum patri suo defuncto, qui dictus est Belus. Hoc idolum Babylonii vocabant Bel, Sidonii Baalim, Judæi Beelzebub. Hoc modo exponit Hieronymus, Beda et Glossa.
paras.en: [[2:16|And it shall be in that day, saith the Lord|Et erit in die illa, ait Dominus]], that is, in the time of the law of the Gospel and of the primitive Church, when the elect among the Jews shall have believed in Christ, [[2:16|That she shall call me|vocabit me]], the converted Synagogue, [[2:16|My husband|Vir meus]]: that is, she shall say that I, the Lord, am her husband, in the sense often touched on before; [[2:16|and she shall call me no more Baali|et non vocabit me ultra, Baali]]: that is, although she could call me so as regards the thing signified (for *Baal* is interpreted "having", and *Baali* "having me"; and so a bride or wife could call her husband or man *Baali*, that is, "having me in marriage" [the margin offers the reading *conjugem*, "having me as his wife"]), yet she shall not call me so, because of the close likeness of this name *Baali* to the name *Baalim*, which is the name of an idol. As if he said: I the Lord so detest and hate idols (and the perfect among the faithful are conformed to me in this) that, because of the likeness of the words, I will not be called *Baali* by the faithful, whose congregation is my wife and bride, but husband or spouse, lest in saying *Baali* they be put in mind of the idol by the name *Baalim*. Moreover Ninus, the builder of Ninive, made an idol of his dead father, who was called Belus. This idol the Babylonians called Bel[[Dan 14:2||]], the Sidonians Baalim[[Judg 2:11||]], the Jews Beelzebub[[Matt 12:24||]]. So Jerome, Bede and the Gloss expound it.

paras.t: Sed Lyræ videtur, quod Rabbi Salomon exponat hunc locum magis catholice, ita quod vir sumitur hic pro sponso, quod est nomen amoris; Baali vero, secundum proprietatem Hebrææ linguæ, significat dominum meum, quod est nomen timoris, juxta illud Malachiæ: Servus timet dominum suum: si ergo Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus? Est itaque sensus, quod populus christifidelis, ex familiaritate cum Deo, vocabunt eum nomine amoris, non timoris: quod proprie competit statui evangelicæ legis, quæ dicitur lex amoris, secundum illud ad Romanos: Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus, Abba (Pater). Unde Augustinus: Brevis, inquit, differentia legis et Evangelii, timor et amor. Vult igitur dicere, quod successerit amor.
paras.en: But it seems to Lyra that Rabbi Salomon expounds this place in a more Catholic way: so that *husband* is taken here for spouse, which is a name of love, while *Baali*, by the idiom of the Hebrew tongue, means "my lord", which is a name of fear; according to that of Malachias, where the servant feareth [[Mal 1:6|his master|dominum suum]] [Denis reads *Servus timet*, "the servant feareth"; in Malachias the servant "honoureth" his master]: [[Mal 1:6|if I be a master, where is my fear|si ergo Dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus]]? The sense, then, is that the Christian people, out of their familiarity with God, will call him by a name of love, not of fear: which belongs properly to the state of the law of the Gospel, which is called the law of love, according to that to the Romans: [[Rom 8:15|you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear: but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons, whereby we cry: Abba (Father)|Non accepistis spiritum servitutis iterum in timore, sed accepistis spiritum adoptionis filiorum, in quo clamamus, Abba (Pater)]]. Hence Augustine says: The difference between the Law and the Gospel is brief: fear and love. He means, then, that love has taken the place of fear.

paras.t: Verumtamen prima expositio videtur consonantior litteræ. Nam subditur: Et auferam nomina Baalim, id est idolorum Baal, de ore ejus, id est de ore Judææ ad Christum conversæ, ita quod ultra non exprimit nomen hoc, nisi forte in detestationem idolorum; et non recordabitur ultra nominis eorum ad hoc ut idola veneretur, imo et rarissime occurrent memoriæ. Hoc patet impletum, quia primitiva Ecclesia ex Judæis collecta, non solum non coluit idola, sed et gentilitatem avertit ab idololatria. Ex quibus patet, quod Dominus non vult a fidelibus Baali dici, propter similitudinem nominis hujus cum Baalim. Denique Aquila diligens et curiosus interpres, secundum Hieronymum sic transtulit: Vocabit me, Vir meus; et non vocabit me, Habens me, id est Baali. Rursus in novo Testamento frequenter Deus exprimitur nomine Domini. Dominus enim potest esse nomen timoris filialis et casti, qui non excluditur ab evangelica caritate, sed eam assequitur.
paras.en: Yet the first exposition seems to agree better with the letter. For there follows: [[2:17|And I will take away the names of Baalim|Et auferam nomina Baalim]], that is, of the idols of Baal, [[2:17|out of her mouth|de ore ejus]], that is, out of the mouth of Judæa converted to Christ, so that she will no longer utter this name, unless perhaps in detestation of idols; [[2:17|and she shall no more remember their name|et non recordabitur ultra nominis eorum]] so as to worship idols; indeed they will very seldom even come to mind. This is plainly fulfilled, for the primitive Church gathered from the Jews not only did not worship idols, but also turned the Gentiles away from idolatry. From this it is clear that the Lord does not wish to be called *Baali* by the faithful, because of the likeness of this name to *Baalim*. Moreover Aquila, a careful and exact translator, according to Jerome rendered it thus: She shall call me, My husband; and she shall not call me, Having me, that is, *Baali*. Again, in the New Testament God is often expressed by the name of Lord. For *Lord* can be a name of filial and chaste fear [that is, the fear of a son who dreads to offend the one he loves, as against servile fear, the fear of punishment], which is not shut out by the charity of the Gospel, but goes along with it.

paras.t: Et percutiam eis fœdus, id est, Judæis ad Christum conversis dabo pacem, vel eamdem legem, cum bestia agri, et cum volucre cœli, et cum reptili terræ, id est cum gentilibus, qui per eorum prædicationem recipient evangelicam legem, et erunt confœderati Judæis in Christo lapide angulari, qui est pax nostra, faciens utraque unum. Ex duobus siquidem populis, quasi ex duobus parietibus, constituit unam Ecclesiam, prout in Joanne protestatur: Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere, et fiet unus pastor et unum ovile. Unde translatio Septuaginta interpretum habet: Et disponam eis testamentum in die illa cum bestiis terræ, et cum volatilibus cœli, et cum reptilibus terræ. De hac quoque gentilium ac Judæorum confœderatione loquitur Isaias: Habitabit lupus, inquiens, cum agno, et pardus cum hœdo accubabit, vitulus et ovis et leo simul morabuntur, et puer parvulus minabit eos. Hinc etiam, sicut in Actibus recolitur, quum Petrus iturus esset ad conversionem gentilium, scilicet Cornelii centurionis et suorum, vidit in visu vas in quo erant omnia genera animantium, dictumque est ei ut comederet ea; quumque renueret, audivit: Quod Deus purificavit, tu commune ne dixeris. Porro gentiles nominibus horum irrationabilium animalium designantur: primo, quoniam bestialiter nimis vixerunt; secundo, quoniam animalia hujusmodi coluerunt, juxta illud ad Romanos: Mutaverunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis, et volucrum et serpentium.
paras.en: [[2:18|I will make a covenant with them|Et percutiam eis fœdus]], that is, to the Jews converted to Christ I will give peace, or the same law, [[2:18|with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air, and with the creeping things of the earth|cum bestia agri, et cum volucre cœli, et cum reptili terræ]], that is, with the Gentiles, who through their preaching will receive the law of the Gospel, and will be leagued with the Jews in Christ, [[Eph 2:20|the chief corner stone|lapide angulari]]: for [[Eph 2:14|he is our peace, who hath made both one|qui est pax nostra, faciens utraque unum]]. For out of two peoples, as out of two walls, he built one Church, as he declares in John: [[John 10:16|other sheep I have that are not of this fold: them also I must bring|Alias oves habeo, quæ non sunt ex hoc ovili; et illas oportet me adducere]], [[John 10:16|And there shall be one fold and one shepherd|et fiet unus pastor et unum ovile]]. Hence the translation of the Seventy interpreters has: And I will make a covenant for them in that day with the beasts of the earth, and with the fowls of the air, and with the creeping things of the earth. Of this league of the Gentiles and the Jews Isaias also speaks: [[Is 11:6|The wolf shall dwell|Habitabit lupus]], he says, [[Is 11:6|with the lamb: and the leopard shall lie down with the kid: the calf and the lion, and the sheep shall abide together, and a little child shall lead them|cum agno, et pardus cum hœdo accubabit, vitulus et ovis et leo simul morabuntur, et puer parvulus minabit eos]]. Hence too, as is recorded in the Acts, when Peter was about to go to convert the Gentiles, namely Cornelius the centurion and his household, he saw in a vision a vessel in which were all kinds of living creatures, and he was told to eat them; and when he refused, he heard[[Acts 10:9||]]: [[Acts 10:15|That which God hath cleansed, do not thou call common|Quod Deus purificavit, tu commune ne dixeris]]. Further, the Gentiles are signified by the names of these irrational animals: first, because they lived all too much like beasts; secondly, because they worshipped animals of this kind, according to that to the Romans: [[Rom 1:23|they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of the image of a corruptible man and of birds|Mutaverunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis, et volucrum]] [[Rom 1:23|and of creeping things|et serpentium]].

paras.t: Spiritualiter vero per bestias agri, possunt intelligi crudeles atque tyranni; per volucres cœli, superbi; per reptilia terræ, avari, gulosi, et luxuriosi carnalibus vitiis pressi.
paras.en: Spiritually, by [[2:18|the beasts of the field|bestias agri]] can be understood the cruel and tyrants; by [[2:18|the fowls of the air|volucres cœli]], the proud; by [[2:18|the creeping things of the earth|reptilia terræ]], the avaricious, the gluttonous and the lustful, weighed down by carnal vices.

paras.t: Hæc itaque faciam in die illa, id est tempore gratiæ, radiante evangelicæ veritatis splendore: de qua dicit Apostolus, Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit; et Isaias, In die illa erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria. Hæc enim præsertim fiebant, divisis et ad loca gentilium destinatis Apostolis.
paras.en: These things, then, I will do [[2:18|in that day|in die illa]], that is, in the time of grace, when the splendour of the gospel truth shines forth: of which the Apostle says: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed And the day is at hand|Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit]]; and Isaias: [[Is 4:2|In that day the bud of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory|In die illa erit germen Domini in magnificentia et gloria]]. For these things came about above all when the Apostles had been parted and sent to the lands of the Gentiles.

paras.t: Et arcum et gladium et bellum conteram de terra, id est, pace hac facta inter credentes, et crudelibus ac superbis gentilibus ad fidem conversis, tollam arma et prælia ab Ecclesia. Hoc maxime factum fuit a conversione Constantini. Nam interim persecutiones generales pro maxima parte quieverunt. Potest quoque referri ad tempus adventus Christi, quando in toto mundo pax fuit, ita quod ad unius viri imperium totus describebatur tunc orbis. Unde habetur in Psalmo: Auferens bella usque ad finem terræ; arcum conteret et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni. In Isaia quoque: Conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium. Et dormire eos faciam fiducialiter, ita quod sine timore hostium ibunt ad lectum. In pace quoque in idipsum dormient, et requiescent in spe futurorum bonorum, quæ nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt. Hinc Jeremias loquitur: In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Et habitare eos faciam in spe.
paras.en: [[2:18|and I will destroy the bow, and the sword, and war out of the land|Et arcum et gladium et bellum conteram de terra]], that is, when this peace has been made among those who believe, and the cruel and proud Gentiles have been converted to the faith, I will take away arms and battles from the Church. This was done above all from the conversion of Constantine; for from then on the general persecutions for the most part ceased. It can also be referred to the time of Christ's coming, when there was peace in the whole world, so that the whole world was then being enrolled at the command of one man[[Luke 2:1||]]. Hence we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 45:10|Making wars to cease even to the end of the earth. He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: and the shield he shall burn in the fire|Auferens bella usque ad finem terræ; arcum conteret et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni]]. In Isaias too: [[Is 2:4|they shall turn their swords into ploughshares|Conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres]], [[Is 2:4|neither shall they be exercised any more to war|nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium]]. [[2:18|and I will make them sleep secure|Et dormire eos faciam fiducialiter]], so that they will go to bed without fear of enemies. [[Ps 4:9|In peace in the self same|In pace quoque in idipsum]] they shall also sleep, and shall rest in the hope of the good things to come, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard: neither hath it entered into the heart of man|nec oculus vidit, nec auris audivit, nec in cor hominis ascenderunt]][[Is 64:4||]]. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 23:6|In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently|In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter]]. Hence the Seventy translated: And I will make them dwell in hope.

paras.t: Et sponsabo, id est, per gratiam, fidem et caritatem conjungam, mihi te plebem seu congregationem fidelium, ut sis sponsa mea, in sempiternum, id est in præsenti et in futuro, quatenus de nuptiis viæ transferaris ad nuptias gloriæ, de quibus in Apocalypsi scribitur: Beati qui ad cœnam nuptiarum Agni vocati sunt. Denique triplex est sponsa Christi, videlicet: universalis, quæ est Ecclesia, cui ait Apostolus, Despondi vos uni viro virginem castam exhibere Christo; particularis, quæ est anima justi; et singularis, puta virgo Maria. Ideo quoque Dominus asserit: Sponsabo te mihi in sempiternum, quoniam statui ac nuptiis Ecclesiæ militantis et christianæ non succedet nisi status et nuptiæ Ecclesiæ triumphantis ac patriæ. Propter quod Christus promisit Ecclesiæ: Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.
paras.en: [[2:19|And I will espouse|Et sponsabo]], that is, through grace, faith and charity I will join [[2:19|thee to me|mihi te]], the people or congregation of the faithful, that thou mayest be my bride, [[2:19|for ever|in sempiternum]], that is, in the present and in the future, so that thou mayest pass from the nuptials of the way to the nuptials of glory [the *way* (*via*): this present life, in which we are still travelling towards our fatherland], of which it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 19:9|Blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb|Beati qui ad cœnam nuptiarum Agni vocati sunt]]. Moreover, the bride of Christ is threefold: universal, which is the Church, to which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 11:2|I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ|Despondi vos uni viro virginem castam exhibere Christo]]; particular, which is the soul of the just man; and singular, namely the Virgin Mary. And the Lord says [[2:19|I will espouse thee to me for ever|Sponsabo te mihi in sempiternum]] for this reason too, that the state and nuptials of the Church militant and Christian will be followed by nothing but the state and nuptials of the Church triumphant and of the fatherland. That is why Christ promised the Church: [[Matt 28:20|behold I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world|Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi]].

paras.t: Et sponsabo te mihi in justitia, id est, dando tibi habitum et actus justitiæ, ut declinans a malo, et faciens bonum, reddas unicuique quod suum est; et judicio: quod est actus justitiæ, tanquam habitus dirigentis ad efficaciter judicandum; et prudentiæ, tanquam habitus actum elicientis. Estque judicium discretio inter bonum et malum, verum et falsum: propter quod efficimur Deo amabiles, prout ad Jeremiam Dominus fatur: Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris. Hoc est ordinatum judicium, de quo Apostolus dicit, Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non judicaremur; et Psalmista, Ideo non resurgunt impii in judicio. Propter hæc duo efficitur anima nostra apta et digna, ut sit sedes seu thronus Sponsi cœlestis, juxta illud in Psalmo: Justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ. Et in misericordia et miserationibus, id est per virtutem misericordiæ et opera ejus, ut sis in te ipsa pia et clemens, compassiva quoque ad alios et benefica eis. Beati enim misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Judicium vero sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam; sed et misericordia superexaltat judicium, ut ait Jacobus. Oportet ergo animam quæ vult esse sponsa Dei, simul habere justitiam, judicium et misericordiam. Propter quod orat Propheta: Bonitatem et disciplinam et scientiam doce me. Nempe per bonitatem misericordiam, per disciplinam justitiam, per scientiam vero discretionem seu judicium intellexit, quatenus sciat homo justitiam et misericordiam irreprehensibiliter contemperare per discretionis judicium.
paras.en: [[2:19|and I will espouse thee to me in justice|Et sponsabo te mihi in justitia]], that is, by giving thee the habit and the acts of justice, so that, declining from evil and doing good[[Ps 36:27||]], thou mayest render to each what is his; [[2:19|and judgment|et judicio]]: which is an act of justice, as of the habit that directs one to judge effectively, and of prudence, as of the habit that elicits the act [the language of the schools: judgment belongs to justice as the virtue that inclines to it, and to prudence as the virtue that brings it forth]. And judgment is the discerning between good and evil, true and false; through which we are made lovable to God, as the Lord says to Jeremias: [[Jer 15:19|thou wilt separate the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth|Si separaveris pretiosum a vili, quasi os meum eris]]. This is ordered judgment, of which the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged|Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non judicaremur]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 1:5|Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment|Ideo non resurgunt impii in judicio]]. By these two our soul is made fit and worthy to be the seat or throne of the heavenly Bridegroom[[Wis 7:27||]] [the margin gives Wis. vii, 27, where wisdom "conveyeth herself into holy souls"], according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 88:15|Justice and judgment are the preparation of thy throne|Justitia et judicium præparatio sedis tuæ]]. [[2:19|and in mercy, and in commiserations|Et in misericordia et miserationibus]], that is, through the virtue of mercy and its works, so that thou mayest be in thyself devout and gentle, and also compassionate towards others and kind to them. For [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati enim misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]]. And [[Jas 2:13|judgment without mercy to him that hath not done mercy|Judicium vero sine misericordia fiet ei qui non fecerit misericordiam]]; but also [[Jas 2:13|mercy exalteth itself above judgment|misericordia superexaltat judicium]], as James says. The soul, then, that would be the bride of God must have justice, judgment and mercy together. That is why the Prophet prays: [[Ps 118:66|Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge|Bonitatem et disciplinam et scientiam doce me]]. For by goodness he meant mercy, by discipline justice, and by knowledge discernment or judgment: so that a man may know how to temper justice and mercy blamelessly together by the judgment of discernment.

paras.t: Et sponsabo te mihi in fide, per dilectionem operante, qua fit primo conjunctio meritoria inter Deum et homines, quoniam sine fide impossibile est placere Deo. Propter quod in Jeremia habetur: Domine, oculi tui respiciunt fidem; et alibi, Justus in sua fide vivet. Itaque virtus et actio virtuosa, videlicet fides, justitia, judicium, misericordia, miseratio, sunt causa formalis desponsationis inter Deum et animam. Et recte ait Dominus Judææ in Christum credenti, Sponsabo te mihi in fide, non, in justitia legis: quia, ut ait Apostolus, Arbitramur hominem justificari per fidem sine operibus legis. Propter quod Christus sæpe testatur in Evangelio: Fides tua te salvum fecit.
paras.en: [[2:20|And I will espouse thee to me in faith|Et sponsabo te mihi in fide]], faith working through charity, by which the meritorious union between God and men is first made, since [[Heb 11:6|without faith it is impossible to please God|sine fide impossibile est placere Deo]]. That is why we have in Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|O Lord, thy eyes are upon truth|Domine, oculi tui respiciunt fidem]] [the Latin has *fidem*, "faith", which is Denis's point; the Douay-Rheims renders it "truth"]; and elsewhere: [[Hab 2:4|the just shall live in his faith|Justus in sua fide vivet]]. So virtue and virtuous action, namely faith, justice, judgment, mercy and commiseration, are the formal cause of the espousal between God and the soul [the *formal cause*: that which makes a thing what it is]. And rightly does the Lord say to Judæa believing in Christ: [[2:20|I will espouse thee to me in faith|Sponsabo te mihi in fide]], not "in the justice of the law"; for, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 3:28|we account a man to be justified by faith, without the works of the law|Arbitramur hominem justificari per fidem sine operibus legis]]. That is why Christ often declares in the Gospel: [[Luke 18:42|thy faith hath made thee whole|Fides tua te salvum fecit]][[Matt 9:22||]].

paras.t: Præterea, secundum Hieronymum, in hoc innotescit benignitas Dei, quod Judæam sæpius aversam et adulterantem, non solum sibi reconciliat, sed desponsat. Ter quoque eam desponsavit: primo, in Abraham; secundo, in legis datione; tertio, in Christi adventu per fidem atque Baptismum, quæ desponsatio manet in posteris usque in sempiternum. Rursus, secundum Glossam, hæc est distantia inter conjugium Dei, et conjugia hominum: quoniam homines de virgine non virginem faciunt, sed corruptam; Deus autem junctus meretricibus, efficit virgines mente integras.
paras.en: Further, according to Jerome, the kindness of God is made known in this, that he not only reconciles to himself Judæa, so often turned away from him and committing adultery, but espouses her. And he espoused her three times: first, in Abraham; secondly, in the giving of the Law; thirdly, at the coming of Christ, through faith and Baptism; and this espousal lasts in her posterity for ever. Again, according to the Gloss, this is the difference between the marriage of God and the marriages of men: men make of a virgin one who is not a virgin but corrupted; but God, joined to harlots, makes them virgins whole in mind.

paras.t: Et scies per experientiam tantorum beneficiorum, quia ego sum Dominus, qui solus valeo tantam tribuere gratiam, cui nullus est similis, et cujus comparatione omnis creatura est serva, qui solus sum Dominus universalis atque liberrimus. Unde per Isaiam fatetur: Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo.
paras.en: [[2:20|and thou shalt know|Et scies]], by the experience of such great benefits, [[2:20|that I am the Lord|quia ego sum Dominus]]: who alone am able to bestow so great a grace, to whom none is like[[Ps 85:8||]], in comparison with whom every creature is a servant; who alone am the universal and supremely free Lord. Hence he declares through Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum; gloriam meam alteri non dabo]].

paras.t: Et erit: In die illa exaudiam, dicit Dominus, et exaudiam cœlos, et illi exaudient terram, etc. Locus iste duobus modis exponitur. Primo, de cœlo et terra materialibus, ac multiplicatione temporalium bonorum. Corporalia autem et inanimata exaudiri dicuntur, dum sortiuntur effectum in his ad quæ naturaliter inclinantur ac ordinantur. Corpora vero cœlestia, naturaliter inclinantur ac ordinantur ad influendum elementis et mixtis terrenis, ad fecundandum et transmutandum ea secundum certum temporum cursum. Est itaque sensus: In die illa, quum desponsata fuerit mihi Synagoga (modo prætacto), exaudiam cœlos, id est, influentiæ eorum dabo effectum, ut terram fecundent. Ideo subditur: et illi exaudient terram, influendo ei necessaria ad fructificandum. Unde latio seu accessus solis in circulo obliquo, dicitur causa generationis et renovationis terræ nascentium. Et terra exaudiet triticum, et vinum, et oleum, id est, fructus istos producet secundum naturalem inclinationem seminis fructuum horum. Semen enim est potentia totum, et habet naturalem aptitudinem ad totius productionem. Et hæc terræ nascentia exaudient Jezrael, id est, desiderio fidelium satisfacient, præbendo necessaria vitæ ut satientur. Jezrael quippe, ut dictum est, interpretatur semen Dei: per quod intelligitur congregatio justorum fidelium. De quibus Isaias prædixit: Isti sunt semen cui benedixit Dominus.
paras.en: [[2:21|And it shall come to pass in that day: I will hear, saith the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth|Et erit: In die illa exaudiam, dicit Dominus, et exaudiam cœlos, et illi exaudient terram]], etc. This place is expounded in two ways. First, of the material heaven and earth, and of the multiplying of temporal goods. Now bodily and inanimate things are said to be *heard* when they obtain their effect in the things to which they are by nature inclined and ordered. And the heavenly bodies are by nature inclined and ordered to influence the elements and the mixed bodies of the earth [*mixed bodies*: things compounded of the four elements], to make them fruitful and to change them according to the fixed course of the seasons. The sense, then, is: [[2:21|in that day|In die illa]], when the Synagogue shall have been espoused to me (in the way just touched on), [[2:21|I will hear the heavens|exaudiam cœlos]], that is, I will give effect to their influence, so that they make the earth fruitful. Therefore there follows: [[2:21|and they shall hear the earth|et illi exaudient terram]], by pouring into it what it needs to bear fruit. Hence the movement or approach of the sun in the oblique circle [the ecliptic, along which the sun moves through the year] is called the cause of the generation and renewal of the things that grow from the earth. [[2:22|And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oil|Et terra exaudiet triticum, et vinum, et oleum]], that is, it will bring forth these fruits according to the natural inclination of the seed of these fruits. For the seed is the whole in potency, and has a natural aptitude to produce the whole. [[2:22|and these|Et hæc]] things that grow from the earth [[2:22|shall hear Jezrahel|exaudient Jezrael]], that is, they will satisfy the desire of the faithful, supplying what is needed for life, so that they are filled. For *Jezrael*, as has been said, is interpreted "seed of God": by which is understood the congregation of the just and faithful. Of whom Isaias foretold: [[Is 61:9|these are the seed which the Lord hath blessed|Isti sunt semen cui benedixit Dominus]].

paras.t: Secundo exponitur sic: Exaudiam cœlos, id est angelicos spiritus et cives cœlestes orantes pro viatoribus. Unde Raphael dixit se Deo obtulisse orationem Tobiæ. Vel per cœlos designantur Apostoli, de quibus cantamus in Psalmo: Cœli enarrant gloriam Dei. Hos Dominus exaudivit pro aliis deprecantes. Et illi cœli exaudierunt terram, id est homines in terra morantes, seu militantem Ecclesiam, docendo atque sanando, ac diversa beneficia suis auditoribus impendendo. Terra quoque exaudit triticum, id est, Ecclesia profert suis membris verbum confortationis et sustentationis internæ, dicendo: Exspecta Dominum, viriliter age, et confortetur cor tuum, et sustine Dominum. Unde in libro Paralipomenon dicitur: Confortamini, et non dissolvantur manus vestræ; erit enim merces operi vestro. Et ad Corinthios: Stabiles estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper, scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino. Et vinum spiritualis ac mysticæ intelligentiæ, de quo Sapientia ait: Bibite vinum quod miscui vobis. Et oleum consolationis, de quo scribit Psalmista: Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo lætitiæ. Propter quod monet Apostolus: Consolamini pusillanimes, suscipite infirmos, patientes estote ad omnes. Et hæc exaudient Jezrael, id est, ad effectum perducent desiderium seminis Dei. Cui ait Christus: Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro vobis dare regnum. Per prædicta enim spiritualia bona, congregatio fidelium pertingit ad regnum perpetuum.
paras.en: Secondly, it is expounded thus: [[2:21|I will hear the heavens|Exaudiam cœlos]], that is, the angelic spirits and the citizens of heaven praying for wayfarers [*viatores*: those still on the way, in this present life]. Hence Raphael said that he had offered the prayer of Tobias to God[[Tob 12:12||]]. Or by the heavens are signified the Apostles, of whom we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 18:2|The heavens shew forth the glory of God|Cœli enarrant gloriam Dei]]. These the Lord heard when they prayed for others. [[2:21|and they shall hear the earth|Et illi cœli exaudierunt terram]] [Denis's words: "and those heavens heard the earth"], that is, men dwelling on earth, or the Church militant, by teaching and healing, and bestowing various benefits on their hearers. [[2:22|And the earth shall hear the corn|Terra quoque exaudit triticum]], that is, the Church brings forth for her members the word of inward strengthening and support, saying: [[Ps 26:14|Expect the Lord, do manfully, and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord|Exspecta Dominum, viriliter age, et confortetur cor tuum, et sustine Dominum]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxvi, 14; the words are Ps 26:14]. Hence it is said in the book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 15:7|take courage, and let not your hands be weakened: for there shall be a reward for your work|Confortamini, et non dissolvantur manus vestræ; erit enim merces operi vestro]]. And to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:58|be ye steadfast and unmoveable: always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labour is not in vain in the Lord|Stabiles estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper, scientes quod labor vester non est inanis in Domino]]. [[2:22|and the wine|Et vinum]] of spiritual and mystical understanding, of which Wisdom says: [[Prov 9:5|drink the wine which I have mingled for you|Bibite vinum quod miscui vobis]]. [[2:22|and the oil|Et oleum]] of consolation, of which the Psalmist writes: [[Ps 44:8|God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness|Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, oleo lætitiæ]]. That is why the Apostle admonishes: [[1 Thess 5:14|comfort the feeble minded: support the weak: be patient towards all men|Consolamini pusillanimes, suscipite infirmos, patientes estote ad omnes]]. [[2:22|and these shall hear Jezrahel|Et hæc exaudient Jezrael]], that is, they will bring to effect the desire of the seed of God; to whom Christ says: [[Luke 12:32|Fear not, little flock, for it hath pleased your Father to give you a kingdom|Nolite timere, pusillus grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro vobis dare regnum]]. For through the spiritual goods just named the congregation of the faithful reaches the everlasting kingdom.

paras.t: Et seminabo eam mihi, id est, Judæam conversam, præsertim Apostolos atque eorum discipulos, mittam ad gloriam nominis mei, in terram, id est ubique terrarum, juxta illud, In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum. Quibus in Marco dicitur: Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Hi enim totum orbem semine verbi cœlestis fecundarunt, quemadmodum ab Isaia dictum est: Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine. Et miserebor ejus quæ fuit Absque misericordia, id est Synagogæ, quæ dum peccatis ac idolis deservivit, fuit juste relicta, et sine gratia gratum faciente. Nemo tamen est penitus sine misericordia, quum dicat Salvator: Diligite inimicos vestros, et eritis filii Altissimi, quia ipse benignus est super ingratos et malos.
paras.en: [[2:23|And I will sow her unto me|Et seminabo eam mihi]], that is, Judæa converted, above all the Apostles and their disciples, I will send out for the glory of my name [[2:23|in the earth|in terram]], that is, everywhere on earth, according to that: [[Ps 18:5|Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth|In omnem terram exivit sonus eorum]]. To them it is said in Mark: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. For they made the whole world fruitful with the seed of the heavenly word, as was said by Isaias: [[Is 27:6|Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed|Florebit et germinabit Israel, et implebunt faciem orbis semine]]. [[2:23|and I will have mercy on her that was without mercy|Et miserebor ejus quæ fuit Absque misericordia]], that is, on the Synagogue, which, while she was given over to sins and idols, was justly forsaken, and without sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God]. Yet no one is wholly without mercy, since the Saviour says: [[Luke 6:35|love ye your enemies|Diligite inimicos vestros]], [[Luke 6:35|and you shall be the sons of the Highest. For he is kind to the unthankful and to the evil|et eritis filii Altissimi, quia ipse benignus est super ingratos et malos]].

paras.t: Et dicam Non populo meo, id est eis qui tempore idololatriæ seu peccati non erant populus meus secundum præsentem justitiam, quamvis fuerint populus meus secundum prædestinationem æternam: Populus meus es tu, per caritatem et gratiam, credendo in Christum. Vel loquitur non de eisdem numero, sed specie. Et ipse dicet: Deus meus es tu, et summum et totum bonum meum, in quo spes mea et salus consistit: quemadmodum scriptum est: In Deo salutare meum, et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Domino.
paras.en: [[2:24|And I will say to that which is not my people|Et dicam Non populo meo]], that is, to those who in the time of idolatry or sin were not my people as regards present justice, although they were my people as regards eternal predestination: [[2:24|Thou art my people|Populus meus es tu]], through charity and grace, by believing in Christ. Or he speaks of the same people not in number but in kind [that is, not of the very persons who fell into idolatry, but of the same nation in later times]. [[2:24|and they shall say: Thou art my God|Et ipse dicet: Deus meus es tu]], and my highest and whole good, in whom my hope and salvation lie: as it is written: [[Ps 61:8|In God is my salvation and my glory: he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God|In Deo salutare meum, et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Domino]].

paras.t: Quidam exponunt hunc locum de gentilitate conversa, quia ad hunc sensum videtur Apostolus allegare hæc verba ad Romanos. Est itaque, secundum hoc, sensus: Miserebor tempore gratiæ, ejus quæ fuit Absque misericordia, id est gentilitati, quæ diu abjecta fuit a Deo. Et dicam Non populo meo, id est gentilibus, qui tempore suæ infidelitatis erant non populus meus: Populus meus es tu. De istis enim in Isaia habetur: Quibus non est narratum de eo, viderunt; et qui non audierunt, contemplati sunt. Ad Ephesios quoque Paulus: Vos qui aliquando eratis longe, nunc facti estis prope in sanguine Christi. De quibus et Petrus locutus est: Qui aliquando non populus, nunc autem populus Dei.
paras.en: Some expound this place of the converted Gentiles, because the Apostle seems to cite these words in this sense to the Romans[[Rom 9:25||]]. The sense, then, on this reading, is: [[2:23|I will have mercy|Miserebor]] in the time of grace [[2:23|on her that was without mercy|ejus quæ fuit Absque misericordia]], that is, on the Gentiles, who were long cast off by God. [[2:24|And I will say to that which is not my people|Et dicam Non populo meo]], that is, to the Gentiles, who in the time of their unbelief were not my people: [[2:24|Thou art my people|Populus meus es tu]]. For of these we have in Isaias: [[Is 52:15|they to whom it was not told of him, have seen: and they that heard not, have beheld|Quibus non est narratum de eo, viderunt; et qui non audierunt, contemplati sunt]] [the margin gives Is. iii, 15; the words are Is 52:15]. And Paul to the Ephesians: [[Eph 2:13|you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh by the blood of Christ|Vos qui aliquando eratis longe, nunc facti estis prope in sanguine Christi]]. Of these Peter too has spoken: [[1 Pet 2:10|Who in times past were not a people: but are now the people of God|Qui aliquando non populus, nunc autem populus Dei]].

2.title: EXPOSITIO MORALIS HUJUS SECUNDI CAPITULI.
2.title_en: Moral exposition of this second chapter.

paras.t: QUONIAM, teste Apostolo, omnia in figura contingebant Judæis, quæ de populo veteris Testamenti litteraliter dicta sunt, ad Ecclesiam moraliter retorquenda.
paras.en: Since, as the Apostle witnesses, [[1 Cor 10:11|all these things happened to them in figure|omnia in figura contingebant]] (that is, to the Jews), the things said literally of the people of the Old Testament are to be turned morally to the Church.

paras.t: Secundum hoc, sensus hujus capituli est : Dicite, o veri Christiani, fratribus vestris christifidelibus, quod sint populus meus : quemadmodum Petrus inducit, Vos genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus acquisitionis ; et sorori vestræ, id est cuicumque particulari Ecclesiæ, vel congregationi devotæ, quod sit misericordiam consecuta. Commemorare enim debemus alterutrum beneficia Dei, ut gratiores Deo reddamur, et ejus succendamur amore, atque dicamus : Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi ?
paras.en: Accordingly, the sense of this chapter is: [[2:1|Say ye|Dicite]], O true Christians, [[2:1|to your brethren|fratribus vestris]], the faithful of Christ, that they are [[2:1|my people|populus meus]], as Peter brings in: [[1 Pet 2:9|you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a purchased people|Vos genus electum, regale sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus acquisitionis]]; [[2:1|and to your sister|et sorori vestræ]], that is, to any particular Church or devout congregation, that she hath [[2:1|obtained mercy|misericordiam consecuta]]. For we ought to recall to one another the benefits of God, that we may be made more grateful to God and set on fire with his love, and may say: [[Ps 115:3|What shall I render to the Lord, for all the things that he hath rendered to me?|Quid retribuam Domino pro omnibus quæ retribuit mihi]] [the margin gives Ps. cxv, 12, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate the verse is Ps 115:3].

paras.t: Interdum etiam licet et expedit, fratres ferventes ac diligentes in opere Dei laudare, sicut Apostolus ubertim suos commendavit discipulos, quatenus provocentur ad meliora et animentur, sciantque quæ a Deo donata sunt eis. Sicut enim imperfecti et vani laudibus extolluntur ac seducuntur, juxta quod Dominus ait per Isaiam, Popule meus, qui te beatum dicunt, ipsi te decipiunt, et viam gressuum tuorum dissipant ; sic discreti et virtuosi dum laudantur, amplius intra se humiliantur, scientes quod a se ipsis nihil habeant, et tanto amplius teneantur Deo cum humilitate et gratitudine famulari, quanto majora et plura fuerint dona a Deo sortiti. Ideo in Isaia legitur : Dicite justo quoniam bene, quoniam fructum adinventionum suarum comedet.
paras.en: At times it is also lawful and expedient to praise brethren who are fervent and diligent in the work of God, as the Apostle commended his disciples abundantly, so that they may be spurred on to better things[[1 Cor 12:31||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor. xii, 1; "be zealous for the better gifts", 1 Cor 12:31, fits better] and encouraged, and [[1 Cor 2:12|may know the things that are given|sciantque quæ a Deo donata sunt]] them from God. For just as the imperfect and the vain are puffed up and led astray by praise, according to what the Lord says through Isaias, [[Is 3:12|O my people, they that call thee blessed, the same deceive thee, and destroy the way of thy steps|Popule meus, qui te beatum dicunt, ipsi te decipiunt, et viam gressuum tuorum dissipant]]; so the discreet and the virtuous, when they are praised, are the more humbled within themselves, knowing that they have nothing of themselves, and that they are bound to serve God with humility and gratitude all the more, the greater and the more numerous the gifts they have received from God. Therefore we read in Isaias: [[Is 3:10|Say to the just man that it is well, for he shall eat the fruit of his doings|Dicite justo quoniam bene, quoniam fructum adinventionum suarum comedet]].

paras.t: Deinde Dominus ait viris perfectis de aliorum salute sollicitis : Judicate, id est, redarguite et vere discernite, matrem vestram, id est religionem prolapsam, in qua regula non servatur, vel Ecclesiam recidivantem, quæ in Christi obsequio non constabilitur ; quoniam ipsa non uxor mea, et ego non vir ejus. Talis enim mater quum sit a summo bono aversa, et Christi amori beneficiisque ingrata, non est sponsa sui Creatoris, sed meretrix. Quum dicat Salvator, Nolite judicare, ne judicemini ; et Paulus, Seniorem ne increpaveris : quomodo nunc jubentur filii matrem judicare? Et respondendum, quod in manifestis licitum est judicare cum debito moderamine. Seniores quoque, qui vere seniores sunt, non sunt increpandi ; sed maledictus puer centum annorum.
paras.en: Then the Lord says to perfect men who are anxious for the salvation of others: [[2:2|Judge|Judicate]], that is, rebuke and truly discern, [[2:2|your mother|matrem vestram]], that is, a religious order fallen away, in which the rule is not kept, or a Church relapsing, which is not made steadfast in the service of Christ; [[2:2|because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband|quoniam ipsa non uxor mea, et ego non vir ejus]]. For such a mother, since she is turned away from the highest good and ungrateful for the love and the benefits of Christ, is not the bride of her Creator but a harlot. Since the Saviour says, [[Matt 7:1|Judge not, that you may not be judged|Nolite judicare, ne judicemini]], and Paul, [[1 Tim 5:1|An ancient man rebuke not|Seniorem ne increpaveris]], how are the children now bidden to judge their mother? The answer is that in manifest things it is lawful to judge, with due moderation. Elders too, who are truly elders, are not to be rebuked; but accursed is the child of a hundred years[[Is 65:20||]] [Denis joins two clauses of Is 65:20: "the child shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed"].

paras.t: Huic insuper fornicariæ atque apostatæ matri, quæ inhæret creaturis magis quam Creatori, præcipit Dominus ut fornicationes et adulteria sua spiritualia atque carnalia abjiciat et derelinquat, sobrie, pie, et juste vivendo in hoc sæculo ; et illud unum quod solum et summe necessarium est, fideli mente contemplando, amando ac retinendo.
paras.en: Moreover, the Lord commands this fornicating and apostate mother, who cleaves to creatures more than to the Creator, to cast off and abandon her fornications and adulteries, spiritual and carnal, living soberly, godly and justly in this world[[Tit 2:12||]], and contemplating, loving and holding fast with a faithful mind that one thing which alone and above all is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]].

paras.t: Ne forte exspoliem eam nudam, id est sacramentis ac ceteris bonis Ecclesiæ eam omnino destituam, dicaturque ei illud Apocalypsis : Quia tu es misera et miserabilis, pauper, cæca et nuda. Et statuam eam secundum diem nativitatis suæ, id est in tanta vilitate, pravitate et egestate, quantam habebat tempore gentilitatis, vel antequam perveniret ad Christi Baptismum : ita ut penitus obtenebretur et induretur peccatis, et fiant novissima ejus pejora prioribus. Imo quodammodo damnabilius est in Christianismo, quam in gentilitate, peccare enormiter, quum melius sit viam justitiæ ignorare, quam agnitam non implere ; et servus sciens voluntatem domini sui, et non faciens, plagis vapulabit multis. Et ponam eam quasi solitudinem, et velut terram inviam. Interdum Ecclesia exigentibus suis peccatis, hæc mala corporaliter patitur, ita quod hostibus traditur atque conteritur. Spiritualiter vero ponitur quasi solitudo, dum divina inhabitatione privata, omnem virorem virtutum, omnem fecunditatem actionum sanctarum, omnemque communionem spiritualium miserabiliter perdit. Ponitur quoque ut terra invia, dum in omnibus agit inordinate, nec procedit per medium rationis, sed per vitiorum extrema, ita quod quicumque sequitur eam, erret, sicut qui ambulat per terram non tritam.
paras.en: [[2:3|Lest I strip her naked|Ne forte exspoliem eam nudam]], that is, lest I deprive her altogether of the sacraments and the other goods of the Church, and that word of the Apocalypse be said to her: Because [[Apoc 3:17|thou art wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked|tu es misera et miserabilis, pauper, cæca et nuda]]. [[2:3|and set her as in the day that she was born|Et statuam eam secundum diem nativitatis suæ]], that is, in as great vileness, depravity and want as she had in the time of her heathendom, or before she came to the Baptism of Christ: so that she is utterly darkened and hardened by sins, and [[Matt 12:45|the last state of that man is made worse than the first|fiant novissima ejus pejora prioribus]]. Nay, in a way it is more damnable to sin grievously in Christendom than in heathendom, since it is better not to know the way of justice than, having known it, not to fulfil it[[2 Pet 2:21||]]; and [[Luke 12:47|that servant, who knew the will of his lord|servus sciens voluntatem domini sui]], and doeth it not, [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|plagis vapulabit multis]]. And [[2:3|I will make her as a wilderness|Et ponam eam quasi solitudinem]], and [[2:3|as a land that none can pass through|velut terram inviam]]. Sometimes the Church, as her sins require, suffers these evils bodily, so that she is handed over to her enemies and crushed. Spiritually, however, she is made as a wilderness when, deprived of God's indwelling, she wretchedly loses all the greenness of the virtues, all fruitfulness in holy works and all communion in spiritual things. She is also made as a land that none can pass through when she acts without order in all things and does not go by the middle way of reason but by the extremes of the vices, so that whoever follows her goes astray, like one who walks through untrodden land.

paras.t: Et filiorum illius non miserebor, nisi pœnitentiam egerint : sicut ait Salvator, Nisi pœnitentiam egeritis, omnes similiter peribitis. Quoniam filii fornicationum sunt, id est, matris suæ vitia imitantur, juxta illud Ezechielis : Sicut mater, ita et filii ejus, et filia matris tuæ es tu. Tales sunt omnes solo nomine informique fide Christiani, et solo habitu vel simulatione religiosi, qui majorem damnationem recipient.
paras.en: [[2:4|And I will not have mercy on her children|Et filiorum illius non miserebor]], unless they do penance: as the Saviour says, [[Luke 13:5|except you do penance, you shall all likewise perish|Nisi pœnitentiam egeritis, omnes similiter peribitis]]. [[2:4|for they are the children of fornications|Quoniam filii fornicationum sunt]], that is, they imitate the vices of their mother, according to that word of Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:44|As the mother was|Sicut mater]], so also are her sons [Denis reads *filii*, "sons", where the Vulgate has *filia*, "daughter"], and [[Ezech 16:45|Thou art thy mother's daughter|filia matris tuæ es tu]]. Such are all who are Christians in name only and by an unformed faith [that is, faith without charity], and religious only in habit or in pretence, who shall receive the greater damnation.

paras.t: Confusa est quæ concepit eos : id est, ecclesia malignantium, vel religio prævaricantium, quæ alios fovet in errore et vitiis, confusione digna effecta est, abominabilia opera exercendo : quibus contingit illud veri proverbii, Canis reversus ad vomitum, et sus lota in volutabro luti. Tanto enim confusibilius est Christianum peccare quam alium, quanto amplior dignitas majorque gratia Christianis a Christo collatæ sunt, quam alicui usquam nationi.
paras.en: [[2:5|she that conceived them is covered with shame|Confusa est quæ concepit eos]]: that is, the church of the malignant, or the religious order of transgressors, which fosters others in error and vice, has been made worthy of confusion by doing abominable works: [[2 Pet 2:22|that of the true proverb has happened to them: The dog is returned to his vomit; and: The sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire|quibus contingit illud veri proverbii, Canis reversus ad vomitum, et sus lota in volutabro luti]][[Prov 26:11||]]. For it is the more shameful for a Christian to sin than for another, by as much as a fuller dignity and a greater grace have been conferred on Christians by Christ than on any nation anywhere.

paras.t: Quia dixit : Vadam post amatores meos, qui dant panes mihi, et aquas et lanam et linum.
