Tales sunt avari, gulosi, et de providentia divina diffidentes, qui sollicitantur in crastinum, et magis confidunt in hominibus quam in Deo : propter quod divitibus atque potentibus sæculi blandiuntur, et in illicitis obsequuntur, quatenus terrena ab eis commoda consequantur. Unde dum temporales adipiscuntur divitias, non cogitant eas sibi a Deo principaliter condonari : propter quod nec gratias referunt ei, nec pauperibus eas communicant. Multi quoque studentium vadunt post amatores suos, id est philosophos, in quorum dictis die ac nocte se occupant, obliviscentes legis Dei, mandatorumque ejus. Contra quos dicit Ecclesiasticus : Quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper ; et in pluribus operibus ejus ne fueris curiosus. Qui philosophi dant eis panem vanæ scientiæ, et aquam agnitionis insipidæ, per quos sibi conquirunt et cumulant lanam et linum, id est pertinentia ad victum atque vestitum.
paras.en: [[2:5|for she said: I will go after my lovers|Quia dixit : Vadam post amatores meos]], [[2:5|that give me my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax|qui dant panes mihi, et aquas et lanam et linum]]. Such are the avaricious, the gluttonous, and those who distrust divine providence, who are anxious for the morrow and trust in men more than in God: for which reason they flatter the rich and the powerful of the world and serve them in unlawful things, so as to obtain earthly advantages from them. Hence, when they gain temporal riches, they do not consider that these are granted them chiefly by God: for which reason they neither give him thanks nor share them with the poor. Many students too go after their lovers, that is, the philosophers, with whose sayings they busy themselves day and night, forgetting the law of God and his commandments. Against these Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 3:22|the things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always, and in many of his works be not curious|Quæ præcepit tibi Deus, illa cogita semper ; et in pluribus operibus ejus ne fueris curiosus]]. These philosophers give them the bread of vain knowledge and the water of tasteless learning, and through them they win and heap up for themselves wool and flax, that is, what belongs to food and clothing.

paras.t: Propter hoc, ecce ego sepiam viam tuam spinis, id est, doloribus et ærumnis variisque diffortuniis, studia vanitatis tuæ et desideria inordinata ab effectu impediam, ut qui non vis blandis et prosperis allici, corrigaris adversis, et sic compellaris intrare : quod utique ad misericordiam pertinet. Et sepiam eam maceria, id est grandi aliquo vel inevitabili obstaculo.
paras.en: [[2:6|Wherefore, behold, I will hedge up thy way with thorns|Propter hoc, ecce ego sepiam viam tuam spinis]], that is, by sorrows and hardships and various misfortunes I will keep the pursuits of thy vanity and thy disordered desires from their effect, so that thou who wilt not be drawn by pleasant and prosperous things mayest be corrected by adversity, and so be compelled to come in: which surely belongs to mercy. [[2:6|and I will stop it up with a wall|Et sepiam eam maceria]], that is, by some great or unavoidable obstacle.

paras.t: Et sequetur per affectum amatores suos, homines mundanos, sive philosophos, et non apprehendet eos, id est, sibi prodesse non poterunt, nec de adversitatibus suis eripere. Unde ait Hieronymus : Ex his intelligimus, quod providentia Dei sæpe nobis contingant adversa et accidant mala, ne habeamus quæ cupimus, et variis calamitatibus hujus sæculi ac miseriis, ad Dei servitutem redire cogamur. Quocontra de reprobis Dominus testatur : Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum, ibunt in adinventionibus suis. Vere enim clementissime agit Omnipotens, dum mala affectantibus, et peccare optantibus ponit obicem, ne quod impie cupiunt, sceleratius perpetrent. Propter quod in libro Machabæorum habetur : Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoribus ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium.
paras.en: [[2:7|And she shall follow|Et sequetur]] in desire [[2:7|after her lovers|amatores suos]], worldly men or philosophers, [[2:7|and shall not overtake them|et non apprehendet eos]], that is, they will not be able to profit her, nor to rescue her from her adversities. Hence Jerome says: From these words we understand that by the providence of God adversities often befall us and evils happen to us, so that we may not have what we desire, and that by the various calamities and miseries of this world we are compelled to return to the service of God. Whereas of the reprobate the Lord testifies: [[Ps 80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: they shall walk in their own inventions|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum, ibunt in adinventionibus suis]]. For truly the Almighty acts most mercifully when he sets a barrier before those who long for evil and wish to sin, lest they carry out still more wickedly what they impiously desire. For this reason we have in the book of Machabees: [[2 Mach 6:13|For it is a token of great goodness, when sinners are not suffered to go on in their ways for a long time, but are presently punished|Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoribus ex sententia agere, sed statim ultiones adhibere, magni beneficii est indicium]].

paras.t: Et dicet, erudita flagellis : Vadam, declinando a malo, et revertar, faciendo bonum ac pœnitendo, ad virum meum priorem, id est ad Sponsum cœlestem, unigenitum Filium Dei, cui in Baptismo fueram desponsata ; quia bene mihi erat tunc, dum ei ex fide, dilectione, et bonis adhæsi operibus, magis quam nunc, quum ab eo aversa, tantis afficior malis. Hoc modo videtur redisse ad Deum, qui ait : Die ac nocte gravata est super me manus tua ; conversus sum in ærumna mea dum configitur spina. Propterea Jeremias ait : Castigasti me, et eruditus sum quasi juvenculus indomitus : postquam enim convertisti me, egi pœnitentiam ; et postquam ostendisti mihi, percussi femur meum. Denique, ampliorem pacem, dulciorem quietem et veræ hilaritatis copiam abundantiorem habet anima Deo inhærens ac serviens, quam quæ carnalibus ac mundanis intenta est rebus, quamvis sæpe multæ sint tribulationes justorum : quoniam Deus consolabitur eos in omni tribulatione ipsorum, ut dicere queant, Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam. Unde Ecclesiastes dicit : Peccatori dedit Deus afflictionem et curam superfluam.
paras.en: [[2:7|and she shall say|Et dicet]], taught by scourges: [[2:7|I will go|Vadam]], by turning aside from evil, [[2:7|and return|et revertar]], by doing good and doing penance, [[2:7|to my first husband|ad virum meum priorem]], that is, to the heavenly Bridegroom, the only-begotten Son of God, to whom I was espoused in Baptism; [[2:7|because it was better with me then|quia bene mihi erat tunc]], when I cleaved to him by faith, love and good works, [[2:7|than now|magis quam nunc]], when, turned away from him, I am afflicted with such great evils. In this way he seems to have returned to God who says: [[Ps 31:4|day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened|Die ac nocte gravata est super me manus tua ; conversus sum in ærumna mea dum configitur spina]]. Therefore Jeremias says: [[Jer 31:18|thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, as a young bullock unaccustomed to the yoke|Castigasti me, et eruditus sum quasi juvenculus indomitus]]: [[Jer 31:19|For after thou didst convert me, I did penance: and after thou didst shew unto me, I struck my thigh|postquam enim convertisti me, egi pœnitentiam ; et postquam ostendisti mihi, percussi femur meum]]. In short, the soul that cleaves to God and serves him has a fuller peace, a sweeter rest and a more abundant store of true gladness than one intent on carnal and worldly things, although often [[Ps 33:20|Many are the afflictions of the just|multæ sint tribulationes justorum]]: for God will comfort them in all their tribulation[[2 Cor 1:4||]], so that they can say: [[Ps 93:19|According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul|Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam]]. Hence Ecclesiastes says: [[Eccles 2:26|to the sinner he hath given vexation, and superfluous care|Peccatori dedit Deus afflictionem et curam superfluam]].

paras.t: Et hæc nescivit, quia ego dedi ei frumentum et vinum et oleum. Sic multi nomine tenus Christiani, non pensant se omnia a Deo adeptos, sed de suis se jactant divitiis, quasi non acceperint. Spiritualiter vero contulit nobis Deus frumentum et vinum, id est, corpus et sanguinem Christi, de quibus in Zacharia habetur : Quid bonum Domini, et quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines? In Psalmo quoque, ubi nostra translatio habet, Erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium, alia habet, Erit frumentum, etc., quod certum est dici de Christo, de quo in illius psalmi fertur exordio : Deus, judicium tuum regi da. Dedit etiam nobis oleum unctionis, quo omnes Christiani unguntur, ut sint genus regale ac sacerdotale. In veteri autem Testamento non nisi reges et sacerdotes ungebantur, secundum Augustinum. Interdum tamen ungebantur aliqui in prophetas. Dedit et nobis oleum, id est dulce memoriale nominis Jesu Christi, de quo Sponsa in Canticis : Oleum, inquit, effusum nomen tuum. Et argentum multiplicavi ei, id est gratiam eloquentiæ in Scripturis : alii enim datur sermo sapientiæ, alii sermo scientiæ ; et aurum, id est divinorum notitiam ; quæ fecerunt Baal, id est, donis istis abusi sunt, fabricantes sibi proprii dogmatis sectam, quod tanquam idolum coluerunt : quod certum est præcipue convenire hæreticis, et ceteris proprii sensus defensoribus. Quocontra clamat Apostolus : Noli verbis contendere ; et iterum, Id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata.
paras.en: [[2:8|And she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil|Et hæc nescivit, quia ego dedi ei frumentum et vinum et oleum]]. So many who are Christians in name only do not consider that they have obtained everything from God, but boast of their riches as though they had not received them. Spiritually, however, God has bestowed on us corn and wine, that is, the body and blood of Christ, of which it is said in Zacharias: [[Zach 9:17|what is the good thing of him, and what is his beautiful thing, but the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins?|Quid bonum Domini, et quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines?]] [the margin gives Zach. ix, 7; the words are Zach 9:17]. In the Psalm too, where our translation has: [[Ps 71:16|there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains|Erit firmamentum in terra in summis montium]], another has: There shall be corn, etc. [*frumentum*, "corn", for *firmamentum*, "firmament"]; and this is certainly said of Christ, of whom it is said at the beginning of that psalm: [[Ps 71:2|Give to the king thy judgment, O God|Deus, judicium tuum regi da]]. He has also given us the oil of anointing, with which all Christians are anointed, that they may be a kingly and priestly race. In the Old Testament, by contrast, only kings and priests were anointed, according to Augustine; yet at times some were anointed as prophets. He has also given us oil, that is, the sweet remembrance of the name of Jesus Christ, of which the Bride says in the Canticles: [[Cant 1:2|Thy name is as oil poured out|Oleum, inquit, effusum nomen tuum]]. [[2:8|and multiplied her silver|Et argentum multiplicavi ei]], that is, the grace of eloquence in the Scriptures: for [[1 Cor 12:8|To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given the word of wisdom: and to another, the word of knowledge|alii enim datur sermo sapientiæ, alii sermo scientiæ]]; [[2:8|and gold|et aurum]], that is, the knowledge of divine things; [[2:8|which they have used in the service of Baal|quæ fecerunt Baal]] [literally "which they made into Baal"], that is, they have abused these gifts, fashioning for themselves a sect of their own teaching, which they have worshipped like an idol: which certainly applies above all to heretics and to the other defenders of their own opinion. Against them the Apostle cries: [[2 Tim 2:14|Contend not in words|Noli verbis contendere]]; and again: [[1 Cor 1:10|that you all speak the same thing and that there be no schisms among you|Id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata]].

paras.t: Idcirco convertar, id est, ad istorum justam punitionem me vertam, et sumam frumentum meum, id est, bona prædicta tollam ab ea, ne illis de cetero abutantur.
paras.en: [[2:9|Therefore will I return|Idcirco convertar]], that is, I will turn myself to the just punishment of these, [[2:9|and take away my corn|et sumam frumentum meum]], that is, I will take the goods spoken of away from her, so that they may not abuse them any further.

paras.t: Et nunc revelabo stultitiam ejus in oculis amatorum ejus : id est, vanitatem, errores et vitia præinductæ impiæ matris seu congregationis rebellis, manifestabo amatoribus ejus, quos ipsa dilexit, quamvis ipsi odiant eam, et visa ejus stultitia ipsam irrideant : qui sunt homines penitus sæculares, de confusione fidelium gloriantes.
paras.en: [[2:10|And now I will lay open her folly in the eyes of her lovers|Et nunc revelabo stultitiam ejus in oculis amatorum ejus]]: that is, the vanity, the errors and the vices of the wicked mother or rebellious congregation spoken of I will make known to her lovers, whom she has loved, although they hate her and, seeing her folly, mock her: these are men wholly worldly, who glory in the confusion of the faithful.

paras.t: Et cessare faciam omne gaudium ejus spirituale : quod ab Apostolo ponitur inter fructus Spiritus Sancti. De quo dicitur : Non est gaudere impiis, dicit Dominus. Facit quoque Deus cessare lætitiam impiorum, vel inducendo adversa, vel auferendo eos celeriter de præsenti hac vita, vel projiciendo eos in tormenta tartarea. Hinc in Job scriptum est : Laus impiorum brevis est, et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti. Et in Psalmo : Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? Subito defecerunt, perierunt propter iniquitatem suam. Ideo dicunt in libro Sapientiæ : Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra, et sicut nuntius præcurrens et avis transvolans. Faciam quoque cessare solennitatem ejus, et omnia festa temporum ejus. Videmus quomodo in diversis regnis destructa sit Religio, et omnis solennitas Christianorum a Sarracenis et aliis propter peccata Ecclesiæ, quæ ob crimina sua privata est Terra sancta ac Sepulcro Domini sui. Denique in his qui diebus festis plus solito vacant inquinamentis carnis et spiritus, aufert Deus veram solennitatem, ita ut dicat : Solennitates vestras odivit anima mea.
paras.en: [[2:11|And I will cause all her mirth to cease|Et cessare faciam omne gaudium ejus]], her spiritual joy, which the Apostle places among the fruits of the Holy Spirit[[Gal 5:22||]]. Of it is said: [[Is 48:22|There is no|Non est]] rejoicing [[Is 48:22|to the wicked, saith the Lord|impiis, dicit Dominus]][[Is 57:21||]] [Denis reads *Non est gaudere impiis*, "there is no rejoicing for the wicked"; Is 48:22 and 57:21 have *pax*, "peace"]. God also makes the gladness of the wicked cease, either by bringing adversity on them, or by taking them swiftly out of this present life, or by casting them into the torments of hell. Hence it is written in Job: [[Job 20:5|the praise of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment|Laus impiorum brevis est, et gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 72:19|How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: they have perished by reason of their iniquity|Quomodo facti sunt in desolationem? Subito defecerunt, perierunt propter iniquitatem suam]]. Therefore they say in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow, and like a post that runneth on|Transierunt omnia illa tanquam umbra, et sicut nuntius præcurrens]], and as a bird flying past[[Wis 5:11||]]. I will also make to cease [[2:11|her solemnities|solennitatem ejus]], [[2:11|and all her festival times|et omnia festa temporum ejus]]. We see how in various kingdoms religion has been destroyed, and every solemnity of the Christians, by the Saracens and others, on account of the sins of the Church, which for her crimes has been deprived of the Holy Land and of the Sepulchre of her Lord. Lastly, in those who on feast days give themselves more than usual to [[2 Cor 7:1|defilement of the flesh and of the spirit|inquinamentis carnis et spiritus]], God takes away the true solemnity, so that he says: [[Is 1:14|your solemnities|Solennitates vestras]] [[Is 1:14|My soul hateth|odivit anima mea]].

paras.t: Et corrumpam vineam ejus et ficum ejus. Per vinum lætitia cordis, per ficum dulcedo temporalis jucunditatis intelligi datur, secundum Glossam. Est itaque sensus, quod delectationi ac suavitati inobedientis Ecclesiæ, omniumque transgressorum, variæ amaritudines commiscentur. Nam animus inordinatus sibi ipsi est pœna, semperque præsumit sæva conscientia perturbata, et conscientia mala affligit injustum. Propter quod in Job legitur : Sonitus terroris semper in auribus impii; et quum pax sit, ille semper insidias suspicatur. Idcirco in Evangelio per spinas intelliguntur divitiæ. De quibus dixit : Mercedes hæ, meæ sunt, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei. Multi enim obtenebrati, bona quæ habent, magis adscribunt parentibus vel amicis, quam Domino. Et ponam eam in saltum, id est, multitudini infructuosarum arborum eam parificabo : sicut Christus disseruit, Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et arescet. Peccator enim impœnitens, infructuosa arbor vocatur, de qua dicitur : Omnis arbor quæ non fecerit fructum bonum, excidetur et in ignem mittetur. Et comedet eam bestia agri, id est diabolus, de quo ait Psalmista : Tu confregisti capita draconis. Qui tunc hominem comedit, dum ei per peccata mortalia incorporatur, et ejus dominationi seu pœnis inferni addicitur.
paras.en: [[2:12|And I will destroy her vines, and her fig trees|Et corrumpam vineam ejus et ficum ejus]]. By wine is given to be understood gladness of heart, by the fig the sweetness of temporal pleasure, according to the Gloss. So the sense is that various bitternesses are mingled with the delight and sweetness of the disobedient Church and of all transgressors. For the disordered mind is its own punishment [a saying of Augustine, Confessions I, 12], and [[Wis 17:10|a troubled conscience always forecasteth grievous things|semperque præsumit sæva conscientia perturbata]], and an evil conscience afflicts the unjust. For this reason we read in Job: [[Job 15:21|The sound of dread is always in his ears: and when there is peace, he always suspecteth treason|Sonitus terroris semper in auribus impii; et quum pax sit, ille semper insidias suspicatur]]. Therefore in the Gospel riches are understood by the thorns[[Matt 13:22||]]. [[2:12|of which she said: These are my rewards, which my lovers have given me|De quibus dixit : Mercedes hæ, meæ sunt, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei]]. For many who are darkened ascribe the goods they have to their parents or friends rather than to the Lord. [[2:12|and I will make her as a forest|Et ponam eam in saltum]], that is, I will make her like a multitude of unfruitful trees: as Christ taught, [[John 15:6|If any one abide not in me, he shall be cast forth as a branch and shall wither|Si quis in me non manserit, mittetur foras sicut palmes, et arescet]]. For the impenitent sinner is called an unfruitful tree, of which it is said: [[Matt 7:19|Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down, and shall be cast into the fire|Omnis arbor quæ non fecerit fructum bonum, excidetur et in ignem mittetur]][[Matt 3:10||]]. [[2:12|and the beasts of the field shall devour her|Et comedet eam bestia agri]], that is, the devil, of whom the Psalmist says: [[Ps 73:14|Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon|Tu confregisti capita draconis]]. He devours a man when the man is made one body with him by mortal sins and is handed over to his dominion or to the pains of hell.

paras.t: Et visitabo super eam dies Baalim, id est peccata quæ fecit, serviendo creaturis magis quam Creatori. Et ornabatur inaure sua et monili suo, id est variis ornamentis corporis in auro, argento, gemmis et vestibus, quatenus pulchritudinem quam non habuit per naturam, adipisceretur per artem, et ibat post amatores suos, ut placeret hominibus, non attendens illud Psalmographi, Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent; et illud, Quicumque voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur. Porro spiritualiter inauris est doctrina, quæ per aurem percipitur; monile vero est prædicatio, quæ per collum emittitur. Elati itaque et inanes, tunc inaure atque monili se ornant, dum docendo aut prædicando cupiunt eloquentes et docti reputari, ab audientibusque laudari.
paras.en: [[2:13|And I will visit upon her the days of Baalim|Et visitabo super eam dies Baalim]], that is, the sins she committed by serving creatures rather than the Creator. [[2:13|and decked herself out with her earrings, and with her jewels|Et ornabatur inaure sua et monili suo]], that is, with various adornments of the body, in gold, silver, gems and garments, so as to gain by art the beauty she did not have by nature, [[2:13|and went after her lovers|et ibat post amatores suos]], to please men, not heeding that word of the Psalmist: [[Ps 52:6|For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men|Quoniam Deus dissipavit ossa eorum qui hominibus placent]]; and that other: [[Jas 4:4|Whosoever therefore will be a friend of this world becometh an enemy of God|Quicumque voluerit amicus hujus mundi fieri, inimicus Dei constituetur]]. Spiritually, moreover, the earring is doctrine, which is taken in through the ear, and the necklace [*monile*, the Douay-Rheims' "jewels"] is preaching, which is sent forth through the throat. So the proud and the empty adorn themselves with earring and necklace when in teaching or preaching they wish to be thought eloquent and learned and to be praised by their hearers.

paras.t: Propter hoc, ecce ego lactabo eam : id est, Ecclesiam vel animam diu afflictam, scilicet pœnitentem, et ad me fideliter suspirantem, consolabor et lætificabo, ita ut per Christum abundet consolatio ejus, et gustet quam suavis est Dominus, dicatque illud Threnorum : Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in se, animæ quærenti eum. Ad hujus lactationis desiderium admonet Petrus in sua prima Canonica : Quasi modo geniti infantes lac concupiscite. Qui vero sic cupit lactari a Deo, renuat interim consolari in rebus mundanis, vanis atque carnalibus, omnem adulterinam delectationem contemnens.
paras.en: [[2:14|Therefore, behold I will allure her|Propter hoc, ecce ego lactabo eam]] [*lactabo*, which the Douay-Rheims renders "I will allure", can also mean "I will give milk to", and Denis goes on to take it so]: that is, the Church or the soul long afflicted, namely the penitent who sighs for me faithfully, I will console and gladden, so that by Christ her comfort may abound[[2 Cor 1:5||]], and she may taste [[Ps 33:9|that the Lord is sweet|quam suavis est Dominus]], and say that word of Lamentations: [[Lam 3:25|The Lord is good to them that hope in him, to the soul that seeketh him|Bonus est Dominus sperantibus in se, animæ quærenti eum]]. To the desire of this milk Peter exhorts in his first canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 2:2|As newborn babes|Quasi modo geniti infantes]] desire milk. But let whoever longs to be given milk thus by God refuse meanwhile to be consoled in worldly, vain and carnal things, despising every adulterous delight.

paras.t: Et ducam eam in solitudinem, id est, ad locum quietum : quemadmodum Christus ascendit in montem solus orare. Qui et dixit discipulis : Venite seorsum in desertum locum, et quiescite pusillum. Solitarius etenim locus, et quies ab exteriori tumultu hominumque occursu, maxime confert ad stabilem ac sincerissimam Dei contemplationem, ad sui ipsius idoneam discussionem, ad cordis munditiam, ad orationum fervorem, ad psalmodiæ dulcedinem, ad illius quoque unius quod solum necessarium est, amorosum, frequentem stabilemque amplexum. Propter quod in Threnis scriptum est : Bonum est cum silentio præstolari salutare Dei; sedebit solitarius et tacebit, quia levabit se super se. Et Isaias ait : In silentio et spe erit fortitudo vestra. Ideo pœnitens ait : Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis. Et loquar ad cor ejus, mentem illuminando et consolando, juxta illud : Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus. Qui enim ab humana consolatione et allocutione propter Deum se abstrahunt, merentur doceri et lætificari a Deo. Unde quum Psalmista dixisset, Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine! consequenter ostendit quibus illa præstetur : Abscondes eos in abscondito faciei tuæ a conturbatione hominum; proteges eos in tabernaculo tuo a contradictione linguarum. Hinc et propheticæ revelationes communiter factæ sunt non in turbis, sed in locis seorsum.
paras.en: [[2:14|and will lead her into the wilderness|Et ducam eam in solitudinem]], that is, to a quiet place: as Christ [[Matt 14:23|went into a mountain alone to pray|ascendit in montem solus orare]]. And he said to his disciples: [[Mark 6:31|Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little|Venite seorsum in desertum locum, et quiescite pusillum]]. For a solitary place, and rest from outward tumult and from meeting with men, helps most of all towards a steady and most pure contemplation of God, a fitting examination of oneself, cleanness of heart, fervour in prayer, sweetness in psalmody, and also the loving, frequent and steady embrace of that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]]. For this reason it is written in Lamentations: [[Lam 3:26|It is good to wait with silence for the salvation of God|Bonum est cum silentio præstolari salutare Dei]]; [[Lam 3:28|He shall sit solitary, and hold his peace|sedebit solitarius et tacebit]], because he will lift himself above himself [Denis reads *quia levabit se super se*; the Douay-Rheims follows *quia levavit super se*, "because he hath taken it up upon himself"]. And Isaias says: [[Is 30:15|in silence and in hope shall your strength be|In silentio et spe erit fortitudo vestra]]. Therefore the penitent says: [[Ps 101:7|I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness|Similis factus sum pelecano solitudinis]]. [[2:14|and I will speak to her heart|Et loquar ad cor ejus]], by enlightening and consoling the mind, according to that word: [[Ps 84:9|I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me|Audiam quid loquatur in me Dominus Deus]]. For those who withdraw from human consolation and converse for God's sake deserve to be taught and gladdened by God. Hence, when the Psalmist had said: [[Ps 30:20|O how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord|Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine!]], he goes on to show to whom it is granted: [[Ps 30:21|Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, from the disturbance of men. Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues|Abscondes eos in abscondito faciei tuæ a conturbatione hominum; proteges eos in tabernaculo tuo a contradictione linguarum]]. Hence also the prophetic revelations were commonly made not among crowds but in places apart.

paras.t: Et dabo ei vinitores, id est pastores, ex eodem loco, id est de numero Christianorum hujusmodi, qui pascant gregem dominicum verbo, vita, et precibus; et vallem Achor ad aperiendam spem. Hæc vallis Achor, seu vallis Conturbationis, est caro nostra mortalis, quæ luctatur et concupiscit adversus spiritum : quæ tunc fidelibus datur, quando per gratiam Dei inordinati motus passionum rationis judicio subjiciuntur : propter quod aperitur eis spes salutis, quando videlicet corpore rationi per omnia obtemperante, serviunt Deo. Ista subjectio mansuetis specialiter est promissa apud Matthæum : Beati mites, quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram.
paras.en: [[2:15|And I will give her vinedressers|Et dabo ei vinitores]], that is, pastors, [[2:15|out of the same place|ex eodem loco]], that is, from the number of such Christians, who may feed the Lord's flock by word, by life and by prayer; [[2:15|and the valley of Achor for an opening of hope|et vallem Achor ad aperiendam spem]]. This valley of Achor, or valley of Trouble, is our mortal flesh, which struggles and [[Gal 5:17|lusteth against the spirit|concupiscit adversus spiritum]] [the margin gives Gal. v, 7; the words are Gal 5:17]: and it is given to the faithful when, by the grace of God, the disordered motions of the passions are made subject to the judgment of reason: for which reason the hope of salvation is opened to them, namely when, the body obeying reason in all things, they serve God. This subjection is promised especially to the meek, in Matthew: [[Matt 5:4|Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land|Beati mites, quoniam ipsi possidebunt terram]].

paras.t: Et canet, id est, Deum laudabit, ibi, videlicet in solitudine, vel prædicta subjectione, juxta dies juventutis suæ, id est, sicut fecit Ecclesia primitiva, et juxta dies ascensionis suæ de terra Ægypti, id est, quemadmodum egit in conversionis suæ exordio, quando de sæculari conversatione et mundi hujus caligine, ad spiritualem vitam accessit. Ut enim Apostolus asserit, Deus eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam (quod per Ægyptum, quæ interpretatur tenebræ, figuratur), et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ. Solet autem in principio conversionis esse specialis fervor devotionis. Sed multi quum spiritu cœperint, carne consummantur : qui tamen quum præinducto modo fuerint lactati, abstracti, atque affati a Deo, redeunt pristinum ad fervorem, et denuo divinis intenti sunt laudibus, sicut olim, ita ut impleant illud Apostoli ad Ephesios : Implemini Spiritu Sancto, loquentes vobismetipsis in psalmis, et hymnis, et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino, gratias agentes pro omnibus semper. Illud quoque in Psalmo : Cantabo Domino in vita mea, psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum.
paras.en: [[2:15|and she shall sing|Et canet]], that is, she shall praise God, [[2:15|there|ibi]], namely in solitude, or in the subjection spoken of, [[2:15|according to the days of her youth|juxta dies juventutis suæ]], that is, as the primitive Church did, [[2:15|and according to the days of her coming up out of the land of Egypt|et juxta dies ascensionis suæ de terra Ægypti]], that is, as she did at the beginning of her conversion, when from a worldly way of life and the darkness of this world she came to the spiritual life. For, as the Apostle asserts, God did [[Gal 1:4|deliver us from this present wicked world|eripuit nos de præsenti sæculo nequam]] (which is figured by Egypt, which is interpreted *darkness*), [[Col 1:13|and hath translated us into the kingdom of the Son of his love|et transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suæ]]. Now at the beginning of conversion there is commonly a special fervour of devotion. But many, having begun in the spirit, end in the flesh[[Gal 3:3||]]; yet these, when they have been given milk, drawn apart and spoken to by God in the way described, return to their former fervour and are once more intent on the divine praises, as before, so that they fulfil that word of the Apostle to the Ephesians: [[Eph 5:18|be ye filled with the Holy Spirit|Implemini Spiritu Sancto]], [[Eph 5:19|Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual canticles, singing and making melody in your hearts to the Lord|loquentes vobismetipsis in psalmis, et hymnis, et canticis spiritualibus, cantantes et psallentes in cordibus vestris Domino]]: [[Eph 5:20|Giving thanks always for all things|gratias agentes pro omnibus semper]]. And that word in the Psalm: [[Ps 103:33|I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being|Cantabo Domino in vita mea, psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum]] [the margin gives Ps. cxii, 33; the words are Ps 103:33].

paras.t: Et sponsabo te mihi in sempiternum. Multiplex est desponsatio Dei cum rationali creatura, et secundum hoc assignatur multiplices nuptiæ. Est enim desponsatio personalis, videlicet hypostatica unio Verbi cum natura humana, cujus thalamus fuit uterus Virginis, juxta illud : Ipse tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo. De quibus nuptiis habetur in Evangelio : Simile est regnum cœlorum homini regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo. Secunda est desponsatio spiritualis et temporalis per fidem et gratiam, de qua agitur modo quum dicitur, Desponsabo te mihi in fide. Tertia est desponsatio spiritualis et æternalis in palatio majestatis per beatificam visionem, de qua in Matthæo habetur : Quæ paratæ erant, intraverunt cum eo ad nuptias. Sunt quoque nuptiæ carnales et sacramentales. Sacramentales autem in paradiso, a Deo cœptæ, institutæ sunt. Unde de eis quoque scriptum est : Erunt duo in carne una. Dicitque Apostolus : Sacramentum hoc magnum est; ego autem dico in Christo et in Ecclesia. Denique, quam ineffabilis dignitas animæ est, ut sit sponsa dilecti ac unigeniti Filii Dei! Expurget se ergo ab omni affectu carnali, et sola quærat cœlestia, quatenus Sponso suo pura, stabilita ac integra mente adhæreat.
paras.en: [[2:19|And I will espouse thee to me for ever|Et sponsabo te mihi in sempiternum]]. Manifold is the espousal of God with the rational creature, and accordingly manifold nuptials are distinguished. For there is the personal espousal, namely the hypostatic union of the Word with human nature [that is, the union of the human nature with the Word in his one Person], whose bridechamber was the womb of the Virgin, according to that word: [[Ps 18:6|as a bridegroom coming out of his bridechamber|tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo]]. Of these nuptials it is said in the Gospel: [[Matt 22:2|The kingdom of heaven is likened to a king who made a marriage for his son|Simile est regnum cœlorum homini regi, qui fecit nuptias filio suo]]. The second is the espousal spiritual and in time, by faith and grace, which is treated now when it is said: [[2:20|I will espouse thee to me in faith|Desponsabo te mihi in fide]]. The third is the espousal spiritual and eternal in the palace of majesty, by the beatific vision, of which it is said in Matthew: [[Matt 25:10|they that were ready went in with him to the marriage|Quæ paratæ erant, intraverunt cum eo ad nuptias]]. There are also carnal and sacramental nuptials; and the sacramental were begun and instituted by God in paradise. Hence of them too it is written: [[Gen 2:24|they shall be two in one flesh|Erunt duo in carne una]]. And the Apostle says: [[Eph 5:32|This is a great sacrament: but I speak in Christ and in the church|Sacramentum hoc magnum est; ego autem dico in Christo et in Ecclesia]]. Lastly, how ineffable is the dignity of the soul, that she should be the bride of the beloved and only-begotten Son of God! Let her therefore purge herself of every carnal affection and seek heavenly things alone, so that she may cleave to her Bridegroom with a pure, steadfast and undivided mind.

paras.t: Et erit : In die illa, dicit Dominus, exaudiam cœlos, et illi exaudient terram. Istud secundum sensum in præcedenti articulo positum, quotidie adimpletur, dum Deus homines virtuosos, quorum conversatio in cœlis est, exaudit pro se ipsis et aliis. Illi quoque exaudiunt terram, id est peccatores et pœnitentes, auxiliando eis pro posse in omnibus, utpote instruendo, orando, increpando, et gratiam sibi concessam, ipsis liberalissime impertiendo.
paras.en: [[2:21|And it shall come to pass in that day|Et erit : In die illa]]: [[2:21|saith the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth|dicit Dominus, exaudiam cœlos, et illi exaudient terram]]. This, in the sense set out in the preceding article, is fulfilled daily, when God hears virtuous men, whose conversation is in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], for themselves and for others. They too hear the earth, that is, sinners and penitents, by helping them as far as they can in all things, namely by instructing, praying, rebuking, and most generously sharing with them the grace granted to themselves.

paras.t: Postremo moralitas eorum quæ nunc omissa sunt, patet ex præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: Lastly, the moral sense of the things now passed over is plain from the preceding article.

3.title: ELUCIDATIO CAPITULI TERTII : ET DIXIT DOMINUS AD ME : ADHUC VADE.
3.title_en: Explanation of the third chapter: And the Lord said to me: Go yet again.

paras.t: CONSEQUENTER prænuntiatur verbis et facto Judæorum ultima ac longissima derelictio, atque eorumdem circa finem mundi finalis conversio. Ut enim in primi expositione capituli habitum est, Prophetæ quandoque verbis, interdum factis prophetant.
paras.en: NEXT there are foretold, in word and in deed, the last and longest abandonment of the Jews, and their final conversion about the end of the world. For, as was said in the exposition of the first chapter, the Prophets sometimes prophesy by words, sometimes by deeds.

paras.t: Et dixit Dominus ad me : Adhuc vade et dilige mulierem dilectam amico. Sicut jam semel, me imperante, ivisti et accepisti fornicariam, et filios fornicationum tibi fecisti, sic nunc denuo vade et dilige mulierem dilectam amico, id est, quæ viro suo ac sponso dilecta fuit et cognita antequam adulteraretur, et adulteram, quæ viro suo fidem conjugalem non conservavit, propter quod juste ab eo dimissa est. Hanc mulierem jubetur Propheta diligere, ut retrahat eam ab adulteriis, non ut ei copuletur sive condormiat : non enim cognovit eam, secundum Hieronymum. Porro dilectio ista, figurativa fuit dilectionis Dei ad filios Israel, spiritualiter cum idolis adulterantes. Ideo subditur : sicut diligit Dominus filios Israel, id est, sic dilige hanc indignam, a qua non diligeris, sed aspernaris, sicut diligit Dominus, vel sicut ego Dominus diligo Israeliticum populum, a quo non amor, sed spernor. Unde in hoc est similitudo, quod adultera et populus Israel diliguntur gratuite, et ob similem finem, videlicet ut cessent a culpa.
paras.en: [[3:1|And the Lord said to me: Go yet again|Et dixit Dominus ad me : Adhuc vade]] [[3:1|and love a woman beloved of her friend|et dilige mulierem dilectam amico]]. As once already, at my command, thou didst go and take a harlot, and didst get thee children of fornications, so now go again and love a woman beloved of her friend [the Latin *amico* also means "lover"], that is, one who was beloved of her husband and spouse and known by him before she became an adulteress, [[3:1|and an adulteress|et adulteram]], one who did not keep conjugal faith with her husband, for which she was justly put away by him. The Prophet is commanded to love this woman so as to draw her back from her adulteries, not to be joined with her or sleep with her: for he did not know her, according to Jerome. Now this love was a figure of God's love for the children of Israel, who were committing adultery spiritually with idols. Therefore it is added: [[3:1|as the Lord loveth the children of Israel|sicut diligit Dominus filios Israel]], that is, so love this unworthy woman, by whom thou art not loved but spurned, [[3:1|as the Lord loveth|sicut diligit Dominus]], or as I the Lord love the Israelite people, by whom I am not loved but spurned. Hence the likeness lies in this, that the adulteress and the people of Israel are both loved freely, and for a like end, namely that they may cease from sin.

paras.t: Et ipsi filii Israel respectant ad deos alienos, id est, idola frequenter adspiciunt cum veneratione et cultu nefario, et diligunt vinacia, id est acina seu folliculos, uvarum, ex quibus vinaciis expressus est vini liquor. Sicque vinacia vacua permanserunt. Per hæc vinacia uvarum, intelliguntur vituli aurei, et cetera idolorum portenta, quæ filii Israel coluerunt ; vel dæmones, secundum Hieronymum, Bedam, et Glossam, quos coluerunt in idolis. Qui, secundum Hieronymum, a propria dignitate prolapsi sunt, et nihil antiquæ gratiæ possidentes, aridi sunt et veteri siccitate marcescentes : propter quod per vinacia designantur. Denique Beda dicit, et partim habetur in Glossa, quod dæmones quamdiu in sua dignitate steterunt, velut uvæ erant, id est pinguedine Spiritus Sancti refecti ; postquam vero superbientes, Deo assimilari voluerunt, evacuati gratia Spiritus Sancti, velut steriles de cœlo projecti sunt. Ex quibus sequi videtur, quod fuerunt in gratia gratum faciente creati, præsertim quum asserat Glossa quod erant in magna pinguedine Spiritus Sancti creati : quod Thomas et alii multi defendunt.
paras.en: [[3:1|and they look to strange gods|Et ipsi filii Israel respectant ad deos alienos]], that is, they often gaze upon idols with veneration and wicked worship, [[3:1|and love the husks|et diligunt vinacia]], that is, the skins or hulls, [[3:1|of the grapes|uvarum]], from which husks the juice of the wine has been pressed out, so that the husks remained empty. By these husks of the grapes are understood the golden calves and the other monstrous idols which the children of Israel worshipped; or the demons, according to Jerome, Bede and the Gloss, whom they worshipped in the idols. These, according to Jerome, fell from their own dignity and, possessing nothing of their former grace, are dry and withering with an old drought: for which reason they are signified by husks. Lastly, Bede says, and it is partly found in the Gloss, that the demons, so long as they stood in their dignity, were like grapes, that is, filled with the richness of the Holy Ghost; but after, swelling with pride, they wished to be made like to God, they were emptied of the grace of the Holy Ghost and cast down from heaven as barren things. From this it seems to follow that they were created in sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], especially since the Gloss asserts that they were created in great richness of the Holy Ghost: which Thomas and many others maintain.

paras.t: Quæritur, quomodo Deus diligere dicitur filios Israel tam iniquos, quum in libro Sapientiæ scriptum sit, Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus ; atque in Psalmo, Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem. Et respondendum, quod Deus diligit omne creatum, quantum ad id quod est per naturam. Quæ quum sit a bono Creatore producta, bona amabilisque consistit. Unde et Deus conservat eam in esse. Peccatores quoque diligere dicitur, quia quantum in se est, non vult mortem eorum, sed ut convertantur et vivant, et debitam eorum vindictam misericorditer differt, semperque paratus est eorum pœnitentiam acceptare ac indulgere. Sic quoque dilexit idololatras Israeliticos. Vel dicitur eos diligere propter temporalia bona quæ exhibet eis, et quia finaliter convertentur. Verumtamen Deus non dicitur reprobos absolute diligere, quoniam voluntate simpliciter dicta seu consequente non vult, nec impendit eis, bona gratiæ finalis in præsenti, bonaque gloriæ in futuro.
paras.en: It is asked how God is said to love the children of Israel, wicked as they were, since it is written in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful|Odio sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 5:7|Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity|Odisti omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]]. The answer is that God loves every created thing as to what it is by nature; for this, since it was brought forth by a good Creator, is good and lovable, and so God also keeps it in being. He is said to love sinners too, because, as far as lies in Him, He wills not their death but that they be converted and live[[Ezech 18:23||]], and mercifully puts off the punishment they deserve, and is ever ready to accept their repentance and to forgive. So too He loved the idolatrous Israelites. Or He is said to love them because of the temporal goods He bestows on them, and because they will at last be converted. Nevertheless God is not said to love the reprobate absolutely, since by His will taken simply, or consequent will [that is, His will regarding a person as he finally turns out, as distinct from the antecedent will by which He wills all to be saved], He does not will for them, nor bestow on them, the goods of final grace in the present life and the goods of glory in the life to come.

paras.t: Pro eo quod nostra translatio habet, Dilectam amico, quidam dicunt in Hebræo haberi, Dilectam socio. Sed his obviat, quod Septuaginta interpretes pro Dilectam amico, transtulerunt, Diligentem mala. Unde probabilius puto, quod nomen Hebraicum, ad amicum, ad socium, et ad mala, æquivocum sit. Nam et Hieronymus dicit, quod significet amicum et mala. Sicque in Hebræo non magis habetur, Dilectam socio, quam, Dilectam amico, sed aliquid ad utrumque indifferens. Rursus pro eo quod nostra translatio habet, Vinacia, dicunt in Hebræo haberi, Scyphos, vel, Dolia, ita quod filii Israel arguuntur de ebrietate, eo quod amant vasa vinorum, propter vina in eis contenta. Quibus obviat, quod nec Septuaginta, nec Symmachus, nec Aquila sic transtulerunt. Unde aptius dici potest, quod sermo Hebraicus sit æquivocus, et sic nostra translatio non dissonat ab Hebræo, nec aliter habere dicenda est, quam Hebraica continet veritas.
paras.en: Where our translation has [[3:1|beloved of her friend|Dilectam amico]], some say that the Hebrew has "beloved of her companion". But against them stands the fact that the Seventy translators, for "beloved of her friend", rendered "loving evil things". Hence I think it more probable that the Hebrew word is equivocal, meaning "friend", "companion" and "evil things"; for Jerome too says that it means both "friend" and "evil things" [the Hebrew consonants *r'* can be read as *rea'*, friend, or *ra'*, evil]. And so the Hebrew has no more "beloved of her companion" than "beloved of her friend", but something open to either. Again, where our translation has [[3:1|husks|Vinacia]], they say that the Hebrew has "cups" or "casks", so that the children of Israel are rebuked for drunkenness, because they love the vessels of wine for the wine they hold. Against them stands the fact that neither the Seventy, nor Symmachus, nor Aquila so translated. Hence it can more fittingly be said that the Hebrew word is equivocal, and so our translation is not at odds with the Hebrew, nor is it to be said to read otherwise than the Hebrew verity holds.

paras.t: Præterea ista adultera, secundum Hieronymum, præsens tempus significat Judæorum, qui sine notitia Scripturarum et gratia Spiritus Sancti diliguntur modo prætacto a Domino, qui omnium exspectat salutem, et pœnitentibus aperit januam. Unde per filios Israel supra significatæ sunt decem tribus. Sed hoc loco per filios Israel, intelliguntur duodecim tribus nunc derelictæ a Deo, ut dicit Hieronymus. Et ita adultera ista designat totum populum Judæorum incredulum, non decem tribus, vel Juda dumtaxat : quamvis quidam dicunt oppositum. Et hoc in sequentibus clarius innotescet.
paras.en: Moreover, according to Jerome, this adulteress signifies the present time of the Jews, who, without understanding of the Scriptures and without the grace of the Holy Ghost, are loved, in the manner just touched on, by the Lord, who awaits the salvation of all and opens the door to the penitent. Hence [or perhaps "now"] above, by the children of Israel the ten tribes were signified; but in this place by the children of Israel are understood the twelve tribes, now abandoned by God, as Jerome says. And so this adulteress stands for the whole unbelieving people of the Jews, not for the ten tribes, or Juda only: though some say the opposite. And this will become clearer in what follows.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur obedientia Prophetæ, seu divinæ exsecutio jussionis. Et fodi eam mihi, id est, adulteram istam conduxi, non ut ei condormiam, sed ut ipsa pretio, quo eam conduco, contenta, cesset adulterare, nec aliis solito copuletur. Septuaginta transtulerunt, Conduxi eam mihi. Sed Hieronymus transtulit, Fodi, ad insinuandum quod ista adultera Synagogam designet, quæ in Scripturis dicitur vinea Dei. Vinea autem colitur fossione. Quindecim argenteis, id est tot nummis, et coro, id est triginta modiis, hordei, et dimidio coro, id est quindecim modiis, hoc est quadraginta quinque modiis hordei. Per quindecim argenteos designatur, quod filii Israel quinto decimo die mensis primi de Ægypto educti sunt, et in Dei servitutem conducti, primogenitis Ægyptiorum percussis. Per modios vero quadraginta quinque, significatur quod filii Israel quadragesimo quinto die postquam Ægyptum egressi sunt, venerunt ad montem Sinai : in quo divino obsequio vehementius deputati sunt, legem recipiendo. Quæ omnia patent in Exodo.
paras.en: Next is described the obedience of the Prophet, or the carrying out of the divine command. [[3:2|And I bought her to me|Et fodi eam mihi]], that is, I hired this adulteress, not to sleep with her, but so that, content with the price for which I hire her, she might cease to commit adultery and not be joined with others as she used to be. The Seventy rendered: I hired her to me. But Jerome rendered *fodi* [literally "I dug"], to suggest that this adulteress signifies the Synagogue, which in the Scriptures is called the vineyard of God; and a vineyard is tilled by digging. [[3:2|for fifteen pieces of silver|Quindecim argenteis]], that is, so many coins, [[3:2|and for a core|et coro]], that is, thirty measures, [[3:2|of barley, and for half a core|hordei, et dimidio coro]], that is, fifteen measures: that is, forty-five measures of barley. By the fifteen pieces of silver is signified that the children of Israel were brought out of Egypt on the fifteenth day of the first month, and hired into the service of God, when the firstborn of the Egyptians had been struck down. By the forty-five measures is signified that on the forty-fifth day after they went out of Egypt the children of Israel came to Mount Sinai, where, by receiving the law, they were bound more strongly to the service of God. All of which is plain in Exodus[[Ex 12:1||]][[Ex 19:1||]] [the margin gives "Exod. xii, xix, etc."; the fifteenth day of the first month is named at Num 33:3].

paras.t: Et dixi ad eam : Dies multos, id est longo tempore, exspectabis me, propter pretium istud quo te conduxi ne forniceris. Non fornicaberis cum alienis, et non eris viro, id est, nulli jungeris, etiam nec mihi qui te conduxi, sed absque coitu materiali et adulterino manebis : ad insinuandum quod Judæi in hac captivitate nec idola colant, nec Deum habeant verum. Sicque nec spiritualiter per idololatriam fornicantur, nec Sponso cœlesti junguntur. Sed et ego exspectabo te, ut tuam fidelitatem et continentiam comprobem atque experiar. Nec interim fornicabor, sed pari par referam, ne putes tibi factam injuriam. Per hoc designatur, quod Dominus Judæorum finalem conversionem exspectat.
paras.en: [[3:3|And I said to her|Et dixi ad eam]]: [[3:3|many days|Dies multos]], that is, for a long time, [[3:3|Thou shalt wait for me|exspectabis me]], because of this price for which I hired thee, that thou mayest not play the harlot. [[3:3|thou shalt not play the harlot|Non fornicaberis]] with strangers, [[3:3|and thou shalt be no man's|et non eris viro]], that is, thou shalt be joined to no one, not even to me who hired thee, but shalt remain without bodily and adulterous intercourse: to suggest that the Jews in this captivity neither worship idols nor have the true God. And so they neither commit fornication spiritually by idolatry, nor are joined to the heavenly Spouse. [[3:3|and I also will wait for thee|Sed et ego exspectabo te]], to prove and try thy fidelity and continence. Nor meanwhile will I commit fornication, but I will repay like with like, lest thou think a wrong has been done thee. By this is signified that the Lord awaits the final conversion of the Jews.

paras.t: Deinde ponitur ratio hujus prophetici facti, et figura per rem figuratam exponitur. Quia, id est, ideo dixi quod diu me exspectabis, nec eris viro, dies multos, videlicet usque ad adventum Eliæ, sedebunt, id est, erunt seu permanebunt, filii Israel, id est duodecim tribus, qui proprie sedent, non stant, quoniam terrenis immersi et vitiis pressi nequeunt contemplari cœlestia, nec ad virtutes assurgere. Unde terrenam prosperitatem temporaleque regnum præstolantur in Messiæ adventu. Sine rege, et sine principe, id est pontifice : non enim habent jam regem aut principem de semine suo, sed aliorum ditione subduntur. Potestque per regem et principem, idem intelligi Christus, de quo Jeremias ait : Regnabit Rex et sapiens erit. Ezechiel quoque de ipso loquitur : Servus meus David princeps eorum. Et sine sacrificio, et sine altari : quia a tempore Titi ac Romanorum, destructa Jerusalem et templo combusto, non potuerunt hostias immolare legales, nec habuerunt altare. Non enim possunt holocausta sua quocumque loco offerre, sed in eo dumtaxat licuit eis hæc immolare, quem Deus specialiter ad hoc elegit, videlicet in Jerusalem. Propter quod in Deuteronomio scriptum est : Cave ne offeras holocausta tua in omni loco quem videris ; sed in eo quem elegerit Dominus in una tribuum tuarum.
paras.en: Then is given the reason for this prophetic deed, and the figure is explained by the thing figured. [[3:4|For|Quia]], that is, I said that thou shalt wait for me long and shalt be no man's for this reason: [[3:4|many days|dies multos]], namely until the coming of Elias, [[3:4|shall sit|sedebunt]], that is, shall be or remain, [[3:4|the children of Israel|filii Israel]], that is, the twelve tribes, who properly sit and do not stand, since, sunk in earthly things and weighed down by vices, they cannot contemplate heavenly things nor rise up to the virtues. Hence they look for earthly prosperity and a temporal kingdom at the coming of the Messias. [[3:4|without king, and without prince|Sine rege, et sine principe]], that is, without high priest: for they have now no king or prince of their own seed, but are subject to the rule of others. And by king and prince the same Christ can be understood, of whom Jeremias says: [[Jer 23:5|a king shall reign, and shall be wise|Regnabit Rex et sapiens erit]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxiii, 5; the words are at Jer 23:5]. Ezechiel too speaks of Him: [[Ezech 34:24|my servant David the prince|Servus meus David princeps]] of them [Denis's wording, *princeps eorum*, is closer to Ezech 37:25]. [[3:4|and without sacrifice, and without altar|Et sine sacrificio, et sine altari]]: because since the time of Titus and the Romans, Jerusalem having been destroyed and the temple burnt, they have not been able to offer the victims of the law, nor have they had an altar. For they cannot offer their holocausts in any place they please; it was lawful for them to offer these only in the place which God chose especially for this, namely in Jerusalem. For which reason it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 12:13|Beware lest thou offer thy holocausts in every place that thou shalt see|Cave ne offeras holocausta tua in omni loco quem videris]]; [[Deut 12:14|But in the place which the Lord shall choose in one of thy tribes|sed in eo quem elegerit Dominus in una tribuum tuarum]].

paras.t: Et sine ephod, id est veste sacerdotali, quod proprie dicitur superhumerale. Quandoque etiam ephod vocatur vestis linea cujus usus erat in Dei obsequio, quemadmodum primo Regum legitur Samuel indutus ephod lineo : quo et David erat indutus, ludens et saliens ante Dei arcam. Verumtamen hoc loco sumitur ephod pro quocumque indumento sacerdotali. Propterea pro Ephod, Septuaginta transtulerunt, Sacerdotium. Et sine theraphim, id est imaginibus Cherubim et Seraphim quæ erant in templo, quæ simul cum templo cessaverunt. Theraphim proprie appellantur simulacra seu figuræ ; sed nunc pro Cherubim ac Seraphim aliisve quibuslibet templi ornamentis sumuntur, secundum Hieronymum. Quidam per theraphim intelligunt imagines in quibus solebant dæmones dare responsa : quibus obviat, quod omnia quibus filii Israel dicuntur hoc loco privari, pertinere videntur ad pœnam eorum atque miseriam propter eorum peccata. Esse vero sine hujusmodi theraphim, felicius est quam ea habere. Denique ephod et theraphim erant in habitaculo Levitæ qui erat sacerdos Michæ, ut legitur in fine Judicum.
paras.en: [[3:4|and without ephod|Et sine ephod]], that is, the priestly vestment, which is properly called the superhumeral. Sometimes too a linen garment used in the service of God is called an ephod, as we read in the first book of Kings that Samuel was clothed with a linen ephod[[1 Kings 2:18||]]; and David too was clothed with it, playing and leaping before the ark of God[[2 Kings 6:14||]]. In this place, however, ephod is taken for any priestly garment; and therefore for "ephod" the Seventy rendered "priesthood". [[3:4|and without theraphim|Et sine theraphim]], that is, the images of the Cherubim and Seraphim that were in the temple, which ceased together with the temple. Theraphim are properly called images or figures; but here they are taken for the Cherubim and Seraphim or any other ornaments of the temple, according to Jerome. Some understand by theraphim the images in which the demons used to give answers: against whom stands the fact that all the things of which the children of Israel are here said to be deprived seem to belong to their punishment and misery for their sins; whereas to be without theraphim of that kind is happier than to have them. Lastly, the ephod and the theraphim were in the dwelling of the Levite who was Micha's priest, as we read at the end of Judges[[Judg 17:5||]].

paras.t: Et post hæc, finita captivitate ista longissima, revertentur filii Israel, spirituali reversione, redeundo ab infidelitate et vitiis ad fidem Christi atque virtutes : quod fiet circa finem mundi, prædicantibus Enoch atque Elia ; et quærent sanctis affectibus, fide atque operibus, Dominum Deum suum, quem nunc interim non habent, sed per incredulitatem perdiderunt, et David regem suum, id est Christum (ut omnes exponunt), de stirpe David progenitum : qui est verus David, id est desiderabilis adspectu et manu fortis ; de quo cantatur, Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum ; et, In quem desiderant angeli prospicere ; itemque, Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio. Frequenter autem in Scripturis propheticis exprimitur Christus nomine David, ut quum dicit Jeremias : Servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis. Iste est igitur rex Judæorum, secundum quod ait : Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus. Habet namque in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum, Rex regum et Dominus dominantium. Hunc quærent Judæi, detecta Antichristi fallacia. Unde translatio Chaldaica authentica apud Hebræos, habet hoc loco : Post hoc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent cultum Dei sui, et obedient Messiæ filio David.
paras.en: [[3:5|And after this|Et post hæc]], when this longest captivity is ended, [[3:5|the children of Israel shall return|revertentur filii Israel]] by a spiritual return, coming back from unbelief and vices to the faith of Christ and the virtues: which will come to pass about the end of the world, when Henoch and Elias preach[[Mal 4:5||]][[Mal 4:6||]]; [[3:5|and shall seek|et quærent]], with holy affections, with faith and works, [[3:5|the Lord, their God|Dominum Deum suum]], whom for the present they have not, but have lost through unbelief, [[3:5|and David, their king|et David regem suum]], that is, Christ (as all expound it), born of the stock of David: who is the true David, that is, "desirable to behold" and "strong of hand" [the meanings given for the name David]; of whom it is sung: [[Ps 44:3|Thou art beautiful above the sons of men|Speciosus forma præ filiis hominum]]; and: [[1 Pet 1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|In quem desiderant angeli prospicere]]; and again: [[Ps 23:8|the Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle|Dominus fortis et potens, Dominus potens in prælio]]. Now in the prophetic Scriptures Christ is often expressed by the name of David, as when Jeremias says: [[Jer 30:9|they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up to them|Servient Domino Deo suo, et David regi suo, quem suscitabo eis]]. He then is the king of the Jews, according to what He says: [[Ps 2:6|But I am appointed king by him over Sion, his holy mountain|Ego autem constitutus sum rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum ejus]]. For He hath [[Apoc 19:16|on his garment and on his thigh written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS|in vestimento et in femore suo scriptum, Rex regum et Dominus dominantium]]. Him the Jews will seek, once the deceit of Antichrist has been laid bare. Hence the Chaldee translation, held authentic among the Hebrews, has in this place: After this the children of Israel shall return, and shall seek the worship of their God, and shall obey the Messias, the son of David.

paras.t: Et pavebunt, id est, reverentialem timorem concipient, ad Dominum Salvatorem, fide ejus recepta, et ad bonum, id est beneficia ejus, vel ad promissa cœlestia, ita quod formidabunt esse ingrati vel cœlesti felicitate privari. Unde in Isaia habetur : Dominum exercituum sanctificate ; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester. Sic et nos debemus pavere ad Dominum, et ad bonum ipsius, ut simus tanto amplius timorati, quanto pluribus atque majoribus beneficiis Christi præventi. Sic ergo in novissimo dierum, videlicet circa finem mundi. Nam et nos sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt, secundum Apostolum. In prima quoque Joannis legitur Canonica : Novissima hora est.
paras.en: [[3:5|and they shall fear|Et pavebunt]], that is, they shall conceive a reverential fear, [[3:5|the Lord|ad Dominum]] the Saviour, having received His faith, [[3:5|and his goodness|et ad bonum]], that is, His benefits, or the heavenly promises, so that they will dread being ungrateful or being deprived of heavenly happiness. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 8:13|Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself: and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread|Dominum exercituum sanctificate ; ipse pavor vester, et ipse terror vester]]. So we too ought to fear the Lord and His goodness, being the more God-fearing the more and greater the benefits of Christ with which we have been forestalled. So then: [[3:5|in the last days|in novissimo dierum]], namely about the end of the world. For we too are those [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]], according to the Apostle. And in the first canonical Epistle of John we read: [[1 John 2:18|it is the last hour|Novissima hora est]].

paras.t: Præterea, ut refert Hieronymus, quidam Judæorum referunt præsens capitulum ad Babylonicam captivitatem, quando septuaginta annis desolatum est templum et altare, victimæ quoque et sacerdotium, et postea sub Zorobabel in Judæam reversi sunt. Sed isti assignare non queunt hujus dirissimæ ac longissimæ captivitatis causam, in qua jam mille et quadringentis circiter annis fuerunt, præsertim quum idola detestentur, nisi fateantur se Christum occidisse. Prædictus etiam error destruitur per hoc quod ait Propheta, In novissimo dierum : quasi dicat, In termino ultimæ ætatis mundi. Post Babylonicam quoque captivitatem non receperunt Christum eis missum, nec pavebant ad bonum ejus, nisi paucissimi aliorum respectu. Loquitur ergo de hac eorum captivitate finali, in qua sedent aversi a Deo. De qua Daniel inducit : Finis ejus vastitas, et usque in finem perseverabit desolatio ; et Psalmista : Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos.
paras.en: Moreover, as Jerome relates, some of the Jews refer the present chapter to the Babylonian captivity, when for seventy years the temple and the altar lay desolate, and the victims too and the priesthood, and afterwards under Zorobabel they returned to Judea. But these cannot assign the cause of this most grievous and longest captivity, in which they have now been for about fourteen hundred years, especially since they detest idols, unless they confess that they killed Christ. The aforesaid error is also overthrown by the Prophet's saying, [[3:5|in the last days|In novissimo dierum]]: as if to say, at the close of the last age of the world. Moreover, after the Babylonian captivity they did not receive the Christ sent to them, nor did they [[3:5|fear the Lord, and his goodness|pavebant ad bonum ejus]], save a very few in comparison with the rest. He speaks therefore of this final captivity of theirs, in which they [[3:4|sit|sedent]] turned away from God. Of which Daniel says: [[Dan 9:26|the end thereof shall be waste|Finis ejus vastitas]], and the desolation shall continue even to the end[[Dan 9:27||]] [the margin gives Dan. ix, 26, 27]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 68:25|Pour out thy indignation upon them: and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them.|Effunde super eos iram tuam, et furor iræ tuæ comprehendat eos.]]

paras.t: Postremo, secundum Bedam, præmemorata bona Judæis ablata, nobis spiritualiter sunt collata. Nos enim habemus regem et principem Christum, verumque sacrificium, scilicet corpus et sanguinem Salvatoris ; altare quoque militantis Ecclesiæ toto orbe diffusum, de quo per Malachiam asserit Dominus, In omni loco sacrificatur, et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda ; ephod quoque, videlicet vestes sacerdotales, seu vestem innocentiæ ac simplicitatis ; et theraphim, id est figuram dominicæ crucis, vel signum atque memoriam Dei cordibus nostris impressam, ita ut Paulus testetur : Christo confixus sum cruci ; et, Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto.
paras.en: Lastly, according to Bede, the goods named above, taken away from the Jews, have been bestowed spiritually on us. For we have Christ as [[3:4|king|regem]] and [[3:4|prince|principem]], and the true [[3:4|sacrifice|sacrificium]], namely the body and blood of the Saviour; and the [[3:4|altar|altare]] of the Church militant spread through the whole world, of which the Lord declares through Malachias: [[Mal 1:11|in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation|In omni loco sacrificatur, et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]]; and an [[3:4|ephod|ephod]], namely priestly vestments, or the garment of innocence and simplicity; and [[3:4|theraphim|theraphim]], that is, the figure of the Lord's cross, or the sign and remembrance of God imprinted on our hearts, so that Paul bears witness: [[Gal 2:19|with Christ I am nailed to the cross|Christo confixus sum cruci]]; and: [[Gal 6:17|I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body|Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto]].

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Audite verbum Domini, filii Israel
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel

paras.t: Nunc in hujus capituli principio ponit Propheta Israelis peccata, propter quæ prædicta mala pœnalia meruerunt. Audite verbum Domini, filii Israel, id est decem tribus, quas Propheta, secundum Hieronymum, hoc loco alloquitur. Aliqui tamen referunt ad universum Judaicum populum. Quia judicium est Domino cum habitatoribus terræ, id est prædictis filiis Israel, ita quod Dominus vult cum eis judicium discussionis peragere, ut pateat quod juste procedat. Tale judicium efficit Deus, quando per servos suos ostendit hominum impietatem et suam justitiam. Unde et cum hominibus et ab hominibus dicitur judicari, qui judicant eum juste procedere in peccatorum punitione. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Tibi soli peccavi, ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis, et vincas quum judicaris. Per Ezechielem quoque ait ad impios Israelitas: Judicabor ibi vobiscum facie ad faciem.
paras.en: Now at the beginning of this chapter the Prophet sets out the sins of Israel, for which they deserved the penal evils foretold. [[4:1|Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel|Audite verbum Domini, filii Israel]], that is, the ten tribes, whom, according to Jerome, the Prophet addresses in this place. Some, however, refer it to the whole Jewish people. [[4:1|for the Lord shall enter into judgment with the inhabitants of the land|Quia judicium est Domino cum habitatoribus terræ]], that is, with the aforesaid children of Israel; so that the Lord wills to carry out with them a judgment of examination, that it may be plain that he proceeds justly. God holds such a judgment when through his servants he shows the impiety of men and his own justice. Hence he is also said to be judged with men and by men, who judge that he proceeds justly in punishing sins. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 50:6|To thee only have I sinned|Tibi soli peccavi]], [[Ps 50:6|that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged|ut justificeris in sermonibus tuis, et vincas quum judicaris]]. And by Ezechiel he says to the impious Israelites: [[Ezech 20:35|there will I plead with you face to face|Judicabor ibi vobiscum facie ad faciem]] [*judicabor*, "I will enter into judgment", the same word as in the verse].

paras.t: Non est enim veritas vitæ, id est vera vita secundum divinam legem rectamque rationem regulata, de qua ait Salvator: Omnis qui facit veritatem, venit ad lucem; et Paulus ad Timotheum: Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe, non sublime sapere, etc., ut apprehendant veram vitam. Vel, Non est veritas doctrinæ et sermonis, consistens in vera significatione verborum, et in hoc ut doctrina æternæ sapientiæ consonet, de qua dicit Christus: Si veritatem dico, quare non creditis mihi? Vel, Non est veritas justitiæ, quæ est æquitas vera, divinæ mentis judicio conformata, de qua dicit Psalmista: Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas. Hæc est veritas, quæ defuit filiis […] Israel, et multis jam deest. Et non […] est misericordia ad proximos […] […] […]
paras.en: [[4:1|for there is no truth|Non est enim veritas]] of life, that is, true life ruled according to the divine law and right reason, of which the Saviour says: [[John 3:21|he that doth truth cometh to the light|Omnis qui facit veritatem, venit ad lucem]]; and Paul to Timothy: [[1 Tim 6:17|Charge the rich of this world not to be highminded|Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe, non sublime sapere]], etc., [[1 Tim 6:19|that they may lay hold on the true life|ut apprehendant veram vitam]]. Or: there is no truth of doctrine and speech, which consists in the true meaning of words, and in this, that doctrine agree with eternal wisdom; of which Christ says: [[John 8:46|If I say the truth to you, why do you not believe me|Si veritatem dico, quare non creditis mihi?]] Or: there is no truth of justice, which is true equity, conformed to the judgment of the divine mind; of which the Psalmist says: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxiv, 10; the verse is Ps 24:10]. This is the truth which was wanting to the children […] of Israel, and is now wanting to many. [[4:1|and there is no|Et non]] […] [[4:1|mercy|est misericordia]] towards neighbours […] […] […]

paras.t: Et non est scientia Dei formata ac salutaris, id est caritate et operibus bonis ornata, de qua Scriptura testatur: Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum. Et Joannes ait: In hoc scimus quoniam cognovimus Deum, si mandata ejus servamus. Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non servat, mendax est. In terra, id est in terrenis hominibus, scilicet filiis Israel colentibus idola, qui unius veri Dei notitiam abjecerunt. Istud præcipue verum est de scientia illa quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti. Illa enim non habetur sine caritate et gratia gratum faciente. Sed quum dicat, Scientia Dei, potest per istam scientiam intelligi sapientia quæ est summi Dei vera ac saporosa notitia, de qua dicit Sapiens: In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Scientia vero Dei informis et nuda, potest esse in impiis, quum ad Romanos dicat Apostolus: Quum cognovissent Deum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt. Dicit autem Hieronymus: Veritas absque misericordia sustineri non potest, et misericordia absque veritate efficit negligentes. Quod de veritate justitiæ maxime verum est. Hinc in Proverbiis scriptum est: Misericordia et veritas non te deserant, et invenies gratiam coram Deo et hominibus.
paras.en: [[4:1|and there is no knowledge of God|Et non est scientia Dei]], formed and saving, that is, adorned with charity and good works [*formata*: knowledge "formed" by charity, as opposed to the "unformed" knowledge spoken of below], of which Scripture testifies: [[Wis 10:10|gave him the knowledge of the holy things|Dedit illi scientiam Sanctorum]]. And John says: [[1 John 2:3|by this we know that we have known him, if we keep his commandments|In hoc scimus quoniam cognovimus Deum, si mandata ejus servamus]]. [[1 John 2:4|He who saith that he knoweth him and keepeth not his commandments is a liar|Qui dicit se nosse Deum, et mandata ejus non servat, mendax est]]. [[4:1|in the land|In terra]], that is, in earthly men, namely the children of Israel worshipping idols, who cast away the knowledge of the one true God. This is true above all of that knowledge which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]]: for that is not had without charity and sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God]. But since he says, *knowledge of God*, by this knowledge may be understood the wisdom which is a true and savoury knowledge of the most high God [*saporosa*: Denis plays on *sapientia* and *sapor*, "taste"], of which the Wise Man says: [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. But an unformed and bare knowledge of God can be in the wicked, since the Apostle says to the Romans: [[Rom 1:21|when they knew God, they have not glorified him as God|Quum cognovissent Deum, non sicut Deum glorificaverunt]]. And Jerome says: Truth without mercy cannot be borne, and mercy without truth makes men negligent. This is most true of the truth of justice. Hence it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:3|Let not mercy aud truth leave thee|Misericordia et veritas non te deserant]], [[Prov 3:4|thou shalt find grace|et invenies gratiam]] [[Prov 3:4|before God and men|coram Deo et hominibus]].

paras.t: Isaias quoque ait: Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes. Quomodo ergo nunc dicitur, Non est scientia Domini in terra? Et respondendum, quod Isaias loquitur pro tempore Christi et evangelicæ legis, quando primo in Judæa, deinde in toto mundo, prædicata est evangelicæ veritatis doctrina. Isaias quoque per terram intelligit electos habitantes in terra. Aliter vero loquitur Osee, ut patuit.
paras.en: Isaias also says: [[Is 11:9|the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea|Repleta est terra scientia Domini, sicut aquæ maris operientes]]. How then is it said now, *There is no knowledge of the Lord in the land*? The answer is that Isaias speaks of the time of Christ and of the law of the Gospel, when the doctrine of the Gospel truth was preached first in Judea, then in all the world. Isaias also understands by the earth the elect who dwell on the earth. But Osee speaks otherwise, as has been shown.

paras.t: Maledictum, id est blasphemia contra Deum, vel convitium in proximum, seu sermo maledicus. Unde dicit Apostolus: Neque maledici regnum Dei possidebunt. Et […] est: Benedicite maledicentibus vobis; benedicite et nolite maledicere. Et mendacium: de quo Sapiens ait, Os quod mentitur, occidit animam; itemque Psalmista, Perdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium; et homicidium; et furtum: quod est contra justitiam, et ex genere mortale, quamvis interdum propter parvitatem nocumenti, sit veniale, præsertim dum probabiliter æstimatur quod possessori seu domino, si id sciret, non displiceret; et adulterium, inundaverunt, id est, copiose eruperunt, seu abundaverunt in filiis Israel, ita quod non solum misericordia, veritate, scientia caruerunt, sed et oppositis impleti sunt vitiis. Et sanguis sanguinem tetigit, dum unus ab alio læsus est, vel se invicem vulneraverunt. Vel, Sanguis sanguinem tetigit, id est, peccatum peccato continuatum est, et veteribus vitiis nova addiderunt impœnitentes. Quibus Isaias asserit: Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum. Quocontra habetur in Ecclesiastico: Non adjicias peccatum super peccatum; subito enim veniet ira Dei, et in die vindictæ disperdet te. Vel, sanguis sanguinem tangit, dum calor concupiscentiæ tendit in actum, seu carnalis affectio suo copulatur objecto. Septuaginta transtulerunt sic, Et sanguinem sanguini miscuerunt.
paras.en: [[4:2|Cursing|Maledictum]], that is, blasphemy against God, or abuse against one's neighbour, or evil-speaking. Hence the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 6:10|nor railers nor extortioners shall possess the kingdom of God|Neque maledici regnum Dei possidebunt]]. And it is […]: Bless them that curse you [the margin gives Rom. xii, 14, which reads "Bless them that persecute you"; Denis's first words are those of Luke 6:28]; [[Rom 12:14|bless, and curse not|benedicite et nolite maledicere]]. [[4:2|and lying|Et mendacium]]: of which the Wise Man says, [[Wis 1:11|the mouth that belieth, killeth the soul|Os quod mentitur, occidit animam]]; and the Psalmist likewise, [[Ps 5:7|thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie|Perdes omnes qui loquuntur mendacium]]; [[4:2|and killing, and theft|et homicidium; et furtum]]: which is against justice, and mortal in its kind, though sometimes, because the harm is slight, it is venial, especially when it is reasonably judged that the possessor or owner would not be displeased if he knew of it; [[4:2|and adultery, have overflowed|et adulterium, inundaverunt]], that is, have broken out in plenty, or abounded among the children of Israel; so that they not only lacked mercy, truth and knowledge, but were also filled with the opposite vices. [[4:2|and blood hath touched blood|Et sanguis sanguinem tetigit]], when one was hurt by another, or they wounded one another. Or, *blood hath touched blood*, that is, sin has been joined on to sin, and being impenitent they have added new vices to the old. To these Isaias declares: [[Is 5:18|Woe to you that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as the rope of a cart|Væ qui trahitis iniquitatem in funiculis vanitatis, et quasi vinculum plaustri peccatum]]. Against this it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:5|add not sin upon sin|Non adjicias peccatum super peccatum]]: [[Ecclus 5:9|For his wrath shall come on a sudden, and in the time of vengeance he will destroy thee|subito enim veniet ira Dei, et in die vindictæ disperdet te]]. Or, blood touches blood when the heat of concupiscence tends to the act, or carnal affection is joined to its object. The Septuagint translated it thus: And they mingled blood with blood.

paras.t: […] mendacia: Nos, inquiunt, scimus quia hic homo peccator est; et, In principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmones. Verumtamen ex consequentibus elucescit, quod ista ad litteram dicantur de Israelitis idololatris pro tempore Osee vel circiter.
paras.en: […] lies: [[John 9:24|We know that this man is a sinner|Nos, inquiunt, scimus quia hic homo peccator est]], they say; and, [[Matt 9:34|By the prince of devils he casteth out devils|In principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmones]]. Yet it is clear from what follows that these things are said literally of the idolatrous Israelites of about the time of Osee.

paras.t: Deinceps ponitur debita pœna pro tantis sceleribus. Propter hoc, id est propter peccata jam dicta, lugebit terra decem tribuum, id est, desolata incultaque erit ad tempus, habitatoribus ejus sublatis. Dicitur enim metaphorice terra lugere, quemadmodum et ridere dum floret atque fructificat.
