Et infirmabitur omnis qui habitat in ea, vel simpliciter omnis homo, vel aliqui de omni genere hominum hujus terræ, vel tam multi, quod alii comparatione eorum quasi nulli videbuntur; in bestia agri et in volucre cœli: id est, habitatores terræ non solum infirmabuntur per hoc quod ipsi dejicientur, sed etiam in hoc quod bestiæ et aves quæ poterant eis esse pro cibo aut solatio, auferentur, vel peste morientur, in vindictam peccatorum. Hujusmodi quoque animantia, secundum Hieronymum, solent deserere terras ab hominibus derelictas. Sed et pisces maris currentis in terra populi Israel (Judæi enim quamlibet magnam aquæ collectionem nominant mare, juxta illud in Genesi: Congregationes aquarum appellavit Deus maria), congregabuntur in mortem, id est deficient. Unde, ut Lyra dicit, Hebræi dicunt, Finientur. Et Septuaginta transtulerunt, Pisces maris deficient, scilicet ea ratione qua bestiæ et volucres.
paras.en: Next is set out the punishment due for such great crimes. [[4:3|Therefore|Propter hoc]], that is, because of the sins already named, [[4:3|shall the land mourn|lugebit terra]] of the ten tribes, that is, it shall be desolate and untilled for a time, its inhabitants being taken away. For the land is said metaphorically to mourn, as also to laugh when it flowers and bears fruit. [[4:3|and every one that dwelleth in it shall languish|Et infirmabitur omnis qui habitat in ea]]: either simply every man, or some of every kind of men of this land, or so many that the others will seem as nothing beside them; [[4:3|with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of the air|in bestia agri et in volucre cœli]]: that is, the inhabitants of the land shall languish not only in that they themselves shall be cast down, but also in that the beasts and birds, which could have served them for food or comfort, shall be taken away, or shall die of pestilence, in punishment of sins. Such creatures too, according to Jerome, are wont to forsake lands abandoned by men. [[4:3|yea, the fishes of the sea also|Sed et pisces maris]] running in the land of the people of Israel (for the Jews call any large gathering of water a sea, according to that in Genesis: [[Gen 1:10|the gathering together of the waters, he called Seas|Congregationes aquarum appellavit Deus maria]]), [[4:3|shall be gathered together|congregabuntur]] unto death, that is, they shall fail. Hence, as Lyra says, the Hebrews read, *They shall be finished*. And the Septuagint translated, The fishes of the sea shall fail, namely for the same reason as the beasts and birds.

paras.t: Vel sic: Infirmabitur omnis qui habitat in ea, in bestia agri, id est occisis crudelibus ac potentibus populi Israel, et in volucre cœli, id est per interfectionem seu captivitatem superborum, sive sublimium personarum populi hujus; sed et pisces maris, id est in aquis carnalis voluptatis detenti, gulosi, avari, qui sic immerguntur sensibilibus, ne videant cœlum, congregabuntur in captivitatem seu mortem. Ista impleta sunt in captivitate decem tribuum ab Assyriis.
paras.en: Or thus: [[4:3|every one that dwelleth in it shall languish|omnis qui habitat in ea]], [[4:3|with the beasts of the field|in bestia agri]], that is, when the cruel and mighty of the people of Israel are slain, [[4:3|and with the fowls of the air|et in volucre cœli]], that is, through the slaying or captivity of the proud, or of the lofty persons of this people; [[4:3|yea, the fishes of the sea|sed et pisces maris]], that is, those held fast in the waters of carnal pleasure, the gluttonous and the avaricious, who are so sunk in the things of sense that they do not see heaven, [[4:3|shall be gathered together|congregabuntur]] into captivity or death. These things were fulfilled in the captivity of the ten tribes by the Assyrians.

paras.t: Verumtamen unusquisque non judicet, id est, justi in populo Israel non reprehendant proximos suos peccantes, et non arguatur vir Israelita transgressor. Cujus ratio subditur: populus enim tuus, o synagoga decem tribuum, sicut hi qui contradicunt sacerdoti, id est, assimilatur populo impudenter peccanti, incorrigibili ac rebelli, qui sacerdotibus ac prælatis aperte resistunt et contradicunt. Tales autem non sunt increpandi, quia non prodest. Propterea in tali casu non tenetur homo ad correctionem fraternam. Hinc Salomon in Proverbiis loquitur: Qui erudit derisorem, ipse sibi injuriam facit. Et in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem. Et iterum ait Scriptura: In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, ne forte despiciant doctrinam eloquii tui. Denique de hujuscemodi populo tam rebelli ac duro scriptum est in Isaia: Scio quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ænea. Quales fuerunt et Judæi tempore Christi, quibus Stephanus loquebatur: Dura cervice et incircumcisi corde et auribus, vos semper restitistis Spiritui Sancto, sicut et patres vestri. Istud est pessimum vitium. Ideo in Proverbiis inducitur: Viro qui corripientem dura cervice contemnit, repentinus ei superveniet interitus.
paras.en: [[4:4|But yet let not any man judge|Verumtamen unusquisque non judicet]], that is, let not the just among the people of Israel reprove their neighbours when they sin, [[4:4|and let not a man be rebuked|et non arguatur vir]], the transgressing Israelite. The reason for this is added: [[4:4|for thy people|populus enim tuus]], O synagogue of the ten tribes, [[4:4|are as they that contradict the priest|sicut hi qui contradicunt sacerdoti]], that is, is like a people sinning shamelessly, incorrigible and rebellious, who openly resist and contradict the priests and prelates. Such men are not to be rebuked, since it does no good; therefore in such a case a man is not bound to fraternal correction. Hence Solomon says in Proverbs: [[Prov 9:7|He that teacheth a scorner, doth an injury to himself|Qui erudit derisorem, ipse sibi injuriam facit]]. And in Ecclesiasticus it is written: [[Ecclus 32:6|Where there is no hearing, pour not out words|Ubi non est auditus, non effundas sermonem]]. And again Scripture says: [[Prov 23:9|Speak not in the ears of fools: because they will despise the instruction of thy speech|In auribus insipientium ne loquaris, ne forte despiciant doctrinam eloquii tui]]. Lastly, of such a people, so rebellious and hard, it is written in Isaias: [[Is 48:4|I knew that thou art stubborn, and thy neck is as an iron sinew, and thy forehead as brass|Scio quia durus es tu, et nervus ferreus cervix tua, et frons tua ænea]]. Such too were the Jews in the time of Christ, to whom Stephen said: [[Acts 7:51|You stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Ghost. As your fathers did|Dura cervice et incircumcisi corde et auribus, vos semper restitistis Spiritui Sancto, sicut et patres vestri]]. This is the worst of vices. Therefore it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 29:1|The man that with a stiff neck despiseth him that reproveth him, shall suddenly be destroyed|Viro qui corripientem dura cervice contemnit, repentinus ei superveniet interitus]].

paras.t: Et corrues tu, populus decem tribuum, hodie, id est, in præsenti, vel cito captivaberis. Prophetæ autem per diem communiter intelligunt tempus, sicque Hodie, exponitur pro hoc tempore, non pro die instante. Et corruet etiam propheta tecum, id est, simul capietur. Hoc pluraliter accipiendum est de falsis seducentibus prophetis, qui populum Israel foverunt in culpis. Tales enim in veteri Testamento ubertim appellantur prophetæ: ut quum dicit Isaias, Propheta docens mendacium, ipse cauda est; et Ezechiel, Propheta quum erraverit, ego Dominus decepi prophetam illum. Vel sensus est, quod decem tribubus captis, non amplius habuerunt Prophetas ut ante.
paras.en: [[4:5|And thou shalt fall|Et corrues]], thou, the people of the ten tribes, [[4:5|today|hodie]], that is, at present; or, thou shalt soon be taken captive. For the Prophets commonly understand by *day* a time, and so *today* is explained as this time, not the day at hand. [[4:5|and the prophet also shall fall with thee|Et corruet etiam propheta tecum]], that is, shall be taken together with thee. This is to be taken in the plural, of the false and seducing prophets who cherished the people of Israel in their sins. For such men are often called prophets in the Old Testament: as when Isaias says, [[Is 9:15|the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail|Propheta docens mendacium, ipse cauda est]]; and Ezechiel, [[Ezech 14:9|when the prophet shall err|Propheta quum erraverit]], [[Ezech 14:9|I the Lord have deceived that prophet|ego Dominus decepi prophetam illum]]. Or the sense is that, once the ten tribes were taken, they no longer had Prophets as before.

paras.t: Nocte tacere feci matrem vestram, id est, o decem tribus, tempore noctis vel in caligine angustiæ et tenebris tribulationis, tradidi Synagogam seu totam vestram congregationem hostibus suis, ita quod præ timore loqui ausa non fuit, sed gemens vultum dejecit in terram. Eadem autem est mater et filii, quia filiorum seu populi collectio, mater vocatur, sicut et Christus ait in Evangelio: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, quoties volui congregare filios tuos? Quidam per matrem hanc intelligunt Jerusalem, quæ ab antiquo fuit totius Israeliticæ plebis metropolis. Unde et mulier sapiens, secundo Regum, dixit ad Joab de civitate Abela: Tu quæris subvertere matrem civitatum in Israel? Jerusalem autem fecit Deus tacere nocte, quoniam noctis tempore capta est a Chaldæis. Loquebatur autem Propheta de futuro per modum præteriti.
paras.en: [[4:5|in the night I have made thy mother to be silent|Nocte tacere feci matrem vestram]] [Denis reads *vestram*, "your mother"; the Vulgate has *tuam*], that is, O ten tribes, in the time of night, or in the gloom of distress and the darkness of tribulation, I delivered the Synagogue, or your whole congregation, to her enemies, so that for fear she dared not speak, but groaning cast her face down to the ground. Now the mother and the children are the same, since the gathering of the children, or of the people, is called the mother; as Christ also says in the Gospel: [[Matt 23:37|Jerusalem, Jerusalem|Jerusalem, Jerusalem]], [[Matt 23:37|how often would I have gathered together thy children|quoties volui congregare filios tuos?]]? Some understand by this mother Jerusalem, which from of old was the chief city of the whole Israelite people. Hence the wise woman also, in the second book of Kings, said to Joab of the city of Abela: [[2 Kings 20:19|thou seekest to destroy|Tu quæris subvertere]] the mother of cities in Israel? [Denis's wording differs from the Vulgate here, which has "to destroy the city, and to overthrow a mother in Israel"] And God made Jerusalem silent in the night, since it was taken by the Chaldeans in the time of night. But the Prophet was speaking of the future after the manner of the past.

paras.t: Conticuit populus meus Israel: populus (inquam) meus vocatione, non prædestinatione, conditione naturæ, non gratiæ communione. Conticuit ergo coram hostibus, et silentio fugere cupiens, eo quod non habuerit scientiam divinorum, formatam et operatoriam. Unde infidelitatis tenebris obfuscatus, coluit idola: ideo meruit opprimi. Qui enim ignorat, ignorabitur, juxta Apostolum. Et Sapiens ait: Vani sunt omnes homines quibus non subest scientia Dei. Hinc in Isaia Dominus ait: Propterea captivus ductus est populus meus, quia non habuit scientiam.
paras.en: [[4:6|My people have been silent|Conticuit populus meus]], Israel: my people (I say) by calling, not by predestination; by the condition of nature, not by the communion of grace. They were silent, then, before their enemies, longing to flee in silence, [[4:6|because they had no knowledge|eo quod non habuerit scientiam]] of divine things, formed and working. Hence, darkened by the shadows of unbelief, they worshipped idols, and so deserved to be oppressed. For [[1 Cor 14:38|if any man know not, he shall not be known|ignorat, ignorabitur]], according to the Apostle. And the Wise Man says: [[Wis 13:1|all men are vain, in whom there is not the knowledge of God|Vani sunt omnes homines quibus non subest scientia Dei]]. Hence the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 5:13|Therefore is my people led away captive, because they had not knowledge|Propterea captivus ductus est populus meus, quia non habuit scientiam]].

paras.t: Quia tu scientiam repulisti, id est doctrinam legis ac Prophetarum, contra quam idola coluisti; vel ipsos sanctos Prophetas te instruentes, persecutus es et sprevisti; repellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi, id est, indignum te arbitrabar ad sacerdotalis officii usum, et hostibus tuis te tradam. In populo namque decem tribuum non erat verum atque legale sacerdotium, sed de extremis populi fecerant sibi sacerdotes, et aureis vitulis, non Deo altissimo, sacrificabant. Denique sacerdotes de tribu Levi in regno Juda meruerunt sacerdotium perdere, et a Chaldæis vastari, quoniam doctrinam Prophetarum, scilicet Jeremiæ et aliorum, repulerunt. — Constat quoque ex his, quod notitia Scripturarum sit sacerdotibus opportuna, ut possint inter verum et falsum, inter bonum et malum discernere, et sibi commissis digne præesse docendo, consulendo, increpando, et aliis modis. Hinc enim in Levitico Dominus dixit ad Aaron: Vinum et omne quod inebriare potest, non bibes tu et filii tui, quando intrabitis in tabernaculum testimonii, ne moriamini; et habeatis scientiam discernendi inter sanctum et profanum, inter pollutum et mundum, doceatisque filios Israel omnia legitima mea. Quanto amplius sacerdotibus evangelicæ legis congruit scientia atque sobrietas?
paras.en: [[4:6|because thou hast rejected knowledge|Quia tu scientiam repulisti]], that is, the teaching of the law and the Prophets, against which thou hast worshipped idols; or, thou hast persecuted and despised the holy Prophets themselves who instructed thee; [[4:6|I will reject thee, that thou shalt not do the office of priesthood to me|repellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi]], that is, I judged thee unworthy of the exercise of the priestly office, and I will deliver thee to thy enemies. For among the people of the ten tribes there was no true and lawful priesthood, but they had made themselves priests of the lowest of the people[[3 Kings 12:31||]], and sacrificed to golden calves[[3 Kings 12:28||]], not to the most high God. Lastly, the priests of the tribe of Levi in the kingdom of Juda deserved to lose the priesthood and to be laid waste by the Chaldeans, because they rejected the teaching of the Prophets, namely of Jeremias and others. It is also clear from this that knowledge of the Scriptures is needful for priests, so that they may discern between true and false, between good and evil, and worthily govern those committed to them, by teaching, counselling, rebuking and in other ways. For hence the Lord said to Aaron in Leviticus: [[Lev 10:9|You shall not drink wine nor any thing that may make drunk, thou nor thy sons, when you enter into the tabernacle of the testimony, lest you die|Vinum et omne quod inebriare potest, non bibes tu et filii tui, quando intrabitis in tabernaculum testimonii, ne moriamini]]; [[Lev 10:10|that you may have knowledge to discern between holy and unholy, between unclean and clean|habeatis scientiam discernendi inter sanctum et profanum, inter pollutum et mundum]], [[Lev 10:11|And may teach the children of Israel all my ordinances|doceatisque filios Israel omnia legitima mea]]. How much more do knowledge and sobriety become the priests of the law of the Gospel?

paras.t: Et oblita es legis Dei tui, id est, divina præcepta non observasti, neque memoriter tenuisti quæ docentur in lege. Quocontra de viro justo habetur: In lege Domini voluntas ejus, et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte; et in Proverbiis: Serva mandata, et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui; liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam. Obliviscar filiorum tuorum et ego, id est, singulis ad te pertinentibus, et tua peccata sectantibus, non succurram in necessitate, sed capi permittam. Quomodo autem Deo competat oblivio, dictum est plenius primo capitulo.
paras.en: [[4:6|and thou hast forgotten the law of thy God|Et oblita es legis Dei tui]], that is, thou hast not observed the divine precepts, nor kept in memory what is taught in the law. Against this it is said of the just man: [[Ps 1:2|his will is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he shall meditate day and night|In lege Domini voluntas ejus, et in lege ejus meditabitur die ac nocte]]; and in Proverbs: [[Prov 7:2|Keep my commandments|Serva mandata]], and [[Prov 7:2|my law as the apple of thy eye|legem quasi pupillam oculi tui]]; [[Prov 7:3|Bind it upon thy fingers, write it upon the tables of thy heart|liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam]]. [[4:6|I also will forget thy children|Obliviscar filiorum tuorum et ego]], that is, I will not help in their need each of those who belong to thee and follow thy sins, but will let them be taken. How forgetfulness befits God has been said more fully in the first chapter.

paras.t: Secundum multitudinem eorum, sic peccaverunt mihi: id est, quo ipsi amplius multiplicati sunt numero, eo plura et graviora commiserunt peccata, idola multiplicando, et filios suos in propriis malis fovendo. Unde et alibi legitur: Secundum numerum civitatum tuarum, Israel, erant dii tui. Gloriam eorum, id est idola in quibus gloriabantur, vel regiam dignitatem, vel gloriationem inanem, in ignominiam commutabo, ita quod rex populi et idola simul destruentur: quemadmodum factum est in captivitate prædicta.
paras.en: [[4:7|According to the multitude of them, so have they sinned against me|Secundum multitudinem eorum, sic peccaverunt mihi]]: that is, the more they were multiplied in number, the more and the graver sins they committed, multiplying idols and cherishing their children in their own evils. Hence it is read elsewhere too: [[Jer 2:28|according to the number of thy cities were thy gods|Secundum numerum civitatum tuarum, Israel, erant dii tui]] [Jeremias has "O Juda" where Denis has "Israel"]. [[4:7|I will change their glory|Gloriam eorum]], that is, the idols in which they gloried, or the royal dignity, or empty boasting, [[4:7|into shame|in ignominiam commutabo]]: so that the king of the people and the idols shall be destroyed together, as was done in the captivity spoken of.

paras.t: Peccata populi mei comedent: id est, sacrificia quæ populus Israel obtulit idolis, manducaverunt sacerdotes. Vel, Peccata populi comederunt, quoniam inducendo populum ad idololatriam, consequebantur quæstum et necessaria victui. Vel, comederunt peccata populi, quoniam adulando et consentiendo peccantibus, incorporaverunt sibi peccata illorum. Et ad iniquitatem eorum sublevabunt animas eorum: id est, sacerdotes isti erexerunt et provocaverunt animos populi ad exercendum et continuandum solita vitia, et in errore eorum confirmaverunt eos verbo et opere, quoniam vitia subditorum non solum non redarguerunt, sed laudaverunt commodi temporalis intuitu.
paras.en: [[4:8|They shall eat the sins of my people|Peccata populi mei comedent]]: that is, the priests ate the sacrifices which the people of Israel offered to idols [*peccatum*, "sin", is also used in the Old Testament for the sin-offering]. Or, they ate the sins of the people, because by leading the people into idolatry they got gain and the necessaries of life. Or, they ate the sins of the people, because by flattering and consenting to sinners they made their sins part of themselves. [[4:8|and shall lift up their souls to their iniquity|Et ad iniquitatem eorum sublevabunt animas eorum]]: that is, these priests roused and stirred up the minds of the people to practise and continue their accustomed vices, and confirmed them in their error by word and deed, since they not only did not rebuke the vices of their subjects but praised them, with an eye to temporal advantage.

paras.t: Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos. Idem hoc habetur in Isaia: et est sensus, quod sicut populus et sacerdos assimilantur in vitiis, sic similes erunt in pœnis. Nam sacerdotes idololatræ decem tribuum, simul cum populo capti sunt et æternaliter perierunt. Et visitabo super eum vias ejus, id est, sacerdotum et populi opera mala juste ulciscar; et cogitationes ejus reddam ei, id est, pœnas quas impie cogitando seu appetendo merentur, eis infligam: quia non solum facta, sed et cogitationes præmiantur a Deo. Denique opera hominis dicuntur viæ, quia sunt medium per quod venitur ad terminum, scilicet ad felicitatem æternam, vel ad perpetuam damnationem. Viæ autem impiorum sunt tenebrosæ et sordidæ, quum careant lumine rationis, et pulchritudini virtutum contrariantur. Propterea in Proverbiis habetur: Via impiorum tenebrosa; nesciunt ubi corruunt. Hinc etiam per Isaiam loquitur Dominus: Ego autem opera eorum et cogitationes eorum venio ut congregem.
paras.en: [[4:9|And there shall be like people like priest|Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos]]. The same is found in Isaias[[Is 24:2||]]; and the sense is that, as people and priest are alike in vices, so they shall be alike in punishments. For the idolatrous priests of the ten tribes were taken captive together with the people, and perished eternally. [[4:9|and I will visit their ways upon them|Et visitabo super eum vias ejus]], that is, I will justly avenge the evil works of the priests and the people; [[4:9|and I will repay them their devices|et cogitationes ejus reddam ei]], that is, I will inflict on them the punishments they deserve by impious thinking or desiring: for not only deeds but thoughts too are requited by God. Now the works of a man are called ways, since they are the means by which one comes to the end, namely to eternal happiness or to everlasting damnation. But the ways of the wicked are dark and filthy, since they lack the light of reason and are contrary to the beauty of the virtues. Therefore it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 4:19|The way of the wicked is darksome: they know not where they fall|Via impiorum tenebrosa; nesciunt ubi corruunt]]. Hence too the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 66:18|But I know their works, and their thoughts: I come that I may gather them together|Ego autem opera eorum et cogitationes eorum venio ut congregem]].

paras.t: Et comedent, et non saturabuntur. Per hoc datur intelligi inopia victualium quam passi sunt tempore obsidionis. Fornicati sunt cum idolis, et non cessaverunt ab idololatria: quia a tempore Jeroboam qui fecit aureos vitulos, non declinaverunt a cultura eorum usque ad captivitatem suam finalem; quoniam Dominum dereliquerunt in non custodiendo præceptum quod dedit per Moysen: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, et illi soli servies. Itaque quum Deus sit ubique incommutabilis et immensus, omnia ambiens, implens ac penetrans, relinquitur et ab eo receditur, non corporali, sed spirituali elongatione, hoc est dissimilitudine culpæ, seu inobedientia. Propter quod Isaias inducit: Iniquitates vestræ diviserunt inter Deum vestrum et vos, et peccata vestra absconderunt faciem ejus, ne exaudiret. In Proverbiis quoque: Longe est Dominus ab impiis: quum ipse nihilo minus sit in omnibus per essentiam, præsentiam atque potentiam, secundum quod ait per Jeremiam: Numquid non cœlum et terram ego impleo?
paras.en: [[4:10|And they shall eat and shall not be filled|Et comedent, et non saturabuntur]]. By this is given to understand the want of victuals which they suffered in the time of the siege. [[4:10|they have committed fornication|Fornicati sunt]] with idols, [[4:10|and have not ceased|et non cessaverunt]] from idolatry: for from the time of Jeroboam, who made the golden calves[[3 Kings 12:28||]], they did not turn from worshipping them until their final captivity; [[4:10|because they have forsaken the Lord in not observing|quoniam Dominum dereliquerunt in non custodiendo]] the precept which he gave through Moses: [[Matt 4:10|The Lord thy God shalt thou adore, and him only shalt thou serve|Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, et illi soli servies]][[Deut 6:13||]] [Denis's wording is that of Matt 4:10; Deut 6:13 has "Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God"]. And so, since God is everywhere unchangeable and immense, encompassing, filling and penetrating all things, he is forsaken and departed from not by bodily but by spiritual distance, that is, by the unlikeness of guilt, or disobedience. Therefore Isaias says: [[Is 59:2|your iniquities have divided between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you that he should not hear|Iniquitates vestræ diviserunt inter Deum vestrum et vos, et peccata vestra absconderunt faciem ejus, ne exaudiret]]. In Proverbs too: [[Prov 15:29|The Lord is far from the wicked|Longe est Dominus ab impiis]]: though he is none the less in all things by essence, presence and power, according to what he says by Jeremias: [[Jer 23:24|do not I fill heaven and earth|Numquid non cœlum et terram ego impleo]]?

paras.t: Fornicatio corporalis et spiritualis, et vinum et ebrietas auferunt cor, id est, actum rationis impediunt, judiciumque pervertunt, et hominem brutis parificant. Tanta est enim, secundum Augustinum, voluptas venerea, quod ea durante, non potest homo aliquem rationis actum exercere. Et Salomon ait: Luxuriosa res vinum, et tumultuosa ebrietas; qui his delectatur, non erit sapiens. Ecclesiasticus quoque asserit: Quam sufficiens homini erudito vinum exiguum! et in dormiendo non laborabis ab illo, nec senties dolorem. Et quoniam vinum aufert cor, non expedit hominem vina potantem arguere, ne rixetur. Propter quod scriptum est: In convivio vini non arguas proximum. Hinc ait Salvator: Attendite ne graventur corda vestra crapula et ebrietate.
paras.en: [[4:11|Fornication|Fornicatio]], bodily and spiritual, [[4:11|and wine, and drunkenness, take away the understanding|et vinum et ebrietas auferunt cor]] [the Latin has *cor*, "the heart"], that is, they hinder the act of reason, pervert the judgment, and make a man like the brutes. For so great, according to Augustine, is venereal pleasure, that while it lasts a man cannot exercise any act of reason. And Solomon says: [[Prov 20:1|Wine is a luxurious thing, and drunkenness riotous: whosoever is delighted therewith, shall not be wise|Luxuriosa res vinum, et tumultuosa ebrietas; qui his delectatur, non erit sapiens]]. Ecclesiasticus also declares: [[Ecclus 31:22|How sufficient is a little wine for a man well taught, and in sleeping thou shalt not be uneasy with it, and thou shalt feel no pain|Quam sufficiens homini erudito vinum exiguum! et in dormiendo non laborabis ab illo, nec senties dolorem]]. And since wine takes away the heart, it is not expedient to rebuke a man drinking wine, lest he quarrel. Therefore it is written: [[Ecclus 31:41|Rebuke not thy neighbour in a banquet of wine|In convivio vini non arguas proximum]]. Hence the Saviour says: [[Luke 21:34|take heed to yourselves, lest perhaps your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness|Attendite ne graventur corda vestra crapula et ebrietate]].

paras.t: Quoniam ergo his vitiis ablatum seu excæcatum fuit cor Israelis, inciderunt amentiam quæ subinfertur. Populus meus in ligno suo, id est ab idolo ligneo, interrogavit quid esset agendum, sive futurum. Coluerunt enim non solum aureos vitulos, sed et alia diversa simulacra Baal. Vel, in ligno suo interrogaverunt, quia (ut dicit Glossa) erat quoddam genus divinationis, quod fiebat in ligno et baculo, per quorum projectionem capiebantur futurorum auguria: quemadmodum ait Ezechiel, quod Nabuchodonosor miscuit sagittas suas seu virgas contra Ammon et Jerusalem, exivitque virga contra Jerusalem. Tale autem genus divinationis observavit plebs Israel. Unde subjungitur: et baculus ejus annuntiavit ei: id est, per quemdam modum motionis seu exitus baculi projecti, judicabant quid esset futurum seu operandum. Spiritus enim fornicationis, id est diabolus, qui se facit in idolis adorari, et ad idololatriam homines tentat atque inducit, decepit eos ad insistendum divinationi tam fatuæ, ceterisque peccatis. Initium quippe fornicationis, exquisitio idolorum, ut legitur in libro Sapientiæ. Et fornicati sunt a Deo suo, id est, per idololatriam Deum patrum suorum offenderunt et dereliquerunt. Hæc est fornicatio spiritualis, de qua ait Psalmista: Fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis. Et Jeremias: Mœchati sunt, inquit, cum ligno et lapide. Nihilo minus possunt hæc accipi de fornicatione carnali, qua dæmon innumerabiles decipit atque obtenebrat, ita quod in irrationabilissima vitia illabuntur.
paras.en: Since, then, by these vices the heart of Israel was taken away or blinded, they fell into the madness which is next described. [[4:12|My people have consulted their stocks|Populus meus in ligno suo]] [the Latin reads "My people asked in their wood"], that is, they [[4:12|consulted|interrogavit]] a wooden idol about what was to be done, or what was to come. For they worshipped not only the golden calves but also various other images of Baal. Or, they asked in their wood, because (as the Gloss says) there was a certain kind of divination done with wood and a staff, by the throwing of which omens of things to come were taken: as Ezechiel says that Nabuchodonosor mingled his arrows, or rods, against Ammon and Jerusalem, and the rod came out against Jerusalem[[Ezech 21:21||]][[Ezech 21:22||]]. Such a kind of divination the people of Israel practised. Hence is added: [[4:12|and their staff hath declared unto them|et baculus ejus annuntiavit ei]]: that is, by some manner of the movement or falling of the staff that was thrown, they judged what was to come or to be done. [[4:12|for the spirit of fornication|Spiritus enim fornicationis]], that is, the devil, who makes himself adored in idols and tempts and leads men into idolatry, [[4:12|hath deceived them|decepit eos]] into holding to so foolish a divination, and to the other sins. For [[Wis 14:12|the beginning of fornication is the devising of idols|Initium quippe fornicationis, exquisitio idolorum]], as we read in the book of Wisdom. [[4:12|and they have committed fornication against their God|Et fornicati sunt a Deo suo]], that is, by idolatry they offended and forsook the God of their fathers. This is the spiritual fornication of which the Psalmist says: [[Ps 105:39|they went aside after their own inventions|Fornicati sunt in adinventionibus suis]] [the Latin has "they committed fornication in their inventions"]. And Jeremias: They [[Jer 3:9|played the harlot|Mœchati sunt]], he says, [[Jer 3:9|with stones and with stocks|cum ligno et lapide]]. Nevertheless these things can be taken of carnal fornication, by which the demon deceives and darkens countless men, so that they slip into the most irrational vices.

paras.t: Super capita montium, id est in locis amœnis et altis, sacrificabant filii Israel idolis, et super colles accendebant thymiama, faciendo velut fumum odoremque thuris ad idolorum honorem, quasi aliquid divinitatis eis inesset. Subtus quercum et populum et terebinthum, id est, sub istis arboribus idola coluerunt: cujus ratio additur, quia bona erat umbra ejus, id est, umbra cujuslibet arborum prædictarum conveniens fuit ad vacandum voluptatibus, quibus serviebant in sacrificiis idolorum, gulæ atque luxuriæ servientes. In quo fecerunt contra legem, quæ jussit ut in loco divinitus præelecto sacrificia fierent, et juxta templum lucus et arbores non plantarentur, ne voluptuosa loca religionem emollirent.
paras.en: [[4:13|upon the tops of the mountains|Super capita montium]], that is, in pleasant and high places, the children of Israel [[4:13|offered sacrifice|sacrificabant]] to idols, [[4:13|and burnt incense upon the hills|et super colles accendebant thymiama]], making as it were the smoke and odour of frankincense in honour of the idols, as though something of divinity were in them. [[4:13|under the oak, and the poplar, and the turpentine tree|Subtus quercum et populum et terebinthum]], that is, under these trees they worshipped idols; the reason for which is added, [[4:13|because the shadow thereof was good|quia bona erat umbra ejus]], that is, the shade of each of these trees was suited to giving themselves up to the pleasures which they served in the sacrifices of idols, serving gluttony and lust. In this they acted against the law, which commanded that sacrifices be made in the place chosen by God[[Deut 12:11||]], and that no grove and trees be planted beside the temple[[Deut 16:21||]], lest pleasant places should soften religion.

paras.t: Ideo fornicabuntur filiæ vestræ, id est, quia vos tanta commisistis flagitia, permittam quod filiæ vestræ alienis illegitime miscebuntur, et quod sponsæ vestræ adulteræ erunt. Hoc fuit tempore captivitatis impletum, quando Assyrii violabant feminas filiorum Israel. Porro quod ait, Ideo, non est sic intelligendum, quod Deus propter peccatum personale unius, puniat alium in spiritualibus, gratiam subtrahendo, et in peccatum directe cadere permittendo; sed peccata parentum ac maritorum exemplariter induxerunt filias et uxores ad aliqua mala, propter quæ meruerunt ultra relinqui et capi, atque aliorum exponi libidini: et hoc Deus ordinavit ad vindictam peccati parentum ac maritorum, ut qui aliter suas spirituales fornicationes pensare et emendare noluerant, ex proprio opprobrio atque dolore, id est filiarum et sponsarum suarum violatione, attenderent quam inique egerunt, recedendo a cultu Sponsi cœlestis. Unde et Isaias Babylonis destructionem et pœnas describens: Uxores, inquit, eorum in oculis ipsorum violabuntur.
paras.en: [[4:13|therefore shall your daughters commit fornication|Ideo fornicabuntur filiæ vestræ]], that is, because you have committed such great crimes, I will permit that your daughters be unlawfully joined with strangers, and that [[4:13|your spouses shall be adulteresses|sponsæ vestræ adulteræ erunt]]. This was fulfilled in the time of the captivity, when the Assyrians violated the women of the children of Israel. Now his saying *therefore* is not to be understood as if God, for the personal sin of one, punished another in spiritual things, by withdrawing grace and letting him fall directly into sin; but the sins of the parents and husbands by their example led the daughters and wives into some evils, for which they deserved to be further abandoned and taken captive, and exposed to the lust of others. And God ordained this in punishment of the sin of the parents and husbands, so that those who otherwise would not weigh and amend their spiritual fornications might, from their own shame and grief, that is, from the violation of their daughters and spouses, take heed how wickedly they had acted in departing from the worship of the heavenly Bridegroom. Hence Isaias too, describing the destruction and punishments of Babylon, says: [[Is 13:16|their wives|Uxores]], he says, before their own eyes [[Is 13:16|shall be ravished|violabuntur]].

paras.t: Non visitabo super filias vestras, id est, peccata earum in præsenti non corrigam flagellatione paterna, quum fuerint fornicatæ, modo præfato; et super sponsas vestras non visitabo, quum adulteraverint, id est, adulteria commiserint: id est, in tantum vobis et illis irascar, quod flagello filiorum nequaquam corripiam eas, sed prorsus dimittam in iniquitatibus suis, ut ambulent in desideriis pravitatis suæ. Magna miseria, dum ideo non adhibetur correctio, quoniam emendatio desperatur. Hoc ergo meretur homo vehementer et impudenter peccando, ut penitus deseratur et prosperetur in malis, atque in his quæ conferunt ad peccandum, bene sibi succedat. Talis fuit populus Israel. Unde et per Ezechielem Dominus protestatur: Zelus meus recessit a te, non irascar tibi amplius. Per Jeremiam quoque: Plaga inimici percussi te, castigatione crudeli: cujus ratio subditur, Insanabilis est dolor tuus. Denique sanctus Apostolus ad Hebræos: Quis (inquit) filius, quem non corripit pater? Quod si extra disciplinam estis, ergo adulteri, et non filii estis. Propterea Jeremias orat: Corripe me, Domine, verumtamen in judicio et non in furore tuo, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me. Itaque quum Deus eos quos amat, arguat et castiget, signum odii reprobationisque divinæ consistit, non castigari a Deo in vita præsenti. Quod enim visitatio electorum per pœnas in hoc sæculo adhibeatur eis, ut per eam quasi quodam cauterio atque amarissimis punctionibus sortiantur animæ sanitatem, constat ex eo quod Dominus ait in Psalmo: Visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum, et in verberibus peccata eorum; misericordiam autem meam non dispergam ab eo. Et apud Jeremiam: Castigo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius, non autem te faciam in consummationem.
paras.en: [[4:14|I will not visit upon your daughters|Non visitabo super filias vestras]], that is, I will not now correct their sins with a father's scourging, [[4:14|when they shall commit fornication|quum fuerint fornicatæ]], in the manner said; [[4:14|and upon your spouses|et super sponsas vestras]] I will not visit, [[4:14|when they shall commit adultery|quum adulteraverint]], that is, shall commit adulteries: that is, I will be so angry with you and with them that I will by no means chastise them with the scourge of sons, but will leave them wholly in their iniquities, to walk in the desires of their own wickedness. It is a great misery when correction is not applied because amendment is despaired of. This, then, a man deserves by sinning violently and shamelessly: to be utterly forsaken, and to prosper in evil, and to have success in the things that serve for sinning. Such were the people of Israel. Hence the Lord protests by Ezechiel too: [[Ezech 16:42|my jealousy shall depart from thee|Zelus meus recessit a te]]; I will [[Ezech 16:42|be angry no more|non irascar tibi amplius]]. By Jeremias also: [[Jer 30:14|I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with cruel chastisement|Plaga inimici percussi te, castigatione crudeli]]; the reason of which is added: [[Jer 30:15|thy sorrow is incurable|Insanabilis est dolor tuus]]. Lastly the holy Apostle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:7|what son is there whom the father doth not correct|Quis (inquit) filius, quem non corripit pater]], he says? [[Heb 12:8|But if you be without chastisement|Quod si extra disciplinam estis]], [[Heb 12:8|then are you bastards and not sons|ergo adulteri, et non filii estis]]. Therefore Jeremias prays: [[Jer 10:24|Correct me, O Lord, but yet with judgment: and not in thy fury, lest thou bring me to nothing|Corripe me, Domine, verumtamen in judicio et non in furore tuo, ne forte ad nihilum redigas me]]. And so, since God rebukes and chastises those whom he loves[[Apoc 3:19||]], it is a sign of divine hatred and reprobation not to be chastised by God in the present life. For that the visitation of the elect by punishments is applied to them in this world, so that by it, as by a kind of cautery and most bitter stings, their souls may obtain health, is clear from what the Lord says in the Psalm: [[Ps 88:33|I will visit their iniquities with a rod and their sins with stripes|Visitabo in virga iniquitates eorum, et in verberibus peccata eorum]]; [[Ps 88:34|But my mercy I will not take away from him|misericordiam autem meam non dispergam ab eo]]. And in Jeremias: [[Jer 30:11|I will chastise thee in judgment, that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent|Castigo te in judicio, ut non tibi videaris innoxius]], [[Jer 30:11|I will not utterly consume thee|non autem te faciam in consummationem]].

paras.t: Quoniam ipsi, id est patres et mariti præfati, cum meretricibus conversabantur, commixtione carnali, et cum effeminatis, id est mollibus seu abscissis vel eunuchatis, sacrificabant Beelphegor: quem nos, secundum Hieronymum, Priapum vocamus, quem mulieres præsertim colebant, propter magnitudinem membri obsceni. Unde tertio Regum legitur Asa rex Juda amovisse matrem suam, ne esset princeps in sacris Priapi. Et populus non intelligens, id est populus Israel sua peccata non recognoscens, nec scientiam Dei habens, idcirco nec pœnitens, vapulabit, id est, percutietur captivitate et pœnis annexis.
paras.en: [[4:14|because themselves|Quoniam ipsi]], that is, the fathers and husbands spoken of, [[4:14|conversed with harlots|cum meretricibus conversabantur]] by carnal intercourse, [[4:14|with the effeminate|et cum effeminatis]], that is, with the soft, or the mutilated or eunuchs, [[4:14|offered sacrifice|sacrificabant]] to Beelphegor, whom we, according to Jerome, call Priapus, whom women especially worshipped because of the size of the obscene member. Hence we read in the third book of Kings that Asa king of Juda removed his mother from being princess in the sacrifices of Priapus[[3 Kings 15:13||]]. [[4:14|and the people that doth not understand|Et populus non intelligens]], that is, the people of Israel not acknowledging their sins, nor having the knowledge of God, and therefore not repenting, [[4:14|shall be beaten|vapulabit]], that is, shall be struck with captivity and the punishments joined to it.

paras.t: Si, id est quamvis et quia, fornicaris cum idolis tu, Israel, id est decem tribus, non delinquat saltem Juda: id est, populus Juda, seu duæ tribus, quæ habent urbem Jerusalem a Deo electam ad sacrificia offerenda, quæ insuper habent sacerdotes de semine Aaron, non conformentur tibi in idololatria ceterisque peccatis. Et nolite, duæ tribus vel decem, ingredi in Galgala, ut ibi idola honoretis. Galgala autem erat locus honorabilis, quoniam populus Israel desertum egrediens, ibi primo castrametatus est, et Josue filios Israel secundo circumcidit: Saul quoque ibi in regem est unctus. Sicque decem tribus propter loci solennitatem, posuerunt et coluerunt in eo idola sua. Et ne ascenderitis in Bethaven, id est in Bethel. Nam locus ille antequam Jeroboam posuit ibi aureum vitulum, dictus est Bethel, id est domus Dei. Postea vero vocatus est Bethaven, id est domus inutilis. Neque juraveritis, Vivit Dominus, id est, nolo ut ore vestro polluto, quo idola laudatis atque per ea juratis, assumatis vel explicetis nomen veri Dei. Jurare nempe debite circumstantionatum, est actus virtutis quæ dicitur latria. Unde idololatræ male sentientes de Deo, non debent per nomen ejus jurare. Vel sensus est, ut non jurent, Vivit Dominus, intelligendo per Dominum aliquod idolum, hoc est, ne applicent formam hanc jurandi diis suis.
paras.en: [[4:15|If|Si]], that is, although and since, [[4:15|thou play the harlot|fornicaris]] with idols, [[4:15|O Israel|tu, Israel]], that is, the ten tribes, [[4:15|at least let not Juda offend|non delinquat saltem Juda]]: that is, let the people of Juda, or the two tribes, who have the city of Jerusalem chosen by God for offering sacrifices, and who moreover have priests of the seed of Aaron, not be made like thee in idolatry and the other sins. [[4:15|and go ye not|Et nolite]], ye two tribes or ten, [[4:15|into Galgal|ingredi in Galgala]], to honour idols there. Now Galgala was an honoured place, because there the people of Israel, coming out of the desert, first encamped[[Jos 4:19||]], and Josue circumcised the children of Israel the second time[[Jos 5:3||]][[Jos 5:9||]]; Saul too was anointed king there[[1 Kings 11:15||]]. And so the ten tribes, because of the solemnity of the place, set up and worshipped their idols in it. [[4:15|and come not up into Bethaven|Et ne ascenderitis in Bethaven]], that is, into Bethel. For that place, before Jeroboam set the golden calf there[[3 Kings 12:29||]], was called Bethel, that is, the house of God; but afterwards it was called Bethaven, that is, the house of vanity [*domus inutilis*, literally "useless house"]. [[4:15|and do not swear: The Lord liveth|Neque juraveritis, Vivit Dominus]], that is, I will not have you take up or utter the name of the true God with your polluted mouth, with which you praise idols and swear by them. For to swear with due circumstances is an act of the virtue called latria [that is, the worship owed to God alone]. Hence idolaters, who think ill of God, ought not to swear by his name. Or the sense is that they should not swear *The Lord liveth*, meaning by *the Lord* some idol; that is, that they should not apply this form of swearing to their gods.

paras.t: Quoniam sicut vacca lasciviens, id est petulanter et valde erronee ex omni parte, declinavit Israel, id est decem tribus, a lege Mosaica, diversis peccatis ac idolis serviendo, et a rectitudine viæ Dei per omnium diverticula vitiorum enormiter evagando, ita ut illud Jeremiæ eis conveniat: A sæculo confregisti jugum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam. Nunc pascet eos Dominus quasi agnum, id est, in proximo est ut tradat eos Dominus in manus Assyriorum, sicque abducti pascantur ut oves, in latitudine, id est spatiosa terra Medorum.
paras.en: [[4:16|For|Quoniam]] [[4:16|like a wanton heifer|sicut vacca lasciviens]], that is, wantonly and very wanderingly on every side, [[4:16|Israel hath gone astray|declinavit Israel]], that is, the ten tribes, has turned aside from the law of Moses, serving various sins and idols, and straying grievously from the right way of God through the byways of all vices; so that that word of Jeremias fits them: [[Jer 2:20|Of old time thou hast broken my yoke, thou hast burst my bands, and thou saidst: I will not serve|A sæculo confregisti jugum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam]]. [[4:16|now will the Lord feed them, as a lamb|Nunc pascet eos Dominus quasi agnum]], that is, it is near that the Lord deliver them into the hands of the Assyrians, and that they, carried off, be pastured like sheep, [[4:16|in a spacious place|in latitudine]], that is, in the wide land of the Medes.

paras.t: Particeps idolorum, id est cultor eorum, factus est Ephraim, id est populus decem tribuum: quæ nomine Ephraim designantur, quoniam primus eorum rex Jeroboam filius Nabat, exstitit Ephrataeus. Idcirco, o Juda, cui superius dictum est, Non delinquat saltem Juda, dimitte eum, id est, a communione et conversatione decem tribuum te averte, ne cum perversis pervertaris.
paras.en: [[4:17|a partaker with idols|Particeps idolorum]], that is, a worshipper of them, has [[4:17|Ephraim|Ephraim]] become, that is, the people of the ten tribes, who are designated by the name of Ephraim because their first king, Jeroboam the son of Nabat, was an Ephrathite[[3 Kings 11:26||]]. Therefore, O Juda, to whom it was said above, [[4:15|at least let not Juda offend|Non delinquat saltem Juda]], [[4:17|let him alone|dimitte eum]], that is, turn away from fellowship and dealings with the ten tribes, lest thou be perverted with the perverse[[Ps 17:27||]].

paras.t: Separatum est convivium eorum, id est, cibus quo vescuntur decem tribus, tibi illicitus est, sicque eorum convivium a tuo distinctum est. Fornicatione fornicati sunt cum diis alienis seu idolis; dilexerunt afferre ignominiam, id est idololatriam introducere, augere, vel conservare, protectores ejus, id est reges, qui populum defendere habent: sicque protectores isti non defenderunt populum suum ab invisibilibus hostibus.
paras.en: [[4:18|Their banquet is separated|Separatum est convivium eorum]], that is, the food on which the ten tribes feed is unlawful for thee, and so their banquet is distinct from thine. [[4:18|they have gone astray by fornication|Fornicatione fornicati sunt]] [literally "they have committed fornication with fornication"] with strange gods or idols; [[4:18|they that should have protected them have loved to bring shame upon them|dilexerunt afferre ignominiam protectores ejus]] [the Latin runs "its protectors have loved to bring shame"], that is, its protectors, the kings, whose part it is to defend the people, loved to bring in, increase or preserve idolatry: and so these protectors did not defend their people from the invisible enemies.

paras.t: Ligavit eum spiritus in alis suis. Hoc dupliciter explanatur. Primo sic: Spiritus malignus in idolis habitans, populum Israel ligavit in alis suis, id est in agilitate et subtilitate sua ipsius, videlicet dæmonis, ita quod subtilitate et agilitate dæmoniaca portat hunc populum ad quæcumque voluerit vitia, sicut avis pullos suos in alis deportat. Unde in Deuteronomio de Deo et electo Israel scriptum est: Expandit alas suas, et assumpsit eum, atque portavit in humeris suis. Sic diabolus alligat sibi perversos: propter quod ad Timotheum dicit Apostolus, Resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem. Secundo sic: Spiritus ligavit eum in alis suis, id est, populum Israel vinxit in ipsius populi intellectu per infidelitatis errorem, et affectu per indurationem in vitiis, ita ut populus iste ad virtutes non volet, nec æterna adspiciat, sed in profundum vitiorum mergatur. Sic omnes in vitiis habituati ac impœnitentes, a dæmone ligantur in alis tam dæmonis quam propriis: quibus illud Isaiæ dicendum est, Excutere de pulvere, et solve vincula colli tui. Et confundentur a sacrificiis suis, id est demerito sacrificiorum idolis oblatorum, quum viderint idololatriam nil profuisse, sed maxime nocuisse.
paras.en: [[4:19|The wind hath bound them up in its wings|Ligavit eum spiritus in alis suis]] [the Latin *spiritus* means both "wind" and "spirit", and Denis takes it as "spirit"]. This is explained in two ways. First thus: the evil spirit dwelling in idols has bound the people of Israel in his wings, that is, in his own agility and subtlety, namely the demon's; so that by demonic subtlety and agility he carries this people to whatever vices he will, as a bird carries its young on its wings. Hence in Deuteronomy it is written of God and the chosen Israel: [[Deut 32:11|he spread his wings, and hath taken him and carried him on his shoulders|Expandit alas suas, et assumpsit eum, atque portavit in humeris suis]]. So the devil binds the perverse to himself; therefore the Apostle says to Timothy that [[2 Tim 2:26|they may recover themselves from the snares of the devil by whom they are held captive at his will|Resipiscant a laqueis diaboli, a quo captivi tenentur ad ipsius voluntatem]]. Secondly thus: the spirit has bound him in his wings, that is, has bound the people of Israel in that people's own understanding by the error of unbelief, and in its affection by hardening in vices, so that this people does not fly to the virtues nor look upon eternal things, but is sunk into the depth of vices. So all who are habituated to vices and impenitent are bound by the demon in the wings both of the demon and their own; to whom must be said that word of Isaias: [[Is 52:2|Shake thyself from the dust|Excutere de pulvere]], and [[Is 52:2|loose the bonds from off thy neck|solve vincula colli tui]]. [[4:19|and they shall be confounded because of their sacrifices|Et confundentur a sacrificiis suis]], that is, through the demerit of the sacrifices offered to idols, when they see that idolatry has profited them nothing, but harmed them greatly.

4.title: Expositio moralis ejusdem capituli quarti
4.title_en: Moral exposition of the same fourth chapter

paras.t: Audite verbum Domini, filii Israel, id est, filii militantis Ecclesiæ, quæ dicitur Israel contemplando cœlestia, quia judicium est Domino Christo, cui Pater dedit omne judicium. Exsecutio enim judiciariæ potestatis seu prolatio sententiæ, spectat ad Christum secundum formam assumptam, prout ipse testatur: Dedit ei potestatem et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est. Cum habitatoribus terræ, id est terrenis hominibus, quorum conversatio non est in cœlis, nec dicere possunt: Quoniam advena ego sum apud te et peregrinus, sicut omnes patres mei; et iterum, Non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus. Tales namque faciunt sibi de via atque exsilio patriam. Non est enim veritas, et non est misericordia, et non est scientia Dei in terra, id est in his carnalibus, quia etsi dicant se nosse Deum, tamen factis negant. Nempe si quis dixerit, quoniam diligo Deum, et mandata ejus non custodit, mendax est. Proinde qui sibi nequam est, cui bonus erit? Ideo monet Scriptura: Miserere animæ tuæ placens Deo.
paras.en: [[4:1|Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel|Audite verbum Domini, filii Israel]], that is, children of the Church militant, which is called Israel from contemplating heavenly things [that is, *Israel* taken as "one who sees God"]; [[4:1|for the Lord shall enter into judgment|quia judicium est Domino]], that is, Christ, to whom the Father [[John 5:22|hath given all judgment|dedit omne judicium]]. For the carrying out of judicial power, or the pronouncing of sentence, belongs to Christ according to the form He assumed, as He Himself testifies: [[John 5:27|And he hath given him power to do judgment, because he is the Son of man|Dedit ei potestatem et judicium facere, quia Filius hominis est]]. [[4:1|with the inhabitants of the land|Cum habitatoribus terræ]], that is, with earthly men, whose conversation is not in heaven[[Phil 3:20||]], and who cannot say: [[Ps 38:13|for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were|Quoniam advena ego sum apud te et peregrinus, sicut omnes patres mei]]; and again: [[Heb 13:14|we have not here a lasting city: but we seek one that is to come|Non habemus hic manentem civitatem, sed futuram inquirimus]]. For such men make for themselves a fatherland out of the road and the exile. [[4:1|for there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God in the land|Non est enim veritas, et non est misericordia, et non est scientia Dei in terra]], that is, in these carnal men; for though they say that [[Tit 1:16|they know God|se nosse Deum]], yet [[Tit 1:16|in their works they deny him|factis negant]]. Indeed, [[1 John 4:20|If any man say: I love God|si quis dixerit, quoniam diligo Deum]], and keepeth not his commandments, [[1 John 4:20|he is a liar|mendax est]] [Denis joins 1 John 4:20 with the words of 1 John 2:4][[1 John 2:4||]]. Moreover, [[Ecclus 14:5|He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good?|qui sibi nequam est, cui bonus erit]]? Therefore Scripture warns: [[Ecclus 30:24|Have pity on thy own soul, pleasing God|Miserere animæ tuæ placens Deo]].

paras.t: Quomodo insuper in malis Christianis impleatur quotidie quod sequitur, non oportet exponere, quum oculis pateat. Jam enim, heu! Maledictum et mendacium, furtum et adulterium inundaverunt, et sanguis sanguinem tetigit. Propter hoc lugebit terra, quia nisi pœnitentiam egerint, sine fine peribunt. Unde et Jacobus dicit: Agite nunc, divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis quæ advenient vobis; risus vester convertatur in luctum.
paras.en: How, moreover, what follows is fulfilled daily in bad Christians there is no need to explain, since it lies open to the eyes. For already, alas! [[4:2|Cursing, and lying|Maledictum et mendacium]], [[4:2|and theft, and adultery, have overflowed|furtum et adulterium inundaverunt]], [[4:2|and blood hath touched blood|et sanguis sanguinem tetigit]]. [[4:3|Therefore shall the land mourn|Propter hoc lugebit terra]]: for unless they do penance, they shall perish without end. Whence James too says: [[Jas 5:1|Go to now, ye rich men: weep and howl in your miseries, which shall come upon you|Agite nunc, divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis quæ advenient vobis]]; [[Jas 4:9|let your laughter be turned into mourning|risus vester convertatur in luctum]].

paras.t: Multi quoque nunc ita peccatis assuescunt, excæcantur et indurantur, ut secundum sensum expositum dici possit: Unusquisque non judicet, et non arguatur vir. Hi sunt qui increpationem seu admonitionem nequeunt sustinere, habentes morbum vocatum, Noli me tangere. Increpantem nempe redarguunt, judicant, et non jam ex caritate, sed passione aut rancore, loqui existimant. Non enim attendunt quam salubre et purgativum sit increpari; quam item meritorium, increpationem pie et æquanimiter ferre. Et si forte excusabiles sumus de eo de quo increpamur, non tamen debemus impatienter recipere, quia in aliis multis, et forte gravioribus, offendimus tam frequenter. Hinc scriptum est in Proverbiis: Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit arguenti, glorificabitur. Ecclesiasticus quoque ait: Quam bonum est, correptum manifestare pœnitentiam! sic enim effugiet peccatum. Postremo, qui admonitionem, increpationem, correctionem seu disciplinam non acceptat, sed spernit aut parvi pendit, similis est vulnerato qui non patitur sibi vulnus suum ostendi aut remedium adhiberi. Et palam est, quod amor privatus atque superbia causa sunt, quod non dignamur redargui aut puniri, quia vel increpantem contemnimus, vel coram aliis magni esse optamus, vel simile aliquid est in causa. Qui autem veraciter prudens est, cum gratiarum actione increpationem acceptat, tanquam veræ ac fraternæ caritatis munusculum, imo munus eximium. Propter quod in Proverbiis inducitur: Argue sapientem, et diliget te.
paras.en: Many, too, are now so accustomed to sins, so blinded and hardened, that according to the sense already explained it may be said: [[4:4|let not any man judge: and let not a man be rebuked|Unusquisque non judicet, et non arguatur vir]]. These are they who cannot bear rebuke or admonition, having the disease called *Touch me not* [the name given to an ulcer that grows worse when treated; Denis applies it to those who will not be corrected]. For they reprove the one who rebukes them, they judge him, and think he speaks no longer out of charity but out of passion or rancour. For they do not consider how wholesome and cleansing it is to be rebuked, nor how meritorious to bear rebuke devoutly and with an even mind. And even if perhaps we are excusable in the matter for which we are rebuked, still we ought not to take it impatiently, since in many other things, and perhaps graver ones, we offend so often. Hence it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 13:18|Poverty and shame to him that refuseth instruction: but he that yieldeth to reproof shall be glorified.|Egestas et ignominia ei qui deserit disciplinam; qui autem acquiescit arguenti, glorificabitur]]. Ecclesiasticus also says: [[Ecclus 20:4|How good is it, when thou art reproved, to shew repentance!|Quam bonum est, correptum manifestare pœnitentiam!]]! for so he shall escape sin [Denis's wording is shorter than the Vulgate's "so thou shalt escape wilful sin"]. Lastly, he who does not accept admonition, rebuke, correction or discipline, but spurns it or makes little of it, is like a wounded man who will not suffer his wound to be shown or a remedy to be applied. And it is plain that self-love and pride are the cause why we do not deign to be reproved or punished: either we despise the one who rebukes us, or we wish to seem great before others, or something of the kind is the cause. But he who is truly prudent accepts rebuke with thanksgiving, as a little gift of true and brotherly charity, nay rather an excellent gift. For which reason it is put in Proverbs: [[Prov 9:8|Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee|Argue sapientem, et diliget te]].

paras.t: Populus enim tuus sicut hi qui contradicunt sacerdoti. Hoc ad Ecclesiam potest referri, in qua sunt multi rebelles et murmuratores, non obtemperantes prælatis, neque Ecclesiæ excommunicationem curantes. De quibus dicit Christus Apostolis, et sub eorum persona cunctis aliorum rectoribus Christi vicariis: Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit. Unde ad Romanos scriptum est: Qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit; qui autem resistunt, ipsi sibi damnationem acquirunt.
paras.en: [[4:4|for thy people are as they that contradict the priest|Populus enim tuus sicut hi qui contradicunt sacerdoti]]. This can be referred to the Church, in which there are many rebels and murmurers, who do not obey their prelates and care nothing for the Church's excommunication. Of these Christ says to the Apostles, and in their person to all who rule others as vicars of Christ: [[Luke 10:16|He that heareth you heareth me: and he that despiseth you despiseth me|Qui vos audit, me audit; et qui vos spernit, me spernit]]. Whence it is written to the Romans: [[Rom 13:2|he that resisteth the power resisteth the ordinance of God. And they that resist purchase to themselves damnation|Qui potestati resistit, Dei ordinationi resistit; qui autem resistunt, ipsi sibi damnationem acquirunt]].

paras.t: Et corrues hodie. Toties enim spiritualiter cadimus, quoties peccamus: quia peccatum ruina est a Deo sublimi, et ab arce virtutum. Ideo in Ecclesiastico legitur: In viam ruinæ non eas. Et Apostolus ad Ephesios: State, inquit, succincti lumbos vestros in veritate. Porro si justus septies cadit, quoties quotidie peccat impœnitens, cujus semper præcedens culpa ad sequentem disponit? Et corruet etiam propheta, id est fallax magister, injustus prælatus, tecum, ut simul pereatis, qui pares estis in vitiis. De talibus contestatur Apostolus: Coacervabunt sibi magistros prurientes auribus; et a veritate quidem auditum avertent, ad fabulas autem convertentur. Nocte, id est per pœnæ seu adversitatis inflictionem, tacere feci, o hæretici seu rebelles, matrem vestram, id est congregationem perversam, incredulam, aut inobedientem, cujus membra et filii estis. Tales enim congregationes, frequenter per pœnas ultionis seu prælia exstirpantur.
paras.en: [[4:5|And thou shalt fall today|Et corrues hodie]]. For we fall spiritually as often as we sin: since sin is a fall from God on high and from the citadel of the virtues. Therefore we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:25|Go not in the way of ruin|In viam ruinæ non eas]]. And the Apostle to the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:14|Stand|State]], he says, [[Eph 6:14|having your loins girt about with truth|succincti lumbos vestros in veritate]]. Further, if [[Prov 24:16|a just man shall fall seven times|justus septies cadit]], how often daily does the impenitent man sin, whose every earlier fault always disposes him to the next? [[4:5|and the prophet also shall fall|Et corruet etiam propheta]], that is, the deceitful master, the unjust prelate, [[4:5|with thee|tecum]], so that you may perish together, being alike in vices. Of such the Apostle bears witness: [[2 Tim 4:3|they will heap to themselves teachers having itching ears|Coacervabunt sibi magistros prurientes auribus]]; [[2 Tim 4:4|And will indeed turn away their hearing from the truth, but will be turned unto fables.|et a veritate quidem auditum avertent, ad fabulas autem convertentur]]. [[4:5|in the night|Nocte]], that is, by the infliction of punishment or adversity, [[4:5|I have made|tacere feci]], O heretics or rebels, [[4:5|thy mother|matrem vestram]] silent [Denis writes *your mother*, speaking to many], that is, the perverse, unbelieving or disobedient congregation, whose members and children you are. For such congregations are often rooted out by punishments of vengeance, or by wars.

paras.t: Conticuit populus meus, id est christiana plebs, a me Christo christiana vocata, eo quod non habuerit scientiam salutarem, de qua ad Philippenses dicit Apostolus: Existimo omnia detrimentum esse, propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Qui autem hac caret scientia, tacet a laude divina, a correptione fraterna, ab instructione perutili, et a confessione pœnitentiali, ita ut dicere habet: Væ mihi, quia tacui; et, Quoniam tacui, inveterarunt ossa mea. Tacet loquenda, loquiturque tacenda. Quum enim ratio voluntatem in omnibus dirigat, qui veritatis non habet notitiam, non operatur virtutem, nec scit quando proferre debet sermonem. Hinc Ecclesiasticus dicit: Est tacens, qui invenitur sapiens; et tacens, non habens sensum loquelæ. Oportet ergo in primis Dominum invocare pro illuminatione intellectus, dicendo cum Psalmista: Da mihi intellectum, ut sciam testimonia tua: quatenus voluntas, in qua est prima origo peccandi, rectificetur in omnibus. Ideo namque ait Scriptura: Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine, et de lege tua docueris eum.
paras.en: [[4:6|My people have been silent|Conticuit populus meus]], that is, the Christian people, called Christian from Me, Christ, [[4:6|because they had no knowledge|eo quod non habuerit scientiam]] of salvation; of which the Apostle says to the Philippians: [[Phil 3:8|I count all things to be but loss for the excellent knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|Existimo omnia detrimentum esse, propter eminentem scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]]. Now he who lacks this knowledge is silent from the divine praise, from brotherly correction, from most useful instruction, and from penitential confession, so that he must say: [[Is 6:5|Woe is me, because I have held my peace|Væ mihi, quia tacui]]; and: [[Ps 31:3|Because I was silent my bones grew old|Quoniam tacui, inveterarunt ossa mea]]. He keeps silent about what should be spoken, and speaks what should be kept silent. For since reason directs the will in all things, he who has no knowledge of the truth does not work virtue, nor does he know when he ought to utter a word. Hence Ecclesiasticus says: [[Ecclus 20:5|There is one that holdeth his peace, that is found wise|Est tacens, qui invenitur sapiens]]; and [[Ecclus 20:6|There is one that holdeth his peace, because he knoweth not what to say|tacens, non habens sensum loquelæ]] [literally "one who keeps silent, not having the sense of speech"]. We must therefore first of all call upon the Lord for the enlightening of the understanding, saying with the Psalmist: [[Ps 118:125|give me understanding that I may know thy testimonies|Da mihi intellectum, ut sciam testimonia tua]]; so that the will, in which is the first origin of sinning, may be set right in all things. For this is why Scripture says: [[Ps 93:12|Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: and shalt teach him out of thy law.|Beatus homo quem tu erudieris, Domine, et de lege tua docueris eum]].

paras.t: Quia tu scientiam repulisti, repellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi. Ex quo innotescit, quod usus sacerdotii horum qui notitiam Scripturarum non curant, inacceptus sit Deo. De hoc in præcedenti articulo satis dictum opinor.
paras.en: [[4:6|because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will reject thee, that thou shalt not do the office of priesthood to me|Quia tu scientiam repulisti, repellam te, ne sacerdotio fungaris mihi]]. From this it is made known that the exercise of the priesthood by those who care nothing for the knowledge of the Scriptures is unacceptable to God. Of this enough has been said, I think, in the preceding article.

paras.t: Secundum multitudinem eorum, sic peccaverunt mihi. Impii enim, rebelles, hæretici, schismatici, quo amplius crescunt sive augentur, eo peccata eorum magnitudine et multitudine amplius invalescunt: quemadmodum equidem in congregatione devota unus provocat alium verbo et opere ad virtutes, sic in conventu malignantium unus alium incitat ad peccata, quoniam cum perversis alii pervertuntur.
paras.en: [[4:7|According to the multitude of them, so have they sinned against me|Secundum multitudinem eorum, sic peccaverunt mihi]]. For the more the wicked, rebels, heretics and schismatics grow or increase, the more their sins prevail in greatness and number: for just as in a devout community one spurs on another by word and deed to the virtues, so in the assembly of the malignant one stirs up another to sins, since with the perverse others are perverted[[Ps 17:27||]].

paras.t: Gloriam eorum, id est temporalem prosperitatem, delectationem carnalem, inania documenta, et cetera in quibus illicite gloriantur, in ignominiam commutabo, id est in confusionem et pœnam æternam, secundum quod Judex affirmat: Væ vobis qui ridetis, quia lugebitis et flebitis; væ vobis divitibus, qui habetis consolationem vestram. Unde in libro Machabæorum habetur: Gloria impii, stercus et vermis; hodie extollitur, et cras non invenitur. De talibus loquitur Dominus per Jeremiam: Dabo eos in vexationem et maledictionem, et in stuporem et sibilum, et in opprobrium, eo quod non audierint verba mea.
paras.en: [[4:7|I will change their glory|Gloriam eorum]], that is, temporal prosperity, carnal delight, empty teachings, and the other things in which they glory unlawfully, [[4:7|into shame|in ignominiam commutabo]], that is, into confusion and eternal punishment; according as the Judge affirms: [[Luke 6:25|Woe to you that now laugh: for you shall mourn and weep|Væ vobis qui ridetis, quia lugebitis et flebitis]]; [[Luke 6:24|woe to you that are rich: for you have your consolation|væ vobis divitibus, qui habetis consolationem vestram]]. Whence we have in the book of Machabees: the glory of the wicked [[1 Mach 2:62|is dung and worms|stercus et vermis]]; [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found|hodie extollitur, et cras non invenitur]] [the Vulgate has "the glory of a sinful man"]. Of such the Lord speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 29:18|I will give them up unto affliction|Dabo eos in vexationem]], [[Jer 29:18|to be a curse, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach|et maledictionem, et in stuporem et sibilum, et in opprobrium]], [[Jer 29:19|Because they have not hearkened to my words|eo quod non audierint verba mea]].

paras.t: Peccata populi mei comedent, et ad iniquitatem sublevabunt animas eorum. Videmus nunc, quomodo multi qui præsunt, de subditorum vivant oblationibus atque redditibus: et tamen quos verbo, prece, exemplarique vita tenentur a peccatis avertere, et ad meliora inducere, variis modis corrumpunt, scandalizant, inficiunt, impie conversando, adulando, consentiendo, cooperando, et debita pastoralis curæ opera negligendo. Quibus competit illud Ecclesiastici: Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus. Unde Jeremias: Quoniam stulte, inquit, egerunt pastores, ideo omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. O quam horrenda et maxima erit horum damnatio, qui pro singulis subditorum suorum, ex eorum negligentia pereuntium, torquebuntur!
paras.en: [[4:8|They shall eat the sins of my people, and shall lift up their souls to their iniquity|Peccata populi mei comedent, et ad iniquitatem sublevabunt animas eorum]]. We see now how many who are set over others live on the offerings and revenues of their subjects; and yet those whom they are bound by word, prayer and an exemplary life to turn away from sins and lead on to better things, they corrupt, scandalize and infect in various ways: by living impiously, by flattering, by consenting, by co-operating, and by neglecting the works due to pastoral care. To these applies that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:2|As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers|Secundum judicem populi, sic et ministri ejus]]. Whence Jeremias: Because, he says, [[Jer 10:21|the pastors have done foolishly|stulte, inquit, egerunt pastores]], therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. O how dreadful and how very great will be the damnation of these, who will be tormented for each one of their subjects who perishes through their negligence!

paras.t: Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos. Heu, quam immoderatissime hoc indesinenter impletur, dum sacerdotes evangelicæ legis, qui ad spiritualis conversationis munditiam obligantur, aliisque in omnibus exemplares esse tenentur, carnalibus vitiis serviunt, vanitati, elationi, curiositati intendunt, propriique gradus dignitatem non ponderantes, vilem atque turpissimam peragunt vitam! Quibus convenit illud Jeremiæ: Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus? Illud quoque Isaiæ: Speculatores cæci; canes muti, non valentes latrare. Contra quos Moyses ait in Levitico: Sacerdotes sancti erunt Deo suo, et non polluent nomen ejus; incensum enim Domini et panes Dei sui offerunt, et ideo sancti erunt.
paras.en: [[4:9|And there shall be like people like priest|Et erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos]]. Alas, how beyond all measure this is fulfilled without ceasing, while priests of the law of the Gospel, who are bound to purity of spiritual life and are obliged to be an example to others in all things, serve carnal vices, give themselves to vanity, pride and curiosity, and, not weighing the dignity of their own rank, lead a vile and most shameful life! To these applies that saying of Jeremias: [[Jer 2:8|The priests did not say: Where is the Lord?|Sacerdotes non dixerunt, Ubi est Dominus?]] And that of Isaias too: [[Is 56:10|His watchmen are all blind|Speculatores cæci]]; [[Is 56:10|dumb dogs not able to bark|canes muti, non valentes latrare]]. Against whom Moses says in Leviticus of the priests: [[Lev 21:6|They shall be holy to their God, and shall not profane his name. For they offer the burnt offering of the Lord, and the bread of their God: and therefore they shall be holy.|sancti erunt Deo suo, et non polluent nomen ejus; incensum enim Domini et panes Dei sui offerunt, et ideo sancti erunt]].

paras.t: Isti comedent corpus Dominicum sacramentaliter, et non saturabuntur effectu et gratia tanti sacramenti, quia non sumunt et spiritualiter, fiuntque rei corporis et sanguinis Domini. Fornicati sunt. Jam enim luxuriæ vitia vigent in eis, et qui deberent angelicam ducere vitam, bestiales effecti sunt, et bestiis decies millies deteriores, qui Filium Virginis tractant ore et manibus quibus contrectant filias Veneris. Tantam quoque suæ conversationis impietatem ingratitudinemque non attendunt, quoniam Fornicatio, vinum et ebrietas auferunt cor. Unde in Ecclesiastico legitur: Vinum et mulieres apostatare faciunt etiam sapientes. Hinc Spiritus fornicationis decepit eos. Cui resistere oportet, non immorando cogitationibus venereorum, et incitamenta atque materiam hujus peccati a se elongando, dominicam quoque passionem cordialiter ac frequenter rememorando, et item æterna supplicia sagaciter intuendo.
paras.en: These [[4:10|shall eat|comedent]] the Lord's body sacramentally, [[4:10|and shall not be filled|et non saturabuntur]] with the effect and grace of so great a sacrament, because they do not receive it spiritually as well, and they become [[1 Cor 11:27|guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord|rei corporis et sanguinis Domini]]. [[4:10|they have committed fornication|Fornicati sunt]]. For the vices of lust now flourish in them; and they who ought to lead an angelic life have become beastly, and ten thousand times worse than beasts, handling the Son of the Virgin with the mouth and hands with which they handle the daughters of Venus. Nor do they consider so great an impiety and ingratitude in their way of life, because [[4:11|Fornication, and wine, and drunkenness, take away the understanding.|Fornicatio, vinum et ebrietas auferunt cor]] [*cor*, literally "the heart"]. Whence we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 19:2|Wine and women make wise men fall off|Vinum et mulieres apostatare faciunt etiam sapientes]] [*apostatare faciunt*, literally "make to apostatize"]. Hence [[4:12|the spirit of fornication hath deceived them|Spiritus fornicationis decepit eos]]. This spirit must be resisted by not dwelling on thoughts of venereal things, by putting far from oneself the incitements and matter of this sin, by recalling the Lord's passion heartily and often, and likewise by shrewdly considering the eternal torments.

paras.t: Super capita montium sacrificabant. Tales sunt hæretici, qui de doctrinæ profunditate se jactant, et in mirabilibus super se ambulant, non consentientes humilibus. Horum filiæ et sponsæ, id est animæ ab eis seductæ, adulteræ sunt, recedendo a copula Sponsi cœlestis, et in humanis adinventionibus gloriantes.
paras.en: [[4:13|They offered sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains|Super capita montium sacrificabant]]. Such are the heretics, who boast of the depth of their doctrine and walk in wonderful things above themselves[[Ps 130:1||]], not consenting to the humble[[Ps 130:2||]] [the margin gives Ps. cxxx, 1, 2; the last words are closer to Rom 12:16, "consenting to the humble"]. Their daughters and spouses, that is, the souls led astray by them, are adulteresses, departing from union with the heavenly Bridegroom and glorying in human inventions.

paras.t: Populus non intelligens beneficia Dei, propria mala, et ea quæ Dei sunt, vapulabit, id est, æternæ damnationis ictibus percutietur.
paras.en: [[4:14|the people that doth not understand|Populus non intelligens]] the benefits of God, their own evils, and the things that are God's, [[4:14|shall be beaten|vapulabit]], that is, shall be struck with the blows of eternal damnation.

paras.t: Si fornicaris tu, Israel, id est, congregatio hæreticorum, quæ per decem tribus, legem Dei deserentes, significatur, non delinquat saltem Juda, id est Ecclesia catholica confitens Domino, quæ per tribum Juda, legem Dei servantem, exprimitur. Nam et Judas interpretatur confessio. Et nolite ingredi in Galgala, id est hæreticorum et perversorum conciliabula, in quibus omnium revelantur peccata. Galgala quippe revelatio seu volutabrum interpretatur. Hinc ait Psalmista: Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo: et hoc, ubi? Respondet, In consilio justorum et congregatione.
paras.en: [[4:15|If thou play the harlot, O Israel|Si fornicaris tu, Israel]], that is, the congregation of heretics, which is signified by the ten tribes that forsook the law of God, [[4:15|at least let not Juda offend|non delinquat saltem Juda]], that is, the Catholic Church confessing the Lord, which is expressed by the tribe of Juda that kept the law of God. For *Judas* too is interpreted "confession". [[4:15|and go ye not into Galgal|Et nolite ingredi in Galgala]], that is, into the conventicles of heretics and perverse men, in which the sins of all are revealed. For *Galgala* is interpreted "revelation" or "wallowing place". Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 110:1|I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart|Confitebor tibi, Domine, in toto corde meo]]: and where is this? He answers: [[Ps 110:1|in the council of the just, and in the congregation|In consilio justorum et congregatione]].

paras.t: Sicut vacca lasciviens declinavit Israel. Hoc competit universis filiis hujus sæculi, qui absque ullo timore perpetrant mala, et concupiscentias sine reluctatione, imo cum deliberatione, sequuntur. Non enim est timor Domini ante oculos eorum. Nunc pascet eos Dominus quasi agnum in latitudine. Hoc impletur dum reprobis temporalium affluentiam tribuit, eosque permittit incedere per viam spatiosam latamque portam, quæ ducit ad perditionem æternam.
paras.en: [[4:16|Israel hath gone astray like a wanton heifer|Sicut vacca lasciviens declinavit Israel]]. This applies to all the children of this world, who [[Eccles 8:11|commit evils without any fear|absque ullo timore perpetrant mala]], and follow their lusts without resistance, nay, with deliberation. For [[Ps 13:3|there is no fear of God before their eyes|Non enim est timor Domini ante oculos eorum]][[Ps 35:2||]] [Denis has *timor Domini*, "fear of the Lord"]. [[4:16|now will the Lord feed them, as a lamb in a spacious place|Nunc pascet eos Dominus quasi agnum in latitudine]]. This is fulfilled when He grants the reprobate an abundance of temporal things, and lets them go by the spacious way and the wide gate that leads to eternal destruction[[Matt 7:13||]].

paras.t: Dilexerunt afferre ignominiam, id est pravas ordinationes, seu opera ignominiosa, vel oppressiones violentas ac inhonestas super subjectos inducere, protectores ejus, id est principes et prælati populi christiani, qui deberent subditos a malis defendere, atque in bonis munire: cujus oppositum agunt indigni rectores, errantes et in errorem mittentes, cæci et duces cæcorum.
paras.en: [[4:18|have loved to bring shame upon them|Dilexerunt afferre ignominiam]], that is, to bring wicked ordinances, or shameful works, or violent and dishonourable oppressions upon their subjects, [[4:18|they that should have protected them|protectores ejus]], that is, the princes and prelates of the Christian people, who ought to defend their subjects from evils and strengthen them in good things.
