But unworthy rulers do the opposite of this, [[2 Tim 3:13|erring, and driving into error|errantes et in errorem mittentes]], [[Matt 15:14|blind, and leaders of the blind|cæci et duces cæcorum]].

5.title: Expositio litteralis capituli quinti: Audite hoc, sacerdotes, etc.
5.title_en: Literal exposition of the fifth chapter: Hear ye this, O priests, etc.

paras.t: Hoc loco ostendit Propheta cur populus Israel captivari meruerit. Audite auribus cordis et corporis, hoc quod dicam, sacerdotes decem tribuum : non quod fuerint veri sacerdotes de tribu Levi, sed sacerdotes aureorum vitulorum, et a populo sacerdotes vocabantur ; et attendite, domus Israel, id est, decem tribus ; et domus, id est, familia, filii et cognati, regis decem tribuum, auscultate : quia vobiscum judicium est, id est, Deus judicium damnationis vobis inducet. De quo judicio ait Salvator : Qui audit verbum meum, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam, et in judicium non venit. Itemque Apostolus : Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur.
paras.en: In this place the Prophet shows why the people of Israel deserved to be led captive. [[5:1|Hear ye|Audite]] with the ears of heart and body [[5:1|this|hoc]] which I shall say, [[5:1|O priests|sacerdotes]] of the ten tribes: not that they were true priests of the tribe of Levi, but priests of the golden calves, and were called priests by the people; [[5:1|and hearken, O ye house of Israel|et attendite, domus Israel]], that is, the ten tribes; and [[5:1|O house|et domus]], that is, the household, sons and kinsfolk, [[5:1|of the king|regis]] of the ten tribes, [[5:1|give ear|auscultate]]: [[5:1|for there is a judgment against you|quia vobiscum judicium est]], that is, God will bring upon you the judgment of damnation. Of which judgment the Saviour says: [[John 5:24|he who heareth my word and believeth him that sent me hath life everlasting: and cometh not into judgment|Qui audit verbum meum, et credit ei qui misit me, habet vitam æternam, et in judicium non venit]]. And likewise the Apostle: [[1 Cor 11:31|if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged|Si nos ipsos dijudicaremus, non utique judicaremur]].

paras.t: Quoniam laqueus, id est causa deceptionis et captivitatis, seu illaqueatores ac seductores, facti estis vos, sacerdotes et principes, seu familia regis, qui aliorum provisores esse deberetis, speculationi, id est plebi, cujus speculatores estis effecti, et quæ per speculationem vestram esset ad cœlestia erigenda ; et facti estis sicut rete expansum super montem Thabor. Quemadmodum enim in monte hoc aves capi solebant per rete, sic rex et majores ac sacerdotes posuerunt in monte isto ministros, qui caperent transeuntes Jerusalem ad immolandum ibi Deo vero in templo. Quidam enim ex decem tribubus idololatriam abhorrebant, et ex devotione secundum legis præceptum ire volebant ad offerendum in Jerusalem ; sed rex et sacerdotes non permiserunt. Porro secundum Hieronymum, Thabor est mons Galilææ, in campestribus situs, rotundus et altus, qui ex omni parte finitur æqualiter : de quo habetur in Psalmo : Thabor et Hermon in nomine tuo exsultabunt. In hoc monte transfiguratus est Christus, et post resurrectionem apparuit Apostolis, secundum expositores. Quem Petrus in secunda sua epistola nominat sanctum : Hanc, inquiens, vocem de cœlo allatam nos audivimus, quum essemus cum ipso in monte sancto.
paras.en: [[5:1|Because|Quoniam]] [[5:1|you have been|facti estis vos]] [[5:1|a snare|laqueus]], that is, a cause of deceit and captivity, or ensnarers and seducers, you priests and princes, or household of the king, who ought to have been the providers for others, [[5:1|to them whom you should have watched over|speculationi]] [the Latin *speculatio* is a watching or watch-tower; Denis takes it of the people, whose watchmen (*speculatores*) the priests were made], that is, to the common people, whose watchmen you were made, and who through your watching ought to have been raised up to heavenly things; and you have become, as it were, [[5:1|a net spread upon|rete expansum super]] mount [[5:1|Thabor|Thabor]]. For as birds were wont to be caught with a net on this mountain, so the king and the great men and the priests set servants on that mountain to catch those passing over to Jerusalem to sacrifice there to the true God in the temple. For some of the ten tribes abhorred idolatry, and out of devotion wished to go, according to the precept of the law, to make offering in Jerusalem; but the king and the priests did not permit it. Further, according to Jerome, Thabor is a mountain of Galilee, set in the plains, round and high, and ending evenly on every side; of which we have in the Psalm: [[Ps 88:13|Thabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name|Thabor et Hermon in nomine tuo exsultabunt]]. On this mountain Christ was transfigured[[Matt 17:1||]][[Matt 17:2||]], and after the resurrection appeared to the Apostles, according to the expositors. Peter in his second epistle calls it holy: [[2 Pet 1:18|And this voice|Hanc]], he says, [[2 Pet 1:18|we heard brought from heaven, when we were with him in the holy mount|vocem de cœlo allatam nos audivimus, quum essemus cum ipso in monte sancto]].

paras.t: Et victimas vestras ac populi declinastis in profundum, id est in barathrum damnationis, atque in lacum peccati : quia quæ Deo fuerant offerenda cum sublimitate virtutum, obtulistis et offerri jussistis in idolorum honorem cum profunditate vitiorum. Et ego Dominus eruditor sum omnium eorum, videlicet sacerdotum, domus regis ac populi : id est, non obstante tanta ipsorum malitia, ego per Prophetas meos doceo eos et moneo ad pœnitentiam.
paras.en: [[5:2|And you have turned aside victims|Et victimas]], your own and the people's, [[5:2|into the depth|declinastis in profundum]], that is, into the abyss of damnation and into the pit of sin: for what was to have been offered to God with the loftiness of virtues, you have offered and commanded to be offered in honour of idols with the depth of vices. [[5:2|and I|Et ego]] the Lord [[5:2|am the teacher of them all|eruditor sum omnium eorum]], namely of the priests, of the king's house and of the people: that is, notwithstanding their so great malice, I teach them by my Prophets and admonish them to penance.

paras.t: Ego scio Ephraim, id est reges successores Jeroboam Ephratæi, qui eum secuti sunt genere vel peccato. Ejus namque idololatriæ et peccatis omnes posteriores reges Israel adhæserunt. Unde per Ephraim designatur, quia Jeroboam primus rex decem tribuum, fuit de genere Ephraim filii Joseph. Et Israel, id est populus decem tribuum, non est absconditus a me, cujus oculis aperta et nuda sunt omnia. Hos autem perversos et reprobos dicitur Deus scire, non scientia approbationis, de qua dicit Apostolus, Si quis diligit Deum, hic cognitus est ab eo ; sed intelligentia visionis. Unde apud Jeremiam Dominus ait : Si occultabitur vir in absconditis, et ego non videbo eum? Hæc ideo loquitur Deus, ut impii audientes se a Deo cognosci, metuant in ejus præsentia prævaricari. Quia nunc fornicatus est Ephraim : successores enim Jeroboam non recesserunt a vitulorum cultura ; contaminatus est Israel, id est, populus eisdem pollutus est vitiis quibus et reges, quorum consilio ad idololatriam devenerunt. Qualis enim est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea, ut dicit Ecclesiasticus. In Proverbiis quoque habetur : Regnantibus impiis, ruinæ hominum. Et rex injustus ministros habet impios, teste Scriptura.
paras.en: [[5:3|I know Ephraim|Ego scio Ephraim]], that is, the kings who succeeded Jeroboam the Ephrathite, who followed him in stock or in sin. For all the later kings of Israel clung to his idolatry and sins. Hence they are signified by Ephraim, because Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes, was of the stock[[3 Kings 11:26||]] of Ephraim the son of Joseph[[Gen 41:52||]]. [[5:3|and Israel|Et Israel]], that is, the people of the ten tribes, [[5:3|is not hid from me|non est absconditus a me]], for [[Heb 4:13|all things are naked and open to his eyes|cujus oculis aperta et nuda sunt omnia]]. Now God is said to know these perverse and reprobate men, not by the knowledge of approval, of which the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 8:3|if any man love God, the same is known by him|Si quis diligit Deum, hic cognitus est ab eo]], but by the understanding of sight [that is, the knowledge of mere vision, by which God sees all things, good and bad, as distinct from the knowledge of approval by which he knows the good as his own]. Hence the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:24|Shall a man be hid in secret places, and I not see him|Si occultabitur vir in absconditis, et ego non videbo eum]]? God says these things so that the wicked, hearing that they are known by God, may fear to transgress in his presence. [[5:3|for now Ephraim hath committed fornication|Quia nunc fornicatus est Ephraim]]: for the successors of Jeroboam did not depart from the worship of the calves; [[5:3|Israel is defiled|contaminatus est Israel]], that is, the people is polluted with the same vices as the kings, by whose counsel they came to idolatry. For [[Ecclus 10:2|what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Qualis enim est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea]], as Ecclesiasticus says. In Proverbs too we have: [[Prov 28:12|when the wicked reign, men are ruined|Regnantibus impiis, ruinæ hominum]]. And an unjust king [[Prov 29:12|hath all his servants wicked|ministros habet impios]], as Scripture witnesses [Denis's "an unjust king" stands for the Douay-Rheims's "a prince that gladly heareth lying words"].

paras.t: Non dabunt, id est, non disponent, cogitationes suas ut revertantur ad Deum suum, quum sint obstinati. Unde non cogitant de remedio pœnitentiæ, sed de continuatione culpæ intentæ, seu exsecutione mali propositi. Quia spiritus fornicationum, id est dæmon ad idololatriam suggerens, qui secundum Apostolum operatur in filiis diffidentiæ, est in medio eorum, tanquam possessor cordis ipsorum, vastis eos tenebris circumplectens : unde nec pœnitent. Et Dominum non cognoverunt cognitione sincera ac formata. Aliqualem tamen de Deo habuerunt notitiam, sicut et multi gentilium, præsertim ex generali fama et instructione prophetica.
paras.en: [[5:4|They will not set|Non dabunt]], that is, will not dispose, [[5:4|their thoughts to return to their God|cogitationes suas ut revertantur ad Deum suum]], since they are obstinate. Hence they do not think of the remedy of penance, but of continuing in the sin they intend, or of carrying out their evil purpose. [[5:4|for the spirit of fornication|Quia spiritus fornicationum]], that is, the devil suggesting idolatry, who, according to the Apostle, [[Eph 2:2|worketh on the children of unbelief|operatur in filiis diffidentiæ]], [[5:4|is in the midst of them|est in medio eorum]], as the possessor of their heart, wrapping them round in vast darkness: hence they do not repent. [[5:4|and they have not known the Lord|Et Dominum non cognoverunt]] with a sincere and formed knowledge [*formata*: that is, quickened by charity, as faith is called "formed" when it is informed by charity]. Yet they had some knowledge of God, as many of the gentiles also had, chiefly from common report and the teaching of the prophets.

paras.t: Et respondebit arrogantia Israel in facie ejus : id est, populus decem tribuum pro sua superbia qua Dei cultum contempsit, debitam luet pœnam, ita quod superbia dabit eis vicem ac reale responsum per ultionis experientiam. Juxta quem modum asserit Isaias : Peccata nostra responderunt nobis. Jeremias quoque ait : Si peccata nostra responderint nobis, Domine, fac propter nomen tuum. Et Israel et Ephraim ruent in iniquitate sua, id est, populus et rex pariter capientur propter facinora sua : sicut impletum est quando ab Assyriis capti sunt, ut legitur quarto Regum. Ruet etiam, id est capietur, Judas, id est regnum Juda, videlicet duæ tribus atque Levitæ, cum eis, id est sicut et decem tribus. Non enim eodem tempore, nec ab eisdem capti sunt hostibus, ut patet ex dictis in expositione primi capituli.
paras.en: [[5:5|And the pride of Israel shall answer in his face|Et respondebit arrogantia Israel in facie ejus]]: that is, the people of the ten tribes, for its pride, by which it despised the worship of God, shall pay the due penalty, so that its pride will give them their requital and a real answer through the experience of vengeance. In the same manner Isaias says: [[Is 59:12|our sins have testified against us|Peccata nostra responderunt nobis]]. Jeremias also says: [[Jer 14:7|If our iniquities have testified against us, O Lord, do thou it for thy name's sake|Si peccata nostra responderint nobis, Domine, fac propter nomen tuum]] [in both places the Latin has the same verb as the verse treated, *respondere*, "to answer"; Jeremias has *iniquitates*, "iniquities", where Denis has *peccata*, "sins"]. [[5:5|and Israel, and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity|Et Israel et Ephraim ruent in iniquitate sua]], that is, the people and the king alike shall be taken for their crimes: as was fulfilled when they were taken by the Assyrians, as is read in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 17:1||]]. [[5:5|also shall fall|Ruet etiam]], that is, shall be taken, [[5:5|Juda|Judas]], that is, the kingdom of Juda, namely the two tribes and the Levites, [[5:5|with them|cum eis]], that is, as the ten tribes also: for they were not taken at the same time, nor by the same enemies, as is clear from what was said in the exposition of the first chapter.

paras.t: In gregibus suis, id est cum capris et ovibus, et in armentis suis, id est vaccis et bobus, vadent decem tribus, et etiam Juda et Benjamin, ad quærendum Dominum, id est ad offerendum Domino hostias de animalibus immolaticiis, quatenus misericordiam impetrent, videlicet liberationem ab hostibus ; et non invenient eum, quoniam sero poenitent, non ex caritate, sed servili timore propter captivitatem instantem. Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait : Si quaeritis, quaerite : id est, si quaeritis me, hoc facite sincere, atque ex caritate et amore justitiae. Apud Jeremiam quoque : Si reverteris, Israel, ad me convertere : hoc est, non tua principaliter commoda quaeras privato amore, sed meum honorem ex spirituali dilectione. Ablatus est ab eis, id est, Deus suae pietatis effectum juste tulit ab eis, quemadmodum in Isaia habetur : Quum multiplicaveritis orationes, non exaudiam ; manus enim vestrae sanguine plenae sunt. Quamdiu enim permanet homo in voluntate peccandi, non veraciter poenitens, non meretur a Domino exaudiri. Hinc Jeremias dicit : Numquid carnes sanctae auferent a te malitias tuas ?
paras.en: [[5:6|With their flocks|In gregibus suis]], that is, with goats and sheep, [[5:6|and with their herds|et in armentis suis]], that is, with cows and oxen, [[5:6|they shall go|vadent]], the ten tribes, and Juda and Benjamin as well, [[5:6|to seek the Lord|ad quærendum Dominum]], that is, to offer the Lord victims from the beasts fit for sacrifice, so as to obtain mercy, namely deliverance from their enemies; [[5:6|and shall not find him|et non invenient eum]], since they repent too late, not out of charity, but from servile fear because of the captivity at hand [servile fear: the fear of punishment only, as distinct from the filial fear of offending God]. Hence the Lord says by Isaias: [[Is 21:12|if you seek, seek|Si quaeritis, quaerite]]: that is, if you seek me, do it sincerely, and out of charity and love of justice. In Jeremias also: [[Jer 4:1|If thou wilt return, O Israel|Si reverteris, Israel]], [[Jer 4:1|return to me|ad me convertere]]: that is, do not seek chiefly thine own advantage out of private love, but my honour out of spiritual love. [[5:6|he is withdrawn from them|Ablatus est ab eis]] [literally "he is taken away from them"], that is, God has justly taken away from them the effect of his loving-kindness, as we have in Isaias: [[Is 1:15|when you multiply prayer, I will not hear: for your hands are full of blood|Quum multiplicaveritis orationes, non exaudiam ; manus enim vestrae sanguine plenae sunt]]. For as long as a man remains in the will to sin, not truly repenting, he does not deserve to be heard by the Lord. Hence Jeremias says: [[Jer 11:15|shall the holy flesh take away from thee thy crimes|Numquid carnes sanctae auferent a te malitias tuas]]?

paras.t: In Domino, id est contra Deum, praevaricati sunt, quia filios alienos a cultu veri Dei genuerunt. Nam filios suos docuerunt idololatrare, ita quod erant filii daemonum magis quam Dei. Quidam etiam per ignem consecraverunt idolis filios suos. Nunc devorabit eos, scilicet decem tribus, mensis : id est, statim, vel infra mensem seu tempus jam proximum, capientur ab hostibus. Vel sensus est, quod quolibet mense adversarii ingrederentur terram eorum, eosque vastarent. Cum partibus suis, id est bonis et possessionibus quas unaquaeque tribus habebat in sorte atque funiculo suo, secundum quod tempore Josue terra partita fuit secundum numerum tribuum Israel. Quidam exponunt sic : Nunc devorabit eos mensis, scilicet Julii, quia in mense Julii capta fertur Samaria, tuncque Assyrii partem populi occiderunt, et bona eorum diripuerunt. Dicitur autem mensis seu tempus facere ea, quae fiunt in eo.
paras.en: [[5:7|against the Lord|In Domino]], that is, against God, they [[5:7|have transgressed|praevaricati sunt]], [[5:7|for they have begotten children that are strangers|quia filios alienos]] to the worship of the true God. For they taught their sons to worship idols, so that they were sons of the devils rather than of God. Some even consecrated their sons to idols through fire. [[5:7|now shall|Nunc]] [[5:7|a month|mensis]] [[5:7|devour them|devorabit eos]], namely the ten tribes: that is, at once, or within a month or a time now near, they shall be taken by their enemies. Or the sense is that every month the enemy would enter their land and lay them waste. [[5:7|with their portions|Cum partibus suis]], that is, with the goods and possessions which each tribe had by its lot and line [that is, the measuring line by which the land was allotted], according as the land was divided in the time of Josue by the number of the tribes of Israel[[Jos 13:1||]] [the margin gives Josue xiii–xxi]. Some expound it thus: [[5:7|now shall a month devour them|Nunc devorabit eos mensis]], namely the month of July, because Samaria is said to have been taken in the month of July, and then the Assyrians slew part of the people and plundered their goods. Now a month, or a time, is said to do the things that are done in it.

paras.t: Clangite buccina in Gabaa, et clangite tuba in Rama : id est, vos de tribu Benjamin, quum videritis aut perceperitis captivitatem decem tribuum, vobis in vicino habitantium, tunc clangite buccina in duabus urbibus firmioribus seu fortalitiis vestrae sortis, scilicet in Gabaa, ubi natus atque moratus est Saul, et in Rama. Hujus buccinationis potest reddi duplex causa : Una, ut populum Juda ac Benjamin excitarent ad praeparandum se contra Assyrios, ne vastarentur ab eis quemadmodum decem tribus, quarum una, scilicet Ephraim, erat proxima populo Benjamin, quoad habitationis vicinitatem. Secunda, ut decem tribuum captivitatem deflerent. Ululate, habitantes in Bethaven, id est Bethel urbe ac fortalitio Ephraim, quae urbs est post tergum tuum, Benjamin, id est in confinio tuo, seu juxta te : nam ibi finiebatur sors Benjamin. Recte vero ait Propheta, Ululate in Bethaven, quia habitatores Bethel jam dirissime capiendi fuerunt.
paras.en: [[5:8|Blow ye the cornet in Gabaa|Clangite buccina in Gabaa]], and blow ye [[5:8|the trumpet in Rama|tuba in Rama]]: that is, you of the tribe of Benjamin, when you see or perceive the captivity of the ten tribes who dwell near you, then blow the cornet in the two strongest cities or fortresses of your lot, namely in Gabaa, where Saul was born and dwelt[[1 Kings 10:26||]], and in Rama. A twofold cause can be given for this blowing of the cornet. The first, that they might rouse the people of Juda and Benjamin to prepare themselves against the Assyrians, lest they be laid waste by them as the ten tribes were, one of which, namely Ephraim, was the nearest to the people of Benjamin as to nearness of dwelling[[Jos 18:11||]]. The second, that they might bewail the captivity of the ten tribes. [[5:8|howl ye|Ululate]], you who dwell [[5:8|in Bethaven|in Bethaven]], that is, in Bethel, a city and fortress of Ephraim, which city is [[5:8|behind thy back, O Benjamin|post tergum tuum, Benjamin]], that is, on thy border, or next to thee: for there the lot of Benjamin ended. And rightly does the Prophet say, [[5:8|howl ye in Bethaven|Ululate in Bethaven]], because the dwellers in Bethel were soon to be taken most cruelly.

paras.t: Ephraim, id est rex et populus decem tribuum, in desolatione erit, quum fuerit ab Assyriis captus. In die correptionis, id est punitionis decem tribuum, et in tribubus Israel ostendi fidem, id est, manifestavi vera atque fidelia esse Prophetarum eloquia, quibus captivitatem Israel praenuntiavi. Nempe ut Jeremias testatur : Quum venerit quod Propheta praedixit, scietur Propheta, quem misit Dominus in veritate. Per hoc ergo quod Dominus tradidit tribus Israel hostibus, sicut praedixit, ostendit in eis, hoc est per eorum captivitatem, fidelitatem verborum suorum, seu Prophetarum qui captivitatem illam praedixerunt.
paras.en: [[5:9|Ephraim|Ephraim]], that is, the king and people of the ten tribes, [[5:9|shall be in desolation|in desolatione erit]] when he has been taken by the Assyrians. [[5:9|in the day of rebuke|In die correptionis]], that is, of the punishment of the ten tribes, and [[5:9|among the tribes of Israel I have shewn that which shall surely be|in tribubus Israel ostendi fidem]] [the Latin *ostendi fidem* is literally "I have shewn faith", that is, faithfulness: so Denis takes it], that is, I have made plain that the sayings of the Prophets, by which I foretold the captivity of Israel, are true and faithful. For as Jeremias testifies: [[Jer 28:9|when his word shall come to pass, the prophet shall be known, whom the hath sent in truth|Quum venerit quod Propheta praedixit, scietur Propheta, quem misit Dominus in veritate]] [Denis's wording differs a little: "when what the prophet foretold shall come"]. By this, then, that the Lord delivered the tribes of Israel to their enemies, as he had foretold, he showed in them, that is, by their captivity, the faithfulness of his words, or of the Prophets who foretold that captivity.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur iniquitas, et ob eam inducta calamitas tribuum Juda ac Benjamin. Facti sunt principes Juda, id est principales et potentiores de regno Juda, quasi assumentes terminum, id est terram decem tribuum occupare et possidere optantes. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt, Quasi transferentes terminum : quoniam sortem suam dilatare quaerebant ultra metam propriae sortis divinitus constitutam : sicque pro eo quod decem tribuum captivitatem deflere debuerant, hinc potius gloriabantur, quod ditiores jam fierent. Hæc dictio, Quasi, dicit hoc loco veritatem, non similitudinem tantum. Super eos, videlicet principes Juda, effundam quasi aquam, id est copiose, iram meam, id est justitiæ meæ effectum, rigorose puniendo eos per Chaldæos propter tantam perversitatem.
paras.en: Next is described the iniquity of the tribes of Juda and Benjamin, and the calamity brought on them for it. [[5:10|The princes of Juda are become|Facti sunt principes Juda]], that is, the chief and more powerful men of the kingdom of Juda, [[5:10|as they that take up the bound|quasi assumentes terminum]], that is, wishing to seize and possess the land of the ten tribes. Hence the Septuagint translated, *As they that remove the bound*: for they sought to widen their lot beyond the limit of their own lot set by God; and so, where they ought to have bewailed the captivity of the ten tribes, they gloried in it rather, because they were now becoming richer. The word *as* here expresses the truth, not only a likeness. [[5:10|upon them|Super eos]], namely the princes of Juda, [[5:10|I will pour out|effundam]] [[5:10|like water|quasi aquam]], that is, abundantly, [[5:10|my wrath|iram meam]], that is, the effect of my justice, punishing them rigorously by the Chaldeans for so great perversity.

paras.t: Calumniam, id est injuriam, patiens est Ephraim, id est populus decem tribuum : non quod non meruerint hanc captivitatem et pœnam, sed quia a regibus Assyriorum injustis, impia voluntate ac mala intentione vastati sunt, et adversariis traditi, a Deo magis alienis quam ipsi, ac pessimis : et quoad hoc, est quædam calumnia non ex parte Dei, sed hostium pessimorum. Quod tamen non fuerit mera calumnia, declaratur quum subditur : fractus judicio, id est, justo Dei judicio dejectus est Ephraim, quoniam cœpit abire a Deo, post sordes, id est idolatriam a tempore Jeroboam primi regis sui.
paras.en: [[5:11|Ephraim is under oppression|patiens est Ephraim]] [the Latin, *calumniam patiens est*, is literally "suffers calumny", that is, a false charge or wrongful treatment; Denis glosses *calumniam* as "injury"], Ephraim being the people of the ten tribes: not that they did not deserve this captivity and punishment, but because they were laid waste, with wicked will and evil intent, by the unjust kings of the Assyrians, and handed over to enemies more estranged from God than they themselves, and most wicked; and in this respect it is a kind of calumny, not on God's part, but on the part of those most wicked enemies. Yet that it was not mere calumny is declared when it is added: [[5:11|and broken in judgment|fractus judicio]], that is, by the just judgment of God Ephraim is cast down, [[5:11|because he began to go|quoniam cœpit abire]] away from God, [[5:11|after filthiness|post sordes]], that is, after idolatry, from the time of Jeroboam his first king.

paras.t: Et ego Deus ero quasi tinea Ephraim, id est decem tribubus, consumendo eas per Assyrios, quemadmodum a tinea consumitur vestis. Et ero quasi putredo quæ ligna et carnes consumit, domui, id est populo, Juda, dejiciendo regnum Juda per Chaldæos. Secundum Hieronymum, Deus comparat se tineæ atque putredini, quia utrumque eorum tarde consumit materiam : sic Deus diu dedit utrique regno pœnitentiæ tempus, et paulatim ea afflixit, donec omnino deleta sunt. Alii dicunt, quod quum tinea soleat citius corrumpere vestem, quam putredo lignum, ideo Dominus perhibet se quasi tineam esse Ephraim, et ut putredinem populo Juda, quoniam regnum decem tribuum captivatum fuit ante regnum Juda.
paras.en: [[5:12|And I|Et ego]] God [[5:12|will be like a moth to Ephraim|ero quasi tinea Ephraim]], that is, to the ten tribes, consuming them by the Assyrians, as a garment is consumed by the moth. [[5:12|and like rottenness|Et ero quasi putredo]], which consumes wood and flesh, [[5:12|to the house|domui]], that is, the people, [[5:12|of Juda|Juda]], casting down the kingdom of Juda by the Chaldeans. According to Jerome, God compares himself to a moth and to rottenness because each of them consumes its matter slowly: so God gave both kingdoms a long time for penance, and afflicted them little by little, until they were wholly destroyed. Others say that since a moth is wont to spoil a garment more quickly than rottenness does wood, the Lord therefore declares himself to be as a moth to Ephraim and as rottenness to the people of Juda, because the kingdom of the ten tribes was led captive before the kingdom of Juda.

paras.t: Et vidit Ephraim languorem suum, id est impotentiam, qua non potuit reluctari Assyriis, vel regi Damasci ; et Juda, id est populus duarum tribuum, vidit, id est consideravit, vinculum suum, id est vastitatem seu captivitatem sibi imminentem tempore Achaz et filiorum Josiæ. Et abiit Ephraim ad Assur, id est, a rege Assyriorum petierunt auxilium contra regem Syriæ et Damasci. Tempore enim Manahem regis Israel contigit hoc, ut dicitur quarto Regum : quia tunc rex Syriæ impugnavit decem tribus, quem rex Assyriorum superavit. Vel sensus est, quod Ephraim ivit ad Assur, quia ad tempus fuit regnum decem tribuum subditum regi Assyriorum, solvens ei tributum per singulos annos. Postmodum vero et misit Ephraim ad regem ultorem, id est regem Ægypti, qui tunc potens exstitit et famosus, ulciscens in adversarios suos, quatenus rex Ægypti erueret eos de manu Assyriorum. Hoc fecit Osee rex Israel. Et ipse rex Ægypti non poterit salvare (* alias sanare) vos, o decem tribus, de potestate Assyriorum : imo rex Assyriorum, audito quod misit Osee rex Israel ad Pharaonem, venit, et cepit atque occidit Osee, et populum transtulit. Nec solvere poterit a vobis, o Juda, vinculum jam præfatum. Non enim potuerunt Ægyptii liberare regnum Juda de manu Chaldæorum, ut legitur secundo Paralipomenon. Tunc quippe cœpit potestas Pharaonis vehementer deficere, dum reges Assyriorum sic invalescebant ; et rex Chaldæorum Nabuchodonosor penitus dejecit regem Ægypti. De hac materia in diversis capitulis multa vaticinatus est Isaias, ut quum ait : Væ qui descendunt in Ægyptum ad auxilium, etc. ; Jeremias quoque et Ezechiel.
paras.en: [[5:13|And Ephraim saw his sickness|Et vidit Ephraim languorem suum]], that is, his powerlessness, by which he could not withstand the Assyrians, or the king of Damascus; [[5:13|and Juda|et Juda]], that is, the people of the two tribes, saw, that is, considered, [[5:13|his band|vinculum suum]], that is, the devastation or captivity hanging over him in the time of Achaz and of the sons of Josias. [[5:13|and Ephraim went to the Assyrian|Et abiit Ephraim ad Assur]], that is, they sought help from the king of the Assyrians against the king of Syria and Damascus. For this happened in the time of Manahem king of Israel, as is said in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 15:19||]]: because the king of Syria then attacked the ten tribes, and the king of the Assyrians overcame him. Or the sense is that Ephraim went to the Assyrian because for a time the kingdom of the ten tribes was subject to the king of the Assyrians, paying him tribute every year. But afterwards Ephraim also [[5:13|sent|misit]] [[5:13|to the avenging king|ad regem ultorem]], that is, to the king of Egypt, who was then powerful and renowned, taking vengeance on his adversaries, so that the king of Egypt might deliver them out of the hand of the Assyrians. This Osee king of Israel did[[4 Kings 17:4||]]. [[5:13|and he|Et ipse]], the king of Egypt, [[5:13|shall not be able to heal|non poterit salvare]] [a printed note gives the variant *sanare*, "heal", the reading of the Vulgate; the text has *salvare*, "save"] [[5:13|you|vos]], O ten tribes, from the power of the Assyrians: nay, the king of the Assyrians, hearing that Osee king of Israel had sent to Pharao, came[[4 Kings 17:5||]], and took and slew Osee[[4 Kings 17:4||]], and carried the people away[[4 Kings 17:6||]]. [[5:13|neither shall he be able to take off|Nec solvere poterit]] [[5:13|from you|a vobis]], O Juda, [[5:13|the band|vinculum]] already mentioned. For the Egyptians could not deliver the kingdom of Juda out of the hand of the Chaldeans, as is read in the second book of Paralipomenon[[4 Kings 24:7||]] [the margin gives "Ibid. xxiv, 7", that is, 4 Kings 24:7, though Denis names Paralipomenon]. For then the power of Pharao began greatly to fail, while the kings of the Assyrians grew so strong; and Nabuchodonosor king of the Chaldeans cast down the king of Egypt utterly[[4 Kings 24:7||]]. Of this matter Isaias prophesied much in divers chapters, as when he says: [[Is 31:1|Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help|Væ qui descendunt in Ægyptum ad auxilium]], etc.; and Jeremias also[[Jer 42:1||]][[Jer 46:1||]], and Ezechiel[[Ezech 17:1||]][[Ezech 29:1||]] [the margin gives Jer. xlii–xliv, xlvi; Ezech. xvii, xxix–xxxii].

paras.t: Quoniam ego Deus omnipotens, quo adversante, nullus valet succurrere, ero quasi leæna Ephraim, id est decem tribubus, eas terribiliter atque velociter per Assyrios puniendo. Septuaginta transtulerunt, Ego quasi panther Ephraim. Panther autem, secundum Hieronymum, est animal sævum ac velocissimum, quo significatur velox interitus Ephraim ab Assyriis. Et quasi catulus leonis ero domui Juda, per Chaldæos destruendo regnum ipsius. Ego capiam, id est, virtutem capiendi donabo Assyriis et Chaldæis, et vadam, non locum mutando, sed per vindictam impios visitando ; tollam totum Israel de terra propria, et non est qui eruat de manu mea, cui nullus potest obsistere. Unde ait Salvator : Nemo potest rapere de manu Patris mei. Et in Job habetur : Deus, cujus iræ resistere nemo potest, et sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem.
paras.en: [[5:14|For I|Quoniam ego]], God almighty, against whom none can give help, [[5:14|will be like a lioness to Ephraim|ero quasi leæna Ephraim]], that is, to the ten tribes, punishing them terribly and swiftly by the Assyrians. The Septuagint translated, *I am as a panther to Ephraim*. Now the panther, according to Jerome, is a fierce and very swift animal, by which is signified the swift destruction of Ephraim by the Assyrians. [[5:14|and like a lion's whelp to the house of Juda|Et quasi catulus leonis ero domui Juda]], destroying his kingdom by the Chaldeans. [[5:14|I will catch|Ego capiam]], that is, I will give the Assyrians and Chaldeans the power to catch, [[5:14|and go|et vadam]], not by changing place, but by visiting the wicked with vengeance; [[5:14|I will take away|tollam]] the whole of Israel from its own land, [[5:14|and there is none that can rescue|et non est qui eruat]] out of my hand, whom none can withstand. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 10:29|no one can snatch them out of the hand of my Father|Nemo potest rapere de manu Patris mei]]. And in Job we have: [[Job 9:13|God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world|Deus, cujus iræ resistere nemo potest, et sub quo curvantur qui portant orbem]].

paras.t: Vadens, id est ultione facta, a vobis recedens per gratiæ atque subsidii subtractionem, revertar ad locum meum, id est, in me ipso quiescam. Locus Dei, est majestas et magnificentia ejus, secundum Hieronymum : imo Divinitas est locus sui ipsius, quia nil extra eam est, quo contineatur. Hinc secundum antiquos philosophos, Infinitum fulcit se ipsum. Vel per locum Dei, intelliguntur electi gentiles, quos, abjectis Judæis, cœpit Deus per gratiam inhabitare. Loquitur autem Deus de se ipso metaphorice per modum judicis irati, qui accedit ad puniendum aliquos : quo facto, ad pristinum revertitur locum. Donec deficiatis victi ab hostibus, et quæratis faciem meam, id est pietatis meæ respectum, seu gratiosam præsentiam : quod fecerunt duæ tribus circa finem Babyloniæ captivitatis. Decem vero tribus circa finem mundi id facturæ creduntur.
paras.en: [[5:15|I will go|Vadens]], that is, vengeance being done, withdrawing from you by the withdrawal of grace and help, [[5:15|and return to my place|revertar ad locum meum]], that is, I will rest in myself. The place of God is his majesty and magnificence, according to Jerome; nay rather, the Godhead is its own place, since there is nothing outside it by which it could be contained. Hence, according to the ancient philosophers, the Infinite upholds itself. Or by the place of God are understood the chosen gentiles, in whom, the Jews being cast off, God began to dwell by grace. Now God speaks of himself metaphorically, after the manner of an angry judge who goes out to punish certain men and, this done, returns to his former place. [[5:15|until you are consumed|Donec deficiatis]], overcome by your enemies, [[5:15|and seek my face|et quæratis faciem meam]], that is, the regard of my loving-kindness, or my gracious presence: which the two tribes did about the end of the Babylonian captivity. The ten tribes are believed to be going to do it about the end of the world.

5.title: Expositio tropologica seu moralis ejusdem capituli quinti.
5.title_en: Tropological or moral exposition of the same fifth chapter.

paras.t: Moraliter, per sacerdotes et domum regis, qui facti sunt laqueus speculationi, et sicut rete expansum ad capiendas subvertendasque animas, intelliguntur principes, doctores, et prælati Ecclesiæ negligentes atque indigni : quos Christus constituit super familiam suam, ut sint provisores et custodes pervigiles dominici gregis ; sed ipsi propria lucra et voluptatem sectantes, negligunt subditorum salutem, quodque damnabilius est, homines innocentes, pios et simplices frequenter derident, persequuntur, atque a bonæ voluntatis exsecutione impediunt, quia nec ipsi intrant, nec introeuntes sinunt intrare. Contra quod admonet Petrus in prima sua Canonica : Pascite qui in vobis est gregem, providentes secundum Deum, non turpis lucri gratia, neque ut dominantes in clero, sed forma gregis effecti, et ex animo. Paulus quoque ad Timotheum : Esto exemplum fidelium, in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate. Denique, qui per verba ornata, per sapientiæ ostentationem, per apparentem sanctitatem, per temporalis prosperitatis virorem, seu gradus vel auctoritatis sublimitatem alios fallunt, hi sunt quasi rete expansum super Thabor montem. De tali etenim legitur monte : Quomodo dicitis animæ meæ, Transmigra in montem sicut passer?
paras.en: Morally, by the [[5:1|priests|sacerdotes]] and the [[5:1|house of the king|domum regis]], who have become [[5:1|a snare to them whom you should have watched over|laqueus speculationi]], and as a net spread to catch and overthrow souls, are understood the princes, doctors and prelates of the Church who are negligent and unworthy: whom Christ has set over his household, to be the providers and the ever-watchful keepers of the Lord's flock; but they, pursuing their own gains and pleasure, neglect the salvation of those in their charge, and, what is more damnable, often deride and persecute innocent, devout and simple men, and hinder them from carrying out their good will, since they neither enter in themselves, nor suffer those who are entering in to enter[[Luke 11:52||]] [the margin gives Luke 11:52; Denis's wording is closer to Matt 23:13]. Against this Peter admonishes in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 5:2|Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking care of it|Pascite qui in vobis est gregem, providentes]] [[1 Pet 5:2|according to God|secundum Deum]], [[1 Pet 5:2|not for filthy lucre's sake|non turpis lucri gratia]], [[1 Pet 5:3|Neither as lording it over the clergy but being made a pattern of the flock from the heart|neque ut dominantes in clero, sed forma gregis effecti, et ex animo]]. And Paul to Timothy: [[1 Tim 4:12|be thou an example of the faithful, in word, in conversation, in charity|Esto exemplum fidelium, in verbo, in conversatione, in caritate]]. Lastly, those who deceive others by ornate words, by a display of wisdom, by an appearance of holiness, by the green flourish of temporal prosperity, or by the loftiness of their rank or authority, are as it were [[5:1|a net spread upon Thabor|rete expansum super Thabor]] mount. For of such a mountain we read: [[Ps 10:2|how then do you say to my soul: Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow|Quomodo dicitis animæ meæ, Transmigra in montem sicut passer?]]?

paras.t: Præterea isti declinant, id est, mittunt seu deprimunt, victimas in profundum, dum spirituales seu corporales oblationes sui vel subditorum, referunt ad finem indebitum, ad gloriam vanam, ad transitorium emolumentum, non ad Dei præconium et peccati emundationem, cœlestisque beatitudinis adeptionem. Contra quos loquitur Christus : Quum facis eleemosynam, nesciat sinistra quid faciat dextra ; itemque : Quum oraveris, intra cubiculum, et ora Patrem in abscondito; et : Videte ne faciatis justitiam vestram coram hominibus, ut videamini ab illis; alioqui mercedem non habebitis a Patre vestro, qui in cœlis est.
paras.en: Moreover these [[5:2|turned aside|declinant]], that is, send or press down, [[5:2|victims into the depth|victimas in profundum]], when they refer the spiritual or bodily offerings of themselves or of those in their charge to an undue end, to vainglory, to passing profit, and not to the praise of God, the cleansing of sin and the attaining of heavenly beatitude. Against them Christ speaks: [[Matt 6:2|when thou dost an alms-deed|Quum facis eleemosynam]], [[Matt 6:3|let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth|nesciat sinistra quid faciat dextra]]; and again: [[Matt 6:6|when thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber|Quum oraveris, intra cubiculum]], and [[Matt 6:6|pray to thy Father in secret|ora Patrem in abscondito]]; and: [[Matt 6:1|Take heed that you do not your justice before men, to be seen by them: otherwise you shall not have a reward of your Father who is in heaven|Videte ne faciatis justitiam vestram coram hominibus, ut videamini ab illis; alioqui mercedem non habebitis a Patre vestro, qui in cœlis est]].

paras.t: Et ego eruditor omnium eorum. Quotidie docet Christus nos omnes per prædicatores, per Scripturas, per signa, per angelicam inspirationem, per divinum instinctum, per naturalis ingenii perspicacitatem : quia signatum est super nos lumen vultus Dei, ita quod ignorantia nos nequaquam excuset. Unde apud Jeremiam Dominus ait : Erudire, ne forte recedat anima mea a te. Impii vero agnitæ veritatis non sequuntur doctrinam, sed vitiis passionibusque vincuntur, et more pecudum, voluptate, non ratione, feruntur.
paras.en: [[5:2|And I am the teacher of them all|Et ego eruditor omnium eorum]]. Daily Christ teaches us all through preachers, through the Scriptures, through signs, through the inspiration of angels, through divine prompting, through the keenness of our natural understanding: because [[Ps 4:7|The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us|signatum est super nos lumen vultus Dei]] [Denis has “the light of the countenance of God”], so that ignorance in no way excuses us. Hence the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 6:8|Be thou instructed|Erudire]], [[Jer 6:8|lest my soul depart from thee|ne forte recedat anima mea a te]]. But the wicked do not follow the teaching of the truth they have known, but are overcome by vices and passions, and after the manner of beasts are carried along by pleasure, not by reason.

paras.t: Ego scio Ephraim, et Israel non est absconditus a me, quia nunc fornicatus est Ephraim, contaminatus est Israel. Ephraim interpretatur augmentum seu incrementum : per quod hoc loco intelliguntur avari, qui thesaurizant sibi in terra, et ignorant cui congregant ea. Hi fornicantur, ponendo spem suam in argento et auro, et animam suam habendo venalem. Per Israel quoque hoc loco intelliguntur ingeniosi, atque informiter docti, nudi speculatores ac frigidi, vani, et ambitiosi, quibus in Isaia dicitur : Sapientia tua et scientia tua deceperunt te. Hi contaminantur, dum quærunt videri, reputari, et in admiratione haberi, pleni inanissima gloriatione in semetipsis, et alios parvi pendentes, non attendentes illud Ecclesiastici : Melior est homo qui minoratur sapientia, et est in timore Dei, quam qui abundat sensu, et transgreditur legem Altissimi. Hunc Ephraim et Israelem scit Christus notitia reprobationis, cujus oculi sunt multo lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum.
paras.en: [[5:3|I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me for now Ephraim hath committed fornication, Israel is defiled|Ego scio Ephraim, et Israel non est absconditus a me, quia nunc fornicatus est Ephraim, contaminatus est Israel]]. Ephraim is interpreted increase or growth: by which in this place are understood the avaricious, who lay up treasure for themselves on earth, and [[Ps 38:7|knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things|ignorant cui congregant ea]]. These commit fornication by putting their hope in silver and gold, and by holding their own soul for sale[[Ecclus 10:10||]]. By Israel too in this place are understood the clever, and those learned without form [that is, learned without the form of charity, which alone gives knowledge its life], bare and cold speculators, vain and ambitious, to whom it is said in Isaias: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia tua et scientia tua deceperunt te]]. These are defiled when they seek to be seen, to be esteemed and to be held in admiration, full of the emptiest boasting within themselves and holding others cheap, not heeding that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 19:21|Better is a man that hath less wisdom|Melior est homo qui minoratur sapientia]], [[Ecclus 19:21|with the fear of God|et est in timore Dei]], [[Ecclus 19:21|than he that aboundeth in understanding, and transgresseth the law of the most High|quam qui abundat sensu, et transgreditur legem Altissimi]]. Such an Ephraim and Israel Christ knows with the knowledge of reprobation [that is, the knowledge by which God foresees those who will be lost], Christ whose eyes [[Ecclus 23:28|are far brighter than the sun, beholding round about all the ways of men|sunt multo lucidiores super solem, circumspicientes omnes vias hominum]].

paras.t: Non dabunt cogitationes suas ut revertantur ad Deum suum : quoniam tales interdum difficilius convertuntur quam simplices et egeni; quia spiritus fornicationis spiritualis, et sæpe etiam corporalis, est in medio eorum : quia in suo ingenio atque divitiis, magis quam in Deo sempiterno, fonte universæ scientiæ ac sufficientiæ, gloriantur.
paras.en: [[5:4|They will not set their thoughts to return to their God|Non dabunt cogitationes suas ut revertantur ad Deum suum]]: since such men are at times converted with more difficulty than the simple and the needy; [[5:4|for the spirit of fornication|quia spiritus fornicationis]], spiritual, and often bodily too, [[5:4|is in the midst of them|in medio eorum]]: for they glory in their own cleverness and riches rather than in the everlasting God, the fount of all knowledge and sufficiency.

paras.t: Et respondebit arrogantia Israel in facie ejus, et Israel et Ephraim ruent in iniquitate sua. Hoc impletur dupliciter : Primo, dum præfatis vitiis implicati, sic deseruntur in præsenti vita a gratia, quod ignominiosa atque turpissima incidunt crimina, sicut de talibus ait Apostolus ad Romanos : Tradidit illos Deus in reprobum sensum, ut faciant ea quæ non conveniunt. Sicque quotidie ruunt in iniquitatibus suis, dum uno peccato trahuntur ad aliud, ita quod præcedens, est dispositio et causa meritoria subsequentis. Secundo, dum pœnam damnationis incurrunt, quemadmodum scriptum est : Exterminati sunt, et ad inferos descenderunt. Ruet etiam Judas, id est vir ecclesiasticus, cum eis : nam boni interdum a talibus subvertuntur ac pereunt.
paras.en: [[5:5|And the pride of Israel shall answer in his face: and Israel, and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity|Et respondebit arrogantia Israel in facie ejus, et Israel et Ephraim ruent in iniquitate sua]]. This is fulfilled in two ways. First, when, entangled in the vices spoken of, they are so forsaken by grace in the present life that they fall into shameful and most foul crimes, as the Apostle says of such men to the Romans: [[Rom 1:28|God delivered them up to a reprobate sense, to do those things which are not convenient|Tradidit illos Deus in reprobum sensum, ut faciant ea quæ non conveniunt]]. And so daily they fall in their iniquities, while they are drawn from one sin to another, so that the one before is the disposition and the meritorious cause [that is, the cause that deserves it as a punishment] of the one after. Secondly, when they incur the penalty of damnation, as it is written: [[Bar 3:19|They are cut off, and are gone down to hell|Exterminati sunt, et ad inferos descenderunt]]. [[5:5|Juda also shall fall|Ruet etiam Judas]], that is, the churchman, [[5:5|with them|cum eis]]: for the good are at times overthrown by such men and perish.

paras.t: In gregibus suis, id est cum vanarum et sæcularium cogitationum tumultibus, et in armentis suis, id est cum carnalium voluptatum passionibus, vadent ad quærendum Dominum : quia si interdum vadant ad locum cultus divini ut orent, tot cogitationibus et affectionibus inordinatis depingitur cor eorum, quod Deum devota tranquillaque mente nequeunt exorare. Ideo sequitur : et non invenient : non enim exaudiri merentur.
paras.en: [[5:6|With their flocks|In gregibus suis]], that is, with the tumult of vain and worldly thoughts, [[5:6|and with their herds|et in armentis suis]], that is, with the passions of fleshly pleasures, [[5:6|they shall go to seek the Lord|vadent ad quærendum Dominum]]: for if at times they go to the place of divine worship to pray, their heart is painted over with so many disordered thoughts and affections that they cannot entreat God with a devout and tranquil mind. Therefore there follows: [[5:6|and shall not find him|et non invenient]]: for they do not deserve to be heard.

paras.t: Filios alienos genuerunt : quia discipulos seu posteros suos fovendo in suis peccatis, reddunt eos a Deo aversos, ut non jam ad Creatorem suum, sed ad dæmonem seductorem pertineant. Nunc devorabit eos mensis, id est, de proximo peribunt, quemadmodum scriptum est : Quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent.
paras.en: [[5:7|they have begotten children that are strangers|Filios alienos genuerunt]]: because by cherishing their disciples or those who come after them in their sins, they turn them away from God, so that they belong no longer to their Creator but to the devil who seduces them. [[5:7|now shall a month devour them|Nunc devorabit eos mensis]], that is, they will shortly perish, as it is written: [[Ps 36:2|For they shall shortly wither away as grass|Quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent]].

paras.t: Clangite buccina, id est, clare et alte prædicate, in Gabaa, id est in colle virtutum, ut prædicationi correspondeant mores et vita. Clangite quoque et tuba in Rama, id est in excelso caritatis ac sapientiæ, sicut ait Apostolus : Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos. Gabaa autem interpretatur collis; Rama vero, excelsum. Ululate in Bethaven, id est in domo idoli, deflendo vehementer eorum peccata qui creaturis potius quam Creatori inhærent atque deserviunt. Hi siquidem quasi idola honorare videntur, secundum quod avaritiam vocat Apostolus idolorum servitutem.
paras.en: [[5:8|Blow ye the cornet|Clangite buccina]], that is, preach clearly and on high, [[5:8|in Gabaa|in Gabaa]], that is, on the hill of the virtues, so that conduct and life may answer to the preaching. Blow also [[5:8|the trumpet in Rama|tuba in Rama]], that is, on the height of charity and wisdom, as the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 2:6|we speak wisdom among the perfect|Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos]]. For Gabaa is interpreted hill, and Rama, height. [[5:8|howl ye in Bethaven|Ululate in Bethaven]], that is, in the house of the idol, bewailing vehemently the sins of those who cleave to and serve creatures rather than the Creator. For these seem as it were to honour idols, according as the Apostle calls avarice [[Eph 5:5|a serving of idols|idolorum servitutem]][[Col 3:5||]].

paras.t: In die correptionis et in tribubus Israel ostendi fidem. Sicut hæc verba in præcedenti articulo de decem tribubus explanata sunt, sic generaliter verum est quod Deus in die castigationis et plagæ impiorum ostendit fidem, id est fidelitatem et veritatem Scripturæ atque sanctorum, dicentium quod Deus habeat omnium providentiam rerum, nilque impræmiatum relinquens, perversos debitis afficit pœnis, etiam interdum in isto sæculo. Unde in Job habetur : Recordare, obsecro, quis unquam innocens periit : quin potius vidi impios Domino flante perisse.
paras.en: [[5:9|in the day of rebuke|In die correptionis]] [[5:9|among the tribes of Israel I have shewn that which shall surely be|et in tribubus Israel ostendi fidem]] [the Latin has *ostendi fidem*, “I have shewn faith”, which Denis goes on to take as fidelity and truth]. As these words were explained in the preceding article of the ten tribes, so it is true in general that God, in the day of the chastisement and scourge of the wicked, shews faith, that is, the fidelity and truth of Scripture and of the saints, who say that God has providence over all things, and, leaving nothing unrewarded, visits the perverse with the punishments they deserve, at times even in this world. Hence we have in Job: [[Job 4:7|Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished being innocent?|Recordare, obsecro, quis unquam innocens periit]] [[Job 4:8|On the contrary, I have seen|quin potius vidi]] the wicked [[Job 4:9|Perishing by the blast of God|Domino flante perisse]].

paras.t: Facti sunt principes Juda, id est prælati Ecclesiæ, quasi assumentes terminum, id est, possessiones suas dilatantes in terminis alienis quos emunt, nec contenti competenti possessione, temporalia immoderanter accumulant, in gravamen et scandalum aliorum. Contra quos scriptum est in Proverbiis : Ne transgrediaris terminos antiquos, quos posuerunt patres tui ; in Deuteronomio quoque, Non transferes terminos quos fixerunt priores in possessione tua. Super eos effundam quasi aquam iram meam. Talium nempe cupiditas vehementer damnanda est, graviterque punitur in præsenti per spiritualium divitiarum (quibus anima spoliatur) subtractionem, in futuro quoque per cruciamenta æterna, quemadmodum in Isaia inducitur : Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum agro copulatis.
paras.en: [[5:10|The princes of Juda are become|Facti sunt principes Juda]], that is, the prelates of the Church, [[5:10|as they that take up the bound|quasi assumentes terminum]], that is, enlarging their possessions into the bounds of others which they buy up; and, not content with a sufficient possession, they heap up temporal goods beyond measure, to the burden and scandal of others. Against them it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 22:28|Pass not beyond the ancient bounds which thy fathers have set|Ne transgrediaris terminos antiquos, quos posuerunt patres tui]]; and in Deuteronomy too: [[Deut 19:14|Thou shalt not take nor remove|Non transferes]] the bounds [[Deut 19:14|which thy predecessors have set in thy possession|quos fixerunt priores in possessione tua]]. [[5:10|I will pour out my wrath upon them like water|Super eos effundam quasi aquam iram meam]]. For the greed of such men is to be vehemently condemned, and is heavily punished in the present by the withdrawal of spiritual riches (of which the soul is stripped), and in the future too by eternal torments, as is set forth in Isaias: [[Is 5:8|Woe to you that join house to house and lay field to field|Væ qui conjungitis domum ad domum, et agrum agro copulatis]].

paras.t: Calumniam patiens est Ephraim. Hoc juxta sensum præhabitum dici potest de ecclesia Christianorum malorum, dum ab infidelibus seu pejoribus prava intentione opprimitur : quod tamen juste patitur ex parte Dei et sui. Unde subjungitur : fractus judicio, quia divinæ æquitatis censura hostibus traditur, quoniam cœpit abire post sordes vitiorum, de quibus in Apocalypsi legitur : Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc.
paras.en: [[5:11|Ephraim is under oppression|Calumniam patiens est Ephraim]]. This, according to the sense given before, can be said of the church of bad Christians, when it is oppressed by unbelievers or by worse men with wicked intent: which nevertheless it suffers justly, on God's part and on its own. Hence there is added: [[5:11|and broken in judgment|fractus judicio]], because by the sentence of divine justice it is handed over to its enemies, [[5:11|because he began to go after filthiness|quoniam cœpit abire post sordes]] of vices, of which we read in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 22:11|he that is filthy, let him be filthy still|Qui in sordibus est, sordescat adhuc]].

paras.t: Et ego quasi tinea Ephraim, id est hæreticis seu prædictis avaris, et quasi putredo domui Juda, id est ecclesiæ peccantium, qui labiis Deum honorant, sed corde longe distant ab eo. Hos namque destruit Deus, nunc spiritualiter omne esse gratiæ gratum facientis eis negando aut subtrahendo ; tandem quoque justas inferet afflictiones.
paras.en: [[5:12|And I will be like a moth to Ephraim|Et ego quasi tinea Ephraim]], that is, to heretics or to the avaricious spoken of above, [[5:12|and like rottenness to the house of Juda|et quasi putredo domui Juda]], that is, to the church of sinners, who honour God with their lips but in heart stand far from him[[Is 29:13||]][[Matt 15:8||]]. For God destroys these: now spiritually, by denying them or withdrawing from them all being of the grace that makes pleasing [that is, sanctifying grace, which makes the soul pleasing to God]; and at last he will also bring just afflictions upon them.

paras.t: Et vidit Ephraim languorem suum, et Juda vinculum suum. Et abiit ad Assur. Sic multi spiritu diffidentiæ tabescentes, dum propria mala et vincula culpæ attendunt, pericula atque injurias imminentes adspiciunt, non convertuntur spe firma ad Deum, nec mente fideli clamant ad eum, sed a filiis hujus sæculi, Deo relicto, quærunt solatium. Contra quos Jeremias scribit : Maledictus qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus : quum utique Dominus juxta sit his qui tribulato sunt corde, et afflictos eripiat, prout in Job asseritur : In sex tribulationibus liberabit te, et in septima non videbis malum. Unde ait in Psalmo : Invoca me in die tribulationis ; eruam te, et honorificabis me.
paras.en: [[5:13|And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Juda his band|Et vidit Ephraim languorem suum, et Juda vinculum suum]]. And he [[5:13|went to the Assyrian|abiit ad Assur]]. So many, wasting away in a spirit of distrust, when they consider their own evils and the bonds of guilt and look upon the dangers and injuries hanging over them, do not turn with firm hope to God, nor cry to him with a faithful mind, but, forsaking God, seek comfort from the children of this world. Against them Jeremias writes: [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord|Maledictus qui confidit in homine, et ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus]]: since surely the Lord [[Ps 33:19|is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart|juxta sit his qui tribulato sunt corde]], and rescues the afflicted, as is asserted in Job: [[Job 5:19|In six troubles he shall deliver thee|In sex tribulationibus liberabit te]], [[Job 5:19|and in the seventh|et in septima]] thou shalt see no evil [Denis reads *non videbis malum*, “thou shalt not see evil”, where the Vulgate has “evil shall not touch thee”]. Hence he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:15|call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me|Invoca me in die tribulationis ; eruam te, et honorificabis me]].

paras.t: Istis igitur tam infideliter se ad Deum habentibus, efficitur Deus quasi leæna catulusque leonis, quos capit et tollit ne videant gloriam Dei, atque in carcere infernali eos concludit, donec quærant faciem ejus : quod nunquam facient, quoniam non est in morte qui memor sit Dei ; in inferno autem quis confitebitur ei ?
paras.en: To these, then, who bear themselves so faithlessly towards God, God becomes [[5:14|like a lioness|quasi leæna]] and [[5:14|a lion's whelp|catulusque leonis]], who catches them and takes them away, that they may not see the glory of God, and shuts them up in the prison of hell, until they seek his face[[5:15||]]: which they will never do, since [[Ps 6:6|there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee|non est in morte qui memor sit Dei]]: [[Ps 6:6|and who shall confess to thee in hell|in inferno autem quis confitebitur ei]]?

6.title: Elucidatio capituli sexti: In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me.
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: In their affliction they will rise early to me.

paras.t: Præsenti capitulo describitur divinæ bonitatis miseratio, Judæorum quoque ad Christum conversio. Dixerat autem Deus in fine præcedentis capituli, Revertar ad locum meum, donec deficiatis et quæratis faciem meam ; nunc autem protinus subdit : In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me, etc. Unde, secundum Glossam et Bedam, verba hæc possunt aptari Judæis qui in Babylonica captivitate oppressi, convertebantur ad Deum. Eritque sensus : In tribulatione sua, qua a Chaldæis in Babylonia affligebantur, mane, id est lumine pœnitentiæ eis infuso, consurgent ad me, excutiendo se a somno peccati et torpore ignaviæ ad vitam meliorem, dicentes ad se invicem salubriter : Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum, quia ipse cepit, id est, manibus Chaldæorum tradidit, et sanabit nos a languore peccati. Nihilo minus, secundum Glossam et Bedam, imo secundum doctores catholicos et Hebræos communiter, capitulum præsens loquitur pro tempore Christi.
paras.en: In the present chapter is described the compassion of the divine goodness, and also the conversion of the Jews to Christ. Now at the end of the preceding chapter God had said, I will [[Osee 5:15|return to my place: until you are consumed, and seek my face|Revertar ad locum meum, donec deficiatis et quæratis faciem meam]]; and now he straightway adds: [[6:1|In their affliction they will rise early to me|In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me]], etc. Hence, according to the Gloss and Bede, these words can be applied to the Jews who, oppressed in the Babylonian captivity, were turning to God. And the sense will be: [[6:1|In their affliction|In tribulatione sua]], with which they were afflicted by the Chaldeans in Babylonia, [[6:1|early|mane]], that is, when the light of penance has been poured into them, [[6:1|they will rise|consurgent]] [[6:1|to me|ad me]], shaking themselves out of the sleep of sin and the torpor of sloth toward a better life, and saying to one another, to their salvation: [[6:1|Come, and let us return to the Lord|Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum]], [[6:2|For he hath taken us|quia ipse cepit]], that is, he has delivered us into the hands of the Chaldeans, [[6:2|and he will heal us|et sanabit nos]] from the languor of sin. Nevertheless, according to the Gloss and Bede, nay, according to the Catholic doctors and the Hebrews generally, the present chapter speaks of the time of Christ.

paras.t: Denique, ut refert Hieronymus, Judæi increduli, qui Jesum Christum non recipiunt pro Messia eis promisso, exponunt hoc modo : In tribulatione sua (hæc sunt verba Dei), id est Judæi in hac captivitate eis a Romanis inducta, mane consurgent ad me : quia quotidie mane et vespere orant Deum liberari a tribulatione captivitatis præsentis per adventum Messiæ, dicentes : Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum, a quo peccando recessimus, et ad quem quotidie pœnitendo redimus ; quia ipse cepit, id est, Romanis tradidit nos propter peccata nostra, et sanabit nos ab hac calamitate in adventu Messiæ. Vivificabit nos vita gratiæ post duos dies : id est, rex Messias statim quum venerit, vivificabit nos ; in die tertia, id est in die judicii, suscitabit nos, et vivemus in conspectu ejus, quia tunc perfecte salvabimur. Judæi ergo per secundum diem, intelligunt Christi primum adventum, quem præstolantur futurum ; per tertium vero diem, intelligunt diem judicii. Quibus Hieronymus objicit, quod respondere nequeunt quis sit primus dies.
paras.en: Further, as Jerome reports, the unbelieving Jews, who do not receive Jesus Christ as the Messias promised to them, expound it in this way: [[6:1|In their affliction|In tribulatione sua]] (these are the words of God), that is, the Jews in this captivity brought upon them by the Romans, [[6:1|they will rise early to me|mane consurgent ad me]]: because daily, morning and evening, they pray God that they may be freed from the affliction of the present captivity through the coming of the Messias, saying: [[6:1|Come, and let us return to the Lord|Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum]], from whom we departed by sinning, and to whom we daily return by repenting; [[6:2|For he hath taken us|quia ipse cepit]], that is, he has delivered us to the Romans for our sins, [[6:2|and he will heal us|et sanabit nos]] from this calamity at the coming of the Messias. [[6:3|He will revive us|Vivificabit nos]] with the life of grace [[6:3|after two days|post duos dies]]: that is, the king Messias will revive us as soon as he comes; [[6:3|on the third day|in die tertia]], that is, on the day of judgment, [[6:3|he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight|suscitabit nos, et vivemus in conspectu ejus]], because then we shall be perfectly saved. So by the second day the Jews understand the first coming of Christ, which they await as still to come; and by the third day they understand the day of judgment. Against them Jerome objects that they cannot answer what the first day is.

paras.t: Porro, ut recitat Lyra, Judæi moderni sequentes Rabbi Salomonem, per primum diem, accipiunt tempus primi templi a Salomone constructi, cui successit nox destructionis illius templi per Chaldæos ; per diem vero secundum, accipiunt tempus secundi templi, a Zorobabel ædificati, cui successit nox destructionis templi illius per Romanos. Per tertium autem diem, accipiunt tempus tertii templi, quod asserunt a Messia ædificandum : de quo templo exponunt, quod in fine Ezechielis scribitur de cujusdam templi structura mirabili. Itaque post duos dies præfatos, videlicet finita captivitate præsenti, et in die tertia, quum Messias construxerit templum, dicunt se vivificandos ac suscitandos. Sed hæc expositio sumit diem satis improprie, fundaturque in errore perfidiæ, quod dicunt Christum nondum venisse.
paras.en: Again, as Lyra relates, the modern Jews, following Rabbi Salomon, take the first day to be the time of the first temple, built by Solomon, which was followed by the night of that temple's destruction by the Chaldeans; the second day, the time of the second temple, built by Zorobabel, which was followed by the night of that temple's destruction by the Romans; and the third day, the time of the third temple, which they assert is to be built by the Messias. To this temple they apply what is written at the end of Ezechiel about the wonderful structure of a certain temple[[Ezech 42:1||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xlii–xlvii; the vision of the temple fills chapters 40–48]. So [[6:3|after two days|post duos dies]] just mentioned, that is, when the present captivity is over, and [[6:3|on the third day|in die tertia]], when the Messias has built the temple, they say that they will be revived and raised up. But this exposition takes *day* quite improperly, and it is founded on the error of their unbelief, in that they say that Christ has not yet come.

paras.t: Supponendo ergo quod verum est, utpote quod Christus jam venit, sicut in sequentibus palam probabitur, exponenda est littera vere atque catholice hoc modo : In tribulatione sua, id est in dolore pœnitentiali pro peccatis : quia veraciter pœnitens, tribulationem animæ habet, juxta illud, Renuit consolari anima mea ; et denuo, Afflictus sum et humiliatus sum nimis, rugiebam a gemitu cordis mei. Non enim leviter est deflendum, nec modice reputandum, quod Deus sublimis offenditur, quod Creator omnipotens inhonoratur, sed cordialissime oportet tristari, humiliari et emendare. Propterea Jeremias hortatur : Luctum unigeniti fac tibi, planctum amarum. Et Moyses : Quum quæsieris Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum, si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ. Vel, In tribulatione sua corporali, quia in Christi adventu subjecti erant Judæi Romanis, qui præfecerunt eis crudelissimos dominos, Herodem et Pilatum, qui Judæos frequenter tribulaverunt, et quosdam eorum vicissim occiderunt.
paras.en: Supposing, then, what is true, namely that Christ has already come, as will be plainly proved in what follows, the letter is to be expounded truly and in a Catholic sense in this way. [[6:1|In their affliction|In tribulatione sua]], that is, in the sorrow of penance for their sins: for one who truly repents has affliction of soul, according to that saying, [[Ps 76:3|My soul refused to be comforted|Renuit consolari anima mea]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxxvi, 3; the words are those of Ps 76:3]; and again, [[Ps 37:9|I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: I roared with the groaning of my heart.|Afflictus sum et humiliatus sum nimis, rugiebam a gemitu cordis mei]] For it is not to be lightly wept over, nor reckoned a small matter, that the most high God is offended, that the almighty Creator is dishonoured; rather one must grieve, be humbled and amend most heartily. Therefore Jeremias exhorts: [[Jer 6:26|make thee mourning as for an only son, a bitter lamentation|Luctum unigeniti fac tibi, planctum amarum]]. And Moses: [[Deut 4:29|And when thou shalt seek|Quum quæsieris]] [[Deut 4:29|the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him|Dominum Deum tuum, invenies eum]]: [[Deut 4:29|yet so, if thou seek him with all thy heart, and all the affliction of thy soul|si tamen toto corde quæsieris eum, et tota tribulatione animæ tuæ]] [*tribulatio*, "affliction", is the word of the verse treated]. Or, [[6:1|In their affliction|In tribulatione sua]] of body: for at the coming of Christ the Jews were subject to the Romans, who set over them most cruel lords, Herod and Pilate, who often afflicted the Jews and from time to time put some of them to death.

paras.t: Mane, id est in spiritualis diei aurora, videlicet mox illustrante eos gratia Spiritus Sancti, qui spiritualem diem facit in anima, dum gratiæ suæ splendore eam in omnibus ad salutem pertinentibus clare irradiat atque accendit : de quo die accipi potest illud Proverbiorum, Justorum semita quasi lux splendens, procedit et crescit usque ad perfectum diem. De hoc Mane fertur in Psalmo : Mane adstabo tibi, et videbo quoniam non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es. Quidam per Mane, intelligunt tempus prædicationis Joannis Baptistæ, cujus doctrina, conversatione, atque baptismo multi Judæorum ad Christum conversi sunt. Dicitur quoque tempus hoc, Mane, quum sit principium temporis gratiæ, quod ad Romanos dies vocatur, dicente Apostolo : Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit. Et alibi : Ecce, inquit, nunc tempus acceptabile, ecce nunc dies salutis. Consurgent ad me, erigendo se ab imis ad summa, a terrenis ad superna, dignosque pœnitentiæ fructus agendo. Unde scriptum est in Job : Si diluculo consurrexeris ad Deum, et Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus, statim evigilabit ad te.
paras.en: [[6:1|early|Mane]], that is, at the dawn of the spiritual day, namely as soon as the grace of the Holy Ghost enlightens them, who makes a spiritual day in the soul when by the splendour of his grace he clearly illumines and kindles it in all things that pertain to salvation. Of this day may be taken that saying of Proverbs: [[Prov 4:18|the path of the just, as a shining light, goeth forwards, and increaseth even to perfect day|Justorum semita quasi lux splendens, procedit et crescit usque ad perfectum diem]]. Of this morning it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 5:5|In the morning I will stand before thee, and I will see: because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.|Mane adstabo tibi, et videbo quoniam non Deus volens iniquitatem tu es]] Some understand by *morning* the time of the preaching of John the Baptist, by whose teaching, life and baptism many of the Jews were converted to Christ. This time is also called *morning* because it is the beginning of the time of grace, which in the Epistle to the Romans is called day, as the Apostle says: [[Rom 13:12|The night is passed And the day is at hand|Nox præcessit, dies autem appropinquavit]]. And elsewhere he says: [[2 Cor 6:2|Behold, now is the acceptable time|nunc tempus acceptabile]]: [[2 Cor 6:2|behold, now is the day of salvation|ecce nunc dies salutis]]. [[6:1|they will rise|Consurgent]] [[6:1|to me|ad me]], raising themselves from the lowest things to the highest, from earthly things to heavenly, and bringing forth [[Luke 3:8|fruits worthy of penance|dignosque pœnitentiæ fructus]]. Hence it is written in Job: [[Job 8:5|if thou wilt arise early to God, and wilt beseech the Almighty|Si diluculo consurrexeris ad Deum, et Omnipotentem fueris deprecatus]], [[Job 8:6|he will presently awake unto thee|statim evigilabit ad te]].

paras.t: Venite, a multis in quibus consistit turbatio, ad unum quod necessarium est, in quo quies vera consistit ; venite, non gressibus corporis, sed sanctis affectionibus cordis et actibus fidei, spei ac caritatis; et revertamur ad Dominum Christum. Quia ipse Dominus cepit, id est, præteritis temporibus punivit, et captivitati exposuit, et sanabit nos jam, quemadmodum Zacharias dixit : Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, quia visitavit et fecit redemptionem plebis suæ. Anna quoque prophetissa loquebatur de Christo omnibus qui exspectabant redemptionem Jerusalem. Et Simeon : Nunc dimittis servum tuum, Domine, etc. Curavit autem Christus electos Judæos spiritualiter a servitute peccati atque vulneribus animæ, corporaliter quoque curavit infirmos eorum, sicut Evangelistæ testantur. Propter quod apud Isaiam prædictum est : Deus vester ipse veniet, et salvos vos faciet : tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt; tunc saliet sicut cervus claudus, et aperta erit lingua mutorum.
paras.en: [[6:1|Come|Venite]], from the many things in which lies disturbance[[Luke 10:41||]], to the one thing that is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]], in which true rest lies; come, not with the steps of the body, but with holy affections of the heart and with acts of faith, hope and charity; [[6:1|and let us return to the Lord|et revertamur ad Dominum]] Christ. [[6:2|For he|Quia ipse]], the Lord, [[6:2|hath taken us|cepit]], that is, punished us in times past and gave us over to captivity, [[6:2|and he will heal us|et sanabit nos]] now, as Zachary said: [[Luke 1:68|Blessed be the Lord God of Israel: because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people.|Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, quia visitavit et fecit redemptionem plebis suæ]] Anna the prophetess also spoke of Christ [[Luke 2:38|to all that looked for the redemption|omnibus qui exspectabant redemptionem]] of Jerusalem [Denis reads "Jerusalem" where the Vulgate has "Israel"]. And Simeon: [[Luke 2:29|Now thou dost dismiss thy servant, O Lord|Nunc dimittis servum tuum, Domine]], etc. And Christ healed the elect among the Jews spiritually, from the servitude of sin and the wounds of the soul; bodily too he healed their sick, as the Evangelists testify. For this reason it was foretold in Isaias: [[Is 35:4|God himself will come and will save you|Deus vester ipse veniet, et salvos vos faciet]]: [[Is 35:5|Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.|tunc aperientur oculi cæcorum, et aures surdorum patebunt]] [[Is 35:6|Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall be free|tunc saliet sicut cervus claudus, et aperta erit lingua mutorum]].

paras.t: Percutiet virga paternæ correctionis in præsenti, ne æternaliter pereamus, et curabit nos, indulgendo et confortando. Unde ait Apostolis : In mundo pressuram habebitis. Denique per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum cœlorum. Hinc in Proverbiis scriptum est : Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et ne deficias quum ab eo corriperis : quem enim diligit Deus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi. Et in Job ait quidam : Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino : increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes, quia ipse vulnerat, et medetur ; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt.
paras.en: [[6:2|he will strike|Percutiet]] with the rod of a father's correction in the present life, lest we perish eternally, [[6:2|and he will cure us|et curabit nos]], by pardoning and strengthening us. Hence he says to the Apostles: [[John 16:33|In the world you shall have distress|In mundo pressuram habebitis]]. And indeed [[Acts 14:21|through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of|per multas tribulationes oportet nos intrare in regnum]] heaven [Denis has "of heaven" where the Vulgate has "of God"]. Hence it is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 3:11|My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him:|Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et ne deficias quum ab eo corriperis]] [[Prov 3:12|For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself|quem enim diligit Deus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi]]. And in Job someone says: [[Job 5:17|Blessed is the man whom God correcteth: refuse not, therefore, the chastising of the Lord|Beatus homo qui corripitur a Domino : increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes]] [[Job 5:18|For he woundeth, and cureth: he striketh, and his hands shall heal.|quia ipse vulnerat, et medetur ; percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt]]

paras.t: Vivificabit nos per gratiæ infusionem, mortem culpæ delendo, corporis quoque immortalitatem in spe exhibendo, post duos dies, id est expleto tempore quod fuit ante legem, et tempore illo quod fuit sub lege, videlicet nunc instante tempore evangelicæ legis, quando plenitudine temporis veniente, Verbum caro factum habitavit in nobis, et dixit : Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat; et iterum, Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant. In die tertia, quando resurgens a mortuis, jam non moritur, suscitabit nos, id est, futuræ resurrectionis spem dabit. Capitis enim præcessio, spes membrorum est. Præterea, resurrectio Christi est causa exemplaris nostræ resurrectionis. Hoc totum scribit ad Corinthios S. Paulus : Christus resurrexit a mortuis primitiæ dormientium, quoniam quidem per hominem mors, et per hominem resurrectio mortuorum ; et sicut in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabuntur. Vel quod ait, Post duos dies, et in die tertia, idem tempus significat, scilicet diem dominicæ resurrectionis : in quo etiam vivificavit nos, quia ut dicit Apostolus, resurrexit propter justificationem nostram ; tunc quoque apparens discipulis, mortem infidelitatis cœpit auferre, et vitam fidei reparare.
paras.en: [[6:3|He will revive us|Vivificabit nos]] by the infusion of grace, blotting out the death of guilt, and also holding out in hope the immortality of the body, [[6:3|after two days|post duos dies]], that is, when the time before the law and the time under the law have been fulfilled, namely now that the time of the law of the Gospel is at hand, when, the fulness of time having come[[Gal 4:4||]], [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum habitavit in nobis]], and said: [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvum facere quod perierat]]; and again, [[John 10:10|I am come that they may have life and may have it more abundantly|Ego veni ut vitam habeant, et abundantius habeant]]. [[6:3|on the third day|In die tertia]], when, [[Rom 6:9|rising again from the dead|resurgens a mortuis]], he [[Rom 6:9|dieth now no more|jam non moritur]], [[6:3|he will raise us up|suscitabit nos]], that is, he will give us the hope of the resurrection to come. For the going before of the head is the hope of the members. Moreover, the resurrection of Christ is the exemplary cause of our resurrection.
