All this St. Paul writes to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:20|Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that sleep|Christus resurrexit a mortuis primitiæ dormientium]], [[1 Cor 15:21|For by a man came death: and by a man the resurrection of the dead.|quoniam quidem per hominem mors, et per hominem resurrectio mortuorum]] [[1 Cor 15:22|And as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive.|et sicut in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabuntur]] Or else, when he says [[6:3|after two days|Post duos dies]] and [[6:3|on the third day|in die tertia]], it signifies the same time, namely the day of the Lord's resurrection, on which he also revived us; for, as the Apostle says, he [[Rom 4:25|rose again for our justification|resurrexit propter justificationem nostram]]; and then too, appearing to the disciples, he began to take away the death of unbelief and to restore the life of faith.

paras.t: Hieronymus per primum diem intelligit primum Salvatoris adventum ; per diem secundum, diem judicii, in quo in majestate et gloria omnibus apparebit ; per tertium, diem æternitatis, quando in patria claritatem suam monstrabit electis. Sed difficile videtur assignare quomodo in hoc tertio die suscitabit nos, vel post prædictum secundum diem vivificabit nos. Glossa vero, per primum diem intelligit tempus a principio mundi usque ad Christi adventum ; per diem secundum, tempus adventus Christi, quo vivificamur per fidem ; per tertium autem, tempus generalis resurrectionis, quando reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ.
paras.en: Jerome understands by the first day the first coming of the Saviour; by the second day, the day of judgment, on which he will appear to all in majesty and glory; by the third, the day of eternity, when in the fatherland he will show his brightness to the elect. But it seems hard to explain how on this third day he will raise us up, or after the said second day will revive us. The Gloss, however, understands by the first day the time from the beginning of the world up to the coming of Christ; by the second day, the time of Christ's coming, in which we are given life through faith; and by the third, the time of the general resurrection, when he [[Phil 3:21|will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory|reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ, configuratum corpori claritatis suæ]].

paras.t: Et vivemus in conspectu ejus : quia post Christi passionem et resurrectionem, fideles vere spiritualiterque vixerunt coram Christo, qui Spiritum Sanctum misit in corda eorum. Sciemus Scripturas et ea quæ fidei sunt, sequemurque opera Christi, conformando nos ejus humilitati, patientiæ, obedientiæ et passioni. Unde et ipse testatur : Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me ; itemque, Qui sequitur me, non ambulat in tenebris, sed habebit lumen vitæ. Hinc ait Psalmista : Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus, ingressus Dei mei, regis mei. Vel, Sequemur Christum, peracto judicio, ascendentes cum ipso in alta cœlorum. Ut cognoscamus Dominum, non per speculum in ænigmate, sed facie ad faciem cognoscentes, sicut et cogniti sumus. Unde in prima sua epistola ait Joannes : Quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est. Hæc cognitio est finis noster et tota merces, de qua ait Salvator ad Patrem : Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum.
paras.en: [[6:3|and we shall live in his sight|Et vivemus in conspectu ejus]]: because after Christ's passion and resurrection the faithful lived truly and spiritually before Christ, who sent the Holy Ghost into their hearts. [[6:3|We shall know|Sciemus]] the Scriptures and the things that are of faith, [[6:3|and we shall follow on|sequemurque]] the works of Christ, conforming ourselves to his humility, patience, obedience and passion. Hence he himself testifies: [[Luke 9:23|If any man will come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me|Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum, et tollat crucem suam quotidie, et sequatur me]]; and likewise, [[John 8:12|He that followeth me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life|Qui sequitur me, non ambulat in tenebris, sed habebit lumen vitæ]]. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 67:25|They have seen thy goings, O God, the goings of my God: of my king|Viderunt ingressus tuos, Deus, ingressus Dei mei, regis mei]]. Or, [[6:3|we shall follow on|Sequemur]] Christ, when the judgment is over, ascending with him to the heights of heaven. [[6:3|that we may know the Lord|Ut cognoscamus Dominum]], knowing him not [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum in ænigmate]], but [[1 Cor 13:12|face to face|facie ad faciem]], even as we are known. Hence John says in his first epistle: [[1 John 3:2|when he shall appear we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is|Quum apparuerit, similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est]]. This knowledge is our end and our whole reward, of which the Saviour says to the Father: [[John 17:3|this is eternal life: That they may know thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent|Hæc est vita æterna, ut cognoscant te solum verum Deum, et quem misisti Jesum Christum]].

paras.t: Quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus. Duplex est Christi egressus : unus æternalis, quo per generationem æternam egreditur de corde Patris : de quo in Michæa scriptum est, Egressus ejus ab initio, a diebus æternitatis ; et ipse Christus apud Joannem, Exivi (inquit) a Patre. Alius temporalis, quo per generationem maternam exivit de inviolato ac integerrimo utero superbenedictissimæ Virginis : de quo cantat Psalmista, Ipse tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo. Et de isto egressu nunc agitur, ut sit sensus : Egressus ejus, id est processus Christi de Virgine Matre, et adventus ejus in hunc mundum per incarnationis mysterium, est præparatus, id est a Deo factus et nobis exhibitus, quasi diluculum, quod est principium diei. Quemadmodum enim hora diluculi oriente luce fugantur tenebræ noctis, et totus mundus solis splendore perfunditur ; sic Christo de Virginis utero prodeunte, atque in mundo se manifestante, caligo ignorantiæ vitiorumque tenebræ dissipari cœperunt, et veritatis emicuit claritas. Hinc scriptum est in Isaia : Propter Sion non tacebo, et propter Jerusalem non quiescam, donec egrediatur ut splendor Justus ejus, et Salvator ejus ut lampas accendatur. Et Christus in Evangelio ait : Ego lux veni in mundum.
paras.en: [[6:3|His going forth is prepared as the morning light|Quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus]]. Christ's going forth is twofold. One is eternal, by which through eternal generation he goes forth from the heart of the Father: of which it is written in Micheas, [[Mich 5:2|his going forth is from the beginning, from the days of eternity|Egressus ejus ab initio, a diebus æternitatis]]; and Christ himself in John, [[John 16:28|I came forth|Exivi]] (he says) [[John 16:28|from the Father|a Patre]]. The other is temporal, by which through his generation from his mother he came forth from the inviolate and wholly untouched womb of the most highly blessed Virgin: of which the Psalmist sings, [[Ps 18:6|he as a bridegroom coming out of his bridechamber|Ipse tanquam sponsus procedens de thalamo suo]]. And it is this going forth that is treated here, so that the sense is: [[6:3|His going forth|Egressus ejus]], that is, Christ's coming forth from the Virgin Mother and his coming into this world through the mystery of the incarnation, [[6:3|is prepared|est præparatus]], that is, wrought by God and shown to us, [[6:3|as the morning light|quasi diluculum]], which is the beginning of the day. For as at the hour of dawn, when the light rises, the darkness of night is put to flight and the whole world is flooded with the splendour of the sun, so when Christ came forth from the Virgin's womb and showed himself in the world, the mist of ignorance and the darkness of vices began to be scattered, and the brightness of truth shone out. Hence it is written in Isaias: [[Is 62:1|For Sion's sake I will not hold my peace, and for the sake of Jerusalem, I will not rest till her just one come forth as brightness, and her saviour be lighted as a lamp.|Propter Sion non tacebo, et propter Jerusalem non quiescam, donec egrediatur ut splendor Justus ejus, et Salvator ejus ut lampas accendatur]] And Christ says in the Gospel: [[John 12:46|I am come, a light into the world|Ego lux veni in mundum]].

paras.t: Et veniet Christus quasi imber nobis temporaneus. Quemadmodum enim imber iste in terra promissionis semina sata coalescere facit in terra, estque multum conveniens terræ, et eam fecundans; sic Christus veniendo in mundum et prædicando, corda hominum fide et gratia per suam fecundavit doctrinam. Unde et ipse ait : Semen est verbum Dei. Et in Joanne ait discipulis : Jam vos mundi estis propter sermonem quem locutus sum vobis. Venit et quasi imber serotinus terræ : quoniam sicut imber serotinus perducit fructus ad maturitatem, sic Christus ope gratiæ suæ perficit fidem nostram, ut per dilectionem operetur, et fructus virtutum producamus, ne simus sterilis arbor. Hinc etenim ait : Sine me nihil potestis facere; et iterum, Semen fecit fructum, aliud centesimum, aliud sexagesimum, aliud tricesimum.
paras.en: [[6:3|and he will come|Et veniet]], Christ, [[6:3|to us as the early|quasi imber nobis temporaneus]] rain. For as this rain in the land of promise makes the seeds sown in the ground take root and grow, and is very well suited to the land and makes it fruitful, so Christ, by coming into the world and preaching, made the hearts of men fruitful with faith and grace through his teaching. Hence he himself says: [[Luke 8:11|The seed is the word of God|Semen est verbum Dei]]. And in John he says to the disciples: [[John 15:3|Now you are clean, by reason of the word which I have spoken to you.|Jam vos mundi estis propter sermonem quem locutus sum vobis]] He came also as [[6:3|the latter rain to the earth|imber serotinus terræ]]: because as the latter rain brings the fruits to ripeness, so Christ by the help of his grace perfects our faith, so that it works through love[[Gal 5:6||]] and we bring forth the fruits of the virtues, lest we be a barren tree. For hence he says: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and again, The seed bore fruit, [[Matt 13:8|some an hundred fold, some sixty fold, and some thirty fold|aliud centesimum, aliud sexagesimum, aliud tricesimum]][[Matt 13:23||]].

paras.t: Vel dicitur imber serotinus, secundum Hieronymum, in quantum æternæ beatitudinis præmia confert. Secundum Glossam quoque, in terra promissionis bis tantum in anno datur pluvia de cœlo : propter quod pluvia temporanea fertur, quæ semina jacta coalescere facit; serotina vero, quæ ea ad maturitatem deducit. Unde de hac terra Moyses ait in Deuteronomio : Terra quam ingredieris, non est sicut terra Ægypti, ubi jacto semine aquæ ducuntur irriguæ; sed montuosa est et campestris, de cœlo exspectans pluvias : quam Dominus Deus tuus semper invisit, et oculi ejus in ea sunt a principio anni usque ad finem. Utinam cor nostrum sit hujusmodi terra, quatenus verbum Dei in eo fructificet, et impleatur in nobis quod Dominus alio loco promittit : Dabo vobis pluviam temporaneam et serotinam.
paras.en: Or he is called [[6:3|the latter rain|imber serotinus]], according to Jerome, inasmuch as he bestows the rewards of eternal beatitude. According to the Gloss also, in the land of promise rain is given from heaven only twice in the year: for which reason one rain is called the early rain, which makes the seeds that have been sown take root, and the other the latter rain, which brings them to ripeness. Hence Moses says of this land in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 11:10|the land, which thou goest to possess, is not like the land of Egypt|Terra quam ingredieris, non est sicut terra Ægypti]], [[Deut 11:10|where, when the seed is sown, waters are brought in|ubi jacto semine aquæ ducuntur irriguæ]]; [[Deut 11:11|But it is a land of hills and plains, expecting rain from heaven|sed montuosa est et campestris, de cœlo exspectans pluvias]]: [[Deut 11:12|the Lord thy God doth always visit it, and his eyes are on it from the beginning of the year unto the end thereof|quam Dominus Deus tuus semper invisit, et oculi ejus in ea sunt a principio anni usque ad finem]]. Would that our heart were such a land, so that the word of God might bear fruit in it, and that might be fulfilled in us which the Lord promises in another place: I will give you [[Deut 11:14|the early rain and the latter rain|pluviam temporaneam et serotinam]] [in the verse the words run "he will give to your land"].

paras.t: Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim? id est populo decem tribuum ; quid faciam tibi, Juda? id est populo duarum tribuum, scilicet Juda ac Benjamin (per quos tribus Levitica datur intelligi). Quasi dicat ipse Dominus : Defectus vestræ salvationis non est ex parte mei, sed vestri, et jam tanta beneficia vobis exhibui, quod merito converteremini ad me, et non obstante malitia vestra, adhuc quodammodo misereor vestri. Itaque his verbis declarat, se habere pii patris affectum ad filios pereuntes. Simile huic est quod ait per Isaiam : Quid ultra debui facere vineæ meæ, et non feci? Et per Michæam : Popule meus, quid tibi feci? aut quid molestus fui tibi? Responde mihi. Hoc quoque affectu loquitur apud Isaiam, Utinam attendisses mandata mea; et in Deuteronomio, Quis det talem eos habere mentem ut timeant me, et bene sit eis? Non ergo Deo imputemus, sed negligentiæ nostræ, quod perimus, vel minus habemus. Misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina : id est, miseratio mea, quam vobis impendere sum paratus, non est fixa et fructuosa in vobis; sed sicut nubes matutina sole ascendente cito pertransit, sic gratia mea in vobis effectum non habet, propter duritiam et ingratitudinem vestram. Est item et quasi ros mane pertransiens, qui solis calore mox exsiccatur. Nomine roris et nubis, gratia atque benignitas Dei significatur. Unde Isaias dicit : Ros lucis, ros tuus; et rursus, Creabit Dominus super omnem locum montis Sion nubem per diem. Deus autem populo Israel, etiam non credenti, multa beneficia et gratias gratis datas concessit : quæ omnia nubi et rori instabili comparantur, quia non perduxerunt eos ad gratiam gratum facientem, celeriterque auferebantur ab eis.
paras.en: [[6:4|What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim?|Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim?]] that is, to the people of the ten tribes; [[6:4|what shall I do to thee, O Juda?|quid faciam tibi, Juda?]] that is, to the people of the two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin (by whom the tribe of Levi is to be understood too). As if the Lord himself were saying: The failure of your salvation is not on my part but on yours; I have already shown you such great benefits that you would rightly be converted to me, and in spite of your malice I still in some way have pity on you. So by these words he declares that he has the affection of a loving father towards his perishing sons. Like this is what he says through Isaias: [[Is 5:4|What is there that I ought to do more to my vineyard, that I have not done to it?|Quid ultra debui facere vineæ meæ, et non feci?]] And through Micheas: [[Mich 6:3|O my people, what have I done to thee, or in what have I molested thee? answer thou me.|Popule meus, quid tibi feci? aut quid molestus fui tibi? Responde mihi.]] With this same affection he speaks in Isaias, [[Is 48:18|O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments|Utinam attendisses mandata mea]]; and in Deuteronomy, [[Deut 5:29|Who shall give them to have such a mind, to fear me|Quis det talem eos habere mentem ut timeant me]], and [[Deut 5:29|that it may be well with them|et bene sit eis]]? Let us not, then, impute it to God but to our own negligence that we perish, or have less. [[6:4|your mercy is as a morning cloud|Misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina]]: that is, my compassion, which I am ready to bestow on you, is not fixed and fruitful in you; but as a morning cloud quickly passes away when the sun rises, so my grace has no effect in you, because of your hardness and ingratitude. It is likewise [[6:4|and as the dew that goeth away in the morning|et quasi ros mane pertransiens]], which is soon dried up by the heat of the sun. By the name of dew and of cloud the grace and kindness of God are signified. Hence Isaias says: [[Is 26:19|thy dew is the dew of the light|Ros lucis, ros tuus]]; and again, [[Is 4:5|the Lord will create upon every place of mount Sion|Creabit Dominus super omnem locum montis Sion]] [[Is 4:5|a cloud by day|nubem per diem]]. Now God granted the people of Israel, even when it did not believe, many benefits and graces freely given [*gratiæ gratis datæ*, gifts such as prophecy or miracles, given for the good of others rather than to sanctify the one who has them]: all of which are compared to an unstable cloud and dew, because they did not bring them to sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God], and were quickly taken away from them.

paras.t: Quidam exponunt hoc modo : Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim, etc.? quasi dicat : Indigni estis salvari, et misericordiam consequi. Cujus ratio subditur : Misericordia vestra, id est, quæ inest vobis formaliter, est quasi nubes matutina, et quasi ros mane pertransiens, id est sine effectu et vana, non virtus vera, sed simulata, quemadmodum nubes matutina est frequenter sine pluvia, et ros matutinus sine humectatione terræ. In quo Judæorum increpatur hypocrisis, quam Christus maxime redarguebat in Scribis, Pharisæis ac sacerdotibus, prout apud Matthæum legitur : Væ, inquiens, vobis Scribis et Pharisæis, qui similes estis sepulcris dealbatis. — Quidam referunt ista ad Judæos et decem tribus Israel, qui erant tempore Osee prophetæ, tuncque in proximo capiendi fuerunt per Assyrios et Chaldæos. Videtur tamen posse referri ad Judæos pro tempore Christi, in quem in primo adventu aliqui de singulis vel pluribus tribubus crediderunt. Plures vero non crediderunt, et eorum qui crediderunt, quidam aversi fuerunt. Propter quod, secundum Evangelistas, exprobravit eis, dicendo: Væ tibi, Corozain; væ tibi, Bethsaida, etc. De quibus et Isaias prædixit: Novissime gravata est via maris trans Jordanem Galilææ gentium.
paras.en: Some expound it in this way: [[6:4|What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim?|Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim]] etc.; as if to say: You are unworthy to be saved and to obtain mercy. The reason for this is added: [[6:4|your mercy|Misericordia vestra]], that is, the mercy that is in you formally [that is, the mercy that is your own quality, not God's mercy towards you], is [[6:4|as a morning cloud, and as the dew that goeth away in the morning|quasi nubes matutina, et quasi ros mane pertransiens]], that is, without effect and empty, not true virtue but feigned, just as a morning cloud is often without rain, and the morning dew without moistening of the earth. In this the hypocrisy of the Jews is rebuked, which Christ rebuked most of all in the scribes, Pharisees and priests, as we read in Matthew: [[Matt 23:27|Woe|Væ]], he says, [[Matt 23:27|to you, scribes and Pharisees|vobis Scribis et Pharisæis]], [[Matt 23:27|you are like to whited sepulchres|qui similes estis sepulcris dealbatis]]. Some refer these words to the Jews and the ten tribes of Israel who lived in the time of the prophet Osee, and were then soon to be taken captive by the Assyrians and Chaldeans. Yet it seems that they can be referred to the Jews of the time of Christ, in whom, at his first coming, some from each or from many of the tribes believed. But more did not believe, and of those who believed some turned away. For this reason, according to the Evangelists, he reproached them, saying: [[Matt 11:21|Woe thee, Corozain, woe to thee, Bethsaida|Væ tibi, Corozain; væ tibi, Bethsaida]], etc. Of these Isaias too foretold: [[Is 9:1|at the last the way of the sea beyond the Jordan of the Galilee of the Gentiles was heavily loaded|Novissime gravata est via maris trans Jordanem Galilææ gentium]].

paras.t: Propter hoc, scilicet quia vobis consulere volui, dolavi: id est, more ædificantis qui ligna dolat, asperitatem materiæ deponendo, dolavi vos, id est, verbis acutis comminatus sum vobis, in Prophetis, id est per os Prophetarum, quatenus obliquitatem vitiorum vestrorum delerem per minas; occidi eos, videlicet negligentes, qui Prophetis non obedierunt, in verbis oris mei: id est, per verba mea eos occidendos prædixi, vel verbis comminatoriis multum eos afflixi ac terrui. Septuaginta transtulerunt, Succidi prophetas vestros, occidi eos verbo oris mei. Et ita sensus est, quod pseudoprophetas Deus occidit, eo quod populum seduxerunt; jussitque eos interfici, vel imperando occidit, ut populus videns illorum occisionem, resipisceret, pœniteret, nec se excusaret dicendo, Seductus sum. Tempore Eliæ occisi sunt prophetæ Baal quadringenti quinquaginta. Denique circa adventum Christi erant pseudoprophetæ in Judæa, de quibus scribitur in Actibus, videlicet Theodas et Judas Galilæus, qui perierunt occisi. Et judicia tua, id est sententia tuæ damnationis, seu æquitas judicii quo te judicabo, quasi lux egredientur, id est, omnibus evidenter innotescent, ita quod scient te juste damnatum, captum, seu derelictum, eo quod post tantam admonitionem converti nolueris. Vel: Judicia tua passiva, id est pœnæ quas tibi infligam, quasi lux egredientur, quoniam manifeste patebunt, ut pro manifestis peccatis inferatur manifesta punitio, sicque pœna sit correspondens peccato. Nunc enim videmus quomodo Judæi vastentur, eo quod in Christum non credant.
paras.en: [[6:5|For this reason|Propter hoc]], namely because I wished to take counsel for your good, [[6:5|have I hewed them|dolavi]]: that is, after the manner of a builder who hews timber, taking off the roughness of the material, I have hewed you, that is, I have threatened you with sharp words, [[6:5|by the prophets|in Prophetis]], that is, through the mouth of the prophets, so as to remove by threats the crookedness of your vices; [[6:5|I have slain them|occidi eos]], namely the negligent, who did not obey the prophets, [[6:5|by the words of my mouth|in verbis oris mei]]: that is, by my words I foretold that they would be slain, or with threatening words I greatly afflicted and terrified them. The Septuagint translated: I have cut down your prophets, I have slain them by the word of my mouth. And so the sense is that God slew the false prophets because they had led the people astray; and he commanded them to be put to death, or slew them by his command, so that the people, seeing them slain, might come to their senses and repent, and not excuse themselves by saying, I was led astray. In the time of Elias four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal were slain[[3 Kings 18:40||]]. And about the time of Christ's coming there were false prophets in Judea, of whom it is written in the Acts, namely Theodas[[Acts 5:36||]] and Judas of Galilee[[Acts 5:37||]], who perished by being slain. [[6:5|and thy judgments|Et judicia tua]], that is, the sentence of thy condemnation, or the justice of the judgment with which I shall judge thee, [[6:5|shall go forth as the light|quasi lux egredientur]], that is, they will be plainly known to all, so that they will know that thou hast been justly condemned, taken captive or forsaken, because after so much warning thou wouldst not be converted. Or: [[6:5|thy judgments|Judicia tua]] taken passively [that is, the judgments thou sufferest], that is, the punishments that I shall inflict on thee, [[6:5|shall go forth as the light|quasi lux egredientur]], because they will be manifestly evident, so that for manifest sins a manifest punishment may be inflicted, and so the punishment may correspond to the sin. For now we see how the Jews are laid waste because they do not believe in Christ.

paras.t: Ideo autem sic punientur: Quia misericordiam volui, id est, opera pietatis et compassionis affectum accepto, et non sacrificium legale, tempore evangelicæ legis, in qua cærimonialia cessaverunt atque mortifera facta sunt, quia non erant nisi figurativa mysteriorum Christi novæque legis: propter quod, veritate impleta ac patefacta, debebant cessare. Et scientiam Dei formatam ac salutarem, caritate ornatam et bonæ operationi conjunctam, volui plus quam holocausta legis: quæ ad Dei honorem totaliter cremabantur, in signum quod homo debet se totum Deo offerre, ejusque obsequio mancipare. Unde Dominus ait in Psalmo: Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, neque de gregibus tuis hircos. Et rursus: Sacrificium et oblationem noluisti, holocaustum et pro peccato non postulasti. Et apud Isaiam: Qui immolat bovem, quasi qui interficiat virum; qui mactat pecus, quasi qui excerebret canem. Quæ omnia accipi possunt pro tempore novæ legis propter causam prætactam, vel pro tempore veteris Testamenti, quantum ad hoc quod non erant per se accepta, neque peccati purgativa, quemadmodum ad Hebræos scribitur: Impossibile est, sanguine hircorum et taurorum auferri peccata. Hæc proprie dicuntur contra Judæos, qui propter occisionem Christi a Romanis vallati, obtulerunt innumerabilia sacrificia Deo pro sua ereptione; sed quia in Christi discipulos non exercuerunt clementiam, et Christi scientiam contempserunt, non meruerunt aliquam misericordiam consequi.
paras.en: And they will be punished thus for this reason: [[6:6|For I desired mercy|Quia misericordiam volui]], that is, I accept works of piety and the affection of compassion, [[6:6|and not sacrifice|et non sacrificium]] of the law, in the time of the law of the Gospel, in which the ceremonial precepts have ceased and have become deadly [that is, keeping them after the Gospel would be a mortal sin], because they were only figures of the mysteries of Christ and of the new law: for which reason, when the truth was fulfilled and laid open, they had to cease. [[6:6|and the knowledge of God|Et scientiam Dei]], formed [*formata*, that is, given its form and life by charity] and saving, adorned with charity and joined to good works, I desired [[6:6|more than holocausts|plus quam holocausta]] of the law, which were wholly burnt to the honour of God, as a sign that man ought to offer his whole self to God and give himself over to his service. Hence the Lord says in the Psalm: [[Ps 49:9|I will not take calves out of thy house: nor he goats out of thy flocks.|Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, neque de gregibus tuis hircos]] And again: [[Ps 39:7|Sacrifice and oblation thou didst not desire|Sacrificium et oblationem noluisti]]; [[Ps 39:7|Burnt offering and sin offering thou didst not require|holocaustum et pro peccato non postulasti]]. And in Isaias: [[Is 66:3|He that sacrificeth an ox, is as if he slew a man: he that killeth a sheep in sacrifice, as if he should brain a dog|Qui immolat bovem, quasi qui interficiat virum; qui mactat pecus, quasi qui excerebret canem]]. All these may be taken of the time of the new law, for the reason touched on above, or of the time of the Old Testament, in that they were not acceptable in themselves, nor did they purge sin, as is written to the Hebrews: [[Heb 10:4|it is impossible that with the blood of oxen and goats sin should be taken away|Impossibile est, sanguine hircorum et taurorum auferri peccata]]. These things are said properly against the Jews who, besieged by the Romans because of the killing of Christ, offered countless sacrifices to God for their deliverance; but because they showed no clemency towards Christ's disciples and despised the knowledge of Christ, they did not deserve to obtain any mercy.

paras.t: Ipsi autem, id est decem et duæ tribus, sicut Adam in paradiso transgressi sunt pactum, id est legem quam pepigi cum eis, quemadmodum Adam contra divinum præceptum comedit de fructu ligni scientiæ boni et mali; ibi, id est in Adam, prævaricati sunt in me: quia in ipso omnes cecidimus, et nascimur filii iræ in originali peccato; vel, Ibi, id est in hoc quod misericordiam et scientiam Dei non prætulerunt sacrificiis legis.
paras.en: [[6:7|But they|Ipsi autem]], that is, the ten and the two tribes, [[6:7|like Adam|sicut Adam]] in paradise [Denis's text adds "in paradise"] [[6:7|have transgressed the covenant|transgressi sunt pactum]], that is, the law that I covenanted with them, just as Adam, against the divine command, ate of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; [[6:7|there|ibi]], that is, in Adam, [[6:7|have they dealt treacherously against me|prævaricati sunt in me]]: for in him we all fell[[Rom 5:12||]], and we are born [[Eph 2:3|children of wrath|filii iræ]] in original sin; or, [[6:7|there|Ibi]], that is, in this, that they did not prefer mercy and the knowledge of God to the sacrifices of the law.

paras.t: Galaad, id est urbs illa sita in tribu Gad, pertinens ad sacerdotes, et civitas fugitivorum, est civitas operantium idolum, quia in ea primo consecratum est idolum, secundum Hieronymum, supplantata sanguine, id est dejecta propter sanguinem in ea impie fusum. Vel hoc ideo dicitur, quoniam primo ab Assyriis capta est, et sanguis civium ejus partim effusus est.
paras.en: [[6:8|Galaad|Galaad]], that is, that city situated in the tribe of Gad, belonging to the priests, and a city of the fugitives [that is, one of the cities of refuge], [[6:8|is a city of workers of idols|est civitas operantium idolum]], because in it an idol was first consecrated, according to Jerome, [[6:8|supplanted with blood|supplantata sanguine]], that is, cast down because of the blood impiously shed in it. Or this is said because it was the first to be taken by the Assyrians, and the blood of its citizens was in part shed.

paras.t: Et quasi fauces virorum latronum : id est, habitatores Galaad assimilati sunt faucibus latronum, aliorum bona devorantium, quoniam aliorum bona diripuerunt et consumpserunt. Particeps fuit Galaad in peccato sacerdotum in via interficientium, id est sacerdotum idolorum, qui per se vel suos ministros spoliabant vel occidebant in via, pergentes de Sichem, id est filios Israel, qui ibant per hanc civitatem seu de ea versus Jerusalem statutis diebus secundum legem, ut hostias offerrent in templo secundum legem : quod prædicti sacerdotes et habitatores Galaad ægre ferentes, posuerunt insidiatores in via, qui pergentes interfecerunt aut spoliaverunt. Denique Sichem, secundum Bedam, quæ modo Neapolis dicitur, erat in confinio decem duarumque tribuum, et sic de ea fuit Israelitis iter versus Jerusalem. Galaad autem interdum est nomen montis, ut patet in Genesi. Quia scelus operati sunt.
paras.en: [[6:9|And like the jaws of highway robbers|Et quasi fauces virorum latronum]]: that is, the inhabitants of Galaad have become like the jaws of robbers who devour the goods of others, since they plundered and consumed the goods of others. [[6:9|they conspire|Particeps]] [*particeps*, "a sharer", which Denis takes of Galaad]: Galaad was a sharer in the sin [[6:9|with the priests who murder in the way|sacerdotum in via interficientium]], that is, of the priests of the idols, who by themselves or through their ministers robbed or slew on the way [[6:9|those that pass out of Sichem|pergentes de Sichem]], that is, the children of Israel who went through this city, or from it, towards Jerusalem on the days appointed by the law, to offer victims in the temple according to the law: which the said priests and the inhabitants of Galaad took ill, and they set men in ambush on the way, who slew or robbed those who passed. Moreover Sichem, which according to Bede is now called Neapolis, was on the border between the ten tribes and the two, and so the Israelites' road to Jerusalem went from it. Galaad, however, is sometimes the name of a mountain, as appears in Genesis[[Gen 31:21||]]. [[6:9|for they have wrought wickedness|Quia scelus operati sunt]].

paras.t: In domo Israel, id est in terra atque familia decem tribuum, vidi horrendum, id est immanissima crimina, scilicet adorationem vitulorum et occisionem pergentium. Unde et Jeremias ait : Obstupuit cœlum super hoc, et expavit terra vehementer. Ibi fornicatus est Ephraim, id est Jeroboam, qui vitulos aureos fecit, eratque de progenie Ephraim, et Ephratæi secuti sunt ejus facinora; contaminatus est Israel vitio idololatriæ, sequens reges suos.
paras.en: [[6:10|in the house of Israel|In domo Israel]], that is, in the land and household of the ten tribes, [[6:10|I have seen a horrible thing|vidi horrendum]], that is, most monstrous crimes, namely the worship of the calves and the slaying of those who passed by. Hence Jeremias too says: The heaven was astonished at this, and the earth was exceedingly afraid[[Jer 2:12||]] [the margin gives "cf. Jer. ii, 12"; Denis quotes loosely, the verse reading "Be astonished, O ye heavens, at this … be very desolate"]. [[6:10|the fornications of Ephraim there|Ibi fornicatus est Ephraim]] [Denis reads "there Ephraim hath committed fornication", where the Vulgate has "the fornications of Ephraim"], that is, Jeroboam, who made the golden calves and was of the stock of Ephraim, and the Ephrathites followed his crimes; [[6:10|Israel is defiled|contaminatus est Israel]] by the vice of idolatry, following its kings.

paras.t: Sed et Juda, id est, populus duarum tribuum, pone messem tibi, id est, segetes et messem in terra tua habebis, quum convertero captivitatem populi mei, id est, quum tempore Cyri regis reduxero duas tribus de captivitate Babylonica ad propriam terram sub duce Zorobabel. In quibus verbis innuit Propheta, quod duæ tribus essent capiendæ ac liberandæ; sed de liberatione decem tribuum non loquitur nisi pro tempore Christi et fine mundi.
paras.en: [[6:11|And thou also, O Juda|Sed et Juda]], that is, the people of the two tribes, [[6:11|set thee a harvest|pone messem tibi]], that is, thou shalt have crops and harvest in thy land, [[6:11|when I shall bring back the captivity of my people|quum convertero captivitatem populi mei]], that is, when in the time of king Cyrus I shall bring back the two tribes from the Babylonian captivity to their own land under the leadership of Zorobabel[[1 Esd 1:1||]][[1 Esd 2:1||]]. In these words the Prophet hints that the two tribes were to be taken captive and set free; but of the deliverance of the ten tribes he speaks only with regard to the time of Christ and the end of the world.

6.title: DE MORALITATE HUJUS CAPITULI SEXTI.
6.title_en: On the moral sense of this sixth chapter.

paras.t: QUEMADMODUM itaque Dominus ait in præsentis capituli principio, In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me, et nos debemus in omni tribulatione corporali seu spirituali, in omni tentatione et persecutione oculos ad Deum dirigere, ejusque clementiam implorare, ut vel liberemur, vel patienter feramus et prævaleamus, quemadmodum ait Psalmista : Ad Dominum, quum tribularer, clamavi. Unde secundo Paralipomenon Josaphat ait : In nobis non est tanta fortitudo, ut possimus resistere; sed quum ignoremus quid agere debeamus, hoc solum habemus residui, ut oculos nostros dirigamus ad te. Magnam nobis spem præstant verba Dei, dicentis : Salus populi ego sum; de quacumque tribulatione clamaverint ad me, exaudiam eos. Multis quoque tribulatio est incitamentum consurgendi ad Deum, qui in prosperis extollerentur : in quibus impleretur illud Isaiæ, Sola vexatio dabit intellectum.
paras.en: Just as the Lord says at the beginning of the present chapter, [[6:1|In their affliction they will rise early to me|In tribulatione sua mane consurgent ad me]], so we too ought, in every tribulation of body or of spirit, in every temptation and persecution, to direct our eyes to God and implore His clemency, that we may either be delivered or bear it patiently and prevail; as the Psalmist says: [[Ps 119:1|In my trouble I cried to the Lord|Ad Dominum, quum tribularer, clamavi]]. Hence in the second book of Paralipomenon Josaphat says: [[2 Par 20:12|as for us we have not strength enough, to be able to resist|In nobis non est tanta fortitudo, ut possimus resistere]]; [[2 Par 20:12|But as we know not what to do, we can only turn our eyes to thee|sed quum ignoremus quid agere debeamus, hoc solum habemus residui, ut oculos nostros dirigamus ad te]]. The words of God give us great hope, when He says: I am the salvation of the people; in whatever tribulation they shall cry to me, I will hear them[[Is 43:1||]][[Ps 36:39||]] [these are the words of the Introit of the Mass of the nineteenth Sunday after Pentecost; the margin gives "Cf. Is. xliii; Ps. xxxvi, 39", passages of like sense]. For many, too, tribulation is a spur to rise up to God, who in prosperity would be lifted up with pride: in them is fulfilled that saying of Isaias, [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand|Sola vexatio dabit intellectum]].

paras.t: Debemus insuper nos invicem cohortari, dicentes, Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum, prout ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus : Adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies, ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati. Peccando autem mortaliter, a Deo omnino recedimus. Venialiter vero peccando, ab ipso aliqualiter elongamur, et nisi adsit custodia diligens, ad recessum disponimur.
paras.en: We ought moreover to exhort one another, saying, [[6:1|Come, and let us return to the Lord|Venite, et revertamur ad Dominum]], as the Apostle says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 3:13|exhort one another every day|Adhortamini vosmetipsos per singulos dies]], [[Heb 3:13|that none of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin|ut non obduretur quis ex vobis fallacia peccati]]. Now by sinning mortally we depart from God altogether; but by sinning venially we are drawn some way off from Him, and unless a careful watch is kept, we are disposed to depart.

paras.t: Vivificabit nos, per gratiæ suæ infusionem, post duos dies, id est post attritionem et invocationem. Contritionem quippe præcedit attritio, quam sequitur divinæ pietatis imploratio; tuncque Deus videns hominem fecisse quod in se est, influit vitam gratiæ, quæ dirimit mortem culpæ. In die tertia, id est in confessione, quæ attritionem et invocationem consequitur, suscitabit nos perfecte, etiam a reatu totaliter aut partim, secundum quantitatem pudoris, contritionis atque fervoris.
paras.en: [[6:3|He will revive us|Vivificabit nos]], by the infusion of His grace, [[6:3|after two days|post duos dies]], that is, after attrition and prayer. For attrition goes before contrition [attrition being sorrow for sin out of fear of punishment, contrition sorrow out of the love of God], and the imploring of God's mercy follows it; and then God, seeing that the man has done what is in him, pours in the life of grace, which ends the death of guilt. [[6:3|on the third day|In die tertia]], that is, in confession, which follows attrition and prayer, [[6:3|he will raise us up|suscitabit nos]] perfectly, even from the debt of punishment [Latin *reatus*: the liability to punishment that remains after the guilt is forgiven], wholly or in part, according to the measure of our shame, contrition and fervour.

paras.t: Quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus. Præter duplicem Christi egressum, in præcedenti articulo positum, est tertius ejus egressus, quo spiritualiter venit ad corda fidelium, de quo ait in Joanne : Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus. Hic ergo egressus præparatus est nobis quasi diluculum seu aurora, ut depellat a nobis obscuritatem peccati, et omne quod saluti animæ adversatur, dummodo mane surgamus ad eum, primo omnium quærentes regnum Dei et justitiam ejus, et cum Psalmista dicentes : Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vigilo; itemque cum Isaia, De mane vigilabo ad te. Stat enim ad ostium pulsans. Et veniet quasi imber nobis temporaneus, rorem consolationis et fecunditatis, aquamque sapientiæ salutaris donando, et serotinus terræ, quando transfert nos de fide ad speciem, de merito ad præmium, de imperfecto ad perfectionem, de quibus ait Apostolus : Quum venerit quod perfectum est, evacuabitur quod ex parte est. Unde in Evangelio scriptum est : Quum sero factum esset, dixit dominus vineæ procuratori : Voca operarios, et redde illis mercedem.
paras.en: [[6:3|His going forth is prepared as the morning light|Quasi diluculum præparatus est egressus ejus]]. Besides the twofold going forth of Christ set out in the preceding article, there is a third going forth of His, by which He comes spiritually into the hearts of the faithful, of which He says in John: [[John 14:23|If any one love me, he will keep my word. And my Father will love him and we will come to him and will make our abode with him|Si quis diligit me, sermonem meum servabit, et Pater meus diliget eum, et ad eum veniemus, et mansionem apud eum faciemus]]. This going forth, then, is prepared for us as the morning light or the dawn, to drive away from us the darkness of sin and all that is against the salvation of the soul, provided that we rise early to Him, seeking first of all [[Matt 6:33|the kingdom of God, and his justice|regnum Dei et justitiam ejus]], and saying with the Psalmist: [[Ps 62:2|O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day|Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vigilo]]; and likewise with Isaias, [[Is 26:9|in the morning early I will watch to thee|De mane vigilabo ad te]]. For He stands at the gate knocking[[Apoc 3:20||]]. [[6:3|and he will come to us as the early|Et veniet quasi imber nobis temporaneus]], giving the dew of consolation and fruitfulness, and [[Ecclus 15:3|the water of wholesome wisdom|aquamque sapientiæ salutaris]]; [[6:3|and the latter rain to the earth|et serotinus terræ]], when He brings us over from faith to sight, from merit to reward, from the imperfect to perfection, of which the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 13:10|when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part shall be done away|Quum venerit quod perfectum est, evacuabitur quod ex parte est]]. Hence it is written in the Gospel: [[Matt 20:8|when evening was come, the lord of the vineyard saith to his steward: Call the labourers and pay them their hire|Quum sero factum esset, dixit dominus vineæ procuratori : Voca operarios, et redde illis mercedem]].

paras.t: Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim? quid faciam tibi, Juda? Hæc possunt esse verba clementissimi Dei ad Christianos peccatores, temporalia congregantes, et labiis tantum confitentes, vel aliis vitiis implicitos, quos Deus ad pœnitentiam indesinenter invitat, eorum damnationi velut compatiens. De quo dicit Apostolus, quod vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire. Hinc et Petrus dicit : Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti. Cui consonans Isaias : Propterea, inquit, exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri. Non ergo divitias bonitatis et longanimitatis ejus contemnamus. Mallet enim Christus animarum amator denuo crucifigi, quam sineret quempiam (quantum in se est) condemnari. Misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina. Multa enim beneficia tribuit istis Deus, videlicet sacramenta Ecclesiæ. Sed ipsi negligunt semetipsos, et misericordia Dei eis oblata, tanquam nubes matutina, non firmatur nec perseverat in eis. Sed utinam gratia et misericordia nostra comparetur nubi de qua loquitur Isaias : Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, et ingredietur Ægyptum; et rursus, Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant?
paras.en: [[6:4|What shall I do to thee, O Ephraim? what shall I do to thee, O Juda?|Quid faciam tibi, Ephraim? quid faciam tibi, Juda?]] These may be the words of the most clement God to Christian sinners who gather up temporal things and confess with their lips only[[Matt 15:8||]], or are entangled in other vices, whom God unceasingly invites to penance, as though suffering with them in their damnation. Of which the Apostle says that He [[1 Tim 2:4|will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth|vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad agnitionem veritatis venire]]. Hence Peter too says: The Lord [[2 Pet 3:9|dealeth patiently for your sake, not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to penance|Patienter agit Dominus propter vos, nolens aliquem perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti]]. In agreement with whom Isaias: [[Is 30:18|Therefore|Propterea]], he says, [[Is 30:18|the Lord waiteth that he may have mercy on you|exspectat Dominus, ut misereatur vestri]]. Let us not then despise [[Rom 2:4|the riches of his goodness|divitias bonitatis]] and His longsuffering. For Christ, the lover of souls, would rather be crucified again than let anyone be condemned (as far as lies in Him). [[6:4|your mercy is as a morning cloud|Misericordia vestra quasi nubes matutina]]. For God bestows many benefits on these, namely the sacraments of the Church. But they neglect themselves, and the mercy of God offered them, like a morning cloud, is not made firm nor does it last in them. But would that our grace and mercy might be likened to the cloud of which Isaias speaks: [[Is 19:1|Behold the Lord will ascend upon a swift cloud, and will enter into Egypt|Ecce Dominus ascendet super nubem levem, et ingredietur Ægyptum]]; and again, [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant]]?

paras.t: Quia misericordiam volui, et non sacrificium. Ex hoc docemur, quam benignos, pios et compassivos, ad ignoscendumque faciles, et ad tribuendum ac succurrendum paratos esse oporteat, ut alter alterius onera portemus, et tales exhibeamus nos proximis nostris, qualem cupimus Deum esse nobis. Propter quod ad Ephesios scribit præcipitque Apostolus : Omnis amaritudo et indignatio et ira et clamor tollatur a vobis ; estote vero invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis. Salomon quoque : Qui pronus est ad misericordiam, benedicetur; et iterum ait, Facere misericordiam, plus placet Deo, quam victimæ. Hæc verba Osee allegat Christus contra Pharisæos apud Matthæum, dum ait : Euntes discite quid sit, Misericordiam volo et non sacrificium.
paras.en: [[6:6|For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice|Quia misericordiam volui, et non sacrificium]]. From this we are taught how kind, loving and compassionate, how ready to forgive, and how prompt to give and to help we ought to be, that we may bear one another's burdens[[Gal 6:2||]], and show ourselves to our neighbours such as we desire God to be to us. For this reason the Apostle writes and commands the Ephesians: [[Eph 4:31|Let all bitterness and anger and indignation and clamour and blasphemy be put away from you|Omnis amaritudo et indignatio et ira et clamor tollatur a vobis]]; [[Eph 4:32|be ye kind one to another: merciful, forgiving one another, even as God hath forgiven you in Christ|estote vero invicem benigni, misericordes, donantes invicem, sicut et Deus in Christo donavit vobis]]. Solomon too: [[Prov 22:9|He that is inclined to mercy, shall be blessed|Qui pronus est ad misericordiam, benedicetur]]; and again he says, [[Prov 21:3|To do mercy|Facere misericordiam]] [[Prov 21:3|pleaseth the Lord more than victims|plus placet Deo, quam victimæ]]. These words of Osee Christ brings forward against the Pharisees in Matthew, when He says: [[Matt 9:13|Go then and learn what this meaneth, I will have mercy and not sacrifice|Euntes discite quid sit, Misericordiam volo et non sacrificium]].

paras.t: Et scientiam Dei plus quam holocausta. Sanctum ergo et acceptissimum Deo est, studio sacræ Scripturæ insistere, sic tamen ut modus servetur, et utiliora non omittantur. Unde dicit Hieronymus : Semper in manibus tuis sacra sit lectio, tenenti tibi codicem somnus subrepat, et cadentem faciem pagina sancta suscipiat; ama scientiam sanctarum Scripturarum, et vitia carnis non amabis. Verumtamen hæc salutaris scientia Dei, interdum pura oratione et immaculatæ conversationis munditia melius atque felicius impetratur. Propter quod Jacobus ait : Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et dabitur ei.
paras.en: [[6:6|and the knowledge of God more than holocausts|Et scientiam Dei plus quam holocausta]]. It is therefore holy and most acceptable to God to apply oneself to the study of Holy Scripture, yet so that measure is kept and more useful things are not left undone. Hence Jerome says: Let holy reading be always in your hands; let sleep steal upon you as you hold the book, and let the sacred page receive your face as it falls; love the knowledge of the holy Scriptures, and you will not love the vices of the flesh. Yet this saving knowledge of God is sometimes better and more happily obtained by pure prayer and by the cleanness of a spotless life. For this reason James says: [[Jas 1:5|if any of you want wisdom, let him ask of God who giveth to all men abundantly and upbraideth not. And it shall be given him|Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et dabitur ei]].

paras.t: Galaad civitas operantium idolum. Galaad interpretatur, transmigratio testimonii : sicque designat perversos prælatos, impiosque doctores seu prædicatores, qui testimonia Scripturarum transferunt in abusionem et voluptatem carnalem, in omnibus quæ operantur propria commoda exquirentes. Isti sunt civitas operantium idolum propriæ adinventionis, non voluntatem divinæ jussionis. Suntque præterea velut fauces latronum, quoniam subditorum bona consumunt, eosque malis exemplis et negligentia ac tepore spiritualiter strangulant et occidunt. Et sunt participes sacerdotum iniquorum, qui pergentes in via virtutum de Sichem, id est opere bono, ad Jerusalem, id est internæ pacis contemplationem, interficiunt, retrahendo eos a bono, atque in vitia inducendo.
paras.en: [[6:8|Galaad is a city of workers of idols|Galaad civitas operantium idolum]]. Galaad is interpreted "the passing over of testimony": and so it signifies perverse prelates and impious doctors or preachers, who turn the testimonies of the Scriptures over to abuse and fleshly pleasure, seeking their own advantage in all that they do. These are the city of workers of the idol of their own invention, not of the will of God's command. And moreover they are [[6:9|like the jaws of highway robbers|velut fauces latronum]], since they consume the goods of their subjects, and by their bad example, their negligence and their lukewarmness spiritually strangle and kill them. And they are partakers of the wicked priests, who murder those that go in the way of virtue from Sichem, that is, from good works, to Jerusalem, that is, to the contemplation of inward peace, drawing them back from good and leading them into vice.

paras.t: In domo Israel vidi horrendum. Horrendum plane est, considerare aut dicere quam immanissima vitia inveniantur jam in Ecclesia Dei, præsertim in his qui spiritualibus deputati videntur, et de Ecclesiæ bonis sustentantur.
paras.en: [[6:10|I have seen a horrible thing in the house of Israel|In domo Israel vidi horrendum]]. Horrible indeed it is to consider or to tell what monstrous vices are found now in the Church of God, above all in those who seem to be set apart for spiritual things and are maintained from the goods of the Church.

paras.t: Postremo, quod in isto capitulo dictum est, Quia ipse cepit et sanabit nos, quidam ad litteram sic exponunt : Ipse Christus cepit, id est, apprehendit nos, eo modo quo ad Hebræos dicit Apostolus, Nusquam angelos apprehendit, sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit : quia videlicet ex semine Abrahæ naturam assumpsit humanam. Hinc et David fatetur : Misit de summo, et accepit me. Quamvis autem expositio ista sit vera, non tamen ad propositum esse censetur, quia pro eo quod nostra translatio continet, Ipse cepit, in Hebræo et in translatione Septuaginta interpretam habetur, Ipse rapuit : et secundum hoc, littera ista exposita est præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: Lastly, what is said in this chapter, [[6:2|he hath taken us, and he will heal us|Quia ipse cepit et sanabit nos]], some expound literally thus: Christ Himself hath taken, that is, laid hold of us, in the way in which the Apostle says to the Hebrews, [[Heb 2:16|nowhere doth he take hold of the angels: but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold|Nusquam angelos apprehendit, sed semen Abrahæ apprehendit]]: because, namely, He took human nature of the seed of Abraham. Hence David too confesses: [[Ps 17:17|He sent from on high, and took me|Misit de summo, et accepit me]]. But although this exposition is true, it is not thought to be to the purpose, because where our translation has "He hath taken", in the Hebrew and in the translation of the Seventy interpreters there stands "He hath snatched away": and according to this the letter was expounded in the preceding article [Art. XIII, Denis's literal exposition of this chapter].

7.title: ELUCIDATIO LITTERALIS CAPITULI SEPTIMI : QUUM SANARE VELLEM ISRAEL, REVELATA EST INIQUITAS EPHRAIM.
7.title_en: Literal explanation of the seventh chapter: When I would have healed Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered.

paras.t: Consequenter ostenditur causa derelictionis decem tribuum, scilicet intolerabilis multiplicitas iniquitatis ipsorum. Itaque Dominus ait: Quum sanare vellem, quantum in me erat, vel voluntate antecedente, non consequente, quæ semper impletur (juxta illud Isaiæ, Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet), Israel, id est populum decem tribuum et unum, a vulneribus animæ, de quibus apud Isaiam habetur, Vulnus et ulcus et plaga tumens; vel a captivitate et tribulatione hostili; revelata est, id est, manifeste ac multipliciter facta est, iniquitas Ephraim, id est Jeroboam Ephratæi, qui aureos vitulos fecit, ac regum ejus iniquitatem sequentium, qui pro magna parte erant de genere Ephraim, et malitia Samariæ, id est habitatorum Samariæ metropolis in regno decem tribuum, qui assecuti sunt peccata et idololatriam regum suorum.
paras.en: Next is shown the cause of the abandonment of the ten tribes, namely the unbearable multitude of their iniquity. And so the Lord says: [[7:1|When I would have healed|Quum sanare vellem]], as far as lay in Me, that is, by My antecedent will, not by My consequent will, which is always fulfilled (according to that of Isaias: [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]) [antecedent and consequent will: the scholastic distinction between what God wills of a thing considered in itself, such as the salvation of all, and what He wills all things considered, which always comes to pass], [[7:1|Israel|Israel]], that is, the people of the ten tribes, and one people, of the wounds of the soul, of which we read in Isaias: [[Is 1:6|wounds and bruises and swelling sores|Vulnus et ulcus et plaga tumens]]; or, of captivity and the oppression of enemies; [[7:1|was discovered|revelata est]], that is, was done openly and in many ways, [[7:1|the iniquity of Ephraim|iniquitas Ephraim]], that is, of Jeroboam the Ephraite, who made the golden calves[[3 Kings 12:28||]], and of his kings who followed his iniquity, who for the most part were of the stock of Ephraim, [[7:1|and the wickedness of Samaria|et malitia Samariæ]], that is, of the inhabitants of Samaria, the chief city in the kingdom of the ten tribes, who followed the sins and the idolatry of their kings.

paras.t: Quia operati sunt mendacium, id est idolum, quod teste Apostolo nihil est: sicque mendacium dicitur, quia opponitur veritati rei seu entis. Quemadmodum enim verum multipliciter dicitur, ita et falsum. Recte quoque idolum vel simulacrum appellatur mendacium, quoniam sicut verum opponitur falso, ita simulacrum Deo, qui veritas est. Denique idolum dicitur nihil, vel non ens, non ex parte materiæ, aut formæ artificialis superinductæ, sed quantum ad id quod esse aut significare putatur. Quidam enim coluerunt idola tanquam animata, et aliquid numinis seu divinitatis habentia, alii tanquam imagines rerum aliquid divinitatis habentium: quorum utrumque est falsum. Propter quod Socrates dixit se malle adorare canem quam idolum, eo quod canis, quum sit opus naturæ, dignior est idolo, quod est opus artis. Vel, per mendacium generaliter intelligi potest dolus atque fallacia, quibus isti pleni fuerunt, sicut communiter fuerunt et sunt Judæi. Unde in Jeremia habetur: Unusquisque a proximo suo se custodiat, et in omni fratre suo non habeat fiduciam.
paras.en: [[7:1|For they have committed falsehood|Quia operati sunt mendacium]], that is, an idol, which, as the Apostle bears witness, [[1 Cor 8:4|is nothing|nihil est]]: and it is called a falsehood because it is opposed to the truth of a thing or being. For as *true* is said in many ways, so also is *false*. An idol or image is also rightly called a falsehood, since as the true is opposed to the false, so is the image to God, who is the truth. Lastly, an idol is called nothing, or non-being, not as regards its matter or the form given it by art, but as regards what it is thought to be or to signify. For some worshipped idols as living things having something of godhead or divinity in them, others as images of things having something of divinity: and both are false. For this reason Socrates said that he would rather adore a dog than an idol, because a dog, being a work of nature, is worthier than an idol, which is a work of art. Or, by *falsehood* may be understood in general deceit and trickery, of which these men were full, as the Jews commonly were and are. Hence it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:4|Let every man take heed of his neighbour, and let him not trust in any brother of his|Unusquisque a proximo suo se custodiat, et in omni fratre suo non habeat fiduciam]].

paras.t: Et fur ingressus est spolians, latrunculus foris. Per furem et latrunculum quidam intelligunt Jeroboam regem, qui occulte et deceptorie aggressus est populum, inducendo eum ad idololatriam, sicque spoliavit eum auxilio Dei et spiritualibus bonis, et velut pessimus latro eorum animas interfecit, quas a fonte vitæ Deo sancto et adorando avertit. Sed quia in præcedenti capitulo dictum est, quod in regno decem tribuum viguerunt latrocinia et rapinæ, potest per furem et latrunculum designari quod in populo isto fuerunt fures latenter ingredientes et spoliantes, latrunculi quoque in locis forinsecus interficientes: sæpe enim ponitur in Scripturis singulare pro plurali.
paras.en: [[7:1|and the thief is come in to steal, the robber is without|Et fur ingressus est spolians, latrunculus foris]]. By the thief and the robber some understand King Jeroboam, who came upon the people secretly and by deceit, leading them into idolatry, and so robbed them of the help of God and of spiritual goods, and like the worst of robbers killed their souls, which he turned away from God, the holy and adorable fountain of life. But since it was said in the preceding chapter that robberies and plunder flourished in the kingdom of the ten tribes[[Osee 6:9||]], the thief and the robber may signify that among this people there were thieves who came in by stealth and plundered, and robbers too who killed people out of doors: for in the Scriptures the singular is often put for the plural.

paras.t: Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis, id est, ne cogitent cum assensu, omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum, id est, quod nunc antiqua et pristina eorum peccata in deserto seu postea perpetrata attendo, et pro illis eos jam punio: ita quod patres comederunt uvam acerbam, et ob id dentes filiorum obstupescant, impleaturque in eis illud Jeremiæ in Threnis: Patres nostri peccaverunt, et non sunt; et nos iniquitates eorum portavimus; nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ: id est, vitia idolatriæ usque in præsens, tam evidenter tamque multiformiter perseverant in eis, quod per modum vestimenti eos circumdant, et testantur quod propter propria crimina puniuntur, nec possunt vetera patrum suorum peccata contra Deum causari. Sic itaque propriis culpis et pœnis pro illis juste inflictis circumdantur atque ligantur, prout in Proverbiis asseritur: Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur. Coram facie mea factæ sunt, id est, me præsente ac intuente prædicta mala egerunt; vel, Coram facie mea factæ sunt, id est, peccata illa mihi ipsi proposui, ut ea ulciscar.
paras.en: [[7:2|And lest they may say in their hearts|Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis]], that is, lest they think it with assent, [[7:2|that I remember all their wickedness|omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum]], that is, that I am now looking to their old and former sins, committed in the desert or afterwards, and am now punishing them for those: as if [[Ezech 18:2|The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge|patres comederunt uvam acerbam, et ob id dentes filiorum obstupescant]], and that of Jeremias in the Lamentations be fulfilled in them: [[Lam 5:7|Our fathers have sinned, and are not: and we have borne their iniquities|Patres nostri peccaverunt, et non sunt; et nos iniquitates eorum portavimus]]; [[7:2|their own devices now have beset them about|nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ]]: that is, the vices of idolatry persist in them down to the present, so plainly and in so many forms that they surround them like a garment, and bear witness that they are punished for their own crimes, and cannot plead against God the old sins of their fathers. So they are surrounded and bound by their own faults and by the penalties justly laid on them for these, as is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 5:22|His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins|Iniquitates suæ capient impium, et funibus peccatorum suorum constringetur]]. [[7:2|they have been done before my face|Coram facie mea factæ sunt]], that is, they did the evils aforesaid while I was present and looking on; or, *they have been done before my face*, that is, I have set those sins before Myself, to avenge them.

paras.t: In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem, id est, populus Israel consentiendo et insistendo peccatis Jeroboam regis, lætum fecit eumdem; et in mendaciis suis, id est verbis mendacibus atque fraudulentis operibus, lætificaverunt principes prædicti Jeroboam: qui regi suo confœderati in malo, gaudebant de idololatria populi. Quidam exponunt hoc de falsis prophetis, quorum consilio dicunt Jeroboam constituisse cultum vitulorum aureorum. Quibus obviare videtur dictum Hieronymi, asserentis quod Jeroboam forte fecit caput vituli aurei, sicut didicit in Ægypto, in qua tale colebatur portentum. Et iterum tertio Regum habetur, quod Jeroboam excogitato consilio fecit hos vitulos, et dies festivos instituit, secundum quod finxit sibi proprio corde. Unde non videtur dicta assertio vera. Potuit tamen esse, quod in processu temporis pseudoprophetæ roboraverunt eum in suo errore, quemadmodum creditur fecisse propheta Samariæ, qui Prophetam de terra Juda missum, et regem Jeroboam increpantem, seduxit.
paras.en: [[7:3|They have made the king glad with their wickedness|In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem]], that is, the people of Israel, by consenting to and keeping on in the sins of King Jeroboam, made him glad; [[7:3|and the princes with their lies|et in mendaciis suis]], that is, with lying words and deceitful works, they made glad [[7:3|the princes|principes]] of the said Jeroboam, who, leagued with their king in evil, rejoiced at the idolatry of the people. Some explain this of the false prophets, by whose counsel, they say, Jeroboam set up the worship of the golden calves. Against them seems to stand the saying of Jerome, who asserts that Jeroboam perhaps made the head of the golden calf as he had learned in Egypt, where such a monster was worshipped. And again it is said in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 12:30||]] that Jeroboam, having found out a device, made these calves[[3 Kings 12:28||]], and appointed feast days, as he had devised in his own heart[[3 Kings 12:33||]]. So the assertion mentioned does not seem true. Yet it may be that in the course of time false prophets strengthened him in his error, as the prophet of Samaria is believed to have done, who deceived the Prophet sent from the land of Juda, who had rebuked King Jeroboam[[3 Kings 13:18||]] [the margin gives III Reg. xiii; the old prophet in fact dwelt in Bethel].

paras.t: Omnes adulterantes, id est, spirituale adulterium seu idololatriam committentes, quasi clibanus succensus a coquente, id est, similes furno a pistore accenso: quoniam sicut pistor fornacem calefacit, sic Jeroboam plebem Israel ad idololatriam provocavit.
paras.en: [[7:4|They are all adulterers|Omnes adulterantes]], that is, committing spiritual adultery, or idolatry, [[7:4|like an oven heated by the baker|quasi clibanus succensus a coquente]], that is, like a furnace lit by the baker: for as the baker heats the furnace, so Jeroboam stirred up the people of Israel to idolatry.

paras.t: Quievit paululum civitas, id est, populus urbis in qua mansit Jeroboam, modico tempore cessavit, a commixtione fermenti, id est ab infectione et communione corruptionis idololatriæ, donec fermentaretur totum, id est, universus populus idololatriæ consentiret. Primo enim Jeroboam non compulit populum ad vitulorum culturam, sed inclinavit: tum ne ab aliquibus bonis et religiosis ei renitentibus impediretur propositum ejus (nam in principio regni sui multi adhuc devoti fuerunt in decem tribubus); tum quia pensavit quod coacta et per necessitatem seu violentiam introducta, citius dissolvuntur, quod autem voluntarie agitur, diutius perseverat. Idcirco civitas parum quievit: nam primo reliquit populum propriæ voluntati, et tunc non exercebatur idololatria tam frequenter; sed paulatim traxit populum ad suam voluntatem, donec omnes consenserunt, quamvis semper fuerunt quidam, aliorum comparatione paucissimi, qui non consenserunt: propter quos positi erant custodes, ne permitterentur Jerosolymam ire et immolare.
paras.en: [[7:4|the city rested a little|Quievit paululum civitas]], that is, the people of the city in which Jeroboam dwelt ceased for a short time [[7:4|from the mingling of the leaven|a commixtione fermenti]], that is, from the infection and fellowship of the corruption of idolatry, [[7:4|till the whole was leavened|donec fermentaretur totum]], that is, till the whole people consented to idolatry. For at first Jeroboam did not force the people to the worship of the calves, but inclined them to it: both so that his purpose should not be hindered by some good and devout men resisting him (for at the beginning of his reign there were still many devout men in the ten tribes); and because he reckoned that things brought in by force, by compulsion or violence, are soon undone, whereas what is done willingly lasts longer. Therefore the city rested a little: for at first he left the people to their own will, and then idolatry was not practised so often; but little by little he drew the people to his will, until all consented, although there were always some, very few in comparison with the rest, who did not consent: on whose account guards were set, so that they should not be allowed to go to Jerusalem and sacrifice.

paras.t: Denique in fermento duo considerantur, videlicet prioris naturæ corruptio, sicque accipitur in malo, et significat corruptionem peccati, seu falsam doctrinam, ut quum ait Salvator: Cavete a fermento Pharisæorum, et a fermento Herodis; et Apostolus: Expurgate vetus fermentum, ut sitis nova conspersio. Sic modo accipitur. Secundo, consideratur in fermento quædam virtualis sapiditas, quæ massam efficit sapidam, et ita accipitur in bono, et designat statum Ecclesiæ, vel efficacem doctrinam, aut simile aliquid, ut dum ait in Evangelio Christus: Simile est regnum cœlorum fermento, quod acceptum abscondit mulier in farinæ tribus satis, donec fermentaretur totum.
paras.en: Lastly, two things are considered in leaven. First, the corruption of its former nature: so it is taken in a bad sense, and signifies the corruption of sin, or false doctrine, as when the Saviour says: [[Mark 8:15|beware of the leaven of the Pharisees|Cavete a fermento Pharisæorum]][[Matt 16:6||]][[Matt 16:11||]], [[Mark 8:15|and of the leaven of Herod|et a fermento Herodis]]; and the Apostle: [[1 Cor 5:7|Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new paste|Expurgate vetus fermentum, ut sitis nova conspersio]]. So it is taken here. Secondly, there is considered in leaven a certain power of savour, which makes the lump savoury: so it is taken in a good sense, and signifies the state of the Church, or effective doctrine, or something of the kind, as when Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 13:33|The kingdom of heaven is like to leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until the whole was leavened|Simile est regnum cœlorum fermento, quod acceptum abscondit mulier in farinæ tribus satis, donec fermentaretur totum]].

paras.t: Dies regis nostri: id est, toto populo igne idololatriæ inflammato, cœperunt idololatrantes dicere coram Jeroboam: Iste est dies solennis, quem Jeroboam rex noster statuit nobis in honore idolorum celebrandum; ideo nunc gaudemus, et ludimus, et idola adoramus. Jeroboam enim præfixit populo certos dies solenniter peragendos, et populus regi suo applausit.
paras.en: [[7:5|The day of our king|Dies regis nostri]]: that is, when the whole people had been set ablaze with the fire of idolatry, the idolaters began to say before Jeroboam: This is the solemn day which Jeroboam our king has appointed us to keep in honour of the idols; therefore now we rejoice, and play, and adore the idols. For Jeroboam fixed for the people certain days to be kept solemnly[[3 Kings 12:32||]][[3 Kings 12:33||]], and the people applauded their king.

paras.t: Cœperunt principes furere a vino: id est, principes Jeroboam prædictis verbis exhilarati, vitiis gulæ serviebant, et præ ebrietate vini, usum rationis amittentes, cultui idolorum irrationabiliter et impudenter vacabant ut furibundi. Extendit manum suam rex Jeroboam cum illusoribus, id est populo atque principibus, qui sibi vanis laudibus illudebant, imo et se ipsos seduxerunt. Rex enim videns subditos sibi sic acclamare, consensit, et eadem fecit quæ populus, in idolorum honorem.
paras.en: [[7:5|the princes began to be mad with wine|Cœperunt principes furere a vino]]: that is, the princes of Jeroboam, cheered by these words, gave themselves to the vices of gluttony, and losing the use of reason through drunkenness, devoted themselves to the worship of idols without reason or shame, like madmen. King Jeroboam [[7:5|stretched out his hand|Extendit manum suam]] [[7:5|with scorners|cum illusoribus]], that is, with the people and the princes, who mocked him with empty praises, and indeed deceived themselves. For the king, seeing his subjects acclaim him so, consented, and did the same as the people, in honour of the idols.

paras.t: Quia applicuerunt subditi, quasi clibanum cor suum ad consilia regis, id est, ferventi affectu consenserunt instigationi Jeroboam suggerentis vitulorum culturam, quum insidiaretur eis, id est, quum ipse Jeroboam fraudulenter averteret eos a veri Dei obsequio. Tota nocte dormivit coquens eos: id est, Jeroboam cernens populum toto affectu sibi acquiescentem, fuit securus, et noctibus intrepide conquievit: qui populum istum coxit, id est, igne idololatriæ induravit, quemadmodum ignis fornacis panes indurat. Nam ante iste Jeroboam formidavit, et inquiete dormivit, timens, si populus Israel iret adorare in templo Jerusalem, quod reverteretur ad successores David, sub quorum dominio fuit templum: sicque metuebat occidi a populo, vel regno privari. Idcirco ex vitioso timore et ambitione, fecit vitulos aureos, ut illos Israel adorans, non amplius proficisceretur Jerusalem. Quumque Jeroboam vidisset se, quod optaverat, assecutum, secure dormivit. Mane ipse succensus, id est, diluculo consurgens Jeroboam, statim ardore idololatriæ est ignitus, quasi ignis flammæ, ita quod ante omnia cum fervore accessit ad idolorum culturam.
paras.en: [[7:6|Because they have applied|Quia applicuerunt]], the subjects, [[7:6|their heart like an oven|quasi clibanum cor suum]] to the counsels of the king, that is, consented with burning affection to the urging of Jeroboam, who prompted the worship of the calves, [[7:6|when he laid snares for them|quum insidiaretur eis]], that is, when Jeroboam himself was craftily turning them away from the service of the true God. [[7:6|he slept all the night baking them|Tota nocte dormivit coquens eos]]: that is, Jeroboam, seeing the people yielding to him with all their heart, was at ease, and rested at night without fear: he who baked this people, that is, hardened them with the fire of idolatry, as the fire of the furnace hardens loaves. For before, this Jeroboam was afraid, and slept uneasily, fearing that if the people of Israel went to worship in the temple of Jerusalem, they would go back to the successors of David, under whose rule the temple was: and so he feared to be killed by the people, or deprived of the kingdom[[3 Kings 12:26||]][[3 Kings 12:27||]]. Therefore out of sinful fear and ambition he made the golden calves[[3 Kings 12:28||]], so that Israel, adoring them, should no longer go to Jerusalem. And when Jeroboam saw that he had gained what he wished, he slept securely. [[7:6|in the morning he himself was heated|Mane ipse succensus]], that is, Jeroboam, rising at dawn, was at once kindled with the heat of idolatry, [[7:6|as a flaming fire|quasi ignis flammæ]], so that before all else he went eagerly to the worship of the idols.

paras.t: Quid plura? Omnes principes et satellites ac subditi ejus calefacti sunt quasi clibanus, id est, exemplo impii regis fervebant ad idololatriam. Ecce quantum nocet iniqua potestas: nam quum Dominus vellet subditos curare, impedita est salus eorum per regis facinora, in quantum imitati sunt ea. Propter quod scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Qualis est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea. Et devoraverunt judices suos, id est, bonos qui eos recte arguebant de idololatria, tandem subverterunt, et suo ac regis consilio atque exemplo ad idololatriam induxerunt; vel, Devoraverunt eos, quia redarguentes, et idola colere non volentes, occiderunt. Omnes reges eorum, videlicet decem tribuum, ceciderunt, id est, peccato idololatriæ lapsi sunt, quoniam nullus eorum recessit a peccato Jeroboam, ut patet tertio et quarto Regum; non est qui clamet in eis ad me, quoniam nullus eorum me veraciter invocavit: quia etsi forte quidam eorum Deum Israel aliquo modo cognovit et invocavit, non tamen digne et virtuose, eo quod idola non abjecit.
paras.en: What more? [[7:7|They were all|Omnes]], his princes and attendants and subjects, [[7:7|heated like an oven|calefacti sunt quasi clibanus]], that is, burned for idolatry by the example of the wicked king. See how much harm wicked power does: for when the Lord wished to heal the subjects, their salvation was hindered by the king's crimes, in so far as they imitated them. For this reason it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:2|what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein|Qualis est rector civitatis, tales et habitantes in ea]]. [[7:7|and have devoured their judges|Et devoraverunt judices suos]], that is, the good men who rightly reproved them for idolatry they at length overthrew, and by their own and the king's counsel and example led into idolatry; or, *they devoured them*, because they killed them when they reproved them and would not worship idols. [[7:7|all their kings|Omnes reges eorum]], namely of the ten tribes, [[7:7|have fallen|ceciderunt]], that is, have fallen into the sin of idolatry, since none of them departed from the sin of Jeroboam, as is plain from the third and fourth books of Kings; [[7:7|there is none amongst them that calleth unto me|non est qui clamet in eis ad me]], since none of them truly called upon Me: for though perhaps some of them in some way knew and called upon the God of Israel, yet not worthily and virtuously, because they did not cast away the idols.

paras.t: Ephraim, id est regnum decem tribuum, in populis ipse commiscebatur, id est, gentilibus assimilatus est, veri Dei cultum derelinquendo, et miscens se vitiis gentilitatis: quia non solum aureos vitulos adoravit, sed insuper deos nationum. Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis, id est, sordibus idololatriæ undique contaminatus, et per pœnitentiam non conversus, quemadmodum panis subcinericius maculatur pulveribus terræ, neque revolvitur. Ideo subdit, qui non reversatur. Sic ipsi non sunt ad Dominum reversi, ita quod verbum Isaiæ completur in eis: Populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum non exquisierunt. De talibus Dominus ait in Jeremia: Quare aversus est populus iste aversione contentiosa?
paras.en: [[7:8|Ephraim|Ephraim]], that is, the kingdom of the ten tribes, [[7:8|himself is mixed among the nations|in populis ipse commiscebatur]], that is, became like the gentiles, forsaking the worship of the true God and mixing himself with the vices of heathendom: for he adored not only the golden calves but the gods of the nations besides. [[7:8|Ephraim is become as bread baked under the ashes|Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis]], that is, defiled on every side with the filth of idolatry and not turned by penance, as bread baked under the ashes is soiled with the dust of the earth and is not turned over. Therefore he adds: [[7:8|that is not turned|qui non reversatur]]. So they have not returned to the Lord, so that the word of Isaias is fulfilled in them: [[Is 9:13|And the people are not returned to him who hath struck them, and have not sought after the Lord of hosts|Populus non est reversus ad percutientem se, et Dominum non exquisierunt]]. Of such the Lord says in Jeremias: [[Jer 8:5|Why then is this people|Quare aversus est populus iste]] [[Jer 8:5|turned away with a stubborn revolting|aversione contentiosa]]?

paras.t: Comederunt alieni, id est extranei et gentiles hostes Israel, robur ejus, id est bona populi hujus, terræ nascentia devorando, thesauros tollendo, et fortes populi occidendo; et ipse nescivit, id est, plagam propriam non attendit, nec Dei justitiam consideravit, nec suæ castigationis contemplatus est causam, videlicet quod propter idololatriam talia pateretur. Simile est quod de regno Juda prædixit Isaias: Deus combussit eum in circuitu, et non cognovit. De quibus scriptum est in Jeremia: Percussisti eos, et non doluerunt. Sed et cani, id est senes, effusi sunt in eo, id est, idololatriæ vitio dediti erant in populo isto. Vel sensus est, quod ipsi usque ad ultimam senectutem et regni sui finem, permanserunt in tanto facinore, prout in libro Job scribitur: Cunctis diebus suis superbit impius. Et ipse populus Israel ignoravit quod finis regni sibi instaret merito hujus peccati.
paras.en: [[7:9|Strangers have devoured|Comederunt alieni]], that is, foreigners and gentiles, the enemies of Israel, [[7:9|his strength|robur ejus]], that is, the goods of this people, devouring what the land brought forth, carrying off their treasures, and killing the strong men of the people; [[7:9|and he knew it not|et ipse nescivit]], that is, he did not heed his own wound, nor consider the justice of God, nor see the cause of his chastisement, namely that he suffered such things for his idolatry. Like this is what Isaias foretold of the kingdom of Juda: God [[Is 42:25|hath burnt him round about, and he knew not|combussit eum in circuitu, et non cognovit]]. Of whom it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|thou hast struck them, and they have not grieved|Percussisti eos, et non doluerunt]]. [[7:9|yea, grey hairs|Sed et cani]], that is, old men, [[7:9|also are spread about upon him|effusi sunt in eo]], that is, were given to the vice of idolatry among this people.
