Or the sense is that they remained in so great a crime right up to extreme old age and the end of their kingdom, as is written in the book of Job: [[Job 15:20|The wicked man is proud all his days|Cunctis diebus suis superbit impius]]. [[7:9|and he|Et ipse]], the people of Israel, [[7:9|is ignorant of it|ignoravit]], that the end of the kingdom was upon him in punishment of this sin.

paras.t: Et humiliabitur superbia Israel, id est, debite punietur et dejicietur, in facie ejus, id est cito, adhuc populo isto, quem alloquor, vivente, et propriam calamitatem spectante ac sentiente. Deus enim superbis resistit; et coram Deo atque hominibus odibilis est superbia. Unde et Isaias ait: Incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum. Nec reversi sunt filii Israel ad Dominum Deum suum, et non quæsierunt eum in omnibus his malis pœnæ et culpæ, quibus gravati sunt: ita quod nec vexatio dedit eis intellectum; nec impletum est in eis illud Isaiæ, in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis. De talibus scriptum est in libro Job: Quasi de industria recesserunt a Deo; et iterum: Dixerunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus. Itemque in Jeremia: Induraverunt faciem suam supra petram, et noluerunt reverti.
paras.en: [[7:10|And the pride of Israel shall be humbled|Et humiliabitur superbia Israel]], that is, shall be duly punished and cast down, [[7:10|before his face|in facie ejus]], that is, soon, while this people whom I address is still living, and sees and feels its own calamity. For God resists the proud; and pride is hateful before God and men. Hence Isaias too says: [[Is 2:17|the loftiness of men shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be humbled|Incurvabitur sublimitas hominum, et humiliabitur altitudo virorum]]. [[7:10|and they have not returned|Nec reversi sunt]], the children of Israel, [[7:10|to the Lord their God, nor have they sought him in all these|ad Dominum Deum suum, et non quæsierunt eum in omnibus his]] evils of punishment and of guilt with which they were weighed down: so that not even vexation gave them understanding; nor was that of Isaias fulfilled in them: [[Is 26:16|in the tribulation of murmuring thy instruction was with them|in tribulatione murmuris doctrina tua eis]]. Of such it is written in the book of Job: [[Job 34:27|Who as it were on purpose have revolted from him|Quasi de industria recesserunt a Deo]]; and again: [[Job 21:14|Who have said to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways|Dixerunt Deo, Recede a nobis, scientiam viarum tuarum nolumus]]. And likewise in Jeremias: [[Jer 5:3|they have made their faces harder than the rock, and they have refused to return|Induraverunt faciem suam supra petram, et noluerunt reverti]].

paras.t: Et factus est Ephraim quasi columba seducta, id est assimilatus columbæ retibus aucupis comprehensæ, non habens ipse Ephraim cor, id est veram sapientiam et rectæ rationis judicium: propter quod dæmonum venantium captus est laqueo, estque secutus errorem qui subditur. De talibus loquitur Dominus in Jeremia: Audi, popule stulte, qui non habes cor. Hoc loco dicit gloriosus Hieronymus: Præcipit Dominus in Evangelio, ut simus simplices quasi columbæ, et astuti quasi serpentes, ut imitantes simplicitatem columbarum et serpentis astutiam, nec aliis nocere possimus, nec ab aliis insidias patiamur, sed simplicitate et prudentia exhibeamus hominem temperatum: quia prudentia absque bonitate, malitia est; et simplicitas absque ratione, stultitia. Porro in columba duo notantur, puta simplicitas et stoliditas. Quoad primum, accipitur in bono, quum ait Salvator: Estote simplices sicut columbæ; et Psalmista: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ? Isaias quoque: Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas? Sic et in Canticis per columbam designatur Ecclesia. Quoad secundum, accipitur in malo, sicut hoc loco. Præterea, secundum Hieronymum, Propheta comparat Ephraim columbæ magis quam ceteris avibus, quoniam aliæ aves cum vitæ suæ periculo proprios protegunt pullos a rapacibus avibus, sola columba ablatos pullos non dolet, neque requirit. Sic regnum Ephraim dissipatum per partes, populum deletum non sensit.
paras.en: [[7:11|And Ephraim is become as a dove that is decoyed|Et factus est Ephraim quasi columba seducta]], that is, like a dove caught in the fowler's nets, [[7:11|not having|non habens]], Ephraim himself, [[7:11|a heart|cor]], that is, true wisdom and the judgment of right reason: for which reason he was caught in the snare of the hunting demons, and followed the error that is told next. Of such the Lord speaks in Jeremias: [[Jer 5:21|Hear, O foolish people, and without understanding|Audi, popule stulte, qui non habes cor]] [Latin: *who hast not a heart*; the margin gives "Ibid. 21", that is, Jer. v, 21]. On this place the glorious Jerome says: The Lord commands in the Gospel that we be [[Matt 10:16|simple as doves|simplices quasi columbæ]] and [[Matt 10:16|wise as serpents|astuti quasi serpentes]], so that, imitating the simplicity of doves and the cunning of the serpent, we may neither be able to harm others nor suffer snares from others, but by simplicity and prudence show ourselves well-tempered men: for prudence without goodness is malice, and simplicity without reason is folly. Moreover, two things are noted in the dove, namely simplicity and dullness. As to the first, it is taken in a good sense, as when the Saviour says: Be ye [[Matt 10:16|simple as doves|simplices sicut columbæ]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 54:7|Who will give me wings like a dove|Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut columbæ]]? And Isaias: [[Is 60:8|Who are these, that fly as clouds, and as doves to their windows?|Qui sunt isti, qui ut nubes volant, et quasi columbæ ad fenestras suas?]]? So too in the Canticle the Church is signified by the dove[[Cant 2:10||]][[Cant 2:14||]]. As to the second, it is taken in a bad sense, as in this place. Further, according to Jerome, the Prophet compares Ephraim to the dove rather than to other birds because other birds protect their young from birds of prey at the risk of their own life, while the dove alone neither grieves for its young when they are taken nor looks for them. So the kingdom of Ephraim, scattered piece by piece, did not feel the destruction of its people.

paras.t: Deinde describitur insipientia Israel. Ægyptum invocabant, id est, invocatione et confidentia Dei relicta, Ægyptiorum subsidium procurare conati sunt tempore tribulationis hostilis: quod fecerunt tempore Osee regis; ad Assyrios abierunt pro auxilio, tempore Manahem regis, ut legitur quarto Regum.
paras.en: Next the folly of Israel is described. [[7:11|they called upon Egypt|Ægyptum invocabant]], that is, forsaking the invocation of God and trust in Him, they tried to obtain the help of the Egyptians in time of trouble from their enemies: which they did in the time of King Osee[[4 Kings 17:4||]]; [[7:11|they went to the Assyrians|ad Assyrios abierunt]] for help, in the time of King Manahem, as we read in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 15:19||]].

paras.t: Et quum profecti fuerint ad Ægyptios sive Assyrios procurandos, expandam super eos rete meum, id est amplitudinem potentiæ meæ, ita quod locum mutando, non effugient manum meam, in qua sunt omnes fines terræ. Maledictus enim, qui ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus. Quasi volucrem cœli detraham eos, id est, dejiciam et ab effectu optato impediam. Simile est quod per Ezechielem loquitur Deus: Expandam super vos rete meum, et capiemini sagena mea. Unde et Isaias testatus est: Ægyptus vane auxiliabitur. Cædam eos, id est puniam, secundum auditionem cœtus eorum, id est universaliter, secundum quod omnes regis sui consilium audierunt, et idolis servierunt.
paras.en: [[7:12|And when they shall go|Et quum profecti fuerint]] to win over the Egyptians or the Assyrians, [[7:12|I will spread my net upon them|expandam super eos rete meum]], that is, the breadth of My power, so that by changing their place they shall not escape My hand, in which are [[Ps 94:4|all the ends of the earth|omnes fines terræ]]. For [[Jer 17:5|Cursed be|Maledictus]] he [[Jer 17:5|maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the Lord|ponit carnem brachium suum, et a Domino recedit cor ejus]]. [[7:12|I will bring them down as the fowl of the air|Quasi volucrem cœli detraham eos]], that is, I will cast them down and keep them from the outcome they desire. Like this is what God says by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 17:20|I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my net|Expandam super vos rete meum, et capiemini sagena mea]] [Denis has *over you … you shall be taken*, where the Douay-Rheims has "over him … he shall be taken"]. Hence Isaias too bore witness: [[Is 30:7|Egypt shall help in vain|Ægyptus vane auxiliabitur]]. [[7:12|I will strike them|Cædam eos]], that is, punish them, [[7:12|as their congregation hath heard|secundum auditionem cœtus eorum]], that is, all together, according as all listened to the counsel of their king and served idols.

paras.t: Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me per idololatriam aliaque peccata, propter quæ meruerunt temporaliter captivari, æternaliterque damnari. Unde in Threnis habetur: Væ nobis, quia peccavimus. Quum enim Deus æternus ac adorandus, sit universæ beatitudinis origo fontana, qui ab ipso discedunt, nil nisi miseriam illabuntur; et si temporaliter prosperari atque florere videantur, tanto infeliciores sunt, quo amplius prosperantur. Vastabuntur, id est, ab Assyriis capientur, quia prævaricati sunt in me, legis præcepta penitus deserendo, imo et contra naturalem rationem idola venerando.
paras.en: [[7:13|Woe to them, for they have departed from me|Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me]] by idolatry and other sins, for which they deserved to be made captive in time and damned for eternity. Hence it is said in the Lamentations: [[Lam 5:16|woe to us, because we have sinned|Væ nobis, quia peccavimus]]. For since God, eternal and adorable, is the fountain-source of all happiness, those who depart from Him fall into nothing but misery; and if they seem to prosper and flourish in time, they are the more unhappy the more they prosper. [[7:13|they shall be wasted|Vastabuntur]], that is, they shall be taken by the Assyrians, [[7:13|because they have transgressed against me|quia prævaricati sunt in me]], utterly forsaking the precepts of the law, and indeed worshipping idols against natural reason.

paras.t: Et ego redemi eos, quia patres eorum eduxi de Ægyptiaca servitute: et has decem tribus Deus frequenter liberavit miraculose ab hostibus, ut patet tertio et quarto Regum; et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia, beneficia mea idolis adscribendo, sicut et patres eorum dixerunt: Isti sunt dii tui, Israel, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti.
paras.en: [[7:13|and I redeemed them|Et ego redemi eos]], for I brought their fathers out of the bondage of Egypt[[Ex 14:1||]]: and God often delivered these ten tribes miraculously from their enemies, as is plain from the third and fourth books of Kings[[3 Kings 20:1||]][[4 Kings 3:1||]][[4 Kings 7:1||]][[4 Kings 13:1||]]; [[7:13|and they have spoken lies against me|et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia]], ascribing My benefits to the idols, as their fathers also said: [[Ex 32:8|These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt|Isti sunt dii tui, Israel, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti]].

paras.t: Et non clamaverunt ad me in corde suo, cordialiter atque attente me deprecando, sed ululabant, id est, idola laudabant et exorabant, in cubilibus suis, in quibus lasciviebant, vel, in delubris, ubi idololatriam exercebant. Et rite canticum idolorum nominat sanctus Propheta ululatum, secundum Glossam, quia amisso rationali sensu, lupis seu canibus similes erant. Super triticum et vinum, id est post immoderatam cibi ac potus sumptionem, ruminabant, id est, more bestiarum ad fauces ea quæ sumpserant, reducebant: in quo de gulæ vitiis arguuntur. Recesserunt a me, qui omnia impleo, non locali distantia, sed affectionis imparilitate, quoniam unionem caritatis et gratiæ abjecerunt. De talibus ait Deus per Isaiam: Ea quæ nolui, elegistis.
paras.en: [[7:14|And they have not cried to me with their heart|Et non clamaverunt ad me in corde suo]], praying to Me from the heart and attentively, [[7:14|but they howled|sed ululabant]], that is, they praised and entreated the idols, [[7:14|in their beds|in cubilibus suis]], in which they wantoned, or, in the shrines where they practised idolatry. And rightly, according to the Gloss, the holy Prophet calls the song of the idols a howling, because, having lost the sense of reason, they were like wolves or dogs. [[7:14|upon wheat and wine|Super triticum et vinum]], that is, after taking food and drink beyond measure, [[7:14|they have thought|ruminabant]] [Latin *ruminabant*, "they chewed the cud", which Denis takes literally], that is, like beasts they brought back to the throat what they had eaten: in which they are rebuked for the vices of gluttony. [[7:14|they are departed from me|Recesserunt a me]], who fill all things: not by distance of place, but by unlikeness of affection, since they cast off the union of charity and grace. Of such God says by Isaias: [[Is 65:12|you have chosen the things that displease me|Ea quæ nolui, elegistis]].

paras.t: Et ego erudivi eos, mittendo eis Prophetas, naturalique lumine rationis eos decorando, de quo legitur: Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine; et confortavi brachia eorum tempore præliorum, ita quod miraculose prævaluerunt. Vel per brachia intelliguntur potentiæ operativæ, videlicet intellectus practicus et voluntas, appetitusque sensitivus: quas Deus confortat, dando promptitudinem operandi. Unde per Ezechielem Dominus ait: Confortavi brachia regis Babylonis, et brachia Pharaonis regis Ægypti confregi. Et in me cogitaverunt malitiam, male sentiendo de me, vel ex proposito me inhonorando, aut dolendo de hoc quod tam potens sum, quod eorum peccata ulcisci possum, eosque punire.
paras.en: [[7:15|And I have chastised them|Et ego erudivi eos]] [Latin *erudivi*, "I have instructed", as Denis takes it here], sending them Prophets, and adorning them with the natural light of reason, of which we read: [[Ps 4:7|The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us|Signatum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine]]; [[7:15|and strengthened their arms|et confortavi brachia eorum]] in time of battle, so that they prevailed miraculously. Or by the arms are understood the operative powers, namely the practical intellect and the will, and the sensitive appetite: which God strengthens by giving readiness in acting. Hence the Lord says by Ezechiel: [[Ezech 30:24|I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon|Confortavi brachia regis Babylonis]], and [[Ezech 30:24|I will break the arms of Pharao|brachia Pharaonis regis Ægypti confregi]] [Denis has the past, *I have strengthened … I have broken*]. [[7:15|and they have imagined evil against me|Et in me cogitaverunt malitiam]], thinking ill of Me, or dishonouring Me of set purpose, or grieving that I am so mighty that I can avenge their sins and punish them.

paras.t: Reversi sunt, id est a me aversi, et ad cœpta mala reflexi, ut essent absque jugo legis per Moysen datæ, et sine obedientia ac timore nominis mei: sicut de populo Juda Dominus ait apud Jeremiam: A sæculo fregisti jugum meum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam. Quocontra scriptum est in Threnis: Bonum est viro quum portaverit jugum ab adolescentia sua. Qualis erat qui ait: Ut jumentum factus sum apud te, et ego semper tecum. Facti sunt ut arcus dolosus. Arcus dolosus vocatur, qui sagittam reflectit in sagittantem. Sic isti sagittas, id est blasphemias, miserunt contra Deum conservatorem ipsorum, qui tenuit eos sicut sagittans arcum: quæ tamen sagittæ Deo non nocuerunt, sed in ipsos retortæ sunt, et eos interfecerunt, quemadmodum scriptum est, Convertetur dolor ejus in caput ejus, et in verticem ipsius iniquitas ejus descendet.
paras.en: [[7:16|They returned|Reversi sunt]], that is, turned away from Me and bent back to the evils they had begun, [[7:16|that they might be without yoke|ut essent absque jugo]] of the law given through Moses, and without obedience to and fear of My name: as the Lord says of the people of Juda in Jeremias: [[Jer 2:20|Of old time thou hast broken my yoke, thou hast burst my bands, and thou saidst: I will not serve|A sæculo fregisti jugum meum, rupisti vincula mea, et dixisti, Non serviam]]. Against which it is written in the Lamentations: [[Lam 3:27|It is good for a man, when he hath borne the yoke from his youth|Bonum est viro quum portaverit jugum ab adolescentia sua]]. Such was he who said: [[Ps 72:23|I am become as a beast before thee: and I am always with thee|Ut jumentum factus sum apud te, et ego semper tecum]]. [[7:16|they became like a deceitful bow|Facti sunt ut arcus dolosus]]. A bow is called deceitful which turns the arrow back on the archer. So these men shot arrows, that is, blasphemies, against God their preserver, who held them as an archer holds the bow: yet these arrows did not harm God, but were turned back on themselves and killed them, as it is written: [[Ps 7:17|His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown|Convertetur dolor ejus in caput ejus, et in verticem ipsius iniquitas ejus descendet]].

paras.t: Cadent in gladio adversariorum, id est, ab Assyriis occidentur, principes eorum: de quibus jam dictum est, Cœperunt principes furere a vino; a furore linguæ suæ, id est propter insensatos sermones blasphemiæ contra Deum altissimum, et propter ardentia verba ad idolorum honorem prolata. Ista subsannatio eorum, id est, præinducta eorum idololatria atque irrisio Dei, similis est subsannationi seu idololatriæ quam didicerunt et exercuerunt in terra Ægypti, in qua, secundum Hieronymum, Apim ceteraque Ægyptiorum coluerunt portenta. Loquitur autem de eisdem specie, non numero. Hi namque quibus loquebatur Osee, non didicerunt prædicta in Ægypto, sed patres eorum.
paras.en: [[7:16|their princes shall fall by the sword|Cadent in gladio]] of their enemies, that is, they shall be killed by the Assyrians, [[7:16|their princes|principes eorum]]: of whom it was said already: [[7:5|the princes began to be mad with wine|Cœperunt principes furere a vino]]; [[7:16|for the rage of their tongue|a furore linguæ suæ]], that is, for their senseless speeches of blasphemy against God most high, and for the burning words uttered in honour of the idols. [[7:16|This is their derision|Ista subsannatio eorum]], that is, their idolatry and mockery of God described above is like the derision, or idolatry, which they learned and practised [[7:16|in the land of Egypt|in terra Ægypti]], where, according to Jerome, they worshipped Apis and the other monsters of the Egyptians. He speaks of the same in kind, not in number [that is, the same sort of sin, not the very same acts or men]. For those to whom Osee spoke did not learn these things in Egypt, but their fathers did.

paras.t: Postremo, quæ dicta sunt in isto capitulo ab illo loco, Cædam eos secundum auditionem cœtus eorum, multum convenienter aptantur Judæis pro tempore Christi. De illis itaque qui Christo non crediderunt, sed procuraverunt mortem ipsius, aut consenserunt, ait Salvator: Cædam eos, id est, per Romanos puniam eos tempore Titi ac Vespasiani, secundum auditionem cœtus eorum, id est generaliter, secundum quod pene omnes audierunt consilia principum sacerdotum, ita ut postularent sibi Barabbam dari, neque interfici. Unde in Isaia Christus testatur: Dies ultionis in corde meo; calcavi eos in furore meo.
paras.en: Lastly, what is said in this chapter from the place [[7:12|I will strike them as their congregation hath heard|Cædam eos secundum auditionem cœtus eorum]] onward fits the Jews of the time of Christ very well. So of those who did not believe in Christ, but brought about His death or consented to it, the Saviour says: [[7:12|I will strike them|Cædam eos]], that is, I will punish them by the Romans in the time of Titus and Vespasian, [[7:12|as their congregation hath heard|secundum auditionem cœtus eorum]], that is, all together, according as almost all listened to the counsels of the chief priests, so that they asked that Barabbas be given them and not put to death[[Matt 27:21||]][[Matt 27:22||]][[Matt 27:23||]]. Hence Christ bears witness in Isaias: [[Is 63:4|the day of vengeance is in my heart|Dies ultionis in corde meo]]; [[Is 63:3|I have trampled on them in my indignation|calcavi eos in furore meo]].

paras.t: Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me, nolentes doctrinam meam recipere, et dicentes: Nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est. Vastabuntur ab exercitu Romanorum: juxta illud Danielis, Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo; quia prævaricati sunt in me, dicentes, Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram; et, Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem. Unde per Jeremiam loquitur Christus: Prævaricatione prævaricata est in me domus Israel, et domus Juda; negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt, Non est ipse. De hac quoque vastatione dixit Salvator: Circumdabunt te inimici tui undique, et ad terram prosternent te, eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ. Et ego redemi eos. Christus enim omnes redemit, quantum ad sufficientiam; solos vero electos, quantum ad efficientiam; et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia, quando dixerunt, In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmones; et item, Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit.
paras.en: [[7:13|Woe to them, for they have departed from me|Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me]], refusing to receive My teaching, and saying: [[John 9:24|We know that this man is a sinner|Nos scimus quia hic homo peccator est]]. [[7:13|they shall be wasted|Vastabuntur]] by the army of the Romans: according to that of Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|a people, with their leader, that shall come, shall destroy the city, and the sanctuary|Civitatem et sanctuarium dissipabit populus cum duce venturo]]; [[7:13|because they have transgressed against me|quia prævaricati sunt in me]], saying: [[Luke 23:2|We have found this man perverting our nation|Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram]]; and: [[John 19:15|We have no king but Caesar|Non habemus regem nisi Cæsarem]]. Hence Christ speaks by Jeremias: [[Jer 5:11|the house of Israel, and the house of Juda have greatly transgressed against me|Prævaricatione prævaricata est in me domus Israel, et domus Juda]]; [[Jer 5:12|They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he|negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt, Non est ipse]]. Of this wasting too the Saviour said: [[Luke 19:43|thy enemies shall cast a trench about thee and compass thee round and straiten thee on every side|Circumdabunt te inimici tui undique]], [[Luke 19:44|And beat thee flat to the ground|et ad terram prosternent te]], [[Luke 19:44|because thou hast not known the time of thy visitation|eo quod non cognoveris tempus visitationis tuæ]]. [[7:13|and I redeemed them|Et ego redemi eos]]. For Christ redeemed all[[Gal 3:13||]] as to sufficiency, but only the elect as to efficacy [that is, His redemption is enough for all men, but takes effect only in the elect]; [[7:13|and they have spoken lies against me|et ipsi locuti sunt contra me mendacia]], when they said: [[Luke 11:15|He casteth out devils by Beelzebub, the prince of devils|In Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmones]]; and again: [[John 19:7|We have a law; and according to the law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God|Nos legem habemus, et secundum legem debet mori, quia Filium Dei se fecit]].

paras.t: Super triticum et vinum ruminabant. Erant enim Scribæ et Pharisæi vitiis gulæ subjecti, juxta illud, Amant primos recubitus in cœnis. Recesserunt a me, quemadmodum in Matthæo habetur: Abeuntes Pharisæi, fecerunt consilium, ut caperent Jesum in sermone.
paras.en: [[7:14|they have thought upon wheat and wine|Super triticum et vinum ruminabant]]. For the Scribes and Pharisees were given to the vices of gluttony, according to that: [[Matt 23:6|they love the first places at feasts|Amant primos recubitus in cœnis]]. [[7:14|they are departed from me|Recesserunt a me]], as it is said in Matthew: [[Matt 22:15|the Pharisees going, consulted among themselves how to insnare him in his speech|Abeuntes Pharisæi, fecerunt consilium, ut caperent Jesum in sermone]].

paras.t: Et ego erudivi eos, evangelicam sapientiam prædicando, et confortavi brachia eorum, quantum in me fuit, quia proposui eis spem regni cœlestis; et in me cogitaverunt malitiam: prout Matthæus inducit: Congregati sunt principes sacerdotum et seniores populi in atrium principis sacerdotum, et consilium fecerunt, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent. Unde per Jeremiam Christus fatetur: Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva; dedit contra me vocem suam. Hoc est quod ait Psalmista ad regem Messiam in psalmo cujus exordium, Domine, in virtute tua lætabitur rex: Quoniam declinaverunt in te mala, cogitaverunt consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire.
paras.en: [[7:15|And I have chastised them|Et ego erudivi eos]], preaching the wisdom of the Gospel, [[7:15|and strengthened their arms|et confortavi brachia eorum]], as far as lay in Me, for I set before them the hope of the heavenly kingdom; [[7:15|and they have imagined evil against me|et in me cogitaverunt malitiam]]: as Matthew relates: [[Matt 26:3|Then were gathered together the chief priests and ancients of the people, into the court of the high priest|Congregati sunt principes sacerdotum et seniores populi in atrium principis sacerdotum]], [[Matt 26:4|And they consulted together that by subtilty they might apprehend Jesus and put him to death|et consilium fecerunt, ut Jesum dolo tenerent et occiderent]]. Hence Christ confesses by Jeremias: [[Jer 12:8|My inheritance is become to me as a lion in the wood: it hath cried out against me|Facta est mihi hereditas mea quasi leo in silva; dedit contra me vocem suam]]. This is what the Psalmist says to the King Messias in the psalm that begins: *In thy strength, O Lord, the king shall joy*: [[Ps 20:12|For they have intended evils against thee: they have devised counsels which they have not been able to establish|Quoniam declinaverunt in te mala, cogitaverunt consilia quæ non potuerunt stabilire]].

paras.t: Reversi sunt, ut essent absque jugo obsequii Christi et præceptorum consiliorumque ejus. De quo ait: Tollite jugum meum super vos. Videbant enim ambitiosi atque avari Judæi, quod Christus in omnibus humilitatem et paupertatem edocuit: quod non sapuit eis, sed dixerunt: Insanit, quid eum auditis? Facti sunt ut arcus dolosus, jacula blasphemiæ projiciendo in Christum: nam et dolose conati sunt eum capere in sermone. Cadent in gladio Romanorum principes eorum, id est sacerdotes Judaicæ plebis, a furore linguæ suæ, id est propter furiosa blasphemiæ verba adversus Christum prolata. Ista subsannatio eorum in terra Ægypti. Quemadmodum enim subsannaverunt Filium Dei incarnatum in terra promissionis, sic in Ægypto subsannaverunt Deum æternum patres eorum per idololatriam.
paras.en: [[7:16|They returned, that they might be without yoke|Reversi sunt, ut essent absque jugo]] of obedience to Christ and to His precepts and counsels, of which He says: [[Matt 11:29|Take up my yoke upon you|Tollite jugum meum super vos]]. For the ambitious and greedy Jews saw that Christ taught humility and poverty in all things: which was not to their taste, but they said: [[John 10:20|is mad. Why hear you him?|Insanit, quid eum auditis]]? [[7:16|they became like a deceitful bow|Facti sunt ut arcus dolosus]], hurling the darts of blasphemy against Christ: for they also tried craftily to ensnare Him in His speech[[Matt 22:15||]][[Luke 11:54||]][[Luke 20:20||]]. [[7:16|shall fall by the sword|Cadent in gladio]] of the Romans [[7:16|their princes|principes eorum]], that is, the priests of the Jewish people, [[7:16|for the rage of their tongue|a furore linguæ suæ]], that is, for the raging words of blasphemy uttered against Christ. [[7:16|This is their derision in the land of Egypt|Ista subsannatio eorum in terra Ægypti]]. For as they derided the incarnate Son of God in the land of promise, so in Egypt their fathers derided the eternal God by idolatry.

7.title: DECLARATIO MORALIS EJUSDEM CAPITULI SEPTIMI.
7.title_en: Moral explanation of the same seventh chapter.

paras.t: De Israel et Ephraim ac Samaria possumus loqui dupliciter: primo, secundum nominum interpretationem; secundo, quoad conversationis illorum maneriem. Quoniam ergo vita decem tribuum, scilicet Ephraim et Israel, pessima fuit, postquam recesserunt de domo David, quia ex tunc idola coluerunt; ideo per eos significantur quandoque inobedientes Christiani, hæretici, ceterique perversi. Loquendo autem de Israel secundum nominis interpretationem, quæ est, Vir videns Deum, non designat proprie nisi fideles et bonos. Ephraim vero quod interpretatur incrementum, significare potest hoc modo et bonos et malos: secundum quod aliqui crescunt in verbis bonis ac spiritualibus, alii in rebus malis, inutilibus sive superfluis. Verumtamen in præsenti loco Israel et Ephraim accipiuntur in malo, secundum quod populus ille pravissimus erat.
paras.en: Of Israel and Ephraim and Samaria we can speak in two ways: first, according to the interpretation of the names; secondly, as regards the manner of their way of life. Since, then, the life of the ten tribes, namely of Ephraim and Israel, was very wicked after they departed from the house of David, because from that time they worshipped idols, they sometimes signify disobedient Christians, heretics and other perverse men. But speaking of Israel according to the interpretation of the name, which is "a man seeing God", it properly designates only the faithful and the good. Ephraim, however, which is interpreted "increase", can in this way signify both the good and the wicked: inasmuch as some increase in good and spiritual words, others in things that are evil, useless or superfluous. In the present place, however, Israel and Ephraim are taken in a bad sense, inasmuch as that people was most depraved.

paras.t: Est itaque tropologicus intellectus: Quum ego Christus post resurrectionem et Spiritus Sancti missionem, sanare vellem Israel, id est populum Ecclesiæ, christianum sola fide ac nomine, qui fide informi speculantur divina; revelata est iniquitas Ephraim, id est, peccata principum ac prælatorum plebis christianæ eruperunt et propalata sunt. Hi enim dicuntur Ephraim, quasi in temporalibus concrescentes, et quoniam præsident aliis, quemadmodum reges decem tribuum communiter de tribu Ephraim exstiterunt. Et malitia Samariæ. Per Samariam decem tribuum metropolim, figurantur principales in domibus prælatorum ac principum, qui communiter primo adhærent iniquitatibus præsidentium. Hi itaque prælati ac principes mali cum suis domesticis, sæpe impediunt subditorum salutem, dum eos blandimentis, comminationibus, vel exemplis trahunt ad culpam, per quam gratiæ Dei obicem ponunt, ne illustrentur atque curentur. Unde apud Jeremiam legitur: Quia stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt, propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. Summo ergo humillimoque affectu exorandus est Deus, ut præstet bonum prælatum, principemque condignum.
paras.en: The tropological sense, then, is this: [[7:1|When|Quum]] I, Christ, after the resurrection and the sending of the Holy Ghost, [[7:1|would have healed Israel|sanare vellem Israel]], that is, the people of the Church, Christian by faith and name alone, who contemplate divine things with an unformed faith [that is, faith without charity, which does not give life to the soul], [[7:1|the iniquity of Ephraim was discovered|revelata est iniquitas Ephraim]], that is, the sins of the princes and prelates of the Christian people broke out and were made public. For these are called Ephraim, as growing great in temporal things, and because they preside over others, just as the kings of the ten tribes commonly came from the tribe of Ephraim. [[7:1|and the wickedness of Samaria|Et malitia Samariæ]]. By Samaria, the capital of the ten tribes, are figured the chief men in the households of prelates and princes, who are commonly the first to cleave to the iniquities of those who preside. These wicked prelates and princes, then, with their households, often hinder the salvation of their subjects, while by flatteries, threats or examples they draw them into sin, by which they put an obstacle to the grace of God, so that they are not enlightened and healed. Hence we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly, and have not sought the Lord|Quia stulte egerunt pastores, et Dominum non exquisierunt]], therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. God, then, is to be entreated with the deepest and humblest affection to grant a good prelate and a worthy prince.

paras.t: Dum ergo superiores subditorum salutem impediunt, impletur quod subditur: Et fur ingressus est spolians. Per quem intelligi potest diabolus, qui tunc corda ingreditur subditorum, et spiritualibus eos bonis destituit, secundum quod ait Salvator in Evangelio: Venit diabolus, et tollit verbum de corde ipsorum, ne credentes salvi fiant. Hic quoque diabolus est, latrunculus foris, animas strangulans, atque in caliginoso aere habitans, et in omni itinere nostro nobis insidians. Vel nomine furis datur intelligi omnis seductor occultus, simulator et callidus: qui mentem lupinam veste ovina abscondens, multos subvertit, spoliat et occidit, idcirco et latrunculus appellatur. De talibus ait Salvator: Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces. Et revera omnis superior sibi commissos negligens aut subvertens, fur dici potest et latro, de cujus manu sanguis pereuntium quæritur.
paras.en: While, then, superiors hinder the salvation of their subjects, what follows is fulfilled: [[7:1|and the thief is come in to steal|Et fur ingressus est spolians]]. By him may be understood the devil, who then enters the hearts of the subjects and strips them of spiritual goods, according to what the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 8:12|the devil cometh and taketh the word out of their heart, lest believing they should be saved|Venit diabolus, et tollit verbum de corde ipsorum, ne credentes salvi fiant]]. This devil too is [[7:1|the robber is without|latrunculus foris]], strangling souls, dwelling in the dark air, and lying in wait for us on every road we take. Or by the name of thief is meant every hidden seducer, dissembling and crafty, who, hiding a wolfish mind under sheep's clothing, overthrows, despoils and kills many; and for this reason he is also called a robber. Of such the Saviour says: [[Matt 7:15|Beware of false prophets, who come to you in the clothing of sheep, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.|Attendite a falsis prophetis, qui veniunt ad vos in vestimentis ovium, intrinsecus autem sunt lupi rapaces]] And indeed every superior who neglects or overthrows those committed to him may be called a thief and a robber, at whose hand the blood of those who perish is required.

paras.t: Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis, omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum, nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ: id est, ne perversi et impœnitentes dicant se puniri propter antiqua sua vel aliorum peccata, per pœnitentiam vel castigationem deleta; jam nunc quotidie tot nova peccata addunt veteribus, quod recentibus vitiis circumdantur et puniri merentur, nec possunt se excusare. De talibus dicit Apostolus: Impii proficient in pejus; et Psalmista, Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum, transierunt in affectum cordis.
paras.en: [[7:2|And lest they may say in their hearts, that I remember all their wickedness: their own devices now have beset them about|Et ne forte dicant in cordibus suis, omnem malitiam eorum me recordatum, nunc circumdederunt eos adinventiones suæ]]: that is, lest the perverse and impenitent say that they are punished for their own old sins or those of others, which have been blotted out by penance or chastisement, even now they daily add so many new sins to the old that they are beset by fresh vices and deserve to be punished, and cannot excuse themselves. Of such the Apostle says: The wicked [[2 Tim 3:13|shall grow worse and worse|proficient in pejus]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 72:7|Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: they have passed into the affection of the heart.|Prodiit quasi ex adipe iniquitas eorum, transierunt in affectum cordis]]

paras.t: Coram facie mea factæ sunt. Hoc est quod fertur in Psalmo: Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita. Apud Job quoque dicitur: Deus novit hominum vanitatem, et videns iniquitatem, nonne considerat? Maxima nobis est ratio abstinendi a culpa, quod Deo præsente, intuente ac judicante, agimus intus et foris quidquid egerimus. Ideo enim ait vir sanctus: Servavi mandata tua et testimonia tua, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo. Præterea, quam vehementer id pertinet ad omnipotentis Dei irreverentiam, quod amplius humanum quam divinum veremur adspectum; quod Deo attendente audemus cogitare quod coram hominibus non audemus exprimere; quod soli facimus opus Dei negligentius, quam faceremus illud si honesti hominis adesset persona! Semper ergo pensemus ac honoremus præsentiam atque intuitum majestatis divinæ, dicentes ad Creatorem: Meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper.
paras.en: [[7:2|they have been done before my face|Coram facie mea factæ sunt]]. This is what is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:6|my offences are not hidden from thee|Delicta mea a te non sunt abscondita]] [the margin gives Ps. lxxviii, 6; the words are Ps 68:6]. In Job also it is said: God [[Job 11:11|knoweth the vanity of men, and when he seeth iniquity, doth he not consider it?|novit hominum vanitatem, et videns iniquitatem, nonne considerat?]] The greatest reason we have for abstaining from sin is that whatever we do, within and without, we do with God present, looking on and judging. For this is why the holy man says: [[Ps 118:168|I have kept thy commandments and thy testimonies: because all my ways are in thy sight.|Servavi mandata tua et testimonia tua, quia omnes viæ meæ in conspectu tuo.]] Moreover, how gravely it touches on irreverence toward almighty God that we fear the sight of man more than that of God; that with God attending we dare to think what we do not dare to utter before men; that when alone we do the work of God more negligently than we would if a respectable man were present! Let us therefore always weigh and honour the presence and the gaze of the divine majesty, saying to the Creator: [[Ps 18:15|the meditation of my heart always in thy sight|meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper]].

paras.t: In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem, et in mendaciis suis principes. Sic subditi dum majorum suorum impiæ voluntati assentiunt, eorumque actus perversos approbant et sequuntur, lætificant eos. Quemadmodum enim boni prælati ac principes de subditorum profectu præcipue gaudent, dicente Joanne in tertia sua Canonica, Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes; sic præsidentes indigni jucundantur in his qui ipsorum conformantur erroribus seu peccatis.
paras.en: [[7:3|They have made the king glad with their wickedness: and the princes with their lies.|In malitia sua lætificaverunt regem, et in mendaciis suis principes.]] So subjects, when they assent to the impious will of their superiors and approve and follow their perverse acts, make them glad. For just as good prelates and princes rejoice above all in the progress of their subjects, as John says in his third canonical Epistle, [[3 John 1:4|I have no greater grace than this, to hear that my children walk in truth|Majorem horum gratiam non habeo, quam ut audiam filios meos in veritate ambulantes]], so unworthy rulers take delight in those who conform themselves to their errors or sins.

paras.t: Omnes isti inepti præsidentes, sunt adulterantes carnaliter aut spiritualiter. Quo contra dicit Apostolus: Non enim sumus sicut plurimi, adulterantes verbum Dei, sed ex sinceritate. Quasi clibanus succensus a coquente, sic inflammati sunt igne libidinis aliorumque vitiorum. Jam videmus quomodo in clericis regnent carnalia vitia, et qui ad ampliorem obligantur munditiam, turpius inquinantur. Quievit paululum civitas a commixtione, donec fermentaretur totum: id est, populus istis indignis prælatis subjectus, successive infectus est, et primo quasi per blandimenta attractus, donec tandem omnino subversus est. Paulatim enim malum invalescit. Idcirco principiis est obstandum, ne parva scintilla universam silvam incendat. Siquidem quod inolitum fuerit, non faciliter emendatur.
paras.en: [[7:4|They are all|Omnes]] these unfit rulers [[7:4|adulterers|sunt adulterantes]], carnally or spiritually. Against which the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 2:17|For we are not as many, adulterating the word of God: but with sincerity|Non enim sumus sicut plurimi, adulterantes verbum Dei, sed ex sinceritate]]. [[7:4|like an oven heated by the baker|Quasi clibanus succensus a coquente]], so are they inflamed with the fire of lust and of other vices. We see now how carnal vices reign among clerics, and those who are bound to greater purity are the more foully defiled. [[7:4|the city rested a little from the mingling|Quievit paululum civitas a commixtione]], [[7:4|till the whole was leavened|donec fermentaretur totum]]: that is, the people subject to these unworthy prelates was infected little by little, and at first drawn as if by flatteries, until at last it was utterly overthrown. For evil grows strong by degrees. Therefore beginnings must be resisted, lest a small spark set the whole forest ablaze. For what has become ingrained is not easily amended.

paras.t: Dies regis nostri. Solent majores in sæculo isto certos præfigere dies ad vacandum spectaculis, vanitatibus seu conviviis; et in illis diebus plebs illis applaudens, vanaque festa ac impia opera peragens, dicit: Dies regis nostri, id est, iste est dies superioris rectorisque nostri, in quo statuit ista quæ agimus, esse agenda. Cœperunt principes furere, id est igne concupiscentiæ inflammari, usumque rationis amittere, et bestialiter se habere, a vino, in quo est luxuria. Nempe in his qui carnem suam nutriunt delicate, vitia copiosius provocantur, et motus libidinosi exsurgunt, ita ut more furentium, impetum passionum sectentur. Extendit manum suam cum illusoribus: id est, impius dominator et pastor subditis sibi vane applaudentibus cooperatur, consentit et commiscetur.
paras.en: [[7:5|The day of our king|Dies regis nostri]]. The great ones of this world are wont to fix certain days for giving themselves to shows, vanities or banquets; and on those days the common people, applauding them and carrying out vain feasts and impious works, say: [[7:5|The day of our king|Dies regis nostri]], that is, this is the day of our superior and ruler, on which he has decreed that these things which we do are to be done. [[7:5|the princes began to be mad|Cœperunt principes furere]], that is, to be inflamed with the fire of concupiscence, to lose the use of reason and to behave like beasts, [[7:5|with wine|a vino]], [[Eph 5:18|wherein is luxury|in quo est luxuria]]. For in those who nourish their flesh delicately, vices are more abundantly stirred up and lustful motions arise, so that like madmen they follow the onrush of the passions. [[7:5|he stretched out his hand with scorners|Extendit manum suam cum illusoribus]]: that is, the impious lord and shepherd works together with his subjects who vainly applaud him, consents to them and mingles with them.

paras.t: Quia applicuerunt quasi clibanum cor suum, id est, prompto animo consenserunt consilio præsidentis; tota nocte, id est durante vitiorum caligine, dormivit, id est, in voluptate et impia securitate quievit, coquens eos, id est, præsidens subditos igne pravitatis indurans, quia non præest in sollicitudine, neque attendit quam districtam ab eo Christus exigit rationem. Si enim unusquisque nostrum, secundum apostolicum documentum, debeat cum metu, timore ac tremore sui ipsius operari salutem: cum quanto metu et cura oportet prælatum sibi aliisque providere, cui tanto gravius instat periculum, quanto pluribus præest? Sed, heu! hoc multi non ponderant, de quibus Isaias inducit: Speculatores cæci, videntes vana et dormientes.
paras.en: [[7:6|Because they have applied their heart like an oven|Quia applicuerunt quasi clibanum cor suum]], that is, they consented with a ready mind to the counsel of the one who presides; [[7:6|all the night|tota nocte]], that is, while the darkness of vices lasts, [[7:6|he slept|dormivit]], that is, he rested in pleasure and impious security, [[7:6|baking them|coquens eos]], that is, the one who presides hardening his subjects with the fire of depravity, because he does not rule [[Rom 12:8|with carefulness|in sollicitudine]], nor considers how strict an account Christ demands of him. For if each of us, according to the Apostle's teaching, must work out his own salvation with dread, fear and trembling[[Phil 2:12||]], with how much dread and care must a prelate provide for himself and for others, on whom the danger presses the more heavily the more men he rules over? But alas, many do not weigh this; of them Isaias says: [[Is 56:10|His watchmen are all blind|Speculatores cæci]], [[Is 56:10|seeing vain things, sleeping|videntes vana et dormientes]].

paras.t: Omnes calefacti sunt igne vitiorum, et devoraverunt judices suos, id est, frequenter persequuntur eos a quibus juste et caritative reprehenduntur. Non enim amat pestilens corripientem. Omnes reges eorum ceciderunt. Inefficaces namque aliorum rectores toties cadunt, quoties peccant, quia peccatum ruina est a rectitudine rationis, a statu virtutis, ab erectione mentis in Deum.
paras.en: [[7:7|They were all heated|Omnes calefacti sunt]] with the fire of vices, [[7:7|and have devoured their judges|et devoraverunt judices suos]], that is, they often persecute those by whom they are justly and charitably rebuked. For the corrupt man loveth not him that reproveth him. [[7:7|all their kings have fallen|Omnes reges eorum ceciderunt]]. For ineffectual rulers of others fall as often as they sin, since sin is a fall from the rectitude of reason, from the state of virtue, from the uplifting of the mind to God.

paras.t: Ephraim, id est præsidentes indigne, in populis ipse commiscebatur, id est, vulgo assimilantur in vili conversatione (quemadmodum dictum est: Erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos), quum tamen in Isaia dicatur: Princeps ea quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit. Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis, qui non reversatur. Sic omnis impœnitens, qui non excutit se a pulveribus terrenæ affectionis, sed jugiter jacet in uno latere, rebus caducis atque carnalibus inhærendo, est velut subcinericius panis, qui non vertitur in alteram partem. Verum qui audit Apostolum, Quæ sursum sunt quærite; et Joannem, Agite dignos fructus pœnitentiæ: non est hujuscemodi panis sic sordidatus, sed panis mundus, de quo fatur Apostolus: Unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus, omnes qui de uno pane et de uno calice participamus.
paras.en: [[7:8|Ephraim himself|Ephraim]], that is, those who preside unworthily, [[7:8|is mixed among the nations|in populis ipse commiscebatur]], that is, they become like the common people in a base way of life (as it is said: [[Osee 4:9|there shall be like people like priest|Erit sicut populus, sic sacerdos]]), whereas in Isaias it is said: [[Is 32:8|the prince will devise such things as are worthy of a prince|Princeps ea quæ digna sunt principe, cogitabit]]. [[7:8|Ephraim is become as bread baked under the ashes, that is not turned|Ephraim factus est subcinericius panis, qui non reversatur]]. So every impenitent man, who does not shake himself free of the dust of earthly affection but lies continually on one side, cleaving to perishable and carnal things, is like bread baked under the ashes that is not turned over to the other side. But he who hears the Apostle, [[Col 3:1|seek the things that are above|Quæ sursum sunt quærite]], and John, [[Luke 3:8|Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of penance|Agite dignos fructus pœnitentiæ]], is not bread of this kind, so soiled, but clean bread, of which the Apostle speaks: [[1 Cor 10:17|we, being many, are one bread, one body: all that partake of one bread|Unus panis, unum corpus multi sumus, omnes qui de uno pane et de uno calice participamus]] [Denis adds "and of one chalice"].

paras.t: Comederunt alieni robur ejus. Hoc fit, dum subversores et dæmones spiritualium bonorum vigore nos privant, ita ut vitiis tanquam effeminati vincamur, nec hostibus animæ reluctemur. Quo contra monet Apostolus ad Ephesios: Confortamini in Domino et in potentia virtutis ejus; induite armaturam Dei, ut possitis stare adversus insidias diabolo. Jacobus quoque: Resistite (inquit) diabolo, et fugiet a vobis. Et ipse nescivit, id est, hanc suam calamitatem, dejectionem, depauperationem non pensavit, nec doluit. Sic multi paulatim evacuantur ac decidunt, nec attendunt: quia et spiritualia dona faciliter, et interdum imperceptibiliter, amittuntur. Sunt insuper aliqui qui adeo infirmantur, quod ægre ferunt, si eis dicatur quod a pristino fervore dilapsi sunt. Unde in Apocalypsi Dominus loquitur: Quomodo dicis, Quia dives sum, quum sis pauper, cæcus et nudus, miser et miserabilis? Memento itaque unde excideris, et pœnitentiam age. Sed et cani effusi sunt in eo, id est, usque in finem vitæ perstiterunt in malo.
paras.en: [[7:9|Strangers have devoured his strength|Comederunt alieni robur ejus]]. This happens when seducers and demons deprive us of the vigour of spiritual goods, so that we are overcome by vices as if unmanned, and do not fight back against the enemies of the soul. Against this the Apostle warns the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:10|be strengthened in the Lord and in the might of his power|Confortamini in Domino et in potentia virtutis ejus]]; [[Eph 6:11|Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil|induite armaturam Dei, ut possitis stare adversus insidias diabolo]]. James also: [[Jas 4:7|resist|Resistite]] (he says) [[Jas 4:7|the devil: and he will fly from you|diabolo, et fugiet a vobis]]. [[7:9|and he knew it not|Et ipse nescivit]], that is, he did not weigh this calamity of his, his downfall and impoverishment, nor grieve over it. So many are emptied little by little and fall away, and do not notice it: for spiritual gifts are lost easily, and sometimes imperceptibly. There are, moreover, some so weak that they take it ill if they are told that they have fallen away from their former fervour. Hence the Lord says in the Apocalypse: How sayest thou, [[Apoc 3:17|I am rich|dives sum]], when thou art [[Apoc 3:17|poor and blind and naked|pauper, cæcus et nudus]], [[Apoc 3:17|wretched and miserable|miser et miserabilis]]? [[Apoc 2:5|Be mindful therefore from whence thou art fallen: and do penance|Memento itaque unde excideris, et pœnitentiam age]]. [[7:9|yea, grey hairs also are spread about upon him|Sed et cani effusi sunt in eo]], that is, they persisted in evil to the end of their life.

paras.t: Et factus est Ephraim, id est prælati vel in temporalibus fecundati, quasi columba seducta: quia nec propriam, nec gregis sibi commissi damnationem et excæcationem attendunt. Isti invocant humana præsidia, quæ per Ægyptum et Assyrios designantur, sed Dominus apprehendit astutos in astutia eorum. Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me. Æternaliter enim peribunt, nisi pœniteant. Vastantur quoque ab invisibilibus hostibus hæretici, qui Scripturam pervertunt, aut loquuntur contra Christum mendacia.
paras.en: [[7:11|And Ephraim is become|Et factus est Ephraim]], that is, prelates, or those made fruitful in temporal things, [[7:11|as a dove that is decoyed|quasi columba seducta]]: for they do not heed the damnation and blinding either of themselves or of the flock committed to them. These call upon human help, which is signified by Egypt and the Assyrians; but the Lord [[Job 5:13|catcheth the wise in their craftiness|apprehendit astutos in astutia eorum]] [Denis has "the crafty" for "the wise"]. [[7:13|Woe to them, for they have departed from me|Væ eis, quoniam recesserunt a me]]. For they will perish eternally unless they do penance[[Luke 13:5||]]. Heretics too, who pervert Scripture or speak lies against Christ, are wasted by invisible enemies.

paras.t: Super triticum et vinum ruminabant. Hoc competit his qui post dominici corporis et sanguinis sumptionem crapulose viventes, usque ad ructum implentur.
paras.en: [[7:14|they have thought upon wheat and wine|Super triticum et vinum ruminabant]] [ruminabant, literally "they chewed the cud", which Denis takes up with the belching that follows]. This fits those who, after receiving the Lord's body and blood, live in gluttony and are filled until they belch.

paras.t: Postremo, quomodo sequentia beneficia Dei sint Christianis impensa, et qualiter ipsi vitia quæ subduntur, committant, ex dictis facillime patet.
paras.en: Lastly, how the benefits of God that follow have been bestowed on Christians, and how they commit the vices that are added, is very easily seen from what has been said.

8.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS CAPITULI OCTAVI : IN GUTTURE TUO SIT TUBA.
8.title_en: Literal exposition of the eighth chapter: Let there be a trumpet in thy throat.

paras.t: Loquitur insuper Dominus ad Osee: In gutture tuo sit tuba, id est, per guttur tuum vocem tubalem forma clare et alte, prænuntiando quæ dico. Unde in Isaia habetur, Quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam; et in Psalmo, Exsultationes (id est jucundæ laudationes) Dei in gutture eorum. Quid autem clamandum sit, subditur: Quasi aquila, id est quidam similis aquilæ, scilicet Nabuchodonosor, qui propter suam atque suorum rapacitatem et velocitatem, vel ob suæ elationis altitudinem, aut regiam excellentiam, aquila nominatur. De quo Ezechiel scribit: Aquila una grandis magnarum alarum venit ad Libanum. De quo subditur: super domum Domini, id est, veniet super templum Jerusalem, ut destruat illud, pro eo quod transgressi sunt Judæi fœdus meum, id est testamentum quod pepigi cum patribus eorum, quod et promiserunt se observaturos, dicendo ad Moysen: Omnia quæ præcepit Dominus, faciemus et erimus obedientes.
paras.en: The Lord further speaks to Osee: [[8:1|Let there be a trumpet in thy throat|In gutture tuo sit tuba]], that is, through thy throat form a trumpet's voice, clear and loud, foretelling what I say. Hence it is said in Isaias, [[Is 58:1|lift up thy voice like a trumpet|Quasi tuba exalta vocem tuam]]; and in the Psalm, [[Ps 149:6|The high praises|Exsultationes]] (that is, joyful praises) [[Ps 149:6|of God shall be in their mouth|Dei in gutture eorum]] [Denis's Latin has *in gutture*, "in their throat", which is why he cites the verse here; the Douay-Rheims has "mouth"]. What is to be cried out is then added: [[8:1|like an eagle|Quasi aquila]], that is, one like an eagle, namely Nabuchodonosor, who is called an eagle because of his own and his men's rapacity and swiftness, or for the height of his pride, or his royal excellence. Of him Ezechiel writes: [[Ezech 17:3|A large eagle with great wings, long-limbed, full of feathers, and of variety, came to Libanus|Aquila una grandis magnarum alarum venit ad Libanum]]. Of him it is added: [[8:1|upon the house of the Lord|super domum Domini]], that is, he will come upon the temple of Jerusalem to destroy it, [[8:1|because they have transgressed|pro eo quod transgressi sunt]], the Jews, [[8:1|my covenant|fœdus meum]], that is, the testament which I made with their fathers, which they also promised to keep, saying to Moses: [[Ex 24:7|All things that the Lord hath spoken, we will do, we will be obedient|Omnia quæ præcepit Dominus, faciemus et erimus obedientes]].

paras.t: Quidam per fœdus istud, intelligunt pactum quod Sedecias juravit regi Nabuchodonosor, utpote quod ei serviret sub tributo, quod postea rupit: de quo in Ezechiele dicitur, Qui dissolvit pactum, numquid effugiet? Unde et Nabuchodonosor, capto Sedecia, dixit ad eum: Deus tuus, qui odio habet iniquitatem tuam, tradidit te in manus meas. Sed prima expositio aptior est. Nam translatio Septuaginta interpretum sic habet: Pro eo quod transgressi sunt testamentum meum. Et legem meam prævaricati sunt: quia et duæ tribus tempore Manassæ idola coluerunt. Unde nec præcepta moralia, nec judicialia, nec cærimonialia servaverunt.
paras.en: Some understand by this covenant the pact which Sedecias swore to king Nabuchodonosor, namely that he would serve him under tribute, which he afterwards broke[[2 Par 36:13||]]: of which it is said in Ezechiel, [[Ezech 17:15|shall he escape that hath broken the covenant|Qui dissolvit pactum, numquid effugiet?]]? And so Nabuchodonosor, when Sedecias was taken, said to him: Thy God, who hates thy iniquity, has delivered thee into my hands. But the first explanation is more fitting. For the translation of the Seventy interpreters reads thus: Because they have transgressed my testament. [[8:1|and have violated my law|Et legem meam prævaricati sunt]]: for the two tribes also worshipped idols in the time of Manasses[[2 Par 33:9||]]. Hence they kept neither the moral, nor the judicial, nor the ceremonial precepts.

paras.t: Me invocabunt pro liberatione a Chaldæis tempore necessitatis, non ex caritate, sed ex servili timore: Cognovimus te, o Domine Deus, Israel, id est nos populus tuus qui dicimur Israel, quoniam nati de Jacob, qui dictus est Israel. Habuerunt enim isti notitiam quamdam de Deo, videlicet quod eduxit patres eorum de Ægypto.
paras.en: [[8:2|They shall call upon me|Me invocabunt]] for deliverance from the Chaldeans in the time of need, not out of charity but out of servile fear: [[8:2|O my God, we, Israel, know thee|Cognovimus te, o Domine Deus, Israel]] [Denis reads *o Domine Deus*, "O Lord God"], that is, we thy people who are called Israel, since we are born of Jacob, who was called Israel[[Gen 32:28||]]. For these had a certain knowledge of God, namely that he brought their fathers out of Egypt.

paras.t: Deinde Dominus ait: Projecit Israel bonum. Tanquam dicat: Quum non sequamini fidem et opera Jacob, sed cultum legemque Dei spreveritis, non estis digni Israel nuncupari. Unde apud Joannem Christus ait Judæis: Si filii Abrahæ estis, opera Abrahæ facite. Inimicus persequetur eum, id est Chaldæi: quod tempore Sedeciæ constat impletum.
paras.en: Then the Lord says: [[8:3|Israel hath cast off the thing that is good|Projecit Israel bonum]]. As if he said: Since you do not follow the faith and works of Jacob, but have spurned the worship and law of God, you are not worthy to be called Israel. Hence in John Christ says to the Jews: [[John 8:39|If you be the children of Abraham, do the works of Abraham|Si filii Abrahæ estis, opera Abrahæ facite]]. [[8:3|the enemy shall pursue him|Inimicus persequetur eum]], that is, the Chaldeans: which, it is clear, was fulfilled in the time of Sedecias[[4 Kings 25:1||]].

paras.t: Ipsi regnaverunt, et non ex me. Hoc aliqui exponunt de Saul. Unde Hieronymus dicit hic, quod Saul non ex Dei voluntate, sed populi errore factus est rex. Alii vero exponunt de Jeroboam primo decem tribuum rege, et successoribus ejus. Propter quod Beda dicit, quod populus contra Dei voluntatem elegit Jeroboam regem.
paras.en: [[8:4|They have reigned, but not by me|Ipsi regnaverunt, et non ex me]]. Some explain this of Saul. Hence Jerome says here that Saul was made king not by the will of God but by the error of the people. Others explain it of Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes, and his successors. For this reason Bede says that the people chose Jeroboam as king against the will of God.

paras.t: Verumtamen obviare videtur quod primo Regum legitur. Quum enim Samuel fudisset oleum super caput Saul: Ecce, ait, unxit te Dominus super hereditatem suam in principem. Postea, stante Saule in medio populi, locutus est Samuel: Certe videtis quem elegit Dominus, quoniam non est similis illi in omni populo. Iterum scriptum est, quod Saule uncto, immutavit ei Deus cor aliud, et prophetavit; item, quod erat vir electus et bonus, et non erat de filiis Israel melior illo. Denique tertio Regum scriptum est, quemadmodum Dominus per Ahiam prophetam dixit ad Jeroboam: Scindam regnum de manu Salomonis, et dabo tibi decem partes; et iterum, Te autem assumam, et regnabis super omnia quæcumque desiderat anima tua. Proinde quum Roboam filius Salomonis, collecto grandi exercitu, vellet pugnare contra Jeroboam, ut reduceret decem tribus ad se, venit Semeias vir Dei, et Deo jubente locutus est Roboam ac populo: Non bellabitis contra filios Israel; a me enim factum est hoc. Dominus quoque promisit Jeroboam, quod ædificaret sibi domum fidelem, sicut fecit ipsi David, si custodiret mandata ipsius.
paras.en: Yet what is read in the first book of Kings seems to stand against this. For when Samuel had poured oil upon the head of Saul, [[1 Kings 10:1|Behold|Ecce]], he said, [[1 Kings 10:1|the Lord hath anointed thee to be prince over his inheritance|unxit te Deus in principem]]. Afterwards, as Saul stood in the midst of the people, Samuel said: [[1 Kings 10:24|Surely you see him whom the Lord hath chosen, that there is none like him among all the people|Certe videtis quem elegit Dominus, quoniam non est similis illi in omni populo]]. Again it is written that when Saul had been anointed, God changed his heart into another[[1 Kings 10:9||]], and he prophesied[[1 Kings 10:10||]]; and also that he was [[1 Kings 9:2|a choice and goodly man, and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he|vir electus et bonus, et non erat de filiis Israel melior illo]]. Lastly, it is written in the third book of Kings how the Lord said to Jeroboam through the prophet Ahias: [[3 Kings 11:31|I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give thee ten tribes|Scindam regnum de manu Salomonis, et dabo tibi decem partes]] [Denis has *partes*, "parts"]; and again, [[3 Kings 11:37|I will take thee, and thou shalt reign over all that thy soul desireth|Te autem assumam, et regnabis super omnia quæcumque desiderat anima tua]]. Accordingly, when Roboam the son of Solomon had gathered a great army and wished to fight against Jeroboam, to bring the ten tribes back to himself, Semeias the man of God came and, at God's command, said to Roboam and the people: You shall not [[3 Kings 12:24|fight against your brethren, the children of Israel|bellabitis contra filios Israel]]: [[3 Kings 12:24|for this thing is from me|a me enim factum est hoc]]. The Lord also promised Jeroboam that he would build him a faithful house, as he did for David himself, if he kept his commandments[[3 Kings 11:38||]].

paras.t: Quamvis ergo verba Hieronymi et Bedæ non reprobem, securius tamen puto, ut locus iste intelligatur de pessimis successoribus Jeroboam, qui intruserunt se ipsos, vel de Saule atque Jeroboam, pro eo tempore quo regia potestate abusi sunt. Præterea nec dicere audeo, quin Jehu, quem unxit adolescens missus ab Eliseo, Deo volente ad regnum promotus sit; sed postea Deum offendit vitulos adorando. Denique dici non potest, quin Salomon fuerit a Deo electus in regem ac principem, et tamen postea impiissime præfuit, reprobarique meruit: non tamen dico eum damnatum.
paras.en: So although I do not reject the words of Jerome and Bede, I think it safer that this place be understood of the very wicked successors of Jeroboam, who thrust themselves in, or of Saul and Jeroboam for the time in which they abused the royal power. Moreover, I do not dare to say that Jehu, whom the young man sent by Eliseus anointed[[4 Kings 9:1||]][[4 Kings 9:6||]], was not raised to the kingdom by God's will; but afterwards he offended God by worshipping the calves[[4 Kings 10:29||]]. Lastly, it cannot be said that Solomon was not chosen by God as king and prince; and yet afterwards he ruled most impiously and deserved to be rejected: yet I do not say that he was damned.

paras.t: Principes exstiterunt isti jam dicti, et non cognovi, id est, non approbavi principatum eorum de tempore illo quo principabantur injuste. Argentum suum et aurum suum, id est de argento et auro, fecerunt sibi idola, in toto vel in parte aurea sive argentea, vel auro atque argento ornata, sicque divitiis a me concessis dire abusi sunt. Utriusque enim regni populus idola varia fabricavit, quia de duarum tribuum regno dixerat Isaias: Repleta est terra ejus idolis; opus manuum suarum adoraverunt. Ut interirent, id est, per Assyrios caperentur. Hæc dictio, ut, denotat hic concomitantiam, non causalitatem: neque enim idola fecerunt ut perirent, sed formationem idolorum consecutus est eorum interitus, sicut culpam sequitur pœna.
paras.en: [[8:4|they have been princes|Principes exstiterunt]], those just named, [[8:4|and I knew not|et non cognovi]], that is, I did not approve their rule for the time in which they ruled unjustly. [[8:4|of their silver and their gold|Argentum suum et aurum suum]], that is, out of silver and gold, [[8:4|they have made idols to themselves|fecerunt sibi idola]], wholly or partly of gold or silver, or adorned with gold and silver; and so they grievously abused the riches I had granted them. For the people of both kingdoms fashioned various idols, since Isaias had said of the kingdom of the two tribes: [[Is 2:8|Their land also is full of idols: they have adored the work of their own hands|Repleta est terra ejus idolis; opus manuum suarum adoraverunt]]. [[8:4|that they might perish|Ut interirent]], that is, be taken by the Assyrians. The word *ut* ["that", "so that"] here denotes what goes with something, not its cause: for they did not make idols in order to perish, but their ruin followed on the making of idols, as punishment follows guilt.

paras.t: Projectus est, id est destructus ab Assyriis, vitulus tuus, id est duo aurei vituli. Ponit enim singulare pro plurali, quia Assyrii destruxerunt fana vitulorum cum vitulis. Simili modo dicitur in Psalmo: Dixit, et venit locusta, id est locustæ quamplurimæ. O Samaria, id est, regio seu populus decem tribuum. Unde Samaria hoc loco non est nomen specialis urbis, sed regionis, quemadmodum et in Joanne ubi legitur: Venit mulier de Samaria haurire aquam. Illa enim mulier non erat de urbe dicta Samaria, sed de civitate Sichar, quæ alio nomine dicta est Sichem. Denique nullus aureorum vitulorum positus fuit in civitate vocata Samaria, sed unus in Bethel, alter in Dan. Iratus est furor meus in eos, id est contra decem tribus idololatras. Usquequo non poterunt emundari per pœnitentiam ab idololatria ista? quasi dicat: Mirum est quod vitium istud tam indelebiliter eis adhæret.
paras.en: [[8:5|is cast off|Projectus est]], that is, destroyed by the Assyrians, [[8:5|Thy calf|vitulus tuus]], that is, the two golden calves. For he puts the singular for the plural, since the Assyrians destroyed the shrines of the calves together with the calves. In the same way it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 104:34|He spoke, and the locust came|Dixit, et venit locusta]], that is, a great many locusts. [[8:5|O Samaria|O Samaria]], that is, the region or people of the ten tribes. So Samaria in this place is not the name of a particular city but of the region, as also in John, where we read: [[John 4:7|There cometh a woman of Samaria, to draw water|Venit mulier de Samaria haurire aquam]]. For that woman was not from the city called Samaria, but from the city of Sichar[[John 4:5||]], which by another name was called Sichem. Moreover, none of the golden calves was set up in the city called Samaria, but one in Bethel, the other in Dan[[3 Kings 12:29||]]. [[8:5|my wrath is kindled against them|Iratus est furor meus in eos]], that is, against the idolatrous ten tribes. [[8:5|How long will they be incapable of being cleansed|Usquequo non poterunt emundari]] by penance from this idolatry? As if he said: It is a wonder that this vice clings to them so indelibly.

paras.t: Quia ex Israel, id est a Jeroboam Israelita, et populo ejus, et ipse, id est vitulus iste, est, ita quod ab aliis gentibus non sumpserunt culturam vitulorum aureorum, ut Baal et Astaroth a Sidoniis, Chamos a Moabitis, et Moloch ab Ammonitis. Artifex fecit illum vitulum aureum opere sculptorio sive fusorio; et non est deus vitulus ab artifice factus: non enim est animatus vel immortalis, sed res artificialis. De hoc multa dicuntur in libro Sapientiæ. Quoniam in aranearum tela erit vitulus Samariæ, id est, vituli aurei terræ Samariæ dissolventur, quemadmodum tela araneæ dissolvitur vento. Assyrii namque comminuerunt eos, et velut in pulverem redegerunt.
paras.en: [[8:6|For itself also is the invention of Israel|Quia ex Israel]] [the Latin runs: *for from Israel it also is*], that is, from Jeroboam the Israelite and his people; and it, that is, this calf, is from Israel, in that they did not take the worship of the golden calves from other nations, as they took Baal and Astaroth from the Sidonians, Chamos from the Moabites, and Moloch from the Ammonites. [[8:6|a workman made it|Artifex fecit illum]], the golden calf, by carving or by casting; [[8:6|and it is no god|et non est deus]], the calf made by the workman: for it is not alive or immortal, but a thing made by art. Much is said of this in the book of Wisdom[[Wis 13:1||]]. [[8:6|for the calf of Samaria shall be turned to spiders' webs|Quoniam in aranearum tela erit vitulus Samariæ]], that is, the golden calves of the land of Samaria will be dissolved, as a spider's web is dissolved by the wind. For the Assyrians broke them in pieces and reduced them as it were to dust.

paras.t: Quia ventum seminabunt, id est, vana idololatriæ opera exercebunt. Unde de verbis inanibus scriptum est in Job: Numquid finem habebunt verba ventosa? Et turbinem metent, id est, tribulationem et tempestatem captivitatis pro mercede recipient. Opus autem meritorium seu demeritorium, est quasi semen, merces vero est tanquam fructus seu messis. Culmus stans non est in eis. Culmus est stipula portans spicas, secundum quod in Genesi legitur Pharao vidisse septem spicas in culmo uno. Porro, ut Beda testatur, dum semina in terram projecta, vento corrumpuntur, et interiorem perdunt medullam, non possunt producere stipulam, nec stipula portat spicam de cujus granis fiat farina. In populo itaque decem tribuum dicitur non esse culmus stans, quoniam opera solida, fructuosa ac meritoria non habebant, sed ventum seminabant dumtaxat. Germen non faciet farinam, id est, operatio eorum nullam habebit prosperitatem, nec sortietur finem salubrem. Quod si fecerit, id est, si aliquid prosperitatis eis evenerit, alieni comedent eam, id est, in usum Assyriorum redigetur; vel ab eis violabitur et destruetur.
paras.en: [[8:7|For they shall sow wind|Quia ventum seminabunt]], that is, they will perform the empty works of idolatry. Hence of empty words it is written in Job: [[Job 16:3|Shall windy words have no end|Numquid finem habebunt verba ventosa]]? [[8:7|and reap a whirlwind|Et turbinem metent]], that is, they will receive as their wages the tribulation and storm of captivity. Now a work of merit or demerit is as it were the seed, while the reward is like the fruit or harvest. [[8:7|there is no standing stalk in it|Culmus stans non est in eis]] [Denis reads *in eis*, "in them"]. The stalk is the straw that carries the ears, as we read in Genesis that Pharao saw seven ears on one stalk[[Gen 41:22||]]. Further, as Bede testifies, when seeds cast into the ground are spoiled by the wind and lose their inner marrow, they cannot put up a stalk, nor does the stalk carry an ear from whose grains meal can be made. So among the people of the ten tribes there is said to be no standing stalk, since they had no solid, fruitful and meritorious works, but only sowed wind. [[8:7|the bud shall yield no meal|Germen non faciet farinam]], that is, their work will have no prosperity, nor will it come to a wholesome end. [[8:7|and if it should yield|Quod si fecerit]], that is, if any prosperity should come to them, [[8:7|strangers shall eat it|alieni comedent eam]], that is, it will be turned to the use of the Assyrians, or be violated and destroyed by them.

paras.t: Devoratus est Israel, id est ab adversariis pro magna parte occisus. Nunc factus est in nationibus, id est, in proximo est ut translatus de propria terra, inter gentes moretur, quasi vas immundum, ita ut contemptui habeatur, et viliter contrectetur.
paras.en: [[8:8|Israel is swallowed up|Devoratus est Israel]], that is, for the most part slain by his enemies. [[8:8|now is he become among the nations|Nunc factus est in nationibus]], that is, he is close to being carried away from his own land to dwell among the gentiles, [[8:8|like an unclean vessel|quasi vas immundum]], so that he is held in contempt and handled with scorn.

paras.t: Quia ipsi ascenderunt ad Assur. Hoc explanatur dupliciter: primo, quod quondam miserunt legatos ad regem Assyriorum pro auxilio, magis sperantes in humano subsidio quam divino, propter quod meruerunt ab Assyriis postea captivari; secundo, quod ascenderunt ad Assyrios capti atque inviti. Onager solitarius sibi, id est, similis factus est onagro solitudinem diligenti, Ephraim, id est decem tribus: quoniam libertate sibi concessa abusus est. Nam sicut onager in eremo hinc inde vagatur sine jugo, sic decem tribus per diversarum gentium idololatriam vagabantur sine jugo legis divinæ. Onagri per deserta vagando pro refrigerio attrahunt ventum, quemadmodum apud Jeremiam legitur, Onagri steterunt in rupibus, traxerunt ventum quasi dracones: sic isti ventum humanæ defensionis attrahere sunt conati. Munera dederunt decem tribus amatoribus, id est Assyriis, cum quibus pacem amicitiamque habebant tempore Manahem regis Israel.
paras.en: [[8:9|For they are gone up to Assyria|Quia ipsi ascenderunt ad Assur]]. This is explained in two ways: first, that they once sent envoys to the king of the Assyrians for help, hoping more in human aid than in divine, for which they deserved to be taken captive by the Assyrians afterwards; second, that they went up to the Assyrians as captives and against their will. [[8:9|a wild ass alone by himself|Onager solitarius sibi]], that is, like a wild ass that loves solitude has become [[8:9|Ephraim|Ephraim]], that is, the ten tribes: since he abused the freedom granted him. For as the wild ass wanders here and there in the desert without a yoke, so the ten tribes wandered through the idolatry of various nations without the yoke of the divine law. Wild asses wandering through the deserts draw in the wind to cool themselves, as we read in Jeremias, [[Jer 14:6|the wild asses stood upon the rocks, they snuffed up the wind like dragons|Onagri steterunt in rupibus, traxerunt ventum quasi dracones]]: so these tried to draw in the wind of human protection. The ten tribes [[8:9|hath given gifts|Munera dederunt]] [[8:9|to his lovers|amatoribus]], that is, to the Assyrians, with whom they had peace and friendship in the time of Manahem king of Israel[[4 Kings 15:19||]][[4 Kings 15:20||]].

paras.t: Sed et mercede conduxerunt nationes Assyriorum ac Ægyptiorum, ut auxilium sibi impenderent. Unde superius dictum est: Abiit Ephraim ad Assur, et misit ad regem ultorem. Cujus pœna subjungitur: Nunc congregabo eos ad prælium contra nationes ut cadant; vel, Congregabo eos, id est, pariter obsideri faciam eos. Et quiescent paulisper ab onere regis et principum, id est, interim non dabunt tributa regi Assyriorum et principibus ejus, donec capti ab eis, non jam tributa, sed se ipsos exhibeant ad omnem injuriam tolerandam, tanquam in extremam captivitatem perducti.
paras.en: [[8:10|But even though they shall have hired the nations|Sed et mercede conduxerunt nationes]] of the Assyrians and Egyptians, to give them help. Hence it was said above: [[Osee 5:13|Ephraim went to the Assyrian, and sent to the avenging king|Abiit Ephraim ad Assur, et misit ad regem ultorem]]. Its punishment is added: [[8:10|now will I gather them together|Nunc congregabo eos]] for battle against the nations, that they may fall; or, I will gather them, that is, I will have them besieged together. [[8:10|and they shall rest a while from the burden of the king, and the princes|Et quiescent paulisper ab onere regis et principum]], that is, for a time they will not pay tribute to the king of the Assyrians and his princes, until, taken by them, they give no longer tribute but themselves, to bear every injury, as men led into the last captivity.

paras.t: Quia multiplicavit Ephraim altaria ad peccandum. Non enim solummodo coluerunt vitulos in Bethel et Dan, sed in montibus quoque ac locis deliciosis coluerunt gentium deos. Factæ sunt ei aræ in delictum, id est, sacrificando in aris, gravissime deliquerunt.
paras.en: [[8:11|Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sin|Quia multiplicavit Ephraim altaria ad peccandum]]. For they worshipped not only the calves in Bethel and Dan, but on the mountains also and in pleasant places they worshipped the gods of the nations. [[8:11|altars are become to him unto sin|Factæ sunt ei aræ in delictum]], that is, by sacrificing on altars they sinned most grievously.

paras.t: Scribam ei multiplices leges meas. Hoc legi potest dupliciter: Primo negative atque ironice, tanquam dicat Deus omnipotens: Quid prodesset, si leges meas multiplices, id est diversa præcepta legalia per Moysen data, videlicet præcepta moralia, judicialia, ac cærimonialia, iterum eis proponerem, vel alia adderem? Quod enim non obedirent, patet ex hoc quod toties leges has contempserunt. Ideo subditur: quæ velut alienæ computatæ sunt, id est, leges meas quasi ad ipsos non pertinentes atque extraneas abjecerunt. Præcepi enim ut mihi soli servirent, et in Jerusalem immolarent: cujus omnino fecerunt oppositum. Secundo legitur affirmative, eritque sensus: Scribam eis multiplices leges meas, id est, per Prophetas sanctos eas in scriptis redigam, et populo huic eas proponam. Hoc enim fecit Deus per Osee, Amos, etc.
paras.en: [[8:12|I shall write to him my manifold laws|Scribam ei multiplices leges meas]]. This can be read in two ways. First, negatively and ironically, as if almighty God said: What would it profit if I set before them again my manifold laws, that is, the various precepts of the law given through Moses, namely the moral, judicial and ceremonial precepts, or added others? For that they would not obey is plain from their having so often despised these laws. Therefore it is added: [[8:12|which have been accounted as foreign|quæ velut alienæ computatæ sunt]], that is, they cast away my laws as not belonging to them and foreign. For I commanded that they should serve me alone and sacrifice in Jerusalem: and they did the very opposite. Second, it is read affirmatively, and the sense will be: [[8:12|I shall write to him my manifold laws|Scribam eis multiplices leges meas]], that is, I will set them down in writing through the holy Prophets and put them before this people. For God did this through Osee, Amos, etc.

paras.t: Hostias offerent, et immolabunt carnes pecorum occisorum, et comedent hostias istas, vel alia quæque edulia, et Dominus non suscipiet, id est, acceptas seu placitas non habebit, eas. Pro quo sciendum, quod aliqui in decem tribubus colebant non solum falsos deos, sed etiam Deum, quemadmodum quarto Regum scribitur de Samaritanis. Aliqui autem eorum non colebant nisi verum Deum, secundum quod tertio Regum Dominus loquitur ad Eliam: Reliqui mihi in Israel septem millia virorum, quorum genua non sunt curvata ante Baal.
