Aliqui vero eorum non nisi idola coluerunt. De his autem qui Deum verum et idola coluerunt, quibus et tertio Regum ait Elias, Usquequo claudicatis in duas partes? nunc agitur. Horum quippe sacrificia, quamvis Deo oblata, Deo non placuerunt, propter idololatriæ admixtionem. Nemo enim potest duobus dominis servire; et teste Apostolo, Nulla conventio Deo cum idolis.
paras.en: [[8:13|They shall offer victims|Hostias offerent]], [[8:13|they shall sacrifice flesh|et immolabunt carnes]] of slaughtered beasts, [[8:13|and shall eat|et comedent]] these victims, or any other food, [[8:13|and the Lord will not receive|et Dominus non suscipiet]], that is, will not hold as accepted or pleasing, [[8:13|them|eas]]. On this it should be known that some in the ten tribes worshipped not only false gods but also God, as is written in the fourth book of Kings of the Samaritans[[4 Kings 17:33||]][[4 Kings 17:41||]]. Some of them, however, worshipped only the true God, as the Lord says to Elias in the third book of Kings: [[3 Kings 19:18|I will leave me seven thousand men in Israel, whose knees have not been bowed before Baal|Reliqui mihi in Israel septem millia virorum, quorum genua non sunt curvata ante Baal]][[Rom 11:4||]]. And some of them worshipped only idols. Here it is of those who worshipped both the true God and idols, to whom Elias also says in the third book of Kings, [[3 Kings 18:21|How long do you halt between two sides|Usquequo claudicatis in duas partes]]? For their sacrifices, though offered to God, did not please God, because of the admixture of idolatry. For [[Matt 6:24|No man can serve two masters|Nemo enim potest duobus dominis servire]]; and, as the Apostle testifies, there is no agreement of God with idols[[2 Cor 6:15||]][[2 Cor 6:16||]].

paras.t: Nunc recordabitur, id est scire et considerare se demonstrabit Deus, iniquitatis, id est idololatriæ eorum, mox tradendo eos in captivitatem, et visitabit peccata eorum cetera per justa tormenta. Ipsi in Ægyptum convertentur, vel per affectum tempore obsidionis, vel ab Ægyptiis postulando auxilium, vel in servitutem tam vilem ac duram collabendo, sicut erat servitus Ægyptiaca quam perpessi sunt in Ægypto patres eorum. Quidam quoque eorum corporaliter intraverunt Ægyptum, et ibi habitaverunt, secundum Glossam.
paras.en: [[8:13|now will he remember|Nunc recordabitur]], that is, God will show that he knows and considers, [[8:13|their iniquity|iniquitatis]], that is, their idolatry, by soon delivering them into captivity, [[8:13|and will visit their sins|et visitabit peccata eorum]], the rest of them, with just torments. [[8:13|they shall return to Egypt|Ipsi in Ægyptum convertentur]], either in desire in the time of the siege, or by asking help of the Egyptians, or by falling into a servitude as base and hard as was the Egyptian servitude which their fathers suffered in Egypt. Some of them also went bodily into Egypt and dwelt there, according to the Gloss.

paras.t: Et oblitus est Israel factoris sui, id est, decem tribus non habuerunt salutarem atque formatam de Deo creatore suo notitiam, prout Moyses ait: Deum qui te genuit, dereliquisti, et oblitus es Domini creatoris tui. Et ædificavit delubra, id est fana idolis in locis excelsis. Et multiplicavit Judas, id est populus subditus regibus ex semine David, videlicet tribus Juda, Benjamin et Levi, urbes munitas. Captis enim decem tribubus, studuerunt terram suam contra hostes munire per fortalitia et machinas varias, ne similia paterentur, ut patet quarto Regum.
paras.en: [[8:14|And Israel hath forgotten his Maker|Et oblitus est Israel factoris sui]], that is, the ten tribes did not have a saving and formed knowledge [that is, knowledge quickened by charity] of God their creator, as Moses says: [[Deut 32:18|Thou hast forsaken the God that begot thee, and hast forgotten the Lord that created thee|Deum qui te genuit, dereliquisti, et oblitus es Domini creatoris tui]]. [[8:14|and hath built temples|Et ædificavit delubra]], that is, shrines for idols in high places. [[8:14|and Juda hath built many|Et multiplicavit Judas]], that is, the people subject to the kings of the seed of David, namely the tribes of Juda, Benjamin and Levi, [[8:14|fenced cities|urbes munitas]]. For when the ten tribes had been taken, they took pains to fortify their land against their enemies with strongholds and various engines, lest they suffer the like, as is plain from the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 18:13||]][[2 Par 26:15||]][[2 Par 32:5||]] [the margin gives these with "cf."; the engines are in 2 Paralipomenon].

paras.t: Et mittam ignem in civitates ejus, et devorabit ædes illius, id est domos. Hoc Beda et Glossa dicunt impletum tempore Ezechiæ, quando Sennacherib rex Assyriorum venit, et occupavit omnes urbes munitas in Juda, quemadmodum in Isaia et quarto libro Regum habetur. Crudelitas autem et persecutio Sennacherib, nomine ignis designatur: nam quælibet gravis pœna solet per ignem significari. Plenius tamen videtur istud impletum tempore Sedeciæ, quando Chaldæi ipsam Jerusalem ceterasque urbes Juda incenderunt et destruxerunt.
paras.en: [[8:14|and I will send a fire upon his cities|Et mittam ignem in civitates ejus]], [[8:14|and it shall devour the houses thereof|et devorabit ædes illius]], that is, the dwellings. Bede and the Gloss say this was fulfilled in the time of Ezechias, when Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came and seized all the fenced cities in Juda, as is found in Isaias and in the fourth book of Kings[[Is 36:1||]][[4 Kings 18:13||]]. The cruelty and persecution of Sennacherib is signified by the name of fire: for any heavy punishment is commonly signified by fire. Yet this seems to have been more fully fulfilled in the time of Sedecias, when the Chaldeans burned and destroyed Jerusalem itself and the other cities of Juda[[4 Kings 25:1||]].

paras.t: Itaque in principio et fine hujus capituli loquitur Propheta de captivitate regni Juda, in medio autem de decem tribuum captivitate. Ex quo innotescit, verum esse quod dictum est, scilicet quod nunc seorsum, nunc commixtim loquatur de utriusque regni statu et captivitate, quamvis pro majori parte loquatur de tribubus decem.
paras.en: So at the beginning and end of this chapter the Prophet speaks of the captivity of the kingdom of Juda, and in the middle of the captivity of the ten tribes. From this it is clear that what was said is true, namely that he speaks now separately, now together, of the state and captivity of both kingdoms, though for the most part he speaks of the ten tribes.

8.title: De tropologico intellectu ejusdem capituli octavi
8.title_en: On the tropological sense of the same eighth chapter

paras.t: Moraliter, Dominus ait prædicatoribus atque doctoribus: In gutture tuo sit tuba, id est, sonore, evidenter et fiducialiter prædica verbum Dei; ne timeas, sed secure et ordinate argue, obsecra, increpa in omni patientia. Unde per Isaiam Dominus ait: Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion; exalta in fortitudine vocem tuam, qui evangelizas Jerusalem. Hinc in Actibus oravit primitiva Ecclesia: Da servis tuis, Domine, cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum. Christus quoque in Evangelio Jacobum et Joannem nominavit filios tonitrui, propter altisonam ac tubalem prædicationem eorum. Quid autem prædicandum sit, subditur: Quia aquila, id est diabolus, propter altitudinem elationis et naturalis ingenii perspicacitatem aquila appellatus, de quo testatur Abdias: Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila, detraham te, dicit Dominus; venit super domum Domini, id est, corda inobedientium Christianorum intravit ac possidet. Hi enim sunt domus Dei fide informi, et nomine tantum: proprie tamen non sunt domus Dei. Pro eo quod transgressi sunt fœdus meum, id est evangelicam legem. Qui enim Christi mandata transgreditur, a dæmone inhabitari meretur; et nisi pœniteat, ejus tormentis æternaliter subjicietur.
paras.en: Morally, the Lord says to preachers and teachers: [[8:1|Let there be a trumpet in thy throat|In gutture tuo sit tuba]]; that is, [[2 Tim 4:2|Preach the word|prædica verbum]] of God resoundingly, plainly and with confidence; fear not, but securely and in due order [[2 Tim 4:2|reprove, entreat, rebuke in all patience|argue, obsecra, increpa in omni patientia]]. Hence the Lord says through Isaias: [[Is 40:9|Get thee up upon a high mountain, thou that bringest good tidings to Sion: lift up thy voice with strength, thou that bringest good tidings to Jerusalem|Super montem excelsum ascende, tu qui evangelizas Sion; exalta in fortitudine vocem tuam, qui evangelizas Jerusalem]]. Hence in the Acts the early Church prayed: [[Acts 4:29|grant unto thy servants that with all confidence they may speak thy word|Da servis tuis, Domine, cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum]]. Christ too in the Gospel named James and John [[Mark 3:17|sons of thunder|filios tonitrui]], because of their loud and trumpet-like preaching. And what is to be preached is added: For [[8:1|eagle|aquila]], that is, the devil, who is called an eagle for the height of his pride and the keenness of his natural wit, of whom Abdias testifies: [[Abd 1:4|Though thou be exalted as an eagle|Si exaltatus fueris ut aquila]], [[Abd 1:4|thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord|detraham te, dicit Dominus]]; comes [[8:1|upon the house of the Lord|super domum Domini]], that is, has entered and possesses the hearts of disobedient Christians. For these are the house of God by unformed faith [that is, faith without charity, which does not give the soul its life], and in name only; properly, however, they are not the house of God. [[8:1|because they have transgressed my covenant|Pro eo quod transgressi sunt fœdus meum]], that is, the law of the Gospel. For whoever transgresses the commandments of Christ deserves to be inhabited by the demon; and unless he repents, he will be subjected to his torments for ever.

paras.t: Me invocabunt, tempore necessitatis et angustiæ, id est ex servili timore potius quam sincera dilectione: Cognovimus te, Israel: id est, nos qui sumus christiana fide atque Baptismo insigniti, propter quod Israel dicimur, veram de te, o Deus, habemus notitiam. Dicunt enim se nosse Deum, quamvis factis negent: sed isti non merentur exaudiri. Qui enim declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis.
paras.en: [[8:2|They shall call upon me|Me invocabunt]] in the time of need and distress, that is, out of servile fear [that is, fear of punishment rather than love of God] rather than sincere love: [[8:2|we, Israel, know thee|Cognovimus te, Israel]]; that is, we who are marked with the Christian faith and with Baptism, for which we are called Israel, have true knowledge of thee, O God. For [[Tit 1:16|They profess that they know God: but in their works they deny him|Dicunt enim se nosse Deum, quamvis factis negent]]: but such men do not deserve to be heard. For [[Prov 28:9|He that turneth away his ears from hearing the law, his prayer shall be an abomination|Qui enim declinat aurem suam ne audiat legem, oratio ejus erit exsecrabilis]].

paras.t: Projecit Israel bonum, id est, ecclesia malignantium sacramenta et beneficia Christi contemnit, vel non digne honorat, gratiam Dei amittit, christianæ sapientiæ negligit dignitatem; non attendit quod nihil felicius Christiano, cui promissa sunt regna cœlorum. Nempe homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit. Inimicus persequetur eum, id est, diabolus, mundus, et caro tentabit superabitque eum. Qui enim divinæ gratiæ spoliatus est ope, omni vento passionum, omni impetu vitiorum, omni tentatione dejicitur, fiuntque novissima hominis illius pejora prioribus. Quocontra ait vir sanctus: Persequar inimicos meos, et comprehendam illos, et non convertar donec deficiant. De habitante quoque in adjutorio Altissimi scriptum est: Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis. Denique propter peccata populi christiani, Terra sancta hereditas nostra data est hostibus, cultoribus immundissimi canis.
paras.en: [[8:3|Israel hath cast off the thing that is good|Projecit Israel bonum]]; that is, the church of the wicked despises the sacraments and benefits of Christ, or does not honour them worthily, loses the grace of God, neglects the dignity of Christian wisdom; it does not consider that nothing is happier than a Christian, to whom the kingdom of heaven is promised. Truly, [[Ps 48:21|Man when he was in honour did not understand|homo quum in honore esset, non intellexit]] [the margin gives Ps. xlviii, 13 and 21; the words stand in both verses]. [[8:3|the enemy shall pursue him|Inimicus persequetur eum]]; that is, the devil, the world and the flesh will tempt him and overcome him. For he who has been stripped of the help of divine grace is thrown down by every wind of passion, every onset of vice, every temptation, and [[Luke 11:26|the last state of that man becomes worse than the first|novissima hominis illius pejora prioribus]]. Against this a holy man says: [[Ps 17:38|I will pursue after my enemies, and overtake them: and I will not turn again till they are consumed.|Persequar inimicos meos, et comprehendam illos, et non convertar donec deficiant]] Of him also who dwells in the aid of the Most High it is written: [[Ps 90:7|A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand|Cadent a latere tuo mille, et decem millia a dextris tuis]]. Lastly, because of the sins of the Christian people, the Holy Land, our inheritance, has been given to the enemy, to the worshippers of a most unclean dog [that is, the followers of Mahomet].

paras.t: Insuper de indignis et ambitiosis principibus ac prælatis, qui se ipsos intrudunt, vel simoniace promoventur, non secundum voluntatem Dei legitimumque processum, loquitur Christus: Ipsi regnaverunt, et non ex me. Nemo enim digne ac deifice præsidens, assumit sibi honorem, sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron, ut dicitur ad Hebræos. Nam et Christus non semetipsum clarificavit, ut pontifex fieret, sed ait: Qui major est vestrum, sit vester minister; et qui voluerit major inter vos fieri, erit minister vester. Isti non pensant verbum Chrysostomi: Quis est qui desiderat prælationem, nisi qui non timet judicium Dei? Quid namque periculosius, nisi illis præesse, ac Deo pro illis rationem exhibere, pro quorum salute passus est verus Deus Unigenitus Patris? Et si unusquisque scire confiterique debet, quod pro sui ipsius regimine insufficiens sit, quomodo potest velle multis præesse? Principes exstiterunt, et non cognovi, id est per approbationem. Non enim utiliter, juste aut Deo placenter dominantur hominibus, qui se ipsos non subdunt divinis præceptis. De quibus scriptum est: Væ terræ cujus rex puer est, et principes mane comedunt. Quales vero esse debeant principes, Moyses tangit in Deuteronomio: Date, inquit, ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes.
paras.en: Moreover, of unworthy and ambitious princes and prelates, who thrust themselves in or are promoted simoniacally [that is, by buying or selling spiritual office], not according to the will of God and lawful procedure, Christ says: [[8:4|They have reigned, but not by me|Ipsi regnaverunt, et non ex me]]. For no one who presides worthily and in a godly manner takes [[Heb 5:4|the honour to himself|sibi honorem]], [[Heb 5:4|but he that is called by God, as Aaron was|sed qui vocatur a Deo tanquam Aaron]], as is said to the Hebrews. For [[Heb 5:5|Christ also did not glorify himself, that he might be made a high priest|Christus non semetipsum clarificavit, ut pontifex fieret]], but he said: [[Matt 23:11|He that is the greatest among you shall be your servant|Qui major est vestrum, sit vester minister]]; and [[Matt 20:26|whosoever is the greater among you, let him be your minister|qui voluerit major inter vos fieri, erit minister vester]] [Denis joins Matt 23:11 and 20:26, exchanging their endings; the margin also gives Matt. xx, 27]. Such men do not weigh the word of Chrysostom: Who is it that desires to be set over others, but he who does not fear the judgment of God? For what is more perilous than to be over those, and to render account to God for those, for whose salvation the true God, the Only-begotten of the Father, suffered? And if each one ought to know and confess that he is insufficient for the ruling of himself, how can he wish to be over many? [[8:4|they have been princes, and I knew not|Principes exstiterunt, et non cognovi]], that is, by approval. For they who do not subject themselves to the divine precepts do not rule over men profitably, justly or in a way pleasing to God. Of them it is written: [[Eccles 10:16|Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and when the princes eat in the morning|Væ terræ cujus rex puer est, et principes mane comedunt]]. What princes ought to be, Moses touches on in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 1:13|Let me have|Date]], he says, [[Deut 1:13|from among you wise and understanding men, and such whose conversation is approved among your tribes, that I may appoint them your rulers|ex vobis viros sapientes et gnaros, quorum conversatio sit probata in tribubus vestris, et ponam eos vobis principes]].

paras.t: Argentum suum et aurum suum fecerunt sibi idola. Hoc faciunt, qui de thesauris suis ædificant sibi habitacula, seu alia quæque artificialia, pretiosa, curiosa, vana, superflua, concupiscentias oculorum suorum, quæ in pauperum sustentationem piosque usus expendi debuerant. Sed quia per aurum sapientia, per argentum eloquentia designatur, illi de argento et auro suo faciunt sibi idola, qui falsa et frivola documenta inveniunt et proponunt, quibus dicitur: Sapientia et scientia tua decepit te.
paras.en: [[8:4|of their silver and their gold they have made idols to themselves|Argentum suum et aurum suum fecerunt sibi idola]]. This is done by those who out of their treasures build themselves dwellings, or any other works of art, costly, curious, vain, superfluous, the lusts of their eyes, which ought to have been spent on the support of the poor and on pious uses. But since by gold wisdom is signified, and by silver eloquence, those make idols for themselves of their silver and gold who devise and put forward false and frivolous teachings, to whom it is said: [[Is 47:10|Thy wisdom, and, thy knowledge, this hath deceived thee|Sapientia et scientia tua decepit te]].

paras.t: Projectus est vitulus tuus, id est caro lasciviens seu concupiscentia carnalis: quæ tunc projicitur, dum divinitus reprobatur, et in pulverem suum revertitur. Usquequo non poterunt emundari? Hoc Dominus ait, quasi admirans impœnitentiam et multiformem transgressionem Christianorum malorum. Impius namque quum in profundum peccatorum venerit, contemnit. De talibus scriptum est in Jeremia: Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et pardus varietates suas, et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum. Unde rursus per Jeremiam loquitur Spiritus Sanctus: Usquequo morabuntur in te cogitationes noxiæ?
paras.en: [[8:5|Thy calf, O Samaria, is cast off|Projectus est vitulus tuus]], that is, the wanton flesh or carnal concupiscence: which is cast off when it is rejected by God and returns to its dust[[Ps 103:29||]]. [[8:5|How long will they be incapable of being cleansed?|Usquequo non poterunt emundari?]] The Lord says this as though marvelling at the impenitence and manifold transgression of wicked Christians. For [[Prov 18:3|The wicked man, when he is come into the depths of sins, contemneth|Impius namque quum in profundum peccatorum venerit, contemnit]]. Of such it is written in Jeremias: [[Jer 13:23|If the Ethiopian can change his skin, or the leopard his spots: you also may do well, when you have learned evil|Si mutare potest Æthiops pellem suam, et pardus varietates suas, et vos poteritis benefacere, quum didiceritis malum]]. Hence again the Holy Ghost speaks through Jeremias: [[Jer 4:14|how long shall hurtful thoughts abide in thee?|Usquequo morabuntur in te cogitationes noxiæ?]]

paras.t: Ideo autem multi non emundantur, quia ex Israel et ipse est, id est, princeps seu prælatus subditos non dirigens, sed subvertens, non instruens, sed corrumpens, est ex populo christiano: propter quod alii eum amplius imitantur, quam si esset penitus alienus et ethnicus; maxime vero nocet tanquam hostis domesticus. Quoniam in aranearum tela erit vitulus Samariæ: id est, omnis carnalis voluptas, et caro spurcissima subito tanquam tela araneæ resolvetur, putrescet, atque deficiet, juxta illud Sapientiæ: Transierunt omnia tanquam umbra præteriens. Et Isaias ait: Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri; exsiccatum est fœnum, et cecidit flos.
paras.en: And many are not cleansed for this reason, [[8:6|For itself also is the invention of Israel|quia ex Israel et ipse est]] [Denis reads *ex Israel et ipse est* as "he too is of Israel"]; that is, the prince or prelate who does not direct his subjects but overthrows them, does not instruct them but corrupts them, is from the Christian people: for which reason others imitate him more than if he were wholly a stranger and a heathen; and he does the most harm as an enemy of the household. [[8:6|for the calf of Samaria shall be turned to spiders' webs|Quoniam in aranearum tela erit vitulus Samariæ]]: that is, all carnal pleasure and the most filthy flesh will suddenly be dissolved like a spider's web, will rot and will fail, according to that saying of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:9|All those things are passed away like a shadow|Transierunt omnia tanquam umbra]] passing by. And Isaias says: [[Is 40:6|All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field|Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri]]; [[Is 40:7|The grass is withered, and the flower is fallen|exsiccatum est fœnum, et cecidit flos]].

paras.t: Quia ventum seminabunt, id est, opera vana et instabilia exercebunt, quæ Apostolus nominat opera carnis. Unde ait Scriptura: Impius facit opus instabile. Et turbinem metent, id est, pœnam et tribulationem pro præmio sortientur. Quæ enim seminaverit homo, hæc et metet, secundum Apostolum; et qui seminat in carne, de carne et metet corruptionem. Tales utique circumferuntur omni vento doctrinæ, et concupiscentiis serviunt, assimilantur viro stulto qui ædificavit domum suam supra arenam. Seminemus ergo opera virtuosa ac solida, de quibus metamus quietem ac pacem æternam.
paras.en: [[8:7|For they shall sow wind|Quia ventum seminabunt]], that is, they will do vain and unstable works, which the Apostle calls [[Gal 5:19|the works of the flesh|opera carnis]]. Hence Scripture says: [[Prov 11:18|The wicked maketh an unsteady work|Impius facit opus instabile]]. [[8:7|and reap a whirlwind|Et turbinem metent]], that is, they will receive punishment and tribulation for their reward. For [[Gal 6:8|what things a man shall sow, those also shall he reap|Quæ enim seminaverit homo, hæc et metet]], according to the Apostle; and [[Gal 6:8|he that soweth in his flesh of the flesh also shall reap corruption|qui seminat in carne, de carne et metet corruptionem]]. Such men indeed are [[Eph 4:14|carried about with every wind of doctrine|circumferuntur omni vento doctrinæ]], and serve their lusts, and are [[Matt 7:26|like a foolish man that built his house upon the sand|viro stulto qui ædificavit domum suam supra arenam]]. Let us therefore sow virtuous and solid works, from which we may reap rest and eternal peace.

paras.t: Devoratus est Israel. Hoc fit, dum Christianus propria iniquitate occiditur atque consumitur, omne esse spirituale gratificans amittendo, in tantum ut quamvis se putet aliquid esse, tamen nihil sit. Nunc factus est in nationibus, id est conversationi infidelium parificatus per peccata innumera, quasi vas immundum, quum sit plenus sordibus vitiorum.
paras.en: [[8:8|Israel is swallowed up|Devoratus est Israel]]. This happens when a Christian is slain and consumed by his own iniquity, losing all the spiritual being that grace gives, so much so that though he [[Gal 6:3|think himself to be some thing, whereas he is nothing|se putet aliquid esse, tamen nihil sit]]. [[8:8|now is he become among the nations|Nunc factus est in nationibus]], that is, made equal through countless sins to the way of life of unbelievers, [[8:8|like an unclean vessel|quasi vas immundum]], since he is full of the filth of vices.

paras.t: Onager solitarius Ephraim: id est, transgressor legis divinæ superbus, onagro similatur, dum concessa libertate abutens, per omnium vitiorum diverticula vagus progreditur, prout Scriptura disseruit: Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur, et tanquam pullum onagri, se liberum natum putat. Sed utinam simus asinus talis de quo scriptum est in Genesi: Issachar, asinus fortis; vidit requiem quod esset bona, et terram quod optima, et supposuit humerum suum ad portandum. Munera dederunt amatoribus suis. Sic multi dant dona adulatoribus laudatoribusque inanibus, et his a quibus cæco amore amantur, ut delectabilia sua vel beneficia adipiscantur.
paras.en: [[8:9|a wild ass alone by himself|Onager solitarius]] is Ephraim: that is, the proud transgressor of the divine law is likened to a wild ass, when, abusing the liberty granted him, he wanders on through the byways of all the vices, as Scripture has set forth: [[Job 11:12|A vain man is lifted up into pride, and thinketh himself born free like a wild ass's colt|Vir vanus in superbiam erigitur, et tanquam pullum onagri, se liberum natum putat]]. But would that we were such an ass as that of which it is written in Genesis: [[Gen 49:14|Issachar shall be a strong ass|Issachar, asinus fortis]]; [[Gen 49:15|He saw rest that it was good: and the land that it was excellent: and he bowed his shoulder to carry|vidit requiem quod esset bona, et terram quod optima, et supposuit humerum suum ad portandum]]. [[8:9|hath given gifts to his lovers|Munera dederunt amatoribus suis]]. So many give gifts to flatterers and empty praisers, and to those by whom they are loved with a blind love, so as to obtain their pleasures or favours.

paras.t: Nunc congregabo eos, et quiescent paulisper ab onere regis et principum. Sic accidit nobis, quando Christus sub alis misericordiæ suæ nos colligit et defendit. Tunc enim divinæ dulcedinis gustu recreati, ab exterioribus molestiis repausamus, et ab onere ejus de quo ait Salvator: Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras; et Apostolus: Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates. De hujusmodi rege dicitur in Job: Ipse est rex super universos filios superbiæ. Sæpe enim concedit Deus servulis suis sabbatum mentis, ut respirent atque futuræ beatitudinis refectionem prælibent. Hinc enim Christus ait Apostolis: Venite seorsum in desertum locum, et requiescite pusillum.
paras.en: [[8:10|now will I gather them together: and they shall rest a while from the burden of the king, and the princes|Nunc congregabo eos, et quiescent paulisper ab onere regis et principum]]. So it happens to us when Christ gathers us under the wings of his mercy and defends us. For then, refreshed by a taste of the divine sweetness, we rest from outward troubles, and from the burden of him of whom the Saviour says: [[John 12:31|now shall the prince of this world be cast out|Nunc princeps hujus mundi ejicietur foras]]; and the Apostle: [[Eph 6:12|our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers|Non est nobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates]]. Of this king it is said in Job: [[Job 41:25|he is king over all the children of pride|Ipse est rex super universos filios superbiæ]]. For God often grants his little servants a sabbath of the mind, that they may breathe again and have a foretaste of the refreshment of the beatitude to come. For hence Christ says to the Apostles: [[Mark 6:31|Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little|Venite seorsum in desertum locum, et requiescite pusillum]].

paras.t: Multiplicavit Ephraim altaria ad peccandum. Hoc agunt hæretici, sacrificantes extra Ecclesiam. Scribam ei multiplices leges meas. Sic Christus quotidie ad memoriam Christianorum reducit evangelicæ legis præcepta per prædicationes et scripta doctorum, quæ ipsi quasi extranea respuunt.
paras.en: [[8:11|Ephraim hath made many altars to sin|Multiplicavit Ephraim altaria ad peccandum]]. This is done by heretics, who sacrifice outside the Church. [[8:12|I shall write to him my manifold laws|Scribam ei multiplices leges meas]]. So Christ daily brings back to the memory of Christians the precepts of the law of the Gospel through the preaching and writings of the doctors, which they reject as though foreign.

paras.t: Ipsi in Ægyptum convertentur, id est ad vitia et delectationes sæculi hujus: quibus contigit illud veri Proverbii: Canis reversus ad vomitum suum; et, Sus lota in volutabro luti.
paras.en: [[8:13|they shall return to Egypt|Ipsi in Ægyptum convertentur]], that is, to the vices and delights of this world: to whom [[2 Pet 2:22|that of the true proverb has happened|contigit illud veri Proverbii]]: [[2 Pet 2:22|The dog is returned to his vomit|Canis reversus ad vomitum suum]][[Prov 26:11||]]; and: [[2 Pet 2:22|The sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire|Sus lota in volutabro luti]].

9.title: EXPOSITIO LITTERALIS CAPITULI NONI : NOLI LÆTARI, ISRAEL.
9.title_en: Literal exposition of the ninth chapter: Rejoice not, O Israel.

paras.t: Deinceps Propheta redarguit decem tribus. Noli lætari intus in corde, o Israel, id est, decem tribus idololatræ, et noli exsultare, signa interioris lætitiæ foris monstrando, sicut populi, id est ut ceteræ nationes. Quasi dicat : Non habes causam gaudendi, sed multipliciter dolendi atque lugendi, magis quam gentiles, qui Dei notitiam non habuerunt, quibus nec data est lex scripta Mosaica : sicque gravius illis deliquisti, quia ut ait Salvator, Cui multum datum est, multum requiretur ab eo ; et, Servus qui scit voluntatem domini sui, et non facit, plagis vapulabit multis. Porro decem tribus gaudebant se esse similes nationibus aliis per hoc, quod proprios deos colebant. Unde putabant se in pace habituras in terra sua, quemadmodum aliæ gentes in suis provinciis pacifice habitabant ; sed nunc dicitur eis ne hoc putent, quia sicut gravius peccaverunt, sic durius punientur.
paras.en: Next the Prophet rebukes the ten tribes. [[9:1|Rejoice not|Noli lætari]] inwardly in thy heart, [[9:1|O Israel|o Israel]], that is, ye ten idolatrous tribes, and [[9:1|rejoice not|noli exsultare]] [Latin *exsultare*, "exult", which Denis takes of joy shown outwardly; the Douay-Rheims has "rejoice" for both words] by showing outwardly the signs of inward joy, [[9:1|as the nations do|sicut populi]], that is, as the other nations. As if he said: Thou hast no cause for rejoicing, but many causes for grieving and mourning, more than the Gentiles, who had not the knowledge of God, and to whom not even the written law of Moses was given: and so thou hast sinned more grievously than they, because, as the Saviour says, [[Luke 12:48|unto whomsoever much is given, of him much shall be required|Cui multum datum est, multum requiretur ab eo]]; and, [[Luke 12:47|that servant, who knew the will of his lord|Servus qui scit voluntatem domini sui]], [[Luke 12:47|and did not|et non facit]], [[Luke 12:47|shall be beaten with many stripes|plagis vapulabit multis]]. Now the ten tribes rejoiced that they were like the other nations in this, that they worshipped gods of their own. Hence they thought that they would dwell in peace in their land, as the other nations dwelt peaceably in their provinces; but now they are told not to think so, because as they have sinned more grievously, so they shall be punished more harshly.

paras.t: Quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo, id est, per idololatriam recessisti ab eo, quod est gravissimum scelus, et vilior atque ingratior factus es gentibus, quæ Deum nullatenus habuerunt. Dilexisti mercedem super omnes areas tritici, id est, temporalia bona, quæ in horreis reconduntur, videlicet triticum, per quod cetera ad victum pertinentia intelliguntur, amasti tanquam præmium idolatriæ tuæ. Nam pro cultu idolorum putabant sibi a diis suis temporalia condonari, sicut superius fassi sunt : Hæ mercedes meæ, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei.
paras.en: [[9:1|for thou hast committed fornication against thy God|Quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo]], that is, thou hast departed from him through idolatry, which is a most grievous crime, and thou art become viler and more ungrateful than the Gentiles, who never had God at all. [[9:1|thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor|Dilexisti mercedem super omnes areas tritici]], that is, thou hast loved as the reward of thy idolatry the temporal goods which are stored in barns, namely wheat, by which the other things that belong to sustenance are understood. For they thought that temporal goods were granted them by their gods in return for the worship of idols, as they confessed above: [[Osee 2:12|These are my rewards, which my lovers have given me|Hæ mercedes meæ, quas dederunt mihi amatores mei]].

paras.t: Deinde Propheta mutat personam, quasi ad alios loquens : Area et torcular, id est blada et vina, quæ in horreo et torculari locantur, non pascet eos, scilicet decem tribus : vel quia non creverunt, quando tempore Eliæ et Achab non pluit in terra Israel annos tres et menses sex, unde et tunc magna exstitit fames ; postmodum quoque sub Eliseo et filio Achab tanta fuit caristia, quod mulieres comederunt fructum ventris sui, sicut in libro Regum plenius recitatur : vel quia ablata sunt eis, præcipue ab Assyriis. Et vinum mentietur eis materialiter, id est, optatum atque speratum usum vini non consequuntur, vino non nato vel ablato. Sicque vinum fuit eis deceptionis occasio atque materia, propter quod dicitur eis mentiri.
paras.en: Then the Prophet changes the person, as if speaking to others: [[9:2|The floor and the winepress|Area et torcular]], that is, the corn and the wines that are laid up in the barn and the winepress, [[9:2|shall not feed them|non pascet eos]], namely the ten tribes: either because these did not grow, as when in the time of Elias and Achab[[3 Kings 17:1||]] [[Jas 5:17|it rained not|non pluit]] in the land of Israel [[Jas 5:17|for three years and six months|annos tres et menses sex]], so that there was a great famine then too; and afterwards also, under Eliseus and the son of Achab, there was such dearth that women ate the fruit of their own womb[[4 Kings 6:25||]][[4 Kings 6:28||]][[4 Kings 6:29||]], as is told more fully in the book of Kings; or because they were taken from them, chiefly by the Assyrians. [[9:2|and the wine shall deceive them|Et vinum mentietur eis]] materially [that is, as the matter or occasion of their deception, not as one who deceives], that is, they do not obtain the use of wine they wished and hoped for, the wine not being produced or being taken away. And so the wine was to them the occasion and the matter of deception, and for this it is said to deceive them [Latin *mentiri*, literally "to lie"].

paras.t: Non habitabunt in terra Domini, id est in terra quam Deus dedit patribus eorum tempore Josue, sed ab Assyriis capientur ac transferentur. Sicque non fame dumtaxat, sed captivitate quoque puniti sunt. Reversus est Ephraim in Ægyptum corde vel idololatriæ imitatione, ita quod in Ægyptum fugere peroptabant, et idololatriam Ægyptiorum sectabantur ; illorum quoque auxilium desideraverunt, pro quo miserunt in Ægyptum legatos, ut dicitur quarto Regum. Sicut per Israel, ita per Ephraim hoc loco accipiuntur decem tribus. Et in Assyriis, id est in terra Assyriorum translatum, pollutum, id est idolothyta seu idolis immolata, alia quoque cibaria in lege prohibita, comedit.
paras.en: [[9:3|They shall not dwell in the Lord's land|Non habitabunt in terra Domini]], that is, in the land which God gave their fathers in the time of Josue, but they shall be taken and carried away by the Assyrians. And so they were punished not by famine only, but by captivity as well. [[9:3|Ephraim is returned to Egypt|Reversus est Ephraim in Ægyptum]] in heart, or by imitating its idolatry, so that they greatly longed to flee into Egypt, and followed the idolatry of the Egyptians; they also desired their help, and for it they sent messengers into Egypt, as is said in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 17:4||]]. As by Israel, so by Ephraim the ten tribes are understood in this place. [[9:3|among the Assyrians|Et in Assyriis]], that is, carried away into the land of the Assyrians, [[9:3|unclean things|pollutum]], that is, idolothytes or things sacrificed to idols, and other foods forbidden in the law, Ephraim [[9:3|hath eaten|comedit]].

paras.t: Non libabunt Domino vinum in terra Assyriorum, in qua sine altari et templo manebunt ; et non placebunt ei sacrificia eorum, quoniam contra præcepta legis omnia fecerunt, et idolis servierunt, quasi panis lugentium : id est, sacrificia eorum Deo displicuerunt, quia immunda fuerunt, sicut immundus est panis vel cibus lugentium mortuum, qui cibus comeditur in domo in qua jacet defunctus. Omnia enim cibaria quæ erant in domo in qua jacuit mortuus, reddebantur secundum legem polluta. Unde subjungitur : Omnis qui comederit eum, contaminabitur : quia tam cibus quam comestor fiebat immundus. Quod autem sacrificium decem tribuum fuerit Deo inacceptum, subjungitur : quia panis eorum, id est cibus quem offerent, animæ et vitæ corporali ipsorum prodest, quum eo vescuntur, sed Deo non placet pro hostia ; non intrabunt in domum Domini, id est, non ingredientur templum Jerusalem, in quo secundum legem sacrificia fuerunt offerenda.
paras.en: [[9:4|They shall not offer wine to the Lord|Non libabunt Domino vinum]] in the land of the Assyrians, where they shall remain without altar and temple; [[9:4|neither shall they please him|et non placebunt ei]], namely [[9:4|their sacrifices|sacrificia eorum]] [Denis joins these words to the preceding: "nor shall their sacrifices please him"], since they did all things against the precepts of the law, and served idols; [[9:4|like the bread of mourners|quasi panis lugentium]]: that is, their sacrifices displeased God, because they were unclean, as the bread or food of those who mourn a dead man is unclean, the food that is eaten in the house where the dead man lies. For all the foods that were in the house where a dead man lay were made unclean according to the law[[Num 19:14||]]. Hence there is added: [[9:4|all that shall eat it shall be defiled|Omnis qui comederit eum, contaminabitur]]: for both the food and the eater became unclean. And why the sacrifice of the ten tribes was unacceptable to God, he adds: [[9:4|for their bread|quia panis eorum]], that is, the food which they would offer, profits [[9:4|their soul|animæ]] and their bodily life when they feed on it, but does not please God as a victim; [[9:4|it shall not enter into the house of the Lord|non intrabunt in domum Domini]] [Denis reads *intrabunt*, "they shall not enter"], that is, they shall not go into the temple of Jerusalem, in which sacrifices were to be offered according to the law.

paras.t: Quid facietis in die solenni, et in die festivitatis Domini? id est, quia nunc dictum est quod vinum et triticum vobis subtrahentur, et capiemini, nec sacrificia vestra Deo placebunt, quomodo ergo implebitis præceptum legis de observatione diei solennis, in quo debetis coram Deo apparere non vacui, sed cum oblationibus et gaudio cordis ? tanquam dicat : Tantus erit dolor, calamitas, atque penuria vestra, imo et pressura, Assyriis terram vestram intrantibus, quod non poteritis diem solennem Deo debite agere, atque implere implenda.
paras.en: [[9:5|What will you do in the solemn day|Quid facietis in die solenni]], and [[9:5|in the day of the feast of the Lord?|in die festivitatis Domini?]] That is: since it has just been said that wine and wheat shall be taken from you, and that you shall be made captive, and that your sacrifices shall not please God, how then will you fulfil the precept of the law about keeping the solemn day, on which you must appear before God not empty[[Ex 23:15||]][[Ex 34:20||]], but with offerings and gladness of heart? As if he said: So great will be your grief, calamity and want, nay, your distress, when the Assyrians enter your land, that you will not be able to keep the solemn day to God as you ought, and to fulfil what must be fulfilled.

paras.t: Præterea quid facturi sint, subditur : Ecce enim profecti sunt, id est proficiscentur : ponit namque præteritum pro præsenti more prophetico, propter certitudinem prophetiæ ; a vastitate, id est, præ tribulatione imminente fugerunt, qui poterant. Ægyptus congregabit eos, id est, in Ægyptum confugerunt, et ibi colligentur : sicque Ægyptus congregavit eos sicut locus congregat locata. Memphis sepeliet eos, id est, in urbe Ægypti dicta Memphis, quæ olim erat Ægypti metropolis, morientur ac sepelientur. Quidam exponunt hæc de reliquiis duarum tribuum, quæ Godolia occiso, cum Johanan filio Caree, dissuadente Jeremia, sed comitante, intraverunt Ægyptum, et ibi postea a Chaldæis occidebantur pro magna parte.
paras.en: What they will do besides is added next: [[9:6|For behold they are gone|Ecce enim profecti sunt]], that is, they shall set out: for he puts the past for the present in the prophetic manner, because of the certainty of the prophecy; [[9:6|because of destruction|a vastitate]], that is, those who could fled before the tribulation that hung over them. [[9:6|Egypt shall gather them together|Ægyptus congregabit eos]], that is, they fled into Egypt and shall be gathered there: and so Egypt gathered them, as a place gathers the things placed in it. [[9:6|Memphis shall bury them|Memphis sepeliet eos]], that is, they shall die and be buried in the city of Egypt called Memphis, which was once the capital of Egypt. Some expound this of the remnant of the two tribes who, after Godolias had been slain[[Jer 41:18||]], went with Johanan the son of Caree[[Jer 41:17||]][[Jer 43:5||]], Jeremias dissuading them but going with them[[Jer 43:6||]], into Egypt[[Jer 43:7||]], and were afterwards slain there for the most part by the Chaldeans.

paras.t: Desiderabile argentum eorum, id est thesauros quos ipsi amaverunt, vel bona quæ argento comparaverunt, scilicet villas et ornamenta villarum, urtica hereditabit, id est, operiet, ita quod villis destructis, infructuosæ ibi herbæ nascentur, et loca in quibus forsitan pretiosa quæque absconderunt, diu erunt inculta, ita quod spinæ et vepres ibi nascentur ; lappa quoque erit in tabernaculis eorum residuis vel destructis, id est in locis ubi domus aliquando stabant. Per quod designatur captivitatis ac desolationis terræ longa protractio : quod totum referri potest ad terram decem tribuum ac duarum, quia post decem tribuum captivitatem ab Assyriis, itemque post duarum tribuum captivitatem a Chaldæis, manserunt regiones earum diu sine habitatoribus notabiliter multis.
paras.en: [[9:6|their beloved silver|Desiderabile argentum eorum]], that is, the treasures which they loved, or the goods which they bought with silver, namely farms and the furnishings of farms, [[9:6|nettles shall inherit|urtica hereditabit]], that is, shall cover, so that when the farms are destroyed fruitless weeds shall spring up there, and the places where perhaps they hid their precious things shall long lie untilled, so that thorns and briars shall grow there; [[9:6|the bur|lappa]] also [[9:6|shall be in their tabernacles|erit in tabernaculis eorum]], whether left standing or destroyed, that is, in the places where houses once stood. By this is signified the long drawing out of the captivity and of the desolation of the land: all of which can be referred to the land of the ten tribes and to that of the two, because after the captivity of the ten tribes by the Assyrians, and likewise after the captivity of the two tribes by the Chaldeans, their regions long remained without any notable number of inhabitants.

paras.t: Venerunt dies visitationis, venerunt dies tribulationis, id est, tempus afflictionis decem tribuum (in quo quod meruerunt recipient) jam est impletum. Scitote Israel stultum, prophetam insanum, virum spiritualem. Hoc quod ait, Scitote, quidam dicunt esse unam dictionem, et quod in Hebræo sit una dictio. Eritque sensus : Scitote, id est, omnes agnoscite Israel, id est Israelitam, esse stultum, id est sine divinorum notitia, prophetam insanum, id est arrepticium seu diabolico spiritu prophetantem, virum spiritualem, id est maligno spiritu adimpletum. Sic ergo Osee loquitur contra falsos arrepticiosque decem tribuum vates, qui populo prospera promittebant, atque sanctorum Prophetarum verbis contradixerunt : quorum stultitia et insania patuit in captivitate decem tribuum.
paras.en: [[9:7|The days of visitation are come|Venerunt dies visitationis]], [[9:7|the days of repaying are come|venerunt dies tribulationis]] [Denis's text reads *tribulationis*, "of tribulation"; the margin gives the other reading *retributionis*, "of repaying", as in the Vulgate], that is, the time of the affliction of the ten tribes (in which they shall receive what they have deserved) is now fulfilled. [[9:7|know ye, O Israel, that the prophet was foolish, the spiritual man was mad|Scitote Israel stultum, prophetam insanum, virum spiritualem]] [Denis divides these words differently from the Douay-Rheims: literally, "Know ye Israel foolish, the prophet mad, the spiritual man"]. As for his saying *Scitote* ("know ye"), some say that it is one word, and that in the Hebrew it is one word. And the sense will be: [[9:7|know ye|Scitote]], that is, all of you acknowledge that [[9:7|Israel|Israel]], that is, the Israelite, is [[9:7|foolish|stultum]], that is, without knowledge of divine things; that [[9:7|the prophet|prophetam]] is [[9:7|mad|insanum]], that is, possessed, or prophesying by a diabolical spirit; that [[9:7|the spiritual man|virum spiritualem]] is one filled with an evil spirit. So then Osee is speaking against the false and possessed seers of the ten tribes, who promised the people prosperity and contradicted the words of the holy Prophets: and their folly and madness were laid bare in the captivity of the ten tribes.

paras.t: Hieronymus vero exponit, ut Scito te, sint duæ dictiones, innuitque in Hebræo sic esse. Et est sensus : O Israel, id est, Israelita vel plebs Israelitica, quæ me aliosque Prophetas Spiritu Sancto impletos, te increpantes, tibique vera prænuntiantes, dixisti insipientes, insanos, et spiritu malo inflatos, jam nunc scito quod tu ipse sis stultus, id est sine intellectu, propheta insanus, promittendo tibi prospera in futurum, et de proprio corde inaniter vaticinando, et item vir spiritualis, id est spiritualibus revelationibus mendaciter occupatus. Frequenter autem loquitur Scriptura de populo quasi de una persona, quemadmodum Dominus ait in Exodo de filiis Israel : Dimitte filium meum, ut sacrificet mihi in deserto. — Vel sic : Scito te, Israel, stultum, id est, te ipsum cognosce insipientem, mihi non acquiescendo ; agnosce etiam prophetam insanum, id est me quem reputabas insanum (eo modo quo principes dixerunt ad Jehu de adolescente quem miserat Eliseus, Quid venit insanus iste ad te?), et virum spiritualem, id est verum vatem, Spiritu Sancto inspiratum.
paras.en: But Jerome expounds it so that *Scito te* ("know thyself") are two words, and he indicates that it is so in the Hebrew. And the sense is: [[9:7|O Israel|O Israel]], that is, Israelite, or people of Israel, who hast called me and the other Prophets, filled with the Holy Ghost, rebuking thee and foretelling thee the truth, unwise, mad, and puffed up with an evil spirit, know now that thou thyself art foolish, that is, without understanding; a mad prophet, by promising thyself prosperity in the future and prophesying emptily out of thine own heart; and likewise a spiritual man, that is, one falsely busied with spiritual revelations. Now Scripture often speaks of a people as of one person, as the Lord says in Exodus of the children of Israel: [[Ex 4:23|Let my son go|Dimitte filium meum]], [[Ex 5:1|that they may sacrifice to me in the desert|ut sacrificet mihi in deserto]] [Denis joins Ex 4:23, "Let my son go, that he may serve me", with Ex 5:1, "Let my people go, that they may sacrifice to me in the desert"]. Or thus: Know thyself, [[9:7|O Israel|Israel]], to be [[9:7|foolish|stultum]], that is, acknowledge that thou thyself art unwise, in not heeding me; acknowledge also [[9:7|the prophet|prophetam]] to be [[9:7|mad|insanum]], that is, me whom thou didst reckon mad (in the way that the captains said to Jehu of the young man whom Eliseus had sent, [[4 Kings 9:11|why came this madman to thee?|Quid venit insanus iste ad te?]]), and [[9:7|the spiritual man|virum spiritualem]], that is, a true seer, inspired by the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Propter multitudinem iniquitatis tuæ, id est magna et multa, enormia et quasi innumera tua peccata, et multitudo amentiæ tuæ, id est, multiplicata est cordis tui excæcatio atque insania, ita quod incorrigibilis exstitisti, et nec signis, neque sermonibus, nec tormentis potuisti ab idololatria revocari, futura supplicia intueri, sanctisque Prophetis fidem adhibere. Peccata enim cor ipsum obtenebrant ; et quanto anima in vitiis amplius habituatur, tanto difficilius edocetur, et irrationabilior in se ipsa efficitur.
paras.en: [[9:7|for the multitude of thy iniquity|Propter multitudinem iniquitatis tuæ]], that is, for thy great and many, enormous and well-nigh countless sins; [[9:7|and the multitude of thy madness|et multitudo amentiæ]], that is, the blindness and madness of thy heart has been multiplied, so that thou hast become incorrigible, and couldst not be called back from idolatry by signs, nor by words, nor by torments, nor be brought to look upon the punishments to come and to give credence to the holy Prophets. For sins darken the heart itself; and the more the soul is habituated to vices, the harder it is to teach, and the more irrational it is made in itself.

paras.t: Speculator Ephraim cum Deo meo propheta. Verba ista exponuntur dupliciter. Hieronymus enim, Beda et Glossa, exponunt hoc modo : Ephraim, id est Jeroboam Ephratæus, primus rex decem tribuum, speculator cum Deo meo, id est, a Deo vero et secundum ejus voluntatem constitutus est speculator populi Israel, propheta, id est, quantum ad hoc habuit Prophetæ officium. Nempe ad hoc Deus dedit principes et Prophetas, ut populum delinquentem erigerent, stantes firmarent, et universorum saluti intenderent. Unde Ezechieli Dominus loquitur : Speculatorem te dedi domui Israel. Sic ergo et Jeroboam a Deo factus est rex, ut speculator condignus esset populi sibi commissi ; ipse vero plebem decepit, eam ad idololatriam inducendo. Ideo sequitur : laqueus ruinæ, id est, Jeroboam factus est populo illaqueator, ad ruinam peccati perducens, in omnibus viis, id est universis operibus, ejus, id est populi vel propriis. Ipsius namque opera pessima, erant aliis exempla peccandi, et consiliis suis ac factis erat causa quod populi opera erant perversa. Unde superius dictum est : Laqueus facti estis speculationi, et sicut rete expansum super Thabor. Insania, id est idolum, cujus cultus est summa insania : et ipsum ex humani cordis insania factum est. Sicque vocatur insania, sicut effectus exprimitur nomine suæ causæ. Itaque, Insania ista posita est in domo Dei ejus, id est in Bethel, quæ interpretatur domus Dei. Unum enim aureorum vitulorum posuit in Bethel, alium in Dan. Vel, In domo Dei ejus, id est in populo decem tribuum, qui adhuc erat domus synagogaque Dei, quando Jeroboam fecit ac posuit vitulos in finibus populi hujus.
paras.en: [[9:8|The watchman of Ephraim was with my God|Speculator Ephraim cum Deo meo]] [[9:8|the prophet|propheta]]. These words are expounded in two ways. For Jerome, Bede and the Gloss expound them thus: [[9:8|Ephraim|Ephraim]], that is, Jeroboam the Ephrathite, the first king of the ten tribes, [[9:8|watchman|speculator]] [[9:8|with my God|cum Deo meo]], that is, he was appointed watchman of the people of Israel by the true God and according to his will; [[9:8|the prophet|propheta]], that is, in this respect he had the office of a Prophet. For God gave princes and Prophets for this end, that they might raise up the people when it fell, strengthen those who stood, and attend to the salvation of all. Hence the Lord says to Ezechiel: [[Ezech 3:17|I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel|Speculatorem te dedi domui Israel]]. So then Jeroboam too was made king by God, to be a worthy watchman of the people entrusted to him; but he deceived the people, leading it into idolatry[[3 Kings 12:28||]]. Therefore there follows: [[9:8|a snare of ruin|laqueus ruinæ]], that is, Jeroboam [[9:8|is become|factus est]] an ensnarer to the people, leading them to the ruin of sin, [[9:8|upon all|in omnibus]] [[9:8|ways|viis]] [the print reads *in omnibus viis*, "in all the ways"; the margin gives the other reading *super omnes vias*, as in the Vulgate], that is, in all the works, [[9:8|his|ejus]], that is, of the people, or his own. For his most wicked works were examples of sin to others, and by his counsels and deeds he was the cause that the works of the people were perverse. Hence it was said above: [[Osee 5:1|you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over|Laqueus facti estis speculationi]], and as [[Osee 5:1|a net spread upon Thabor|rete expansum super Thabor]]. [[9:8|madness|Insania]], that is, the idol, whose worship is the height of madness: and the idol itself was made out of the madness of the human heart. And so it is called madness, as an effect is expressed by the name of its cause. So then, this [[9:8|madness|Insania]] is set [[9:8|in the house of his God|in domo Dei ejus]], that is, in Bethel, which is interpreted "the house of God". For he set one of the golden calves in Bethel, the other in Dan[[3 Kings 12:29||]]. Or, [[9:8|in the house of his God|In domo Dei ejus]], that is, in the people of the ten tribes, which was still the house and synagogue of God when Jeroboam made the calves and set them up in the borders of this people.

paras.t: Alii satis probabiliter exponunt sic : Speculator Ephraim, id est custos et annuntiator populi Ephratæi seu decem tribuum, cum Deo meo, id est secundum revelationem et voluntatem divinam, vel loquens cum Deo, est propheta verus ac spiritualis. Tanquam dicat : Veros Prophetas dedit Deus populo huic, qui sunt veri speculatores ejus, annuntiando quæ vera sunt, et saluti ejus sollicite intendendo. Unde Isaias loquitur de se ipso : Super speculam Domini ego sum stans jugiter per diem. Et Habacuc ait : Super custodiam meam stabo. Laqueus ruinæ factus est Propheta talis populo Israel, non directe, sed occasionaliter, super omnes vias ejus, id est in omni actione populi. Decem enim tribus prædicationem sanctorum Prophetarum non solum spreverunt, sed insuper insidiabantur eis usque ad mortem, ita quod bona facta et sancta verba Prophetarum, erant eis occasio magnæ culpæ, laqueusque ruinæ : ex sua enim malitia inde scandalizabantur, unde debuerant emendari. Hinc et Apostolus ait : Christi bonus odor sumus in omni loco : aliis quidem odor vitæ in vitam, aliis odor mortis in mortem. Insania in domo Dei ejus. Per domum Dei, intelligunt templum Dei in Jerusalem : in quo fuit insania, quia et duæ tribus insanissima opera ibi fecerunt, Zachariam filium Joiadæ lapidando, et idola venerando tempore Joas et Achaz.
paras.en: Others expound it, quite probably, thus: [[9:8|The watchman of Ephraim|Speculator Ephraim]], that is, the guardian and herald of the Ephrathite people, or of the ten tribes, [[9:8|with my God|cum Deo meo]], that is, according to the divine revelation and will, or speaking with God, is a true and spiritual [[9:8|prophet|propheta]]. As if he said: God has given this people true Prophets, who are its true watchmen, announcing what is true and attending carefully to its salvation. Hence Isaias says of himself: [[Is 21:8|I am upon the watchtower of the Lord, standing continually by day|Super speculam Domini ego sum stans jugiter per diem]]. And Habacuc says: [[Hab 2:1|I will stand upon my watch|Super custodiam meam stabo]]. Such a Prophet [[9:8|is become|factus est]] [[9:8|a snare of ruin|Laqueus ruinæ]] to the people of Israel, not directly but by occasion, [[9:8|upon all his ways|super omnes vias ejus]], that is, in every action of the people. For the ten tribes not only spurned the preaching of the holy Prophets, but even lay in wait for them to the death, so that the good deeds and holy words of the Prophets were to them an occasion of great guilt and a snare of ruin: for out of their own malice they took scandal at the very thing by which they ought to have been amended. Hence the Apostle too says: [[2 Cor 2:15|we are the good odour of Christ|Christi bonus odor sumus]] in every place [these last words are from 2 Cor 2:14]: to some indeed [[2 Cor 2:16|the odour of life unto life|odor vitæ in vitam]], to others [[2 Cor 2:16|the odour of death unto death|odor mortis in mortem]]. [[9:8|madness is in the house of his God|Insania in domo Dei ejus]]. By the house of God they understand the temple of God in Jerusalem: in which there was madness, because the two tribes also did most mad deeds there, stoning Zacharias the son of Joiada[[2 Par 24:21||]], and worshipping idols in the time of Joas[[2 Par 24:18||]] and of Achaz[[2 Par 28:1||]][[4 Kings 16:1||]].

paras.t: Profunde, id est ex deliberatione, enormiter et animo obstinato, peccaverunt decem tribus, sicut in diebus Gabaa : id est, quemadmodum peccaverunt filii Benjamin tempore judicum, vexantes concubinam Levitæ incredibili libidine usque ad necem : de quo facto nec pœnituerunt veraciter, sicut nec decem tribus de idololatria sua. Recordabitur iniquitates eorum. Et quid sit hoc, exponit subdendo : et visitabit, id est ulciscetur, peccata eorum : hoc est, Deus qui diu patientissime distulit pœnam, ita quod quasi oblitus videbatur eorum facinora, ostendet se intueri ac detestari crimina ista, tradendo decem tribus in manus Assyriorum.
paras.en: [[9:9|deeply|Profunde]], that is, deliberately, enormously and with obstinate mind, the ten tribes [[9:9|have sinned|peccaverunt]], [[9:9|as in the days of Gabaa|sicut in diebus Gabaa]]: that is, as the sons of Benjamin sinned in the time of the judges, abusing the Levite's concubine with incredible lust even to her death[[Judg 19:25||]]: a deed of which they did not truly repent, as neither did the ten tribes of their idolatry. [[9:9|he will remember their iniquity|Recordabitur iniquitates eorum]]. And what this means he explains by adding: [[9:9|and will visit|et visitabit]], that is, will avenge, [[9:9|their sin|peccata eorum]]: that is, God, who long and most patiently put off the punishment, so that he seemed as it were to have forgotten their misdeeds, will show that he beholds and detests these crimes, by delivering the ten tribes into the hands of the Assyrians.

paras.t: Quasi uvas in deserto inveni Israel : id est, universo pene mundo ad idololatriam declinante, inveni, non utique a casu, sed clementer electum, et gratiose quæsitum, atque ex Ægypto deductum : reperi duodecim tribus Israel in deserto solitudinis quo ambulabant, quasi uvas, id est ceteris gentibus pretiosiores, uberiores, et Deo familiares : quemadmodum in Deuteronomio inducitur : Invenit eum in terra deserta, in loco horroris et vastæ solitudinis. Quasi prima poma, id est primitivos fructus, ficulneæ, seu ficus primi temporis : ita quod sicut hujusmodi poma sunt delectabiliora, meliora, et avidius colliguntur, sic populus Israel fuit dilectus et præelectus populus Dei et germen ipsius, quemadmodum asserit Isaias : Vir Juda germen delectabile ejus. Hinc in Deuteronomio Moyses dixerat populo isti : Te elegit Dominus Deus tuus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram. In cacumine ejus, id est in principio, vel altiori gratiæ statu, seu originali propagine populi hujus, qui per ficulneam designatur, vidi, id est, misericorditer cognovi, patres eorum, Abraham, Isaac et Jacob, qui fuerunt principium propagationis plebis istius, et posteris suis per gratiam altiores. Si enim totus populus Judæorum per modum arboris consideretur et velut una progenies, præfati Patriarchæ stabunt in vertice, quorum meritis et posteris misertus est Deus. Propter quod in Deuteronomio legitur : En Domini Dei tui cœlum est et cœli cœlorum, terra et omnia quæ in eis sunt ; et tamen patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus et amavit eos, elegitque semen eorum post eos.
paras.en: [[9:10|I found Israel like grapes in the desert|Quasi uvas in deserto inveni Israel]]: that is, when almost the whole world was turning aside to idolatry, I found, not indeed by chance, but as one mercifully chosen, graciously sought, and led out of Egypt, I came upon the twelve tribes of Israel in the desert of the wilderness through which they were walking, like grapes, that is, more precious than the other nations, more fruitful, and familiar to God: as is set forth in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:10|He found him in a desert land, in a place of horror, and of vast wilderness|Invenit eum in terra deserta, in loco horroris et vastæ solitudinis]]. [[9:10|like the firstfruits|Quasi prima poma]], that is, the first fruits of the fig tree, or figs of the early season: so that, as such fruits are more delightful and better, and are gathered more eagerly, so the people of Israel was the beloved and chosen people of God and his plant, as Isaias asserts: [[Is 5:7|the man of Juda, his pleasant plant|Vir Juda germen delectabile ejus]]. Hence Moses had said to this people in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 7:6|The Lord thy God hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus Deus tuus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]]. [[9:10|in the top thereof|In cacumine ejus]], that is, in the beginning, or in the higher state of grace, or in the first stock of this people, which is signified by the fig tree, [[9:10|I saw|vidi]], that is, I mercifully knew, [[9:10|their fathers|patres eorum]], Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who were the beginning of the propagation of this people, and stood higher than their descendants by grace. For if the whole people of the Jews be considered after the manner of a tree, and as one progeny, the aforesaid Patriarchs will stand at the top; and for their merits God has had mercy on their descendants also. For this reason we read in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 10:14|Behold heaven is the Lord's thy God, and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all things that are therein|En Domini Dei tui cœlum est et cœli cœlorum, terra et omnia quæ in eis sunt]]; [[Deut 10:15|And yet the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers, and loved them and chose their seed after them|et tamen patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus et amavit eos, elegitque semen eorum post eos]].

paras.t: Ipsi autem intraverunt ad Beelphegor, id est ad cultum idoli sic vocati, quod erat Deus Moabitarum : quando videlicet ad consilium Balaam missæ sunt mulieres Madianitæ, quæ facerent filios Israel secum peccare, et deum suum, videlicet Beelphegor, adorare, quemadmodum in Numeris habetur. Et abalienati sunt, id est a Deo per idololatriam alieni effecti, quidam eorum, non omnes, in confusione, id est in confusibili ac inordinatissima veneratione Beelphegor : tuncque corporaliter fornicabantur cum prædictis mulieribus, edebantque de sacrificiis idoli Phogor, juxta illud Psalmi, Et initiati sunt Beelphegor, et comederunt sacrificia mortuorum. Et abominabiles facti sunt, sicut ea quæ dilexerunt, id est idola quæ coluerunt. Nam sicut idola naturali vita corporalique sensu carent, dicente Psalmista, Oculos habent, et non videbunt, etc. ; sic ipsi vita gratiæ et spirituali sensu privati sunt. Unde ait Scriptura : Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea, et omnes qui confidunt in eis.
paras.en: [[9:10|but they went in to Beelphegor|Ipsi autem intraverunt ad Beelphegor]], that is, to the worship of the idol so called, which was the god of the Moabites: namely when, at the counsel of Balaam[[Num 31:16||]], the Madianite women were sent to make the children of Israel sin with them and adore their god, Beelphegor, as is related in Numbers[[Num 25:1||]][[Num 25:2||]][[Num 25:3||]]. [[9:10|and alienated themselves|Et abalienati sunt]], that is, were made strangers to God through idolatry (some of them, not all), [[9:10|to that confusion|in confusione]], that is, in the shameful and most disordered worship of Beelphegor: and then they committed fornication in the body with the said women, and ate of the sacrifices of the idol Phogor, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 105:28|They also were initiated to Beelphegor: and ate the sacrifices of the dead|Et initiati sunt Beelphegor, et comederunt sacrificia mortuorum]]. [[9:10|and became abominable, as those things were, which they loved|Et abominabiles facti sunt, sicut ea quæ dilexerunt]], that is, the idols which they worshipped. For as the idols lack natural life and bodily sense, as the Psalmist says, [[Ps 113:13|they have eyes and see not|Oculos habent, et non videbunt]], etc., so they were deprived of the life of grace and of spiritual sense. Hence Scripture says: [[Ps 113:16|Let them that make them become like unto them: and all such as trust in them|Similes illis fiant qui faciunt ea, et omnes qui confidunt in eis]] [the margin gives Ps. cxiii, 5 and 8 "according to the Hebrew"; in the Vulgate these are Ps 113:13 and 16].

paras.t: Ephraim, id est populus decem tribuum, quasi avis avolavit, id est, a propria terra velociter ductus est per captivitatem in terram Assyriorum. Ponit autem præteritum pro futuro. Gloria eorum a partu, et ab utero, et a conceptu. Hoc dupliciter legitur. Primo sic : Gloria eorum, id est gloriatio decem tribuum, fuit a partu, id est de hoc quod multos procreaverint filios, quorum procreatio, per partum, uterum et conceptum significatur : sicque jactabant se quod populum regni Juda multitudine vincerent, feminasque fecundas haberent. Secundo sic : Gloria eorum, id est, gloriatio eorum etiam avolavit a partu, etc., id est a filiis ipsorum, ita quod filii quoque destituti sunt divinæ protectionis auxilio, et ab hostibus capti.
paras.en: [[9:11|Ephraim|Ephraim]], that is, the people of the ten tribes, [[9:11|like bird|quasi avis]] [[9:11|hath flown away|avolavit]], that is, has been swiftly carried off from his own land by captivity into the land of the Assyrians. Now he puts the past for the future. [[9:11|their glory|Gloria eorum]] [[9:11|from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception|a partu, et ab utero, et a conceptu]]. This is read in two ways. First thus: [[9:11|their glory|Gloria eorum]], that is, the boasting of the ten tribes, was [[9:11|from the birth|a partu]], that is, from their having begotten many sons, the begetting of whom is signified by birth, womb and conception: and so they boasted that they surpassed the people of the kingdom of Juda in numbers, and had fruitful women. Secondly thus: [[9:11|their glory|Gloria eorum]], that is, their boasting, also [[9:11|hath flown away|avolavit]] [[9:11|from the birth|a partu]], etc., that is, from their sons, so that their sons too were deprived of the help of the divine protection, and taken by their enemies.

paras.t: Quod et si enutrierint filios suos, id est, quamvis eos ad incrementum perduxerint, absque liberis eos faciam in hominibus, id est, filios eorum ab Assyriis permittam interfici. Quidam autem referunt ista ad pressuram et calamitatem Israel quam ab Hazaele rege Syriæ passi sunt, qui eos dirissime devastavit, ut dicitur quarto Regum.
paras.en: [[9:12|And though they should bring up their children|Quod et si enutrierint filios suos]], that is, although they rear them to their full growth, [[9:12|I will make them without children among men|absque liberis eos faciam in hominibus]], that is, I will let their sons be slain by the Assyrians. Some, however, refer this to the distress and calamity which Israel suffered from Hazael king of Syria, who laid them waste most cruelly, as is said in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 10:32||]][[4 Kings 10:33||]].

paras.t: Sed et væ eis quum recessero ab eis. Huic loco paululum immorari oportet. Dicunt enim frater Raimundus, in lingua Hebræa multum peritus, et Lyra, quod locus iste sit unus de punctis veteris Testamenti, a Judæis incredulis post Christi adventum corruptis. Unde secundum eos, vera littera hæc est : Quia etiam væ eis, incarnatio mea de eis. Probationem hujus prosequitur Lyra. Exponunt ergo hanc partem de populo Juda a Romanis vastato, ita quod Osee ex occasione captivitatis decem tribuum, occasionaliter loquitur de destructione Judæorum a Romanis, eo quod Filium Dei ex ipsis incarnatum abjecerunt. Ait ergo Unigenitus Dei per Prophetam : Væ eis, id est, temporalis captivitatis afflictio, atque æternæ damnationis illatio, instat Judæis ; incarnatio mea de eis, id est, ex Virgine de eorum stirpe progenita, humanam carnem assumpsi. Huic autem assertioni concordat, quod translatio Septuaginta interpretum ac Theodotionis, sic continet : Sed et væ eis est, caro mea ex eis. Ex quibus arguitur, quod Christus sit Deus et homo in unitate Personæ.
paras.en: [[9:12|yea, and woe to them, when I shall depart from them|Sed et væ eis quum recessero ab eis]]. We must dwell a little on this place. For Brother Raymund [Raymund Martini, the Dominican author of the *Pugio fidei*], who was very skilled in the Hebrew tongue, and Lyra say that this place is one of the points of the Old Testament corrupted by the unbelieving Jews after the coming of Christ. Hence according to them the true letter is this: "For woe also to them, my incarnation is from them." Lyra goes on to prove this. They expound this part, then, of the people of Juda laid waste by the Romans, so that Osee, taking occasion from the captivity of the ten tribes, speaks incidentally of the destruction of the Jews by the Romans, because they rejected the Son of God who had become incarnate from among them. The Only-begotten of God, then, says through the Prophet: "Woe to them", that is, the affliction of temporal captivity and the infliction of eternal damnation hang over the Jews; "my incarnation is from them", that is, I took human flesh from the Virgin born of their stock. And with this assertion agrees the fact that the translation of the Seventy interpreters, and that of Theodotion, read thus: "Yea, and woe to them; my flesh is from them." From these words it is argued that Christ is God and man in unity of Person.

paras.t: Verum, ut recitat Lyra, Rabbi Salomon adinvenit quamdam solutionem ad hæc, dicens quod in Hebræo scriptum sit : Væ eis quum recessero ab eis. Hieronymus quoque hoc dicit. Sed ad hoc respondet Lyra, quod littera ista corrupta fuit antequam Hieronymus transtulit. — Porro Hieronymus et alii communiter exponunt hæc de decem tribubus, ut sit sensus : Væ eis quum recessero ab eis, id est, quum auxilium meum eis subtraxero, et adversariis suis ipsos tradidero : imo æternum væ eis, dum Deus gratiam in præsenti, et gloriam in futuro eis abstraxit.
paras.en: But, as Lyra relates, Rabbi Salomon devised a certain answer to this, saying that in the Hebrew it is written: "Woe to them when I shall depart from them." Jerome too says this. But Lyra replies to this that this letter had been corrupted before Jerome made his translation. Further, Jerome and others commonly expound these words of the ten tribes, so that the sense is: [[9:12|woe to them, when I shall depart from them|Væ eis quum recessero ab eis]], that is, when I have withdrawn my help from them and delivered them to their adversaries: nay, eternal woe to them, since God withdrew from them grace in the present and glory in the future.

paras.t: Ephraim, ut vidi, Tyrus erat : id est, olim populus decem tribuum fuit tantæ multitudinis, abundantiæ et excellentiæ, quando videlicet Jeroboam primo elegerunt in regem, et nondum idololatriam inciderunt, quod Tyro similes erant ; fundata in pulchritudine, id est, quæ Tyrus posita fuit in maxima excellentia in introitu maris. Quanta enim fuerit gloria Tyri, Ezechiel diffuse prosequitur. Et Ephraim educet ad interfectores, id est Assyrios vel Hazaelem Syriæ regem, filios suos. Non sponte, sed necessitate compulsi, patres cum filiis tradiderunt se hostibus.
paras.en: [[9:13|Ephraim, as I saw, was a Tyre|Ephraim, ut vidi, Tyrus erat]]: that is, the people of the ten tribes was once of such numbers, wealth and excellence, namely when they first chose Jeroboam as king and had not yet fallen into idolatry, that they were like Tyre; [[9:13|founded in beauty|fundata in pulchritudine]], that is, which Tyre was set in the greatest excellence at the entry of the sea. For how great the glory of Tyre was, Ezechiel sets out at length[[Ezech 26:1||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xxvi–xxviii]. [[9:13|and Ephraim shall bring out|Et Ephraim educet]] [[9:13|to the murderer|ad interfectores]] [Denis reads *interfectores*, "to the murderers"; the margin gives the other reading *interfectorem*, "to the murderer", as in the Vulgate], that is, to the Assyrians, or to Hazael king of Syria, [[9:13|his children|filios suos]]. Not of their own will, but compelled by necessity, fathers with their sons gave themselves up to the enemy.

paras.t: Consequenter Propheta precatur vel prænunciat, auferri decem tribubus occasionem superbiæ : jam enim prædictum est, quod de multitudine prolis inaniter gloriabantur. Da eis, Domine, id est, rogo ut des, vel dabis. Propheta enim hæc orat zelo justitiæ et caritatis affectu, ne superbiendo gravius peccent ; vel prænuntiat ea more prophetico. Quid dabis eis ? Cur quærit, nisi ut audientes reddat attentos ? Et respondet : Da eis vulvam sine liberis, id est conjuges infecundas, et ubera arentia, ut nec concipiant, nec lactent infantes. Quod in multis feminis illorum erat impletum : nam et Hazael scidit prægnantes.
paras.en: Next the Prophet prays, or foretells, that the occasion of pride be taken from the ten tribes: for it has already been said that they boasted vainly of the number of their offspring. [[9:14|Give them, O Lord|Da eis, Domine]], that is, I pray that thou give, or, thou wilt give. For the Prophet prays this out of zeal for justice and with the affection of charity, lest by pride they sin more grievously; or he foretells it in the prophetic manner. [[9:14|What wilt thou give them?|Quid dabis eis]] Why does he ask, except to make his hearers attentive? And he answers: [[9:14|Give them a womb without children|Da eis vulvam sine liberis]], that is, barren wives, [[9:14|and dry breasts|et ubera arentia]], so that they may neither conceive nor suckle infants. And this was fulfilled in many of their women: for Hazael too ripped up women with child[[4 Kings 8:12||]].

paras.t: Omnes nequitiæ eorum in Galgal : id est, decem tribus peccata sua multipliciter commiserunt in loco qui dicitur Galgala, ubi Josue populum circumcidit, quievit, et arcam ad tempus reposuit, ut patet in libro Josue. Propter quod filii Israel, propter loci hujus solennitatem coluerunt in eo idola sua, et alia innumerabilia commiserunt facinora. Quia ibi exosos habui eos, non quoad naturam secundum se consideratam, sed ut tot peccatis contaminatam. Odio quippe sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus ; sed impietas secundum se oditur a Deo, impius vero ratione impietatis, qua Deo dissimilis redditur. Similitudo enim causa amoris, et dissimilitudo odii causa est. Non quod in Deo sit rancoris affectus, quum ipse sit essentialiter amor seu caritas ; sed odire asseritur eos quos detestatur et reprobat. Denique constat ex his, quod dum beneficiis Dei abutimur, expediens est ut tollantur a nobis, ne abutendo damnabilius pereamus. Unde de lingua, quæ data est ad laudandum Deum, et ad proferendum utilia, orat Psalmista : Muta fiant labia dolosa. Itaque, Exosos habui eos propter multitudinem adinventionum ipsorum, id est innumera vitia, quæ ex propria cogitatione conceperunt et effectui manciparunt. De domo mea ejiciam eos, id est de terra Israel quam eis concessi, vel domibus et urbibus suis sibi a me collatis.
paras.en: [[9:15|All their wickedness is in Galgal|Omnes nequitiæ eorum in Galgal]]: that is, the ten tribes committed their sins in many ways in the place called Galgala, where Josue circumcised the people[[Jos 5:3||]], rested[[Jos 5:9||]][[Jos 5:10||]], and for a time set down the ark, as appears in the book of Josue. For this reason the children of Israel, because of the sacredness of this place, worshipped their idols in it, and committed countless other crimes. [[9:15|for there I hated them|Quia ibi exosos habui eos]]: not as to their nature considered in itself, but as defiled by so many sins. For [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful alike|Odio quippe sunt Deo impius et impietas ejus]]; but wickedness is hated by God in itself, and the wicked man by reason of the wickedness by which he is made unlike God. For likeness is the cause of love, and unlikeness the cause of hatred. Not that there is in God any feeling of rancour, since he is essentially love or charity; but he is said to hate those whom he detests and rejects. Lastly, it is clear from this that when we abuse God's benefits, it is expedient that they be taken from us, lest by abusing them we perish more damnably. Hence, of the tongue, which was given for praising God and for uttering useful things, the Psalmist prays: [[Ps 30:19|Let deceitful lips be made dumb|Muta fiant labia dolosa]]. So then, [[9:15|I hated them|Exosos habui eos]] [[9:15|for the wickedness of their devices|propter multitudinem adinventionum ipsorum]] [Denis reads *multitudinem*, "for the multitude"; the margin gives the other reading *malitiam*, "for the wickedness", as in the Vulgate], that is, their countless vices, which they conceived out of their own thought and carried into effect. [[9:15|I will cast them forth out of my house|De domo mea ejiciam eos]], that is, out of the land of Israel which I granted them, or out of their houses and cities, bestowed on them by me.

paras.t: Non addam ut diligam eos, id est, de captivitate ista non redimam eos, sed usque in finem sæculi derelinquam. Dicitur autem Deus diligere eos quibus benefacit. Simpliciter vero loquendo, diligit eos quos ad bona gloriæ præordinavit, quibus in præsenti dat bona gratiæ gratum facientis. Propterea, si nunc aliquem temporaliter puniat usque ad mortem, hanc tamen punitionem ordinat ad bonum animæ ejus, videlicet ne æternaliter pereat, sed purgatus et castigatus gratiam sortiatur, dicitur eum diligere. Sic autem non afflixit decem tribus ; sed temporaliter ac æternaliter eas reliquit pro majori utique parte, quia nec in captivitate pœnituerunt, nisi pro modica parte, ut dictum est, et ex libro Tobiæ aliqualiter elici potest : ideo non addit diligere eos. Omnes principes eorum recedentes.
paras.en: [[9:15|I will love them no more|Non addam ut diligam eos]], that is, I will not redeem them from this captivity, but will leave them until the end of the world. Now God is said to love those to whom he does good. But speaking simply, he loves those whom he has foreordained to the goods of glory, to whom in the present he gives the goods of the grace that makes pleasing [*gratia gratum faciens*, that is, sanctifying grace, by which a man is made pleasing to God]. And so, if he now punishes someone in time, even to death, but ordains this punishment to the good of his soul, namely that he may not perish eternally, but, purged and chastised, may obtain grace, he is said to love him.
