But he did not so afflict the ten tribes; rather he abandoned them in time and in eternity, for the greater part at least, because they did not repent even in captivity, except for a small part, as has been said, and as can in some measure be gathered from the book of Tobias[[Tob 1:12||]][[Tob 13:8||]]: therefore he does not go on to love them. [[9:15|all their princes are revolters|Omnes principes eorum recedentes]].

paras.t: Percussus est Ephraim ab hostibus, et partim occisus, partim translatus, vulneratus aut venditus ; radix eorum exsiccata est, id est, virtus generativa ipsis pro parte ablata est. Vel per radicem intelligitur omnipotens virtus Dei, in qua primo erant quasi in radice fundati : quæ dicitur exsiccata, non in se, sed quantum ad eos, quibus cessavit rorem gratiæ, vim prolificandi, ac cetera beneficia consueta influere. Vel radix sunt sancti Patriarchæ, qui malis filiis non subvenerunt. Fructum nequaquam facient, meritorie operando, aut filios generando : quod non est de omnibus universaliter intelligendum, alioqui tota gens illa jam defecisset. Quod et si genuerint, interficiam amantissima uteri eorum, id est eorum carissimos filios. Unde jam dixit : Absque liberis eos faciam.
paras.en: [[9:16|Ephraim is struck|Percussus est Ephraim]] by his enemies, and partly slain, partly carried away, wounded or sold; [[9:16|their root is dried up|radix eorum exsiccata est]], that is, the power of generation has in part been taken from them. Or by the root is understood the almighty power of God, in which they were at first founded as in a root: and it is said to be dried up, not in itself, but as regards them, into whom it ceased to pour the dew of grace, the power of begetting offspring, and its other accustomed benefits. Or the root is the holy Patriarchs, who did not come to the help of their wicked sons. [[9:16|they shall yield no fruit|Fructum nequaquam facient]], by working meritoriously or by begetting sons: which is not to be understood of all universally, or else that whole nation would by now have died out. [[9:16|And if they should have issue, I will slay the best beloved fruit of their womb|Quod et si genuerint, interficiam amantissima uteri eorum]], that is, their dearest sons. Hence he has already said: [[9:12|I will make them without children|Absque liberis eos faciam]].

paras.t: Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus de propria terra in Assyrios, quia non audierunt eum, id est, præceptis divinæ legis et verbis Prophetarum non obedierunt ; et erunt vagi in nationibus, habitando inter gentiles in locis non propriis, et per diversos errores atque peccata vagando.
paras.en: [[9:17|My God will cast them away|Abjiciet eos Dominus Deus meus]] from their own land among the Assyrians, [[9:17|because they hearkened not to him|quia non audierunt eum]], that is, did not obey the precepts of the divine law and the words of the Prophets; [[9:17|and they shall be wanderers among the nations|et erunt vagi in nationibus]], dwelling among the Gentiles in places not their own, and wandering through divers errors and sins.

paras.t: Postremo multa eorum quæ circa finem hujus capituli dicta sunt, Judæis qui Christum crucifixerunt, posterisque eorum convenienter aptantur. Illi enim a Romanis gravissime arctabantur ; et Deus habuit eos exosos propter multitudinem adinventionum suarum contra Christum. Ejecit quoque eos de domo sua, id est de Jerusalem et Judæa ; nec addidit eos diligere, sed usque in finem eorum desolatio permanet. Omnes etiam principes eorum, puta pontifices, fuerunt recedentes a Christo. Sed et radix eorum quodammodo exsiccata est ; nec faciunt fructum virtutum, sed sunt arbores steriles. Abjecit insuper eos Dominus Deus, quia non audierunt vocem ejus, nec Christi prædicationem receperunt, dicentes : Non est hic homo a Deo. Unde usque in præsens sunt vagi in nationibus.
paras.en: Lastly, many of the things said towards the end of this chapter are fittingly applied to the Jews who crucified Christ, and to their descendants. For they were most grievously hemmed in by the Romans; and God held them in hatred for the multitude of their devices against Christ. He also cast them out of his house, that is, out of Jerusalem and Judea; nor did he go on to love them, but their desolation lasts to the end. All their princes too, the pontiffs for example, were [[9:15|revolters|recedentes]] from Christ. And [[9:16|their root|radix eorum]] is in a manner [[9:16|dried up|exsiccata est]]; nor do they bear the fruit of virtues, but are barren trees. Moreover the Lord God cast them away, [[9:17|because they hearkened not|quia non audierunt]] to his voice, nor received the preaching of Christ, saying: [[John 9:16|This man is not of God|Non est hic homo a Deo]]. Hence to this day they are [[9:17|wanderers among the nations|vagi in nationibus]].

9.title: Explanatio moralis ejusdem capituli noni.
9.title_en: Moral explanation of the same ninth chapter.

paras.t: Per Israel legem Dei abjicientem, significantur mali Christiani, falsi religiosi, atque hæretici. Quibus nunc dicitur : Noli lætari, Israel, noli exsultare, id est, nec intus nec foris gaudete, sicut populi, id est, quemadmodum lætari possunt qui humane ac rationabiliter conversantur; quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo, id est, præceptis Christi non obtemperasti. Mali itaque non habent in se causam justæ lætitiæ, sed incumbit eis dolere ac plangere ; nec gloriari vel jactare se habent de hoc quod sunt christiani, sed humiliari et contristari, quod fidem Christi non adornaverunt operibus, et solo nomine seu fide informi christiani consistunt. Et idem exstat judicium de falsis religiosis, sub habitu spirituali cor sæculare atque carnale gerentibus : quibus dicit Jeremias : Scito et vide quia malum et amarum est te reliquisse Dominum Deum tuum, et non esse timorem ejus apud te. Jacobus quoque : Risus vester in luctum convertatur, et gaudium in mærorem. Verumtamen isti exsultare possunt et debent in spe miserationis divinæ et in operibus pœnitentiæ, gratias Domino referentes quod non statim quum peccaverunt tam graviter, vindicavit in eis.
paras.en: By Israel casting away the law of God are signified bad Christians, false religious and heretics. To them it is now said: [[9:1|Rejoice not, O Israel: rejoice not|Noli lætari, Israel, noli exsultare]], that is, rejoice neither inwardly nor outwardly, [[9:1|as the nations do|sicut populi]], that is, as those can rejoice who live in a human and reasonable way; [[9:1|for thou hast committed fornication against thy God|quia fornicatus es a Deo tuo]], that is, thou hast not obeyed the commandments of Christ. The wicked, then, have in themselves no cause of just joy; it falls to them rather to grieve and lament. Nor ought they to glory or boast of being Christians, but to be humbled and saddened that they have not adorned the faith of Christ with works, and remain Christians in name alone, or by unformed faith [that is, faith not formed by charity, which does not give the soul life]. And the same judgment holds of false religious, who bear a worldly and carnal heart under a spiritual habit: to whom Jeremias says: [[Jer 2:19|Know thou, and see that it is an evil and a bitter thing for thee, to have left the Lord thy God, and that my fear is not with thee|Scito et vide quia malum et amarum est te reliquisse Dominum Deum tuum, et non esse timorem ejus apud te]]. James too: [[Jas 4:9|let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow|Risus vester in luctum convertatur, et gaudium in mærorem]]. Yet these can and ought to exult in the hope of the divine mercy and in works of penance, giving thanks to the Lord that he did not at once take vengeance on them when they sinned so grievously.

paras.t: Dilexisti mercedem super omnes areas tritici. Hoc secundum sensum in præcedenti articulo positum faciunt, qui actum prædicationis, vel cetera opera spiritualia ex suo genere bona, exhibent fine præpostero, scilicet propter commodum temporale et corporales divitias : cujus oppositum dicit se fecisse Apostolus ; quoniam temporalia et corporalia, ad bona divina ac spiritualia quasi ad finem sunt referenda : cujus oppositum agunt avari atque hypocritæ, imitantes Pharisæos, qui ut ait Salvator, devorant domos viduarum sub prolixæ orationis obtentu.
paras.en: [[9:1|thou hast loved a reward upon every cornfloor|Dilexisti mercedem super omnes areas tritici]]. This, in the sense set down in the preceding article, is done by those who perform the act of preaching, or other spiritual works good in their kind [that is, good by the kind of act they are, before the end and circumstances are considered], for a perverse end, namely for temporal gain and bodily riches: the opposite of which the Apostle says he did[[Acts 20:33||]][[Acts 20:34||]][[Acts 20:35||]][[1 Cor 4:12||]][[1 Thess 2:9||]][[2 Thess 3:8||]]; for temporal and bodily things are to be referred to divine and spiritual goods as to their end. The opposite of this is done by the covetous and the hypocrites, imitating the Pharisees, who, as the Saviour says, [[Mark 12:40|devour the houses of widows under the pretence of long prayer|devorant domos viduarum sub prolixæ orationis obtentu]][[Luke 20:47||]].

paras.t: Area, id est, Ecclesia Dei, in qua velut in horreo continentur fideles et sacramenta ac alimonia animarum. Unde Joannes Baptista dicit de Christo : Triticum congregabit in horreum suum. Et Isaias loquitur Synagogæ : Tritura mea et filia areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino exercituum, annuntiavi vobis. Et torcular, id est passio Salvatoris vel persecutio adversitatis. Unde habetur in Isaia : Torcular calcavi solus. Non pascet eos : quia instructionem bonorum non advertunt ; nec participes sunt meritorum Ecclesiæ, quum sint extra caritatem; nec dicere possunt cum Psalmista, Particeps ego sum omnium timentium te; nec sortiuntur effectum, fructum seu meritum dominicæ passionis, quoniam sacramenta Christi non venerantur, neque suscipiunt ea reverenter. Insuper per adversa non purgantur, quia non sustinent ea patienter. Et vinum mentietur eis. Per vinum intelligi potest sanguis Christi, sub vini speciebus contentus : qui dicitur eis mentiri, dum ejus potatione damnationem potius quam salutem merentur. Qui enim biberit calicem Domini indigne, judicium sibi bibit, et reus erit sanguinis Christi.
paras.en: [[9:2|The floor|Area]], that is, the Church of God, in which, as in a barn, are contained the faithful, and the sacraments and nourishment of souls. Whence John the Baptist says of Christ: [[Matt 3:12|gather his wheat into the barn|Triticum congregabit in horreum suum]]. And Isaias says to the Synagogue: [[Is 21:10|O my thrashing, and the children of my floor, that which I have heard of the Lord of hosts|Tritura mea et filia areæ meæ, quæ audivi a Domino exercituum]], [[Is 21:10|I have declared unto you|annuntiavi vobis]]. [[9:2|and the winepress|Et torcular]], that is, the passion of the Saviour, or the persecution of adversity. Whence we have in Isaias: [[Is 63:3|I have trodden the winepress alone|Torcular calcavi solus]]. [[9:2|shall not feed them|Non pascet eos]]: for they do not heed the instruction of the good; nor are they partakers of the merits of the Church, since they are outside charity; nor can they say with the Psalmist, [[Ps 118:63|I am a partaker with all them that fear thee|Particeps ego sum omnium timentium te]]; nor do they obtain the effect, fruit or merit of the Lord's passion, since they do not venerate the sacraments of Christ, nor receive them reverently. Moreover they are not purged by adversities, since they do not bear them patiently. [[9:2|and the wine shall deceive them|Et vinum mentietur eis]] [*mentietur*, literally "shall lie to them"]. By the wine may be understood the blood of Christ, contained under the species of wine: which is said to lie to them when by drinking it they merit damnation rather than salvation. For he that shall [[1 Cor 11:27|drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily|biberit calicem Domini indigne]], [[1 Cor 11:29|drinketh judgment to himself|judicium sibi bibit]], and [[1 Cor 11:27|shall be guilty|reus erit]] of the blood of Christ.

paras.t: Non habitabunt in terra Domini, id est in Ecclesia triumphanti seu patria, de qua cantatur : Credo videre bona Domini in terra viventium. Propter quod scriptum est : Neque habitabit juxta te malignus, neque permanebunt injusti ante oculos tuos. Nunc quoque non habitant per caritatem et sanctam conversationem in Ecclesia militanti, nec actualiter perfecteque pertinent ad mysticum corpus Christi, quemadmodum de talibus fert Joannes in prima sua Canonica : In nobis erant, sed non erant ex nobis.
paras.en: [[9:3|They shall not dwell in the Lord's land|Non habitabunt in terra Domini]], that is, in the Church triumphant or heavenly fatherland, of which it is sung: [[Ps 26:13|I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.|Credo videre bona Domini in terra viventium]] Wherefore it is written: [[Ps 5:6|Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.|Neque habitabit juxta te malignus, neque permanebunt injusti ante oculos tuos]] And even now they do not dwell, by charity and holy conversation, in the Church militant, nor do they actually and perfectly belong to the mystical body of Christ, as John says of such men in his first canonical Epistle: They were among us, but [[1 John 2:19|they were not of us|non erant ex nobis]] [Denis's *In nobis erant*, "they were among us", stands where the Vulgate has *Ex nobis prodierunt*, "they went out from us"].

paras.t: Reversus est Ephraim, id est, mundana sibi adaugens est quilibet Christianus, in Ægyptum, redeundo ad sæcularem vitam et priores ignorantiæ tenebras. Quocontra admonet in prima sua epistola Petrus : Succincti lumbos mentis vestræ, sobrii, perfecti, sperate in eam quæ vobis offertur gratiam, non configurati prioribus ignorantiæ vestræ tenebris, sed secundum eum qui vos vocavit, Sanctum : et ipsi sancti in omni conversatione sitis. Et Paulus : Nolite, inquit, conformari huic sæculo. Tales sunt carnales ac tepidi religiosi, qui exterioribus consolatiunculis gaudent. Et in Assyriis pollutum comedit. Assyrii interpretantur dirigentes : per quos intelliguntur prudentes hujus sæculi, de quibus ait Salvator, Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt; et Jeremias, Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt. Inter hos comedit pollutum, qui illorum peccatis communicat opere aut consensu, vel non corrigit quum potest et debet. Unde hortatur Apostolus : Exite de medio eorum, et immundum ne tetigeritis.
paras.en: [[9:3|Ephraim is returned|Reversus est Ephraim]], that is, any Christian who heaps up worldly things for himself, [[9:3|to Egypt|in Ægyptum]], by going back to the worldly life and the former darkness of ignorance. Against this Peter warns in his first Epistle: [[1 Pet 1:13|having the loins of your mind girt up, being sober, trust perfectly in the grace which is offered you|Succincti lumbos mentis vestræ, sobrii, perfecti, sperate in eam quæ vobis offertur gratiam]], [[1 Pet 1:14|not fashioned according to the former|non configurati prioribus]] darkness of your ignorance [Denis reads *tenebris*, "darkness", where the Vulgate has *desideriis*, "desires"], [[1 Pet 1:15|But according to him that hath called you, who is holy, be you also in all manner of conversation holy|sed secundum eum qui vos vocavit, Sanctum : et ipsi sancti in omni conversatione sitis]]. And Paul: [[Rom 12:2|be not|Nolite]], he says, [[Rom 12:2|conformed to this world|conformari huic sæculo]]. Such are carnal and lukewarm religious, who delight in petty outward consolations. [[9:3|and hath eaten unclean things among the Assyrians|Et in Assyriis pollutum comedit]]. *Assyrians* is interpreted "directing": by them are understood the prudent of this world, of whom the Saviour says, [[Luke 16:8|the children of this world are wiser in their generation than the children of light|Filii hujus sæculi prudentiores filiis lucis in generatione sua sunt]]; and Jeremias, [[Jer 4:22|they are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge|Sapientes sunt ut faciant mala, bene autem facere nescierunt]]. Among these he eats unclean things who shares in their sins by deed or consent, or does not correct them when he can and ought. Whence the Apostle exhorts: [[2 Cor 6:17|Go out from among them|Exite de medio eorum]], and [[2 Cor 6:17|touch not the unclean thing|immundum ne tetigeritis]].

paras.t: Non libabunt Domino vinum. Per vinum frequenter designatur sapientia, quæ est notitia sapida. Qui ergo per sapientiam sibi concessam Deum non veneratur, neque fructuose ea perutitur, non libat Domino vinum, sed dicitur ei illud Isaiæ : Vinum tuum mixtum est aqua. Et non placebunt ei sacrificia eorum ex parte offerentium. Qui enim non est in caritate, nihil facit Deo acceptum seu meritorium. Et quamvis sacrificium novæ legis, videlicet Sacramentum altaris (quod pluraliter sacramenta et sacrificia dicitur propter pluralitatem specierum sub quibus consistit), sit semper placitum Deo ex propria dignitate, tamen ex parte indigne offerentium dicitur non placere, quamvis in se placeat, quoniam peccat qui offert imparatus. Quasi panis lugentium luctu inordinato pro temporalium amissione vel de profectu alterius. Talium enim panis, id est lacrimæ, seu operatio, Deo non placent.
paras.en: [[9:4|They shall not offer wine to the Lord|Non libabunt Domino vinum]]. By wine wisdom is often signified, which is savoury knowledge [*sapientia*, "wisdom", is *notitia sapida*, "knowledge that has savour": a play on the two words]. He, then, who does not worship God by the wisdom granted him, nor use it fruitfully, does not offer wine to the Lord; rather that word of Isaias is said to him: [[Is 1:22|thy wine is mingled with water|Vinum tuum mixtum est aqua]]. [[9:4|neither shall they please him|Et non placebunt ei]], [[9:4|their sacrifices|sacrificia eorum]] [Denis reads these words together: "and their sacrifices shall not please him"], on the part of those who offer them. For he who is not in charity does nothing acceptable or meritorious before God. And although the sacrifice of the new law, namely the Sacrament of the altar (which is called in the plural sacraments and sacrifices because of the plurality of the species under which it exists), is always pleasing to God by its own dignity, yet on the part of those who offer it unworthily it is said not to please, though in itself it pleases; for he sins who offers unprepared. [[9:4|like the bread of mourners|Quasi panis lugentium]], who mourn with an inordinate grief over the loss of temporal things, or over another's progress. For the bread of such, that is, their tears or their work, does not please God.

paras.t: Denique in præcedenti articulo verba ista ad litteram exposita sunt, ita quod per panem lugentium, designatur cibus deflentium mortuum. Sed nunc addam quod ibi omisi. Hieronymus enim, per panem lugentium, litteraliter intelligit sacrificium legis quod offerebatur pro mortuis. Unde Glossa ait : Apud Judæos sacrificium pro mortuo offerebatur, quæ oblatio panis lugentium dicitur, quia a lugentibus offerebatur. Quum autem quis de illo comedebat, ipse immundus et sacrificium immundum dicebatur.
paras.en: Further, in the preceding article these words were expounded according to the letter, so that by [[9:4|the bread of mourners|panem lugentium]] is meant the food of those who weep for one dead. But now I will add what I left out there. For Jerome understands by the bread of mourners, literally, the sacrifice of the law that was offered for the dead. Whence the Gloss says: Among the Jews a sacrifice was offered for the dead, and this offering is called the bread of mourners, because it was offered by mourners. And when anyone ate of it, both he and the sacrifice were called unclean.

paras.t: Quid facietis in die solenni, in quo deberetis cum speciali devotione Deo vacare, et negligentias dierum ferialium recuperare? quasi dicat : Dies solennes non expenditis fructuose.
paras.en: [[9:5|What will you do in the solemn day|Quid facietis in die solenni]], on which you ought to give yourselves to God with special devotion, and make up for the negligences of the weekdays? As if to say: You do not spend the solemn days fruitfully.

paras.t: Ecce enim profecti sunt, id est, ab ecclesiastica unitate et caritate recesserunt, a vastitate, id est propter adversitatem tentationis seu persecutionis. De quibus in Evangelio scribitur : Quia ad tempus credunt, et tempore tentationis recedunt. Ægyptus congregabit eos. Ægyptus figura est mundi hujus, qui totus in maligno positus est : eos autem qui a Deo recedunt, recipit mundus. Desiderabile argentum eorum, id est sæcularem prudentiam quam dilexerunt, urtica hereditabit, id est pœnalis punctura damnationis : quia ut dicit Apostolus ad Romanos, Prudentia carnis, mors est; lappa, id est spina seu remorsus conscientiæ, in tabernaculis, id est cordibus eorum. Synderesis enim remurmurat malo; et dum impii intra se redeunt, non veram mentis quietem seu tranquillitatem, sed conscientiæ remorsum inveniunt.
paras.en: [[9:6|For behold they are gone|Ecce enim profecti sunt]], that is, they have withdrawn from the unity and charity of the Church, [[9:6|because of destruction|a vastitate]], that is, on account of the adversity of temptation or persecution. Of them it is written in the Gospel: [[Luke 8:13|for they believe for a while and in time of temptation they fall away|Quia ad tempus credunt, et tempore tentationis recedunt]]. [[9:6|Egypt shall gather them together|Ægyptus congregabit eos]]. Egypt is a figure of this world, which wholly [[1 John 5:19|is seated in wickedness|in maligno positus est]]: and those who withdraw from God, the world takes in. [[9:6|their beloved silver|Desiderabile argentum eorum]], that is, the worldly prudence which they loved, [[9:6|nettles shall inherit|urtica hereditabit]], that is, the penal sting of damnation: for, as the Apostle says to the Romans, [[Rom 8:6|the wisdom of the flesh is death|Prudentia carnis, mors est]] [*prudentia*, "prudence", which the Douay-Rheims renders "wisdom"]; [[9:6|the bur|lappa]], that is, the thorn or remorse of conscience, [[9:6|in their tabernacles|in tabernaculis]], that is, in their hearts. For synderesis [that is, the natural habit of the first principles of moral action, the spark of conscience] murmurs against evil; and when the wicked return within themselves, they find not true quiet or tranquillity of mind, but remorse of conscience.

paras.t: Venerunt dies visitationis. Dies enim mortis et particularis judicii, singulis nobis indesinenter propinquat. Propter quod Jacobus dicit : Ecce judex ante januam adsistit. Scito te, o Israel, stultum : id est, tu, Christiane, qui fide, non caritate et opere, christianus es, nosce te esse stultum, quia non habes sapientiam veram, illam quæ est unum de septem donis Spiritus Sancti, de qua Sapientiæ primo inducitur : In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia. Scito quoque te esse prophetam insanum, dum tibi longam vitam promittis, dicens illud Lucæ : Anima, habes multa bona reposita in annos plurimos ; requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare. Tali enim dicitur : Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetent a te : quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt?
paras.en: [[9:7|The days of visitation are come|Venerunt dies visitationis]]. For the day of death and of the particular judgment draws unceasingly nearer to each of us. Wherefore James says: [[Jas 5:9|Behold the judge standeth before the door|Ecce judex ante januam adsistit]]. [[9:7|know ye, O Israel|Scito te, o Israel]], that thou art [[9:7|foolish|stultum]] [Denis reads *Scito te, o Israel, stultum*, "know thyself, O Israel, to be foolish"; the Vulgate has *Scitote, Israël, stultum prophetam*]: that is, thou, O Christian, who art a Christian by faith, not by charity and works, know that thou art foolish, because thou hast not true wisdom, that which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]], of which it is said in the first chapter of Wisdom: [[Wis 1:4|wisdom will not enter into a malicious soul|In malevolam animam non introibit sapientia]]. Know also that thou art a [[9:7|mad|insanum]] [[9:7|prophet|prophetam]], when thou promisest thyself a long life, saying that word in Luke: [[Luke 12:19|Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years. Take thy rest: eat, drink, make good cheer|Anima, habes multa bona reposita in annos plurimos ; requiesce, comede, bibe, epulare]]. For to such a one it is said: [[Luke 12:20|Thou fool, this night do they require thy soul of thee. And whose shall those things be which thou hast provided?|Stulte, hac nocte animam tuam repetent a te : quæ autem parasti, cujus erunt?]]

paras.t: Speculator Ephraim, id est, prælatus Ecclesiæ, cum Deo meo propheta, id est, a Deo quasi propheta effectus est, dum populo futura prædicit, videlicet universale judicium, gaudia Beatorum, et pœnas reproborum. Vel est propheta, exponendo Scripturas et interpretando. Sic enim, secundum Ambrosium, Apostolus loquitur de Prophetis, dicendo : Prophetæ duo vel tres dicant, et ceteri taceant; itemque, Potestis per singulos prophetare.
paras.en: [[9:8|The watchman of Ephraim|Speculator Ephraim]], that is, a prelate of the Church, [[9:8|was with my God: the prophet|cum Deo meo propheta]], that is, he has been made by God as it were a prophet, when he foretells things to come to the people, namely the universal judgment, the joys of the blessed and the pains of the reprobate. Or he is a prophet by expounding and interpreting the Scriptures. For it is in this sense, according to Ambrose [that is, the commentary on St Paul then ascribed to Ambrose], that the Apostle speaks of prophets, saying: [[1 Cor 14:29|let the prophets speak, two or three|Prophetæ duo vel tres dicant]], and let the rest keep silence [Denis reads *ceteri taceant*, "let the rest keep silence", where the Vulgate has *ceteri dijudicent*, "let the rest judge"]; and again: [[1 Cor 14:31|you may all prophesy, one by one|Potestis per singulos prophetare]].

paras.t: Laqueus ruinæ factus est super omnes vias ejus. Hoc intelligi potest de prælato malo et bono. Malus enim prælatus, est aliis directe laqueus ruinæ, quos male agendo, vel debita omittendo, subvertit. Bonus quoque prælatus est aliis laqueus ruinæ occasionaliter et indirecte, quoniam multi sunt qui ejus justitiam ferre non possunt, in quibus veritas parit odium, et suo superiori rebelles sunt. Insania, id est gravis error, irrationabilis vita, et bestialis concupiscentia, sunt in domo Dei ejus, id est in congregatione talis prælati, quæ merito esset Ecclesia Dei per caritatem, sed sola fide Ecclesia est. Qui enim bono carent prælato vel ei resistunt, multis modis insaniunt.
paras.en: [[9:8|is become a snare of ruin upon all his ways|Laqueus ruinæ factus est super omnes vias ejus]]. This can be understood both of a bad prelate and of a good one. For a bad prelate is directly a snare of ruin to others, whom he overthrows by doing evil or by leaving undone what he ought. A good prelate too is a snare of ruin to others, by occasion and indirectly [that is, as the occasion of their fall, not its cause], since there are many who cannot bear his justice, in whom truth begets hatred, and they rebel against their superior. [[9:8|madness|Insania]], that is, grave error, an irrational life and bestial concupiscence, are [[9:8|in the house of his God|in domo Dei ejus]], that is, in the congregation of such a prelate, which would rightly be the Church of God by charity, but is the Church by faith alone. For those who lack a good prelate, or resist him, are mad in many ways.

paras.t: Profunde peccaverunt, sicut in diebus Gabaa. Hoc competit omnibus qui ex proposito, deliberatione, habitu vitioso, animo indurato, Deum offendunt, qui difficulter sanantur; qui autem peccat ex sola ignorantia, infirmitate vel passione, sanatur faciliter.
paras.en: [[9:9|They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gabaa|Profunde peccaverunt, sicut in diebus Gabaa]]. This fits all who offend God of set purpose, with deliberation, from a vicious habit, with a hardened mind: these are healed with difficulty; but he who sins from ignorance alone, or weakness, or passion, is easily healed.

paras.t: Quasi uvas in deserto inveni Israel, id est electos gentiles mihi pretiosos et caros, quos post passionem per Apostolos ad fidem converti. In cacumine ejus, id est in præcipuo statu seu principio militantis Ecclesiæ, vidi patres eorum, id est Apostolos, qui eos spiritualiter genuerunt in Christo, sicut ad Galatas scribit Apostolus : Filioli, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis. Ipsi autem, non iidem numero, sed quidam de fide ipsorum, intraverunt ad Beelphegor. Tales sunt avari, gulosi et lubrici, quorum deus est vel aurum, vel venter, aut venus : qui abalienati sunt a Deo et abominabiles, sicut ea quæ colunt ac diligunt.
paras.en: [[9:10|I found Israel like grapes in the desert|Quasi uvas in deserto inveni Israel]], that is, the chosen Gentiles, precious and dear to me, whom after the passion I converted to the faith through the Apostles. [[9:10|in the top thereof|In cacumine ejus]], that is, in the foremost state or beginning of the Church militant, [[9:10|I saw their fathers|vidi patres eorum]], that is, the Apostles, who begot them spiritually in Christ, as the Apostle writes to the Galatians: [[Gal 4:19|My little children, of whom I am in labour again, until Christ be formed in you.|Filioli, quos iterum parturio, donec formetur Christus in vobis]] [[9:10|but they|Ipsi autem]], not the very same persons, but some who shared their faith, [[9:10|went in to Beelphegor|intraverunt ad Beelphegor]]. Such are the covetous, the gluttonous and the lustful, whose god is either gold, or the belly, or lust[[Phil 3:19||]]: who have [[9:10|alienated themselves|abalienati sunt]] from God, and are [[9:10|abominable|abominabiles]], like the things which they worship and love.

paras.t: Ephraim quasi avis avolavit : id est, talium quilibet celeriter a Deo recessit, tanquam levis et vagus : quorum gloria est a partu et ab utero, id est in actibus venereis seu multitudine filiorum carnalium, qui plerumque filiis suis privantur.
paras.en: [[9:11|Ephraim|Ephraim]] [[9:11|hath flown away like bird|quasi avis avolavit]]: that is, each of such men has swiftly departed from God, as one light and unsettled: whose [[9:11|glory|gloria]] is [[9:11|from the birth, and from the womb|a partu et ab utero]], that is, in venereal acts, or in a multitude of carnal children; and such men are for the most part deprived of their children.

paras.t: Ephraim ut Tyrus erat, id est, ecclesia malignorum olim in Baptismo vel postea, erat tanta gratia totque virtutibus adornata, quot terrenis divitiis Tyrus quondam abundavit; Ephraim educet ad interfectores filios suos, id est, dæmonibus animarum occisoribus exponit posteros suos seu imitatores, quos in propriis fovet peccatis, quemadmodum scriptum est : Dimiserunt reliquias suas parvulis suis. Hoc faciunt et mali prælati, pestiferique doctores, de quibus dicitur : Cæci sunt et duces cæcorum. Hi pariter cadunt in lacum gehennæ, traduntque se ipsos adversariis suis dæmonibus, quibus dant locum.
paras.en: [[9:13|Ephraim, as I saw, was a Tyre|Ephraim ut Tyrus erat]], that is, the church of the wicked, once, in Baptism or afterwards, was adorned with as much grace and as many virtues as Tyre once abounded in earthly riches; [[9:13|Ephraim shall bring out his children to the murderer|Ephraim educet ad interfectores filios suos]], that is, he exposes his posterity or imitators to the demons, the slayers of souls, cherishing them in his own sins, as it is written: [[Ps 16:14|they have left to their little ones|Dimiserunt reliquias suas parvulis suis]]. This bad prelates also do, and pestilent teachers, of whom it is said: [[Matt 15:14|they are blind, and leaders of the blind|Cæci sunt et duces cæcorum]]. These fall together into the pit of hell, and hand themselves over to their adversaries the demons, to whom they give place.

paras.t: Omnes nequitiæ eorum in Galgal, id est in volutabro vel cœno carnalis seu turpis affectionis, ex qua prodeunt vitia. Galgal autem interpretatur revelatio, vel volutabrum. Ibi exosos habui eos : quoniam propter interiorem immunditiam displicent Deo homines operaque eorum. De domo mea ejiciam eos, id est de societate electorum militantis ac triumphantis Ecclesiæ. De militanti quippe Ecclesia scribit Timotheo Apostolus : Scias quomodo te oporteat conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna et firmamentum veritatis. Non addam ut diligam eos, quoniam æternaliter damnabuntur. Omnes principes eorum, id est negligentes prælati ac impii dominatores, sunt recedentes a Deo per culpam, quærentes semetipsos potius quam aliorum salutem.
paras.en: [[9:15|All their wickedness is in Galgal|Omnes nequitiæ eorum in Galgal]], that is, in the wallowing-place or mire of carnal or base affection, from which vices come forth. For *Galgal* is interpreted "revelation", or "wallowing-place". [[9:15|there I hated them|Ibi exosos habui eos]]: since because of inward uncleanness men and their works displease God. [[9:15|I will cast them forth out of my house|De domo mea ejiciam eos]], that is, out of the fellowship of the elect of the Church militant and triumphant. For of the Church militant the Apostle writes to Timothy: [[1 Tim 3:15|that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth|Scias quomodo te oporteat conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi, columna et firmamentum veritatis]]. [[9:15|I will love them no more|Non addam ut diligam eos]], since they will be damned eternally. [[9:15|all their princes|Omnes principes eorum]], that is, negligent prelates and impious rulers, [[9:15|are revolters|sunt recedentes]] from God by sin, seeking themselves rather than the salvation of others.

paras.t: Percussus est Ephraim, id est, mali Christiani per peccatum læsi sunt a diabolo, et in naturalibus vulnerati, atque ad opera bona ineptiores effecti. Radix eorum, id est gratia, in qua fuerant radicati, exsiccata est, id est destructa, quia non habuit humorem bonæ operationis se conservantis, nec divinæ pietatis influentia est compluta : quod contigit ex eorum negligentia. Unde et pœnitens ait in Psalmo : Percussus sum ut fœnum, et aruit cor meum, quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum. Fructum nequaquam facient: quoniam nemo potest sine gratia promereri, vel fructus spirituales producere, de quibus ad Galatas dicit Apostolus : Fructus Spiritus est : caritas, gaudium, pax, patientia, longanimitas, bonitas, etc. Quod et si genuerint spiritualiter vel carnaliter sibi similes in peccatis, ita quod patrem sequatur sua proles, interficiam amantissima uteri eorum, id est, eos quos maxime dilexerunt, et ex utero suo, id est corde per instructionem pestiferam, vel ventre per carnalem propagationem, genuerunt in esse naturæ aut culpæ seu utroque, occidam, omne spirituale ac beatificum esse subtrahendo, eosque damnando, ita quod spiritualiter nihil erunt, imo et nihil respectu ultimi finis et electorum, qui esse gratiæ vel gloriæ sunt sortiti.
paras.en: [[9:16|Ephraim is struck|Percussus est Ephraim]], that is, bad Christians have been wounded by the devil through sin, and hurt in their natural powers, and made less apt for good works. [[9:16|their root|Radix eorum]], that is, grace, in which they had been rooted, [[9:16|is dried up|exsiccata est]], that is, destroyed, because it had not the moisture of good works to preserve it[[Luke 8:6||]], nor was it watered by the inflowing of the divine goodness: which came about through their own negligence. Whence the penitent too says in the Psalm: [[Ps 101:5|I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: because I forgot to eat my bread.|Percussus sum ut fœnum, et aruit cor meum, quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum]] [[9:16|they shall yield no fruit|Fructum nequaquam facient]]: for no one can merit without grace, or bring forth spiritual fruits, of which the Apostle says to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:22|the fruit of the Spirit is, charity, joy, peace, patience|Fructus Spiritus est : caritas, gaudium, pax, patientia]], longanimity, goodness, etc. [[9:16|And if they should have issue|Quod et si genuerint]], spiritually or carnally, children like themselves in sin, so that the offspring follows the father, [[9:16|I will slay the best beloved fruit of their womb|interficiam amantissima uteri eorum]], that is, those whom they most loved, and whom from their womb (that is, from the heart by pestilent instruction, or from the belly by carnal propagation) they begot into the being of nature, or of guilt, or both, I will kill, by withdrawing from them all spiritual and beatific being, and by damning them, so that spiritually they will be nothing; indeed nothing also with regard to the last end and to the elect, who have obtained the being of grace or of glory.

10.title: Expositio litteralis capituli decimi: Vitis frondosa Israel.
10.title_en: Literal exposition of the tenth chapter: Israel a vine full of branches.

paras.t: Hoc loco ostendit Propheta qualiter decem tribus beneficiis Dei abusæ sint. Et ut earum ingratitudo clarius innotescat, primo inducit quales olim erant dono piissimi Dei.
paras.en: In this place the Prophet shows how the ten tribes abused the benefits of God. And that their ingratitude may be the more clearly seen, he first sets forth what they once were by the gift of the most loving God.

paras.t: Vitis frondosa Israel, id est Synagoga seu domus aut familia decem tribuum: de quibus Propheta nunc specialiter tractat, quamvis quod dicit, toti duodecim tribuum Synagogæ olim convenerit, quæ fuit similis vineæ pulchræ, frondibus ac uvis fecundæ. Habuit enim multas personas tanquam frondes vel uvas, erantque personæ illæ fructibus virtutum ornatæ, antequam idololatria tempore Jeroboam subintravit. Propter quod subditur: Fructus adæquatus est ei, id est, secundum multitudinem ac pulchritudinem suam, fructum protulit operum bonorum, ita quod numero hominum et merito vitæ proportionabiliter crevit, maxime tempore David et Salomonis. Vel, Fructus adæquatus est ei, quoniam terra eis concessa, fertilissima fuit, et populo sufficientiam terræ nascentium protulit. Sed prima expositio melior est, quoniam Septuaginta interpretum translatio talis est: Fructus multus in ea.
paras.en: [[10:1|Israel a vine full of branches|Vitis frondosa Israel]], that is, the Synagogue, or the house or family, of the ten tribes, of whom the Prophet is now treating in particular; although what he says once fitted the whole Synagogue of the twelve tribes, which was like a fair vine, rich in leaves and grapes. For it had many persons, as it were leaves or grapes, and those persons were adorned with the fruits of the virtues, before idolatry crept in in the time of Jeroboam. Wherefore it is added: [[10:1|the fruit is agreeable to it|Fructus adæquatus est ei]] [the Latin *adæquatus* means "made equal to" or "matched to it"], that is, in proportion to its multitude and beauty it brought forth the fruit of good works, so that it grew in the number of its men and in the merit of its life alike, above all in the time of David and Solomon. Or, [[10:1|the fruit is agreeable to it|Fructus adæquatus est ei]], because the land granted to them was most fertile, and brought forth for the people a sufficiency of what grows from the earth. But the first explanation is the better, since the translation of the Seventy interpreters runs thus: Much fruit in it.

paras.t: Denique, pro eo quod nostra translatio continet, Vitis frondosa Israel, Aquila transtulit, Vitis aquosa Israel: quod secundum Hieronymum, in malam partem accipitur, pro his qui cultu Dei relicto, venerati sunt idola. Vitis enim aquosa nisi fuerit a vinitore putata, tota in frondes excrescit, et humorem quem debuit in vina mutare, superflua foliorum ac frondium extensione dispergit. Totæ erant decem tribus crescentes in multitudinem hominum, sed fructum bonæ conversationis Deo agricolæ non exhibentes: quia pro eo quod debuerunt facere uvas, fecerunt labruscas. — Solet autem populus Israel nomine vineæ designari: sicut in Psalmo, Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti; et in Jeremia, Pastores multi demoliti sunt vineam meam; et in Isaia, Vinea Domini Sabaoth, domus Israel. De qua in Evangelio ait Salvator: Homo quidam plantavit vineam, et locavit eam agricolis. Quæ quondam in tantum fuit frondosa, ut dicat Psalmista: Extendit palmites suos usque ad mare, et usque ad flumen propagines ejus.
paras.en: Further, where our translation has [[10:1|Israel a vine full of branches|Vitis frondosa Israel]], Aquila translated, Israel a watery vine: which, according to Jerome, is taken in a bad sense, of those who forsook the worship of God and venerated idols. For a watery vine, unless it is pruned by the vinedresser, runs wholly into leafage, and the moisture it ought to turn into wine it scatters in a needless spreading of leaves and branches. Such were the ten tribes: growing into a multitude of men, but not yielding to God, the husbandman, the fruit of a good life; for where they ought to have made grapes, they [[Is 5:2|brought forth wild grapes|fecerunt labruscas]]. — Now the people of Israel is often signified by the name of a vineyard: as in the Psalm, [[Ps 79:9|Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt|Vineam de Ægypto transtulisti]]; and in Jeremias, [[Jer 12:10|Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard|Pastores multi demoliti sunt vineam meam]]; and in Isaias, [[Is 5:7|the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel|Vinea Domini Sabaoth, domus Israel]] [Denis has *Domini Sabaoth*, "of the Lord of Sabaoth"]. Of which the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Luke 20:9|A certain man planted a vineyard and let it out to husbandmen|Homo quidam plantavit vineam, et locavit eam agricolis]][[Matt 21:33||]]. And it was once so full of branches that the Psalmist says: [[Ps 79:12|It stretched forth its branches unto the sea, and its boughs unto the river.|Extendit palmites suos usque ad mare, et usque ad flumen propagines ejus]]

paras.t: Deinde scribitur ingratitudo atque abusio vineæ hujus. Secundum multitudinem fructus sui multiplicavit altaria, id est, quo copiosior fuit in divitiis et multitudine populi, eo plura construxit altaria ad idola honoranda; juxta ubertatem terræ suæ, id est secundum quod terram fertilissimam possidebat, exuberavit simulacris, id est, plurimis idolis abundavit, diversarum gentium deos colendo, ut dictum est.
paras.en: Next is described the ingratitude and abuse of this vine. [[10:1|according to the multitude of his fruit, he hath multiplied altars|Secundum multitudinem fructus sui multiplicavit altaria]], that is, the richer it was in wealth and in the multitude of its people, the more altars it built to honour idols; [[10:1|according to the plenty of his land|juxta ubertatem terræ suæ]], that is, in proportion as it possessed a most fertile land, [[10:1|he hath abounded with idols|exuberavit simulacris]], that is, it abounded in very many idols, worshipping the gods of divers nations, as has been said[[Osee 8:11||]][[Osee 8:14||]].

paras.t: Divisum est cor eorum. Hoc dupliciter elucidatur. Primo, secundum Hebræos, qui quamdiu reges decem tribuum et ipsæ tribus pari consensu idola honorabant, non venit captivitas: quia tunc culpa populi aliquo modo excusabatur propter imperium atque tyrannidem regum, inducentium subditos ad idololatriam, imo et prohibentium ne irent ad sacrificandum in Jerusalem Domino. Ultimus vero rex Israel dictus Osee, qui licet fecerit malum coram Domino, non tamen sicut patres ejus, ut legitur quarto Regum, præcepit ne vituli aurei tanto studio colerentur; sed dedit licentiam populo eundi et sacrificandi in Jerusalem: cui populus contradixit. Sicque divisum fuit cor populi a corde regis, et nullam idololatriæ excusationem habebant. Propter quod mox venit extrema captivitas, sicut subjungitur: nunc interibunt, id est, protinus ab Assyriis vastabuntur. Quidam enim eorum erant occisi; alii autem translati, quos fecit Salmanasar rex Assyriorum habitare juxta flumen Gozan in civitatibus Medorum, ut scribitur quarto Regum. — Secundo exponitur sic: Divisum est cor eorum, id est, partim Deo, partim idolis ministrando, atque in duas partes claudicando, habent mentem divisam, non totaliter Deo se unientem.
paras.en: [[10:2|Their heart is divided|Divisum est cor eorum]]. This is explained in two ways. First, according to the Hebrews, who say that as long as the kings of the ten tribes and the tribes themselves honoured idols with one consent, the captivity did not come: for then the guilt of the people was in some measure excused by the command and tyranny of the kings, who led their subjects into idolatry, and even forbade them to go and sacrifice to the Lord in Jerusalem[[3 Kings 12:28||]]. But the last king of Israel, called Osee, who, though he [[4 Kings 17:2|did evil before the Lord|fecerit malum coram Domino]], yet not as his fathers, as we read in the fourth book of Kings, commanded that the golden calves should not be worshipped with so much zeal, and gave the people leave to go and sacrifice in Jerusalem; and the people refused him. And so the heart of the people was divided from the heart of the king, and they had no excuse for their idolatry. Wherefore the last captivity soon came, as is added: [[10:2|now they shall perish|nunc interibunt]], that is, they shall straightway be laid waste by the Assyrians. For some of them were slain, and others carried away, whom Salmanasar king of the Assyrians made to dwell [[4 Kings 17:6|by the river of Gozan, in the cities of the Medes|juxta flumen Gozan in civitatibus Medorum]], as is written in the fourth book of Kings. — Secondly it is explained thus: [[10:2|Their heart is divided|Divisum est cor eorum]], that is, by serving partly God and partly idols, and so halting between two sides[[3 Kings 18:21||]], they have a divided mind, not one wholly united to God.

paras.t: Ipse Deus omnipotens per manum Assyriorum confringet simulacra eorum, id est idola et vitulos aureos Israelitarum, aurum et alia pretiosa sibi inde tollentium, et depopulabitur aras eorum, id est altaria idololatriæ deputata.
paras.en: He himself, God almighty, by the hand of the Assyrians, [[10:2|shall break down their idols|confringet simulacra eorum]], that is, the idols and golden calves of the Israelites, the Assyrians carrying off for themselves the gold and other precious things from them; [[10:2|he shall destroy their altars|et depopulabitur aras eorum]], that is, the altars given over to idolatry.

paras.t: Quia nunc dicent filii Israel: Non est rex nobis. Hoc dicere poterant, capto jam ultimo eorum rege Osee. Vel dixerunt hoc jam ante, ut ideo dicant, Regem non habemus, quoniam nunc quem habemus, non potest regiæ dignitatis officium exercere in nobis, adversariis nostris reluctando. Ad utrumque istorum quod sequitur, pertinet. Non enim timemus Dominum: idcirco meruimus nostrum perdere regem, nec ipse potuit nos tueri, quibus restitit Deus. Et rex quid faciet nobis? id est, quid poterit nos juvare rex homo, quum Deus rex omnipotens nobis resistat? Istud præcipue dicebant boni in decem tribubus, qui propter peccata in Deum commissa, fatebantur populum Israel opprimi.
paras.en: [[10:3|For now they shall say|Quia nunc dicent]], the children of Israel: [[10:3|We have no king|Non est rex nobis]]. They could say this once their last king, Osee, had been taken. Or they said it already before, meaning: We have no king, because the one we now have cannot exercise the office of the royal dignity among us by resisting our adversaries. What follows belongs to either reading. [[10:3|because we fear not the Lord|Non enim timemus Dominum]]: therefore we have deserved to lose our king, nor could he protect us, whom God withstood. [[10:3|and what shall a king do to us?|Et rex quid faciet nobis?]] that is, how can a human king help us, when God, the almighty King, resists us? This was said chiefly by the good among the ten tribes, who confessed that the people of Israel was being oppressed for the sins committed against God.

paras.t: Deinde Propheta ex parte Dei redarguit populum istum, verbis pseudoprophetarum acquiescentem. Loquimini verba visionis inutilis, id est, verba falsorum prophetarum, vobis pacem et prospera pollicentium, repetite cum credulitate et allegatione, quasi oppositum vobis evenire non poterit. Vel istud est verbum populi ad pseudoprophetas, a quibus desiderabant prospera sibi sponderi. Sed quoniam sponsio talis fuit conficta et fallax, sanctus Osee rem ipsam respiciens, vocat verba illa prophetica, verba visionis inutilis: quia re vera sic fuit, licet populus Israel non ita putaverit. Et simili modo dicitur in Isaia: Loquimini nobis placentia, videte nobis errores. Et ferietis fœdus cum mendacio, id est, cum sermonibus falsis seu deceptoribus vatibus consensum seu confœderationem habebitis, dicendo: Pax erit nobis. Et germinabit quasi amaritudo, id est, confœderatio ista tanquam semen amarum, producet judicium damnationis super sulcos agri, id est habitatores terræ vestræ, per modum sulcorum ab Assyriis opprimendos, eo quod tali pacto consenserint.
paras.en: Then the Prophet, on God's behalf, rebukes this people for giving ear to the words of the false prophets. [[10:4|You speak words of an unprofitable vision|Loquimini verba visionis inutilis]], that is, repeat with belief and appeal to them the words of the false prophets who promise you peace and prosperity, as though the opposite could not befall you. Or else this is the word of the people to the false prophets, by whom they wished prosperity to be promised them. But since such a promise was feigned and deceitful, holy Osee, looking to the thing itself, calls those prophetic words words of an unprofitable vision: for so in truth it was, although the people of Israel did not think so. And in like manner it is said in Isaias: [[Is 30:10|speak unto us pleasant things, see errors for us|Loquimini nobis placentia, videte nobis errores]]. [[10:4|and you shall make a covenant|Et ferietis fœdus]] with a lie [Denis's text adds *cum mendacio*, "with a lie", which is not in the Douay-Rheims or the Clementine Vulgate], that is, you shall have agreement or alliance with false speeches, or with deceiving seers, saying: Peace shall be ours[[Ezech 13:10||]]. [[10:4|shall spring up as bitterness|Et germinabit quasi amaritudo]], that is, this alliance, like a bitter seed, shall bring forth [[10:4|judgment|judicium]] of damnation [[10:4|in the furrows of the field|super sulcos agri]], that is, upon the inhabitants of your land, who are to be pressed down by the Assyrians like furrows, because they consented to such a pact.

paras.t: Vaccas Bethaven, etc. Hunc locum Hieronymus et ejus sequaces ita exponunt: Vaccas, id est vitulum aureum, qui derisorie dicitur vaccæ, ponendo plurale pro singulari, quemadmodum in Exodo dixerunt filii Israel de vitulo aureo: Isti sunt dii tui, Israel, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti; Bethaven, id est vitulum istum positum in Bethel, quæ alio nomine dicitur Bethaven, id est domus idoli; coluerunt habitatores Samariæ, id est decem tribus. Potest enim nomine Samariæ, urbs metropolitana vel tota regio decem tribuum designari. Signum autem quod coluerunt vitulum istum ex corde, est quia luxit super eum, id est de vitulo isto, populus ejus: id est, decem tribus planxerunt ac doluerunt, dum vitulus iste missus fuit regi Assyriorum, ut statim dicetur. Ingemuerunt ergo quod deus quem colebant, esset eis ablatus. Et æditui ejus, id est sacerdotes custodes vituli: æditui namque, quasi ædem idoli tuentes, dicuntur; super eum, id est de vitulo isto, exsultaverunt: quia pro vitulis aureis quos furtim sustulerunt, reposuerunt vitulos æneos deauratos. Unde quum vituli deaurati exportati fuerunt, gaudebant quod furtum eorum mansit occultum. Istud, ut refert Hieronymus, dicunt Hebræi. Exsultaverunt ergo æditui in gloria ejus, id est in auro quo vitulus tam pretiose et gloriose erat formatus; vel, In gloria ejus, id est in aureo vitulo, quod fuit gloria populi; quia migravit ab eo, id est, quia vitulus recessit a populo, secundum populi æstimationem. Putabant enim aureum vitulum sublatum, et ad Assyrios missum.
paras.en: [[10:5|the calf of Bethaven|Vaccas Bethaven]], etc. Jerome and his followers explain this place thus: [[10:5|the calf|Vaccas]], that is, the golden calf, which is called in derision *vaccæ* [that is, "cows" or "heifers", in the plural; the Douay-Rheims renders it "the calf"], putting the plural for the singular, as in Exodus the children of Israel said of the golden calf: [[Ex 32:8|These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt|Isti sunt dii tui, Israel, qui te eduxerunt de terra Ægypti]]. [[10:5|of Bethaven|Bethaven]], that is, this calf set up in Bethel, which by another name is called Bethaven, that is, house of the idol; [[10:5|The inhabitants of Samaria have worshipped|coluerunt habitatores Samariæ]], that is, the ten tribes. For by the name of Samaria may be signified the chief city or the whole country of the ten tribes. And the sign that they worshipped this calf from the heart is [[10:5|for the people thereof have mourned over it|quia luxit super eum]], that is, over this calf; [[10:5|the people thereof|populus ejus]], that is, the ten tribes, lamented and grieved when this calf was sent to the king of the Assyrians, as will be said presently. So they groaned because the god they worshipped had been taken from them. [[10:5|and the wardens of its temple|Et æditui ejus]], that is, the priests who were the calf's keepers: for they are called *æditui* as guarding the *ædes* [that is, the temple] of the idol; [[10:5|over it|super eum]], that is, over this calf, [[10:5|that rejoiced|exsultaverunt]]: because in place of the golden calves, which they had secretly carried off, they had put back calves of bronze overlaid with gold. So when the gilded calves were carried away, they rejoiced that their theft remained hidden. This, as Jerome reports, is what the Hebrews say. So the wardens rejoiced [[10:5|in its glory|in gloria ejus]], that is, in the gold of which the calf had been so richly and gloriously made; or, [[10:5|in its glory|In gloria ejus]], that is, in the golden calf, which was the glory of the people; [[10:5|because it is departed from it|quia migravit ab eo]], that is, because the calf went away from the people, as the people supposed. For they thought the golden calf had been taken away and sent to the Assyrians.

paras.t: Siquidem et ipse vitulus deauratus, in Assur delatus est, munus regi ultori, id est, regi Assyriorum transmissus est a rege Israel pro munere: qui rex Assyriorum dicitur ultor, quia fecit vindictam in regem Syriæ, impugnantem regem Israel. Legitur autem quarto Regum, quod Manahem rex Israel misit Phul regi Assyriorum mille argenti talenta, ut sibi præberet auxilium, inter quæ aliqui dicunt vitulos prædictos fuisse directos. Confusio Ephraim, id est regem Israel, qui dicitur Ephraim, quoniam primus rex decem tribuum fuerat Ephratæus, capiet, id est, operiet et implebit; et confundetur Israel in voluntate sua, id est in eo quod fecit secundum proprium placitum, non secundum Deum, procurando videlicet sibi auxilium impii regis per missionem sacrilegorum donorum. Quum enim rex Assyriorum cognovisset quod vituli non essent aurei, sed deaurati forinsecus, iratus est vehementer, putans fraudem a rege, non a sacerdotibus, factam; scripsitque regi Israel quod factum fuit: quo audito confusus est, et inde magis displicuit, unde placere speravit.
paras.en: [[10:6|For itself also|Siquidem et ipse]], the gilded calf, [[10:6|is carried into Assyria|in Assur delatus est]], [[10:6|a present to the avenging king|munus regi ultori]], that is, it was sent by the king of Israel to the king of the Assyrians as a present: and the king of the Assyrians is called the avenger because he took vengeance on the king of Syria, who was making war on the king of Israel. Now we read in the fourth book of Kings that Manahem king of Israel sent Phul king of the Assyrians a thousand talents of silver, that he might give him aid[[4 Kings 15:19||]]; and some say that the calves spoken of were sent among these. [[10:6|shame|Confusio]] [[10:6|Ephraim|Ephraim]], that is, the king of Israel, who is called Ephraim because the first king of the ten tribes had been an Ephraimite, [[10:6|shall fall upon|capiet]] [the Latin *capiet* is "shall seize"], that is, shall cover and fill him; [[10:6|and Israel shall be confounded in his own will|et confundetur Israel in voluntate sua]], that is, in what he did after his own pleasure and not according to God, namely in procuring for himself the help of an ungodly king by sending sacrilegious gifts. For when the king of the Assyrians learned that the calves were not of gold, but only gilded on the outside, he was exceedingly angry, thinking that the fraud had been committed by the king and not by the priests; and he wrote to the king of Israel what had been done: on hearing which the king was put to shame, and gave the more offence by the very thing by which he had hoped to please.

paras.t: Porro contra hanc expositionem quidam multipliciter arguit. Primo, quia videtur satis extorta. Secundo, nam conjunctio, Quia, exprimit causam dicti præcedentis; sed quod dictum est, Quia luxit populus ejus, non est causa quod habitatores Samariæ colebant vitulos. Tertio, quoniam dictum illud de furto et deauratione vitulorum, videtur confictum, eo quod Rabbi Salomon inde nil referat. Dicit ergo in Hebræo sic haberi: Ad vaccas Bethaven timuerunt habitatores Samariæ, id est, propter asportationem vituli aurei ad regem Assyriorum, timuerunt habitatores Samariæ, ne propter inhonorationem hanc vituli aliquid mali eis acciderent. Noster autem translator videtur credidisse quod timor iste fuerit reverentiæ: ideo pro Timuerunt, transtulit, Coluerunt.
paras.en: Against this explanation, however, a certain writer argues in several ways. First, because it seems rather forced. Secondly, because the conjunction *Quia* ["for", "because"] expresses the cause of what was said before; but what is said, [[10:5|for the people thereof have mourned|Quia luxit populus ejus]], is not the cause of the inhabitants of Samaria's worshipping the calves. Thirdly, because that story of the theft and gilding of the calves seems made up, since Rabbi Salomon reports nothing of it. He says, then, that the Hebrew reads thus: At the calves of Bethaven the inhabitants of Samaria feared; that is, because of the carrying off of the golden calf to the king of the Assyrians, the inhabitants of Samaria feared lest some evil should befall them on account of this dishonour done to the calf. But our translator seems to have believed that this fear was one of reverence: and so for *Timuerunt* [they feared] he put *Coluerunt* [they worshipped].

paras.t: Sed dicendum, quod expositio S. Hieronymi atque translatio ejus sint veræ; nec ad improbationem expositionis ejus sufficit simpliciter dicere quod videatur extorta. Ex prædictis etiam constat, quod non sit extorta, sed textui consona: propter quod Glossa et Beda et alii communiter eam sequuntur. Ad secundum argumentum dicendum, quod conjunctio, Quia, non semper in Scripturis dicit causam a priori, quæ est causa rei, sed sæpe denotat a posteriori, quæ est causa signi, sicut in Psalmo: Confitebor nomini tuo, Domine, quoniam bonum est; quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me. Non etiam dicit semper causam dicti præcedentis, sed subinde exprimit causam dicti sequentis, ut in illo Jeremiæ: Quia stulte egerunt pastores, propterea omnis grex eorum dissipatus est. Itemque in Psalmo: Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis super millia, elegi abjectus esse in domo Dei mei. Itaque, Quia, hoc loco notat causam a posteriori, ut lucet ex elucidatione inducta. Ad tertium dico, quod nequaquam putare debemus B. Hieronymum dictum illud de furto et deauratione vitulorum finxisse, nec diceret hoc asseri ab Hebræis, nisi de hoc certus fuisset, quia sæpissime contulit cum Hebræis. Nec sequitur: Rabbi Salomon non dicit hoc, ergo non est. Præterea translatio Hieronymi hoc loco bona est, et Hebraicæ consona veritati: imo translatio Septuaginta interpretum magis consonat translationi Hieronymi, quam litteræ quam prædictus adstruit in Hebræo haberi. Sic enim transtulerunt Septuaginta: Apud vitulum domus On morabantur, qui habitabant in Samaria. Per hoc namque, quod dicunt eos esse moratos apud vitulum domus On, id est Bethaven, datur intelligi quod cultui idoli insistebant. Verum esse potest, quod dictio Hebraica sit æquivoca ad Timuerunt, et Coluerunt.
paras.en: But it must be said that St. Jerome's explanation and his translation are true; nor is it enough, to disprove his explanation, simply to say that it seems forced. Indeed it is plain from what has been said that it is not forced but agrees with the text: and for this reason the Gloss and Bede and others commonly follow it. To the second argument it must be said that the conjunction *Quia* in the Scriptures does not always state the cause *a priori*, which is the cause of the thing, but often denotes it *a posteriori*, which is the cause of the sign [that is, the reason why we know that a thing is so, rather than the reason why it is so], as in the Psalm: I [[Ps 53:8|will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good|Confitebor nomini tuo, Domine, quoniam bonum est]]; [[Ps 53:9|For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble|quoniam ex omni tribulatione eripuisti me]]. Nor does it always state the cause of what was said before, but at times expresses the cause of what is said after, as in that word of Jeremias: [[Jer 10:21|Because the pastors have done foolishly|Quia stulte egerunt pastores]], therefore [[Jer 10:21|all their flock is scattered|omnis grex eorum dissipatus est]]. And likewise in the Psalm: [[Ps 83:11|For better is one day in thy courts above thousands. I have chosen to be an abject in the house of my God|Quia melior est dies una in atriis tuis super millia, elegi abjectus esse in domo Dei mei]]. And so *Quia* in this place marks the cause *a posteriori*, as is clear from the explanation given. To the third I say that we must by no means think that blessed Jerome invented that story of the theft and gilding of the calves; nor would he say that the Hebrews asserted it unless he had been certain of it, for he very often conferred with the Hebrews. Nor does it follow: Rabbi Salomon does not say this, therefore it is not so. Moreover, Jerome's translation in this place is good and agrees with the Hebrew verity: indeed, the translation of the Seventy interpreters agrees more with Jerome's translation than with the reading which the writer mentioned maintains is found in the Hebrew. For the Seventy translated thus: They that dwelt in Samaria lingered by the calf of the house of On. For by saying that they lingered by the calf of the house of On, that is, Bethaven, it is given to be understood that they were intent on the worship of the idol. It may well be true that the Hebrew word is equivocal, meaning both *Timuerunt* [they feared] and *Coluerunt* [they worshipped].

paras.t: Transire fecit Samaria regem suum: id est, decem tribus per idololatriam meruerunt regnum sibi auferri, et regem suum transire, id est deficere, ita quod nullum de cetero regem habent. Potest quoque specialiter accipi de ultimo rege eorum Osee, quem fecerunt secum transire in manus hostiles, per hoc quod consilium ejus abjecerunt non eundo in Jerusalem ad sacrificandum Domino, præsertim quia et ipse Osee aliunde peccavit, quamvis minus quam prædecessores ejus. Quasi spumam super faciem aquæ, id est viliter atque celeriter, sicut spuma est res vilis, et cito discurrit ac dissolvitur, currendo in superficie aquæ.
paras.en: [[10:7|Samaria hath made her king to pass|Transire fecit Samaria regem suum]]: that is, the ten tribes by their idolatry deserved to have the kingdom taken from them and their king to pass away, that is, to fail, so that from then on they have no king. It may also be taken in particular of their last king, Osee, whom they made to pass with them into the hands of their enemies, in that they rejected his counsel by not going to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord; the more so because Osee himself also sinned in other ways, though less than his predecessors. [[10:7|as froth upon the face of the water|Quasi spumam super faciem aquæ]], that is, basely and swiftly, as froth is a worthless thing, and quickly runs off and dissolves as it passes over the surface of the water.

paras.t: Et disperdentur, id est, ab Assyriis destruentur, excelsa idoli, id est loca sublimia in quibus idola coluerint: quod idolum fuit peccatum Israel, id est materia maximi peccati Israelitarum, qui in vitulorum aliorumque adoratione deorum gravissime peccaverint. Lappa et tribulus, id est herbæ infructuosæ sponte nascentes, videlicet spinæ, vepres, urticæ, etc., ascendent super aras eorum, id est super loca altarium sacrilegorum ab Assyriis destructorum: per quod insinuatur longa desolatio terræ. Et dicent, captivitate jam instante, præ vehementi pavore, montibus, Operite nos; et collibus, Cadite super nos. Per quod innuitur, quod magis optabant mori subita morte, quam videre ea quæ inferunt mortem, et crudelissimis hostibus tradi. Siquidem gravior mors exspectata, quam illata. Hoc quoque dixerunt Judæi tempore captivitatis suæ ab exercitu Romanorum, quemadmodum Christus bajulans sibi crucem, prædixit: Tunc incipient montibus dicere, Cadite super nos, etc.
paras.en: [[10:8|shall be destroyed|Et disperdentur]], that is, shall be laid waste by the Assyrians, [[10:8|the high places of the idol|excelsa idoli]], that is, the lofty places in which they worshipped idols: which idol was [[10:8|the sin of Israel|peccatum Israel]], that is, the matter of the greatest sin of the Israelites, who sinned most grievously in the adoration of the calves and other gods. [[10:8|the bur and the thistle|Lappa et tribulus]], that is, unfruitful plants that spring up of themselves, namely thorns, briars, nettles, etc., [[10:8|shall grow up over their altars|ascendent super aras eorum]], that is, over the places of the sacrilegious altars destroyed by the Assyrians: by which a long desolation of the land is hinted at. [[10:8|and they shall say|Et dicent]], when the captivity is already at hand, out of violent dread, [[10:8|to the mountains Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us|montibus, Operite nos; et collibus, Cadite super nos]]. By which it is signified that they would rather die a sudden death than see the things that bring death and be handed over to most cruel enemies. For death awaited is heavier than death inflicted. The Jews also said this in the time of their captivity by the army of the Romans, as Christ foretold when he was carrying his cross: [[Luke 23:30|Then shall they begin to say to the mountains: Fall upon us|Tunc incipient montibus dicere, Cadite super nos]], etc.

paras.t: Ex diebus Gabaa, id est a tempore quo filii Benjamin in Gabaa civitate sua sceleratissime oppresserunt uxorem Levitæ, peccavit Israel, id est duodecim tribus: non quia peccatum illud in filios Benjamin ulti sunt (in hoc enim bene fecerunt: quamvis, secundum Hieronymum, moti fuerint ad pugnam illam magis ex naturali dolore, quam amore justitiæ), sed propter illud quod subditur: ibi steterunt, id est, ulto illo peccato, non processerunt ad vindicandum injuriam Dei in filios Dan, qui idolum Michæ coluerunt. Potius quippe et primo debebant ulcisci injuriam Dei, videlicet idololatriam, et destruere idolum Michæ, quam humanam injuriam. Quia ergo non correxerunt scelus quod corrigere debebant atque valebant, participes erant in malo. Denique factum illud de idolo Michæ, contigit circa tempus quo oppressa fuit uxor Levitæ.
paras.en: [[10:9|From the days of Gabaa|Ex diebus Gabaa]], that is, from the time when the sons of Benjamin in Gabaa, their city, most wickedly abused the wife of the Levite[[Judg 19:25||]], [[10:9|Israel hath sinned|peccavit Israel]], that is, the twelve tribes: not because they avenged that sin upon the sons of Benjamin (for in this they did well, although, according to Jerome, they were moved to that battle more by natural grief than by love of justice), but because of what is added: [[10:9|there they stood|ibi steterunt]], that is, having avenged that sin, they did not go on to avenge the wrong done to God upon the sons of Dan, who worshipped the idol of Michas[[Judg 18:31||]]. For they ought rather, and first, to have avenged the wrong done to God, namely idolatry, and to have destroyed the idol of Michas, than a wrong done to man. Since, then, they did not correct a crime which they both ought and were able to correct, they were sharers in the evil. Moreover, that affair of the idol of Michas happened about the time when the wife of the Levite was abused.

paras.t: Non comprehendet eos in Gabaa prœlium. Hoc Beda ita exponit: Non comprehendet, id est, populus Israel non periit in bello contra filios Benjamin, super filios iniquitatis, id est ob id quod contra filios Benjamin prædicti sceleris auctores aut defensores congressi sunt (in hoc enim, ut dictum est, bene fecerunt); sed quoniam non vindicavit hæc plebs in primis injuriam Dei, destruendo Micham et domum ac idolum ejus, propter quod bis victi fuerunt a filiis Benjamin: et redit hoc in idem cum præinductis, quia et Micham et tribum Dan tenebantur occidere. Secundum hanc autem expositionem Propheta ponit futurum pro præterito, scilicet Comprehendet, pro Comprehendit. — Hieronymus vero videtur ita exponere: Non comprehendet, id est, non invadet ac superabit, eos, scilicet decem tribus, in Gabaa, id est ratione pugnæ quam populus Israel intulit Gabaonitis propter oppressionem uxoris præfatæ, prælium captivitatis quo jam dejiciendi sunt, sicut subjungitur.
paras.en: [[10:9|shall not overtake them|Non comprehendet eos]] [[10:9|the battle in Gabaa|in Gabaa prœlium]]. Bede explains this thus: [[10:9|shall not overtake|Non comprehendet]], that is, the people of Israel did not perish in the war against the sons of Benjamin [[10:9|against the children of iniquity|super filios iniquitatis]], that is, because they fought against the sons of Benjamin, the authors or defenders of the crime spoken of (for in this, as has been said, they did well); but because this people did not first avenge the wrong done to God by destroying Michas and his house and his idol, they were for that reason twice defeated by the sons of Benjamin[[Judg 20:21||]][[Judg 20:25||]]: and this comes to the same as what was said before, since they were bound to put to death both Michas and the tribe of Dan. According to this explanation the Prophet puts the future for the past, namely *Comprehendet* [shall overtake] for *Comprehendit* [overtook]. — Jerome, however, seems to explain it thus: [[10:9|shall not overtake|Non comprehendet]], that is, shall not fall upon and overcome, [[10:9|them|eos]], namely the ten tribes, [[10:9|in Gabaa|in Gabaa]], that is, by reason of the battle which the people of Israel waged against the Gabaonites [Denis means the men of Gabaa] for the abuse of the wife spoken of, [[10:9|the battle|prælium]] of the captivity by which they are now to be cast down, as is added.

paras.t: Juxta desiderium meum, id est, secundum propriam voluntatem et zelum justitiæ meæ, quo impiorum justam punitionem amo, corripiam eos, tradendo manibus Assyriorum. Juxta hunc modum loquendi ait Dominus in Isaia: Heu! ego consolabor super hostibus meis, et vindicabor de inimicis meis; et apud Ezechielem: Complebo furorem meum, et requiescere faciam indignationem meam, et consolabor. Itaque Deus sanctus et justus lætatur in punitione pravorum. Sed obviare videtur illud Sapientiæ: Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætatur in perditione vivorum; et illud in Tobia, Non delectaris in perditionibus nostris. Et respondendum, quod Deus non gaudet in damnatione seu punitione hominum, in quantum sunt homines, sed in quantum impœnitentes, vel in quantum temporalis afflictio expedit eis, tanquam medicinale emplastrum. Sic quoque non delectatur in ipsa perditione vel punitione, in quantum sunt quædam mala ac privativa, sed ut sunt effectus justitiæ. Propter quod ait in Proverbiis: Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, et subsannabo, quum vobis quod timebatis, evenerit. In his autem atque similibus verbis loquitur Deus affectu ac more humano, quia et desiderium proprie sumptum, videlicet pro appetitu boni absentis, non competit Deo, in quo præsentialiter æternaliterque consistit omnium bonorum atque pulchrorum ac desiderabilium perfecta possessio.
paras.en: [[10:10|According to my desire|Juxta desiderium meum]], that is, according to my own will and the zeal of my justice, by which I love the just punishment of the wicked, [[10:10|I will chastise them|corripiam eos]], by delivering them into the hands of the Assyrians. In this manner of speaking the Lord says in Isaias: [[Is 1:24|Ah! I will comfort myself over my adversaries: and I will be revenged of my enemies|Heu! ego consolabor super hostibus meis, et vindicabor de inimicis meis]]; and in Ezechiel: [[Ezech 5:13|I will accomplish my fury, and will cause my indignation to rest upon them, and I will be comforted|Complebo furorem meum, et requiescere faciam indignationem meam, et consolabor]]. So God, holy and just, rejoices in the punishment of the wicked. But that word of Wisdom seems to stand against this: [[Wis 1:13|God made not death, neither hath he pleasure in the destruction of the living|Deus mortem non fecit, nec lætatur in perditione vivorum]]; and that in Tobias: [[Tob 3:22|thou art not delighted in our being lost|Non delectaris in perditionibus nostris]]. And the answer is that God does not rejoice in the damnation or punishment of men inasmuch as they are men, but inasmuch as they are impenitent, or inasmuch as temporal affliction is good for them, like a healing plaster. So too he does not delight in perdition or punishment itself, inasmuch as these are certain evils and privative things [that is, consisting in the lack of some good], but as they are effects of justice. Wherefore he says in Proverbs: [[Prov 1:26|I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared|Ego quoque in interitu vestro ridebo, et subsannabo, quum vobis quod timebatis, evenerit]]. In these and like words God speaks with human feeling and after the manner of men; for desire, too, taken properly, namely for the appetite of an absent good, does not befit God, in whom the perfect possession of all things good and beautiful and desirable is present and eternal.

paras.t: Congregabuntur super eos populi, id est, collectim in eos irruet exercitus cum rege Assyriorum adveniens, quum corripientur propter duas iniquitates suas, id est omissionis divini cultus, et commissionis idololatriæ. Unde apud Jeremiam loquitur Dominus de regno Juda: Duo mala fecit populus meus: me dereliquerunt fontem aquæ vivæ, et foderunt sibi cisternas dissipatas. Quidam per duas iniquitates, intelligunt duos vitulos aureos; alii, quod injuriam Dei non vindicaverunt in cultoribus idoli Michæ, et vitulos aureos adoraverunt. Sed non apparet quod isti ab Assyriis capti, puniti sunt propter peccatum quod contigit tempore Michæ et Judicum. Possumus quoque, per duas iniquitates intelligere persecutionem Prophetarum et idololatriam, vel idololatriam et contemptum præcepti seu exhortationis Osee regis Israel, ut irent et sacrificia Deo offerrent in templo Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[10:10|the nations shall be gathered together against them|Congregabuntur super eos populi]], that is, the army coming with the king of the Assyrians will rush upon them in a body, [[10:10|when they shall be chastised for their two iniquities|quum corripientur propter duas iniquitates suas]], that is, the omission of the worship of God and the commission of idolatry. Hence in Jeremias the Lord says of the kingdom of Juda: [[Jer 2:13|my people have done two evils. They have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have digged to themselves cisterns, broken cisterns|Duo mala fecit populus meus: me dereliquerunt fontem aquæ vivæ, et foderunt sibi cisternas dissipatas]]. Some understand by the two iniquities the two golden calves; others, that they did not avenge the wrong done to God upon the worshippers of the idol of Michas, and that they adored the golden calves. But it does not appear that these, taken captive by the Assyrians, were punished for a sin committed in the time of Michas and of the Judges. We may also understand by the two iniquities the persecution of the Prophets and idolatry; or idolatry and contempt of the command or exhortation of Osee king of Israel that they should go and offer sacrifices to God in the temple of Jerusalem.

paras.t: Ephraim vitula docta diligere trituram. Secundum Hieronymum, locus iste usque ad finem capituli, magnis est obscuritatibus involutus. Denique consuetudo sanctarum est Scripturarum, maxime prophetalium, ut per tropologiam atque metaphoram historiæ exprimat veritatem. Ait ergo: Ephraim vitula, etc., id est, decem tribus pares sunt vaccæ seu vitulæ terenti seu trituranti in horreo, hoc est excutienti grana a paleis, ferreos orbes ad hoc deputatos super segetum acervos trahendo, secundum quod moris est grana excutere in Palæstina: quæ vitula amat trituram, id est locum trituræ, vel fruges seu messem excutiendam. Quemadmodum itaque vitula talis amat trituram, quia alitur ibi, juxta illud, Non alligabis os bovi trituranti: unde non vult inde cito exire; et si percussa ac fatigata parumper egreditur, tamen statim revertitur ut pascatur: sic populus Israel dilexit idololatriam. Et licet ob hoc frequenter castigaretur et hostibus traderetur, noluit tamen reverti ad Dominum; et si interdum rediit, non diu adhæsit, sed mox ad idololatriæ rediit vitia: quod etiam constat in libro Judicum. Cujus debita pœna subjungitur.
paras.en: [[10:11|Ephraim is a heifer taught to love to tread out corn|Ephraim vitula docta diligere trituram]]. According to Jerome, this place, as far as the end of the chapter, is wrapped in great obscurity. Now it is the custom of the holy Scriptures, especially of the prophetic ones, to express the truth of the history by tropology and metaphor [*tropologia* here means figurative speech, not the moral sense]. He says, then: [[10:11|Ephraim is a heifer|Ephraim vitula]], etc., that is, the ten tribes are like a cow or heifer treading or threshing on the floor, that is, beating the grain out from the chaff by drawing over the heaps of sheaves the iron wheels made for the purpose, as is the custom of threshing grain in Palestine: which heifer loves the threshing, that is, the threshing floor, or the grain or harvest to be threshed. So, just as such a heifer loves the threshing, because she is fed there, according to that word, [[1 Cor 9:9|Thou shalt not muzzle the mouth of the ox that treadeth out the corn|Non alligabis os bovi trituranti]][[Deut 25:4||]], and so does not wish to leave it quickly, and if, struck and wearied, she goes out for a little, yet at once returns to feed: so the people of Israel loved idolatry. And though for this they were often chastised and delivered to their enemies[[4 Kings 17:7||]], yet they would not return to the Lord; and if at times they came back, they did not cleave to him long, but soon went back to the vices of idolatry: as is also plain in the book of Judges[[Judg 2:10||]]. Its due punishment is then added.
