paras.t: Et ego transivi, id est, transire feci hostes eorum, puta Assyrios, super pulchritudinem colli ejus, id est super pulchra, delicate nutrita, superba atque rebellia colla decem tribuum, subjugando eas totaliter hostium potestati conculcantium eas. Juxta quem modum loquendi ait Isaias: Posuisti dorsum tuum transeuntibus. Deus enim resistit superbis, et dejicit eos. Ascendam super Ephraim, id est, per adventum Assyriorum opprimam eos. Arabit Judas: id est, duæ tribus, videlicet Juda et Benjamin cum filiis Levi, visa decem tribuum extrema punitione et captivitate, cœperunt corda sua excolere, et vomere pœnitentiæ a pristina duritia frangere, atque ad virtutes disponere: quod factum est tempore Ezechiæ, qui eos hortabatur ad hoc. Confringet sibi sulcos, id est, obicem gratiæ tollet a se, et virtutum dura ac terrena obstacula conteret, Jacob, id est, tam illi qui ex decem tribubus manus hostium evaserunt, et ad consilium Ezechiæ Deum verum coluerunt, venientes in Jerusalem ad faciendum Pascha, sicut per litteras eis intimaverat Ezechias (de qua re Isaias prophetice prænuntiavit, et secundo Paralipomenon clarius recitatur), quam illi qui ex regno Juda ad meliora inducti sunt ex consideratione captivitatis decem tribuum.
paras.en: [[10:11|but I passed over|Et ego transivi]], that is, I made their enemies, namely the Assyrians, to pass over [[10:11|upon the beauty of her neck|super pulchritudinem colli ejus]], that is, over the fair, delicately nourished, proud and rebellious necks of the ten tribes, subjecting them wholly to the power of enemies who trampled on them. In which manner of speaking Isaias says: Thou hast laid thy back for them that pass over[[Is 51:23||]] [the margin has *Cf.*; the Douay-Rheims reads "thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as a way to them that went over"]. For [[1 Pet 5:5|God resisteth the proud|Deus enim resistit superbis]], and casts them down. [[10:11|I will ride upon Ephraim|Ascendam super Ephraim]], that is, by the coming of the Assyrians I will crush them. [[10:11|Juda shall plough|Arabit Judas]]: that is, the two tribes, namely Juda and Benjamin with the sons of Levi, having seen the final punishment and captivity of the ten tribes, began to till their hearts, and to break them up from their former hardness with the ploughshare of penance, and to dispose them to the virtues: which was done in the time of Ezechias, who exhorted them to this[[2 Par 29:1||]][[2 Par 30:1||]]. [[10:11|shall break the furrows for himself|Confringet sibi sulcos]], that is, shall take away from himself the obstacle to grace, and shall break up the hard and earthly hindrances to the virtues, [[10:11|Jacob|Jacob]], that is, both those of the ten tribes who escaped the hands of the enemy and at the counsel of Ezechias worshipped the true God, coming to Jerusalem to keep the Pasch, as Ezechias had made known to them by letters (of which Isaias prophetically foretold[[Is 17:7||]], and which is related more clearly in the second book of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 30:1||]]), and those of the kingdom of Juda who were led on to better things by considering the captivity of the ten tribes.

paras.t: Seminate vobis in justitia, id est, opera bona secundum præcepta legis juste peragite, et velut semina quædam præmittite, ut felicem mercedem in futuro obtineatis: quæ enim seminaverit homo, hæc et metet; et metite, id est, opera bona per modum seminis sata colligite, in ore misericordiæ, id est in communicatione pietatis sinceræ, quatenus de bonis operibus non intumescatis, sed mutuo gratiam divinitus datam communicetis, secundum quod scriptum est in prima Petri epistola: Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes. Sit ergo justitia per misericordiam temperata, ne sit crudelis, sed peccatoribus condolens, omnibusque benigna, quemadmodum ad Romanos admonet Paulus: Debemus nos firmiores aliorum imbecillitatem portare, et non nobis placere. Innovate vobis, id est, ad salutem vestram intus recens facite, novale, id est cor seu agrum cordis vomere pœnitentiæ nunc proscissum. Novale enim, ad litteram, dicitur ager nunc primum proscissus. Hoc est quod admonet Apostolus: Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ, et exuite veterem hominem cum actibus suis. Propter quod orat Psalmista: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis. Oportet itaque vetera vitia abjectare, spinas passionum et tribulos inordinationum eradicare, et semen verbi cœlestis corde puro recipere. Propterea in Jeremia habetur: Novate vobis novale, et nolite serere super spinas. Qui autem passiones et vitia de agro cordis sui non abjicit, habet timere ne Christus eum visitans, dicat illud Proverbiorum: Per agrum hominis pigri transivi, et ecce totum repleverunt urticæ.
paras.en: [[10:12|Sow for yourselves in justice|Seminate vobis in justitia]], that is, do good works justly according to the precepts of the law, and send them on ahead like seeds, that you may obtain a happy reward in the time to come: for [[Gal 6:8|what things a man shall sow, those also shall he reap|quæ enim seminaverit homo, hæc et metet]]; [[10:12|and reap|et metite]], that is, gather in the good works sown as seed, [[10:12|in the mouth of mercy|in ore misericordiæ]], that is, in the sharing of sincere kindness, so that you be not puffed up over your good works, but share with one another the grace given you from God, according to what is written in the first epistle of Peter: [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]]. Let justice, then, be tempered by mercy, that it be not cruel, but compassionate to sinners and kind to all, as Paul admonishes the Romans: [[Rom 15:1|we that are stronger ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not to please ourselves|Debemus nos firmiores aliorum imbecillitatem portare, et non nobis placere]]. [[10:12|break up|Innovate vobis]] [the Latin *innovate* is "renew"], that is, make fresh within you, for your salvation, [[10:12|your fallow ground|novale]], that is, the heart, or the field of the heart, now broken up by the ploughshare of penance. For *novale*, literally, means a field now broken up for the first time. This is what the Apostle admonishes: [[Eph 4:23|be renewed in spirit of your mind|Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ]], and [[Col 3:9|stripping yourselves of the old man with his deeds|exuite veterem hominem cum actibus suis]]. Wherefore the Psalmist prays: [[Ps 50:12|Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels|Cor mundum crea in me, Deus, et spiritum rectum innova in visceribus meis]]. So we must cast away the old vices, root out the thorns of the passions and the thistles of disorder, and receive the seed of the heavenly word with a pure heart[[Luke 8:15||]]. Therefore it is said in Jeremias: [[Jer 4:3|Break up anew your fallow ground, and sow not upon thorns|Novate vobis novale, et nolite serere super spinas]]. But he who does not cast the passions and vices out of the field of his heart has cause to fear lest Christ, visiting him, say that word of Proverbs: [[Prov 24:30|I passed by the field of the slothful man|Per agrum hominis pigri transivi]], [[Prov 24:31|And behold it was all filled with nettles|et ecce totum repleverunt urticæ]].

paras.t: Pro eo quod nostra translatio continet, Innovate vobis novale, Septuaginta transtulerunt: Illuminate vobis lumen scientiæ, id est, bene agendo adipisci satagite veram prudentiam et sanctæ discretionis splendorem, per quem valeatis discernere qualiter justitia per misericordiam sit temperanda, et econtra. Sicque Propheta docet nos tria habere, dicendo: Seminate in justitia, etc. Pro quibus orat vir sanctus: Bonitatem et disciplinam et scientiam doce me. Quod autem lumen scientiæ obtineatur recte conversando seu præcepta implendo, constat ex eo quod scriptum est in Ecclesiastico: Fili, concupiscens sapientiam, conserva justitiam, et Deus præbebit illam tibi. Et iterum scriptum est: Pie agentibus dedit sapientiam.
paras.en: Where our translation has [[10:12|break up your fallow ground|Innovate vobis novale]], the Seventy translated: Light for yourselves the light of knowledge; that is, by doing well strive to gain true prudence and the splendour of holy discretion, by which you may be able to discern how justice is to be tempered by mercy, and the reverse. And so the Prophet teaches us to have three things, saying: [[10:12|Sow for yourselves in justice|Seminate in justitia]], etc. For which the holy man prays: [[Ps 118:66|Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge|Bonitatem et disciplinam et scientiam doce me]]. And that the light of knowledge is obtained by living rightly, or by fulfilling the precepts, is plain from what is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 1:33|Son, if thou desire wisdom, keep justice, and God will give her to thee|Fili, concupiscens sapientiam, conserva justitiam, et Deus præbebit illam tibi]]. And again it is written: [[Ecclus 43:37|to the godly he hath given wisdom|Pie agentibus dedit sapientiam]].

paras.t: Præterea, quia Osee novit ista doctrinæ suæ monita non esse perfecte implenda a populo, nisi pro tempore Christi ac evangelicæ legis, adjecit: Tempus autem requirendi Dominum per caritatem et reformationem perfectam ac opera bona, erit quum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam, id est Christus, quando videlicet per se ipsum, et deinde per Apostolos, evangelicæ legis perfectionem cœperit prædicare. Unde in Isaia de Christo ait Pater cœlestis: In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus plurimos. Tunc enim electi Judæi toto ad Deum conversi sunt corde. Hinc habetur in Psalmo: Orietur in diebus ejus justitia, et abundantia pacis. — Quidam exponunt istud quod ait, Quum venerit qui docebit, etc., de Ezechia rege, qui docuit populum colere Deum. Quod non videtur convenienter dictum, quia Osee hæc dixit imminente decem tribuum captivitate, quæ facta est undecimo anno imperii Achaz: et tunc Ezechias habuit viginti circiter annos. Achaz namque regnavit sedecim annis, et Ezechias cœpit regnare quum esset viginti quinque annorum. Pauci quoque ex decem tribubus acquieverunt consilio Ezechiæ. Aptius ergo de Christo accipitur, qui in Isaia protestatur, Ego qui loquor justitiam; qui præceptis legis adjecit evangelicorum consiliorum justitiam: Nisi, inquiens, abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum.
paras.en: Moreover, because Osee knew that these admonitions of his teaching would not be perfectly fulfilled by the people except in the time of Christ and of the law of the Gospel, he added: [[10:12|but the time to seek the Lord is|Tempus autem requirendi Dominum]] by charity and perfect reformation and good works [[10:12|when he shall come that shall teach you justice|quum venerit qui docebit vos justitiam]], that is, Christ, namely when he began to preach the perfection of the law of the Gospel, by himself and then by the Apostles. Hence in Isaias the heavenly Father says of Christ: [[Is 53:11|by his knowledge shall this my just servant justify many|In scientia sua justificabit ipse servus meus plurimos]] [Denis's text lacks *justus*, "just"]. For then the chosen among the Jews were converted to God with their whole heart. Hence it is said in the Psalm: [[Ps 71:7|In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace|Orietur in diebus ejus justitia, et abundantia pacis]]. — Some explain what he says, [[10:12|when he shall come that shall teach|Quum venerit qui docebit]], etc., of king Ezechias, who taught the people to worship God[[2 Par 29:1||]] [the margin gives II Par. xxix–xxxi]. But this does not seem fittingly said, since Osee said these things when the captivity of the ten tribes was at hand, which took place in the eleventh year of the reign of Achaz; and Ezechias was then about twenty years old. For Achaz reigned sixteen years[[4 Kings 16:2||]], and Ezechias began to reign when he was twenty-five years old[[4 Kings 18:2||]]. Besides, few of the ten tribes heeded the counsel of Ezechias. It is more aptly taken, then, of Christ, who declares in Isaias, [[Is 63:1|I, that speak justice|Ego qui loquor justitiam]]; who added to the precepts of the law the justice of the evangelical counsels, saying: [[Matt 5:20|unless|Nisi]], he says, [[Matt 5:20|your justice abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|abundaverit justitia vestra plus quam Scribarum et Pharisæorum, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum]].

paras.t: Consequenter ait Propheta ad decem tribus, sibi inobedientes in prædictis doctrinis: Arastis impietatem, id est, peccata in animo concepistis per cogitationem et consensum; iniquitatem messuistis, id est, ad effectum impie cogitata deduxistis, vel captivitatem pro mala aratione recepistis; comedistis frugem mendacii, id est, fructum erroris consecuti estis, et vobis incorporastis, delectando in vitiis, vel experiendo pro peccatis debitas pœnas, sicque fecistis directe contraria documentis præhabitis. Quia confisus es, o popule decem tribuum, in viis tuis, id est peccatis et actibus idololatriæ, æstimans te liberandum ab hostibus idola invocando; confisus es quoque et in multitudine fortium tuorum, id est principum, potentium atque nobilium, vel in robore tui exercitus et multitudine pugnatorum, non in Deo.
paras.en: Then the Prophet says to the ten tribes, who disobeyed him in the teachings given above: [[10:13|You have ploughed wickedness|Arastis impietatem]], that is, you conceived sins in your mind by thought and consent; [[10:13|you have reaped iniquity|iniquitatem messuistis]], that is, you carried into effect what you wickedly thought, or you received captivity in return for your evil ploughing; [[10:13|you have eaten the fruit of lying|comedistis frugem mendacii]], that is, you gained the fruit of error and took it into yourselves, by delighting in vices, or by suffering the penalties due to your sins: and so you did the direct contrary of the teachings given before. [[10:13|because thou hast trusted|Quia confisus es]], O people of the ten tribes, [[10:13|in thy ways|in viis tuis]], that is, in your sins and acts of idolatry, thinking that you would be delivered from your enemies by calling upon idols; thou hast trusted also [[10:13|in the multitude of thy strong ones|et in multitudine fortium tuorum]], that is, of your princes, mighty men and nobles, or in the strength of your army and the multitude of your fighting men, and not in God.

paras.t: Consurget tumultus in populo tuo, id est, exercitus Assyriorum cum tumultu, sonitu seu clangore invadet te; vel, Consurget tumultus, id est sonus confusus et ululatus, in populo tuo fugiente Assyrios; et omnes munitiones tuæ, id est fortalitia atque præsidia, vastabuntur ab hostibus jam præfatis; sicut vastatus, id est captus ac interfectus, est Salmana, princeps Madianitarum, a domo, id est populo seu familia, ejus, videlicet Gedeonis, qui judicavit, id est, reprobavit atque damnavit, Baal, idolum quod coluit Israel: cujus fanum quoque Gedeon destruxit, et lucum aramque demolitus est. Aliqui textus habent, Qui vindicavit Baal, id est, Gedeon in Baal vindictam exercuit. De hac re plenius legitur in libro Judicum, ubi habetur quod Gedeon cum suo exercitu persecutus est Zebee et Salmana, comprehenditque eos, et propria manu occidit. Nunc tamen dicuntur vastati a domo Gedeonis, quia cooperabatur Gedeoni in persequendo et capiendo. Consensit insuper ei in hoc, quod illos occidit. Istud itaque contigit in die prœlii, quando Gedeon cum viris trecentis pugnavit contra maximum exercitum Madianitarum, matre super filios, id est de filiorum interfectione, allisa, id est nimio mœrore confracta, vel simul cum illis occisa. Præfati namque principes cum Madianitis interfecerunt multos filiorum Israel, matribus eorum præsentibus, quæ multo mœrore confectæ, vel simul occisæ defecerunt. Legitur quoque in Judicum libro, quod Gedeon dixit Zebee et Salmana: Quales fuerunt viri quos occidistis in Thabor? Qui responderunt: Similes tui, et unus ex eis quasi filius regis. Quibus Gedeon dixit: Fratres mei fuerunt, filii matris meæ. Vivit Dominus, si servassetis eos, non vos occiderem. Unde quod ait Propheta, Matre super filios allisa, specialiter accipi potest de matre hac, tam speciosis filiis destituta.
paras.en: [[10:14|A tumult shall arise among thy people|Consurget tumultus in populo tuo]], that is, the army of the Assyrians will fall upon thee with tumult, din or blare of trumpets; or, [[10:14|A tumult shall arise|Consurget tumultus]], that is, a confused noise and wailing, among thy people as they flee from the Assyrians; [[10:14|and all thy fortresses|et omnes munitiones tuæ]], that is, strongholds and garrisons, [[10:14|shall be destroyed|vastabuntur]] by the enemies already named; [[10:14|as Salmana was destroyed|sicut vastatus]], that is, taken and slain, [[10:14|Salmana|est Salmana]], prince of the Madianites, [[10:14|by the house|a domo]], that is, the people or household, [[10:14|of him|ejus]], namely of Gedeon, [[10:14|that judged|qui judicavit]], that is, rejected and condemned, [[10:14|Baal|Baal]], the idol which Israel worshipped: whose shrine also Gedeon destroyed, and pulled down its grove and altar[[Judg 6:25||]][[Judg 6:27||]]. Some texts have: Who avenged Baal, that is, Gedeon took vengeance on Baal. Of this matter we read more fully in the book of Judges, where it is told that Gedeon with his army pursued Zebee and Salmana, took them, and slew them with his own hand. Yet they are here said to be destroyed by the house of Gedeon, because it worked with Gedeon in pursuing and taking them; and it consented with him, moreover, in his slaying them. This, then, happened [[10:14|in the day of battle|in die prœlii]], when Gedeon with three hundred men fought against the very great army of the Madianites, [[10:14|the mother|matre]] [[10:14|upon her children|super filios]], that is, at the slaying of her sons, [[10:14|being dashed in pieces|allisa]], that is, broken by excessive grief, or else slain together with them. For the princes named, with the Madianites, slew many of the sons of Israel in the presence of their mothers, who, worn out with great grief, or slain with them, perished. We read also in the book of Judges that Gedeon said to Zebee and Salmana: [[Judg 8:18|What manner of men were they, whom you slew in Thabor? They answered: They were like thee, and one of them as the son of a king|Quales fuerunt viri quos occidistis in Thabor? Qui responderunt: Similes tui, et unus ex eis quasi filius regis]]. To whom Gedeon said: [[Judg 8:19|They were my brethren, the sons of my mother. As the Lord liveth, if you had saved them, I would not kill you|Fratres mei fuerunt, filii matris meæ. Vivit Dominus, si servassetis eos, non vos occiderem]]. Hence what the Prophet says, [[10:14|the mother being dashed in pieces upon her children|Matre super filios allisa]], may be taken in particular of this mother, bereft of such comely sons.

paras.t: Sic fecit vobis, o decem tribus, Bethel, id est idololatria quam exercuistis in urbe Bethel, in qua unus positus erat de aureis vitulis, quem colendo meruistis perire, quemadmodum periit Salmana: et hoc, a facie malitiæ nequitiarum vestrarum, id est propter perversitatem vitiorum vestrorum, quæ adspexi, et oculis meis præsentia erant. Vel per Bethel intelligitur vitulus aureus, qui fuit eis materia occasioque peccandi; vel certe sacerdotes vituli habitantes in Bethel, qui populum in idololatria confortabant.
paras.en: [[10:15|So hath Bethel done to you|Sic fecit vobis]], O ten tribes, [[10:15|Bethel|Bethel]], that is, the idolatry you practised in the city of Bethel, in which one of the golden calves had been set up, by worshipping which you deserved to perish as Salmana perished: and this [[10:15|because of the evil of your iniquities|a facie malitiæ nequitiarum vestrarum]], that is, for the perversity of your vices, which I beheld, and which were present before my eyes [Denis's *a facie*, literally "from the face", is rendered "because of" in the Douay-Rheims]. Or by Bethel is understood the golden calf, which was to them the matter and occasion of sinning; or else the priests of the calf dwelling in Bethel, who strengthened the people in idolatry.

10.title: Elucidatio tropologica ejusdem capituli decimi.
10.title_en: Tropological explanation of the same tenth chapter.

paras.t: De militanti denique Ecclesia Christi veraciter dicitur: Vitis frondosa Israel: Ecclesia enim Israel nuncupatur, quoniam oculis fidei conspicit Deum. Habet ergo hæc vitis frondes magnas atque pulcherrimas, puta Apostolos et apostolicæ perfectionis imitatores, virore virtutum splendentes, ipsamque Ecclesiam mirabiliter adornantes, qui primitias Spiritus receperunt; qui etiam botri vocantur, vinum sapientiæ continentes, et internæ refectionis nobis propinantes saporem. De qua vinea in Canticis scriptum est: Vinea fuit pacifico in ea quæ habet populos. De qua in Evangelio ait Salvator: Ite et vos in vineam meam. Sed et Christus qui est verissimus Israelita, tanquam vir videns Deum per speciem a maternæ suæ conceptionis exordio, vocat se vineam: Ego, inquiens, sum vitis vera, et Pater meus agricola est. Ipse enim spiritualiter protulit botros Ecclesiæ.
paras.en: Lastly, of the Church of Christ militant it is truly said: [[10:1|Israel a vine full of branches|Vitis frondosa Israel]]. For the Church is called Israel because she beholds God with the eyes of faith [the name Israel being interpreted "a man seeing God"]. This vine therefore has great and most beautiful branches, namely the Apostles and the imitators of apostolic perfection, shining with the green freshness of the virtues and wonderfully adorning the Church herself, who received the firstfruits of the Spirit[[Rom 8:23||]]; and they are also called clusters, since they hold the wine of wisdom and pour out for us the savour of inward refreshment. Of this vineyard it is written in the Canticle: [[Cant 8:11|The peaceable had a vineyard, in that which hath people|Vinea fuit pacifico in ea quæ habet populos]]. Of it the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Matt 20:4|Go you also into my vineyard|Ite et vos in vineam meam]][[Matt 20:7||]]. And Christ too, who is the truest Israelite, as a man seeing God by sight [that is, by open vision, not by faith] from the very beginning of his conception in his mother, calls himself the vineyard: [[John 15:1|I|Ego]], he says, [[John 15:1|am the true vine: and my Father is the husbandman|sum vitis vera, et Pater meus agricola est]]. For it is he who spiritually brought forth the clusters of the Church.

paras.t: Fructus adæquatus est ei: id est, vinea ista secundum gratiam sibi concessam, copiosum attulit fructum, optime conversando, alios convertendo, instruendo, perficiendo, et in omni dono Spiritus Sancti quotidie proficiendo. Nec enim unquam tanta gratia alicui congregationi collata est, ut Ecclesiæ Christianorum. Propter quod tempus novæ legis vocatur tempus gratiæ. Porro qui satagit digne conversari vocatione qua vocatus est, et dicere potest cum Apostolo, Gratia Dei in me vacua non fuit, iste adæquat fructum gratiæ sibi exhibitæ, et dignus est nomine christiano.
paras.en: [[10:1|the fruit is agreeable to it|Fructus adæquatus est ei]] [Latin *adæquatus*, "made equal": Denis takes it of fruit that matches the grace received]; that is, this vineyard, according to the grace granted her, has borne abundant fruit, by living most excellently, by converting others, by instructing and perfecting them, and by advancing daily in every gift of the Holy Ghost. For never was so great a grace bestowed on any assembly as on the Church of the Christians. For which reason the time of the New Law is called the time of grace[[Eph 2:7||]]. Further, he who takes care to live worthily of the calling to which he is called[[Eph 4:1||]], and can say with the Apostle, The grace of God [[1 Cor 15:10|in me hath not been void|in me vacua non fuit]], makes his fruit equal to the grace shown him, and is worthy of the Christian name.

paras.t: Secundum multitudinem fructus sui multiplicavit altaria. Hoc accipi potest in bono, quod Ecclesia multiplicavit materialia templa atque altaria, secundum multitudinem fructus sui, id est secundum eminentiam devotionis sibi infusæ; vel secundum quod in exterioribus divitiis abundavit, cupiens cultum Dei et oblationem sacrificii evangelicæ legis multiplicari, et toto orbe diffundi. Juxta ubertatem terræ suæ, id est fecunditatem sui cordis, in quo, tanquam in bona terra, verbum Dei receptum est atque fructificavit, exuberavit simulacris, id est imaginibus Crucifixi et Sanctorum, qui sunt quasi scripturæ simplicium, et memoriam provocant, devotionemque inflammant; vel, Exuberavit simulacris, id est formis seu speciebus intelligibilibus divinorum, quæ jugiter contemplatur, ex visibilibus invisibilia contuendo, et in cœlestium memoria se indesinenter (quantum vitæ præsentis permittit fragilitas) occupando. Utinam animæ nostræ bonis simulacris dominicæ passionis, horrendæ mortis, futuri judicii, cœlestium gaudiorum, infernaliumque pœnarum depingantur.
paras.en: [[10:1|according to the multitude of his fruit, he hath multiplied altars|Secundum multitudinem fructus sui multiplicavit altaria]]. This can be taken in a good sense: that the Church has multiplied material temples and altars according to the multitude of her fruit, that is, according to the eminence of the devotion poured into her; or according as she has abounded in outward riches, desiring that the worship of God and the offering of the sacrifice of the gospel law be multiplied and spread through the whole world. [[10:1|according to the plenty of his land|Juxta ubertatem terræ suæ]], that is, the fruitfulness of her heart, in which, as in good ground, the word of God has been received and has borne fruit[[Luke 8:15||]], [[10:1|he hath abounded with idols|exuberavit simulacris]] [Latin *simulacris*, "images"], that is, with images of the Crucified and of the Saints, which are as it were the writings of the simple, and stir the memory and kindle devotion; or, [[10:1|he hath abounded with idols|Exuberavit simulacris]], that is, with intelligible forms or species [that is, the likenesses by which the mind knows things] of divine things, which she contemplates continually, beholding the invisible things through the visible, and occupying herself unceasingly (so far as the frailty of the present life allows) in the remembrance of heavenly things. Would that our souls were painted with the good images of the Lord's passion, of dreadful death, of the judgment to come, of the joys of heaven, and of the pains of hell!

paras.t: Præterea accipi possunt ista in malo, de ingratis et reprobis, qui multitudine beneficiorum Christi abutentes, vanitates sibi quasi altaria quædam multiplicant, in quibus offerunt diabolo sua obsequia, non Dei, sed proprium desiderantes honorem. Exuberant quoque simulacris, id est mundanis cogitationibus, inutilibus phantasiis, cogitantes de feminis et pecuniis, de fama gloriaque terrena. Quibus dicit Joannes: Custodite vos a simulacris; et Dominus per Isaiam: Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis. Horum Deus confringet simulacra, et depopulabitur aras, quando ipsi cum vanitatibus et phantasmatibus suis condemnabuntur: quia nec opus nec ratio erunt apud inferos. Et in Job habetur: Vidi impios Domino flante periisse. De quibus cantatur in Psalmo: Iter impiorum peribit; et iterum, Quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent.
paras.en: These words can also be taken in a bad sense, of the ungrateful and reprobate, who, abusing the multitude of Christ's benefits, multiply vanities for themselves as so many altars, on which they offer their service to the devil, desiring not God's honour but their own. They abound also with idols, that is, with worldly thoughts and useless fancies, thinking of women and money, of fame and earthly glory. To them John says: [[1 John 5:21|keep yourselves from idols|Custodite vos a simulacris]]; and the Lord through Isaias: [[Is 1:16|take away the evil of your devices from my eyes|Auferte malum cogitationum vestrarum ab oculis meis]]. God [[10:2|shall break down their idols|confringet simulacra]], and [[10:2|shall destroy their altars|depopulabitur aras]], when they shall be condemned with their vanities and phantasms: for [[Eccles 9:10|neither work, nor reason|nec opus nec ratio]] [[Eccles 9:10|shall be in hell|erunt apud inferos]] [the margin gives Eccle. iv, 10; the words are from Eccles 9:10]. And it is said in Job: [[Job 4:8|I have seen|Vidi]] the wicked [[Job 4:9|perishing by the blast of God|Domino flante periisse]]. Of them it is sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 1:6|the way of the wicked shall perish|Iter impiorum peribit]]; and again, [[Ps 36:2|For they shall shortly wither away as grass|Quoniam tanquam fœnum velociter arescent]].

paras.t: Hi frequenter merentur bonis privari rectoribus, et tanquam oves errantes dimitti; tuncque dicere possunt: Non est rex nobis. Sed quoniam inter perversos communiter inveniuntur aliqui boni, qui propter peccata sua vel cohabitantium sibi pensant id factum, idcirco in horum persona subjungitur: Non enim timemus Dominum. Justi quippe solent se impiis, cum quibus sunt, et quorum peccata deplorant, connumerari, quemadmodum Esdras et Daniel. Unde Esdras: Peccata, inquit, nostra creverunt usque ad cœlos. Et rex quid faciet nobis? id est, princeps seu pastor nil proficit subditis, nisi Deus adsit per gratiam. Nisi enim Dominus ædificaverit domum et custodierit civitatem, inaniter laboratur.
paras.en: Such men often deserve to be deprived of good rulers and to be left like straying sheep; and then they can say: [[10:3|We have no king|Non est rex nobis]]. But since among the wicked some good men are commonly found, who reckon that this has come about on account of their own sins or those of the people they live among, therefore in their person is added: [[10:3|because we fear not the Lord|Non enim timemus Dominum]]. For the just are wont to number themselves with the wicked among whom they are and whose sins they lament, as did Esdras and Daniel. Hence Esdras: [[1 Esd 9:6|our sins|Peccata]], he says, [[1 Esd 9:6|are grown up even unto heaven|creverunt usque ad cœlos]]. [[10:3|and what shall a king do to us?|Et rex quid faciet nobis?]] That is, a prince or pastor profits his subjects nothing unless God be present by grace. For [[Ps 126:1|unless the Lord build the house|Nisi enim Dominus ædificaverit domum]] and [[Ps 126:1|keep the city|custodierit civitatem]], the labour is in vain.

paras.t: Loquimini verba visionis inutilis. Hoc derisorie dicitur contra somniatores et somniorum observatores, qui suas imaginationes vel diabolicas illusiones advertunt, reputant et enarrant, quasi visiones prophetias: quod in Levitico prohibetur, Non observabitis somnia; et in Ecclesiastico inducitur, Quasi qui apprehendit umbram et sequitur ventum, secundum hoc visio somniorum. Rursusque ait Scriptura: Somnia extollunt imprudentes. Ferietis fœdus cum mendacio. Hoc agunt fraudulenti, mendosi, simulatores, et callidi, qui in sua vulpina calliditate atque palliata confidunt astutia; qui dicunt illud Isaiæ: Posuimus mendacium spem nostram, et mendacio protecti sumus. Istis germinabit, seu orietur, quasi amaritudo amarissima damnationis judicium, quum Deus apprehenderit astutos in astutia eorum, et perdere cœperit omnes qui loquuntur mendacium. Feriamus igitur fœdus cum veritate, immobiliter inhærentes testimoniis Scripturarum, et veritas certissime liberabit nos.
paras.en: [[10:4|You speak words of an unprofitable vision|Loquimini verba visionis inutilis]]. This is said in mockery against dreamers and observers of dreams, who heed, weigh and tell over their own imaginings or the illusions of the devil as though they were visions and prophecies: which is forbidden in Leviticus, You shall not [[Lev 19:26|observe dreams|observabitis somnia]]; and is set forth in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 34:2|like to him that catcheth at a shadow, and followeth after the wind|Quasi qui apprehendit umbram et sequitur ventum]], even so is [[Ecclus 34:3|the vision of dreams|visio somniorum]]. And again Scripture says: [[Ecclus 34:1|dreams lift up fools|Somnia extollunt imprudentes]]. [[10:4|and you shall make a covenant|Ferietis fœdus]] with a lie. This is what the deceitful do, the lying, the dissemblers and the crafty, who trust in their foxlike cunning and cloaked astuteness; who say that word of Isaias: [[Is 28:15|we have placed our hope in lies, and by falsehood we are protected|Posuimus mendacium spem nostram, et mendacio protecti sumus]]. For these [[10:4|shall spring up|germinabit]], or shall arise, [[10:4|as bitterness|quasi amaritudo]] most bitter, the [[10:4|judgment|judicium]] of damnation, when God shall catch the crafty [[Job 5:13|in their craftiness|in astutia eorum]], and shall begin to destroy [[Ps 5:7|all that speak a lie|omnes qui loquuntur mendacium]]. Let us then make a covenant with the truth, cleaving immovably to the testimonies of the Scriptures, and the truth will most surely set us free[[John 8:32||]].

paras.t: Vaccas Bethaven, id est lascivias carnis, coluerunt habitatores Samariæ, id est hi qui se dicunt et simulant permanere in custodia præceptorum Christi: quales sunt hypocritæ, clerici lubrici, et carnales religiosi. Samaria autem custoditio interpretatur. Quia luxit super eum populus ejus. Hoc fit, dum boni subditi, et vulgus indoctum, sed timoratum, superiorum suorum et clericorum ac religiosorum turpiter conversantium peccata deplangit. Et æditui ejus super eum exsultaverunt. Hoc plane contingit, dum summi prælati ac sacerdotes, qui esse tenentur diligentissimi custodes Ecclesiæ, de prædictorum lubrica conversatione lætantur, gaudentes de hoc quod sibi parificantur in vitiis carnis.
paras.en: [[10:5|the calf of Bethaven|Vaccas Bethaven]] [Latin *vaccas*, "the cows"], that is, the wantonness of the flesh, [[10:5|the inhabitants of Samaria have worshipped|coluerunt habitatores Samariæ]], that is, those who say and pretend that they abide in the keeping of Christ's commandments: such as hypocrites, unchaste clerics and carnal religious. For Samaria is interpreted *keeping*. [[10:5|for the people thereof have mourned over it|Quia luxit super eum populus ejus]]. This comes about when good subjects, and the unlearned but God-fearing common people, bewail the sins of their superiors, and of clerics and religious who live shamefully. [[10:5|and the wardens of its temple that rejoiced over it|Et æditui ejus super eum exsultaverunt]]. This plainly happens when the highest prelates and priests, who are bound to be the most diligent guardians of the Church, take pleasure in the unchaste life of those just named, rejoicing that these are made their equals in the vices of the flesh.

paras.t: Siquidem et ipse vitulus, id est motus lascivus, in Assur delatus est, id est ad diabolum dirigentem ad mala: Assur enim interpretatur dirigens; munus regi ultori, id est principi tenebrarum, per quem divina justitia ulciscitur hominum crimina, cui et impii dant se ipsos et opera sua. Quocontra monet Apostolus: Nolite locum dare diabolo.
paras.en: [[10:6|For itself also|Siquidem et ipse]], the calf, that is, the wanton impulse, [[10:6|is carried into Assyria|in Assur delatus est]], that is, to the devil, who directs to evil deeds: for Assur is interpreted *directing*; [[10:6|a present to the avenging king|munus regi ultori]], that is, to the prince of darkness, through whom divine justice avenges the crimes of men, and to whom the wicked give both themselves and their works. Against which the Apostle warns: [[Eph 4:27|Give not place to the devil.|Nolite locum dare diabolo]]

paras.t: Confusio operiet Ephraim, id est eos qui temporalia thesaurizant. Dives enim quum obierit, nihil secum auferet; apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia, ut dicitur in Job. Ephraim autem interpretatur augmentum. Et confundetur Israel, id est quicumque fidelis, in voluntate sua, id est, propriæ voluntatis affectiones, non divina præcepta, sequendo, nec ejus inhærendo vestigiis qui ait: Descendi de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me. In quo inobedientes, præsertim religiosi rebelles et murmuratores notantur. Propter quod ad Hebræos jubet Apostolus: Obedite præpositis vestris, et subjacete illis. Porro, si nostra voluntas divina caritate formetur, et præceptis dominicis subjiciatur; tunc opus bonum erit tanto amplius Deo gratum ac meritorium, quanto vehementius ex voluntate agentis procedit, quoniam Deus magis pensat muneratque affectum quam opus. Sed tunc voluntas hominis est magis divina quam humana dicenda. Grandis ergo perfectio est, voluntate tota ac prompta facere quod jubetur, suadetur, aut postulatur.
paras.en: [[10:6|shame shall fall upon Ephraim|Confusio operiet Ephraim]], that is, upon those who hoard up temporal things. For [[Job 27:19|the rich man|Dives]] when he dies [[Job 27:19|shall take away nothing with him|nihil secum auferet]]; [[Job 27:20|Poverty like water shall take hold on him|apprehendet eum quasi aqua inopia]], as is said in Job. For Ephraim is interpreted *increase*. [[10:6|and Israel shall be confounded|Et confundetur Israel]], that is, every believer, [[10:6|in his own will|in voluntate sua]]: that is, by following the inclinations of his own will, not the divine commandments, and not cleaving to the footsteps of him who says: [[John 6:38|I came down from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him that sent me|Descendi de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me]]. In this the disobedient are censured, especially rebellious and murmuring religious. For which reason the Apostle commands in the Epistle to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:17|Obey your prelates and be subject to them|Obedite præpositis vestris, et subjacete illis]]. Further, if our will be formed by divine charity and subjected to the Lord's commandments, then a good work will be the more pleasing to God and the more meritorious the more strongly it proceeds from the will of the doer, since God weighs and rewards the affection more than the work. But then the will of man is to be called divine rather than human. It is therefore a great perfection to do with the whole and ready will what is commanded, counselled, or asked.

paras.t: Transire fecit Samaria regem suum. Sic multi perversi merentur sibi auferri prælatum seu principem bonum.
paras.en: [[10:7|Samaria hath made her king to pass|Transire fecit Samaria regem suum]]. So many wicked men deserve to have a good prelate or prince taken from them.

paras.t: Præterea in die judicii dicturi sunt reprobi quod subditur: Dicent montibus, Operite nos; et collibus, Cadite super nos. Tantus enim erit horror illius judicii, ut sanctus Job dicat: Quis mihi tribuat ut in inferno protegas me et abscondas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus? Hinc scriptum est in Apocalypsi: Reges terræ, principes et tribuni, divites et fortes, absconderunt se in speluncis et petris montium, dicentes montibus et petris: Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni.
paras.en: Moreover, on the day of judgment the reprobate will say what follows: [[10:8|they shall say to the mountains Cover us; and to the hills: Fall upon us|Dicent montibus, Operite nos; et collibus, Cadite super nos]]. For so great will be the horror of that judgment that holy Job says: [[Job 14:13|Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell, and hide me till thy wrath pass|Quis mihi tribuat ut in inferno protegas me et abscondas me, donec pertranseat furor tuus?]] Hence it is written in the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 6:15|the kings of the earth and the princes and tribunes and the rich and the strong|Reges terræ, principes et tribuni, divites et fortes]] [[Apoc 6:15|hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of mountains|absconderunt se in speluncis et petris montium]], saying [[Apoc 6:16|to the mountains and the rocks: Fall upon us and hide us from the face of him that sitteth upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb|montibus et petris: Cadite super nos, et abscondite nos a facie sedentis super thronum, et ab ira Agni]].

paras.t: Ex diebus Gabaa, id est a tempore elationis, peccavit Israel, id est fidelis infideliter agens: nam ex superbia oriuntur diversa peccata. Gabaa autem interpretatur collis, quo nomine designatur elatio. Hinc scriptum est in Tobia: Superbiam in animo tuo nunquam dominari permittas. Congregabuntur super eos populi, id est, contra impios Christianos convenient alii ad debellandum eos, quum corripientur propter duas iniquitates suas, id est propter peccatum in Deum et in proximum. Interdum enim dat Deus impios hostibus suis propter hæc duo peccata. Peccatum vero in Deum est, quod fit contra tria præcepta primæ tabulæ; quod autem fit contra præcepta secundæ tabulæ, est peccatum in proximum.
paras.en: [[10:9|From the days of Gabaa|Ex diebus Gabaa]], that is, from the time of pride [Latin *elatio*, a lifting up of oneself], [[10:9|Israel hath sinned|peccavit Israel]], that is, the believer acting unbelievingly: for from pride arise sins of every kind. For Gabaa is interpreted *hill*, and by this name pride is signified. Hence it is written in Tobias: [[Tob 4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind|Superbiam in animo tuo nunquam dominari permittas]]. [[10:10|and the nations shall be gathered together against them|Congregabuntur super eos populi]], that is, against wicked Christians others will come together to overcome them, [[10:10|when they shall be chastised for their two iniquities|quum corripientur propter duas iniquitates suas]], that is, for sin against God and against their neighbour. For at times God gives the wicked over to their enemies on account of these two sins. Sin against God is that which is done against the three commandments of the first table; but that which is done against the commandments of the second table is sin against one's neighbour.

paras.t: Ephraim vitula docta diligere trituram. Hoc competit his qui non emendantur flagellis, vel qui lassantur in via perditionis et ambulant vias difficiles, jugumque Christi suave ac leve abjiciunt, qui in contrectatione terrenarum rerum infatigabiliter occupantur: quod est, hujusmodi homines vitulæ trituranti sunt similes, ut patet ex proprietatibus vitulæ talis, in præcedenti articulo positis. Et ego transivi super pulchritudinem colli ejus, id est, talium colla humiliavi, et per pœnas mihi subjeci. Propter quod in Isaia legitur: Pro eo quod elevatæ sunt filiæ Sion, et ambulabant collo extento, nudabit Dominus verticem filiarum Sion. Et in Ecclesiastico Sapientia ait: Omnium excellentium et sublimium colla propria virtute calcavi. Solet enim in colli erectione cordis superbia demonstrari atque rebellio, juxta illud in Job: Cucurrit impius adversus Deum erecto collo.
paras.en: [[10:11|Ephraim is a heifer taught to love to tread out corn|Ephraim vitula docta diligere trituram]]. This fits those who are not amended by scourges, or who weary themselves in the way of perdition and walk hard ways[[Wis 5:7||]], and cast off the sweet and light yoke of Christ[[Matt 11:30||]], who are tirelessly busied in handling earthly things: that is, such men are like a heifer treading out corn, as is clear from the properties of such a heifer set out in the preceding article. [[10:11|but I passed over upon the beauty of her neck|Et ego transivi super pulchritudinem colli ejus]], that is, I have humbled the necks of such men and subjected them to me by punishments. For which reason we read in Isaias: [[Is 3:16|Because the daughters of Sion are haughty, and have walked with stretched out necks|Pro eo quod elevatæ sunt filiæ Sion, et ambulabant collo extento]], [[Is 3:17|the Lord will make bald the crown of the head of the daughters of Sion|nudabit Dominus verticem filiarum Sion]]. And in Ecclesiasticus Wisdom says: The necks of all the high and lofty I have trodden down by my own power[[Ecclus 24:11||]] [Denis reads *colla*, "necks", where the Vulgate has *corda*, "hearts", and *sublimium*, "lofty", for *humilium*, "low"]. For the pride and rebellion of the heart is wont to be shown in the raising of the neck, according to that word in Job: The wicked [[Job 15:26|hath run against|Cucurrit]] God [[Job 15:26|with his neck raised up|erecto collo]].

paras.t: Ascendam super Ephraim, id est, debitas castigationes super prædictos perversos inducam. Arabit Judas: id est, verus confessor fidei et actu ecclesiasticus, visa impiorum punitione, cor suum ad meliora disponet, et ferro pœnitentiæ ad gratiæ susceptionem pleniorem aperiet atque aptabit: tunc enim lavat in sanguine peccatoris manus suas. Et in Proverbiis habetur: Pestilente flagellato, stultus sapientior erit. Confringet sibi sulcos Jacob: id est, contra vitia luctans, eademque supplantans, cordis sui a se removebit duritiam, et franget se ipsum, petens sibi dari cor carneum, sciens scriptum: Qui cordis est duri, incidet in mala. Hoc nempe est quod docet Salvator: Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum. Sulci autem animæ, sunt duri inordinatique motus, et universa gratiæ impedimenta. Hac quoque confractione præcipue egent, qui ex naturali dispositione iracundi, superbi, pertinaces, vel ad alia mala proclives sunt.
paras.en: [[10:11|I will ride upon Ephraim|Ascendam super Ephraim]] [Latin *ascendam*, "I will go up"], that is, I will bring due chastisements upon the wicked men just named. [[10:11|Juda shall plough|Arabit Judas]] [Juda being interpreted "confession"]: that is, the true confessor of the faith, a churchman in deed, seeing the punishment of the wicked, will dispose his heart to better things, and with the iron of penance [as with a ploughshare] will open it up and make it fit for a fuller reception of grace: for then [[Ps 57:11|he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner|lavat in sanguine peccatoris manus suas]]. And it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 19:25|The wicked man being scourged, the fool shall be wiser|Pestilente flagellato, stultus sapientior erit]]. [[10:11|Jacob shall break the furrows for himself|Confringet sibi sulcos Jacob]]: that is, wrestling against vices and supplanting them [Jacob being interpreted "supplanter"], he will remove from himself the hardness of his heart and will break himself, asking that a heart of flesh be given him[[Ezech 11:19||]], knowing that it is written: [[Prov 28:14|he that is hardened in mind shall fall into evil|Qui cordis est duri, incidet in mala]] [Denis reads "hard of heart" where the Vulgate has "hard of mind"]. This indeed is what the Saviour teaches: [[Luke 9:23|If any man will come after me, let him deny himself|Qui vult venire post me, abneget semetipsum]]. Now the furrows of the soul are hard and disordered impulses, and all hindrances to grace. And those have special need of this breaking who by natural disposition are wrathful, proud, stubborn, or prone to other evils.

paras.t: Arastis impietatem, iniquitatem messuistis, comedistis frugem mendacii. Arat impietatem, qui malum propositum concipit, et ad peccandum animam suam disponit, quemadmodum in Proverbiis dicitur: Cor cogitans cogitationes pessimas. Metit autem iniquitatem, qui procedit in opus. Comedit vero frugem mendacii, qui lætatur quum male fecerit, et in malitia gloriatur. Unde de impiis scriptum est in Proverbiis: Comedent igitur fructus suos, suisque consiliis saturabuntur. Comedunt quoque frugem mendacii, qui debitis afficiuntur et adimplentur tormentis, prout apud Jeremiam Dominus protestatur: Ecce ego cibabo populum istum absinthio, et potabo eos felle. Qui autem opus Dei reverenter delectabiliterque persolvit, comedit frugem justitiæ, et cum Christo dicere potest illud Joannis: Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei qui in cœlis est.
paras.en: [[10:13|You have ploughed wickedness, you have reaped iniquity, you have eaten the fruit of lying|Arastis impietatem, iniquitatem messuistis, comedistis frugem mendacii]]. He ploughs wickedness who conceives an evil purpose and disposes his soul to sin, as is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 6:18|A heart that deviseth wicked plots|Cor cogitans cogitationes pessimas]]. He reaps iniquity who goes on to the deed. And they eat the fruit of lying who [[Prov 2:14|are glad when they have done evil|lætatur quum male fecerit]], and [[Ps 51:3|glory in malice|in malitia gloriatur]]. Hence it is written of the wicked in Proverbs: [[Prov 1:31|Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way, and shall be filled with their own devices.|Comedent igitur fructus suos, suisque consiliis saturabuntur]] They too eat the fruit of lying who are visited with and filled with the torments they have deserved, as the Lord declares in Jeremias: [[Jer 9:15|Behold I will feed this people with wormwood|Ecce ego cibabo populum istum absinthio]], [[Jer 23:15|and will give them gall to drink|et potabo eos felle]] [the margin gives Jer. xxiii, 15; Denis's first words are those of Jer 9:15]. But he who performs the work of God with reverence and delight eats the fruit of justice, and can say with Christ that word of John: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem]] of my Father who is in heaven [Denis ends with words from Matt 7:21; in John the verse ends "of him that sent me"].

paras.t: Quia confisus es in viis tuis. Quidam confidunt in viis propriæ pravitatis, de quibus scriptum est in Isaia: Confidunt in nihili, et loquuntur vanitates. Alii vero confidunt in viis suæ justitiæ, putantes se aliquid esse, et dicentes se divites, non attendentes imperfectiones ac negligentias suas. Et in multitudine fortium tuorum. Isti enim confidunt in fortibus actibus suis, non sequentes vestigia ejus qui profitetur: Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius; et alterius, Omnes justitiæ nostræ quasi pannus menstruatæ. Unde Job loquitur: Etiam si justus fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea.
paras.en: [[10:13|because thou hast trusted in thy ways|Quia confisus es in viis tuis]]. Some trust in the ways of their own wickedness, of whom it is written in Isaias: [[Is 59:4|they trust in a mere nothing, and speak vanities|Confidunt in nihili, et loquuntur vanitates]]. Others trust in the ways of their own justice, thinking themselves to be something[[Gal 6:3||]], and calling themselves rich[[Apoc 3:17||]], not heeding their own imperfections and negligences. And [[10:13|in the multitude of thy strong ones|in multitudine fortium tuorum]]. For these trust in their own strong deeds, not following the footsteps of him who professes: [[Ps 70:16|O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone|Domine, memorabor justitiæ tuæ solius]]; and of another: [[Is 64:6|all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|Omnes justitiæ nostræ quasi pannus menstruatæ]]. Hence Job says: [[Job 9:21|Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of|Etiam si justus fuero, hoc ipsum ignorabit anima mea]] [Denis reads *justus*, "just", where the Vulgate has *simplex*, "simple"].

paras.t: Consurget tumultus, id est inordinatio vitiorum, multiplexque tentatio et afflictio, in populo tuo; et omnes munitiones tuæ vastabuntur, id est, universa in quibus inaniter confidebant, peribunt. Humiliemur ergo sub potenti manu Dei; nec arbitremur nos apprehendisse, sed quæ priora sunt obliviscentes in anteriora extendamur, proficiendo quotidie in timore atque sollicita cordis custodia. Quum enim consummaverit homo, tunc incipiet. Et in solo Deo tota mente sperantes, dicamus carmen illud deificum, prorsusque dulcissimum: In Deo salutare meum et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Deo est.
paras.en: [[10:14|A tumult shall arise|Consurget tumultus]], that is, the disorder of the vices, and manifold temptation and affliction, [[10:14|among thy people|in populo tuo]]; [[10:14|and all thy fortresses shall be destroyed|et omnes munitiones tuæ vastabuntur]], that is, all the things in which they vainly trusted shall perish. Let us therefore be humbled [[1 Pet 5:6|under the mighty hand of God|sub potenti manu Dei]]; and let us not think that we have apprehended, but, forgetting the former things, let us stretch forth to those that are before[[Phil 3:13||]], advancing daily in fear and in a solicitous watch over the heart[[Mich 6:8||]]. For when [[Ecclus 18:6|a man hath done, then shall he begin|consummaverit homo, tunc incipiet]]. And hoping in God alone with our whole mind, let us say that godlike and altogether most sweet song: [[Ps 61:8|In God is my salvation and my glory: he is the God of my help, and my hope is in God.|In Deo salutare meum et gloria mea; Deus auxilii mei, et spes mea in Deo est]]

paras.t: Sic fecit vobis, o Christiani Christo ingrati, Bethel, id est hi qui videntur aliis in spiritualibus præsidere, sed pessimæ conversationis exemplo inficiunt quos salvarent. Bethel autem interpretatur domus Dei. Præsidentes vero in spiritualibus, maxime esse videntur domus Dei. Et ne subditi pereuntes, totam suam damnationem et culpam in prælatos et clericos retorquerent, adjectum est: a facie malitiæ nequitiarum vestrarum. Interdum enim merentur tales superiores habere, vel eorum perversitati nimis faciliter se conformant, paratiores sequi malos quam bonos. Cetera patent ex præcedenti articulo.
paras.en: [[10:15|So hath Bethel done to you|Sic fecit vobis]], O Christians ungrateful to Christ: Bethel, that is, those who seem to preside over others in spiritual things, but by the example of a most wicked life infect those whom they should save. For Bethel is interpreted *house of God*; and those who preside in spiritual things seem most of all to be the house of God. And lest perishing subjects should throw back the whole of their damnation and guilt upon prelates and clerics, it is added: [[10:15|because of the evil of your iniquities|a facie malitiæ nequitiarum vestrarum]]. For at times they deserve to have such superiors, or they conform themselves too readily to their perversity, being readier to follow the wicked than the good. The rest is clear from the preceding article.
